<meta>Following the description of the spine, this page details the physical appearance of the volume’s exterior edges, focusing on the craftsmanship of the binding.</meta>

->THE FORE-EDGE<-

The photograph captures the <term>fore-edge<gloss>the outer edge of the book's pages, opposite the spine</gloss></term> of this substantial volume. The edges of the paper have been treated with a mottled or marbled pattern in a reddish-brown hue. This <term>marbling<gloss>a decorative technique where colors are floated on a liquid surface and transferred to paper</gloss></term> was a common feature of 17th and 18th-century bookbinding, serving both to beautify the book and to hide the inevitable dust and finger marks that accumulate over centuries of use.

On either side of the paper edges, the edges of the leather <term>boards<gloss>the stiff front and back covers of a book</gloss></term> are visible. These are embellished with intricate, repeating <term>gold tooling<gloss>the process of pressing heated metal tools into leather through gold leaf to create a permanent, glittering design</gloss></term>. The motifs are stylized floral and foliate (leaf-like) patterns that run along the rim of the covers. 

The leather shows the natural signs of its age, including wear and softening of the material, particularly at the top and bottom corners.

<summary>This page describes the physical characteristics of the book's exterior, including its marbled page edges and the gold-tooled decorative patterns on the leather covers.</summary>

# The Complete Book
# On the Judgments or Fates of the Stars
## By <term>Halim, son of Abenragel<note>Known in the West as Haly Abenragel (Abū l-Hasan 'Alī ibn Abī l-Rijāl), he was an 11th-century Arab astrologer. His work was highly influential in Europe after being translated into Latin in the 13th century.</note></term>, an Arab, to whom sometimes the forename Albohazen is added:

# Venice
## 1485.

<summary>This title page introduces a 1485 Venetian edition of Haly Abenragel’s influential astrological treatise, "De Judiciis Stellarum." The handwritten notes trace the book's journey from the Benedictine Abbey of Saint-Ouen to the private collection of Anthony de Lamare, and finally to the Library of Sainte-Geneviève in 1753.</summary>

<keywords>astrology, Haly Abenragel, incunabula, Venice printing, provenance, Sainte-Geneviève, Maurists, 15th century</keywords>

--- Page 12 ---
<meta>The previous page established the title and author of this 1485 volume, Haly Abenragel's work on astrology. This page contains the formal dedication from the printer, Erhard Ratdolt, to the Bishop of Augsburg, Johannes von Werdenberg.</meta>

# To the most distinguished Prelate of the sacred cathedral of the imperial city of <term>Augsburg<note>The Latin text uses "Augusta," referring to Augusta Vindelicorum, the Roman name for Augsburg, Germany.</note></term>:
## To the most venerable father, as pious as he is respected:
### And to the most magnificent Count, <term>Johannes von Werdenberg<note>Johannes II von Werdenberg (c. 1430–1486) served as the Bishop of Augsburg. He was a significant patron of the arts and learning during the early days of the printing press.</note></term>. <term>Erhard Ratdolt<note>A pioneering German printer from Augsburg who worked in Venice before returning to his hometown. He is famous for producing the first printer's specimen sheet and for his innovations in printing diagrams and multiple colors.</note></term> of Augsburg, printer of books, sends his reverent greetings.

<image-desc>A large decorative woodcut initial 'C' containing a stylized five-petaled flower surrounded by leafy vines and floral motifs, set within a square frame.</image-desc>

Most worthy father, when I reflect upon your singular virtues, I see that our city-state is rightly called fortunate among the other cities of our German nation. For she has obtained you—a man of noble blood—as a father and most upright shepherd, highly accomplished in all <term>liberal arts<note>The "liberalibus disciplinis" or liberal arts were the traditional core of medieval education: grammar, logic, rhetoric, arithmetic, geometry, music, and astronomy.</note></term> and most gracious toward everyone.

Since I knew this well, a short time ago I dared to present to you certain small works printed by us. I learned from my correspondence that you received them with such kindness; and when I later approached you in person, I felt my service so highly approved in my presence that you spurred me on to print even greater things.

Therefore, since among the other things that can be rightly praised in you, I know you to be no small student of the <term>science of the stars<note>original: "Siderali scientie." In the 15th century, the distinction between astronomy and astrology was not as sharp as it is today; both were considered part of the same "science."</note></term>, you will now receive this most divine work of Haly Abenragel explaining the <term>fates of the stars<note>original: "fata stellarum." This refers to the book's title, "The Judgments of the Stars."</note></term>. It has recently been printed by us with the greatest diligence and dedicated to your name as a token and monument of my singular goodwill and highest respect toward you. Indeed, this respect is so great that I think of nothing else day or night but how to do something pleasing for you and to repay, in some small part, my duty for your countless favors toward me.

Farewell, glory and pillar of our homeland; keep me (as you do) in your good graces.

<summary>In this formal dedication, the celebrated printer Erhard Ratdolt presents his edition of Haly Abenragel's astrological treatise to Johannes von Werdenberg, the Bishop of Augsburg. Ratdolt praises the Bishop's intellect and patronage, noting that the Bishop's personal interest in the "science of the stars" inspired the publication of this significant volume.</summary>

<keywords>Erhard Ratdolt, Johannes von Werdenberg, Augsburg, book dedication, history of printing, astrology, patronage, 15th century, incunabula</keywords>

<margin>From the Monastery of Saint Ouen of the <term>Congregation of Saint Maur<note>The Maurists were a French Benedictine congregation known for their high standards of scholarship.</note></term>.</margin>

### ¶ Preface to the tables of the work.

This is the tabular index of chapters for the finished work and the complete book concerning the fates of the stars. It consists of eight principal parts: The first three measure the prognostications for all kinds of <term>interrogations<note>Also known as horary astrology, where a chart is drawn to answer a specific question.</note></term>. The two that follow explain concisely the fates of the stars for any <term>nativity<note>A birth chart or "geniture."</note></term>. The sixth unrolls the fates of the stars more exactly by repeating the <term>revolution of the years<note>A technique for predicting the year's events based on the sun's return to its birth position.</note></term> for anyone born. The seventh teaches the beginnings of human works, which are commonly called <term>elections<note>The practice of choosing the most auspicious time to begin an undertaking.</note></term>. The eighth encompasses the prognostications for the whole world and its nations regarding the revolution of the years of the world, great conjunctions, eclipses, and comets. This work was produced by <term>Albohazen Hali<note>The Latinized name for Abū l-Hasan 'Alī ibn Abī l-Rijāl (died c. 1037), a court astrologer in Tunisia.</note></term>, son of Abenragel the Arab. Under the direction of Alfonso, the illustrious king of the Romans and of Castile, it was translated from Arabic into Spanish, and thereafter from Spanish into Latin, beginning under a happy fate. ¶ The use of these tables is in this manner: once the desired chapter is found in the table, the number of the book's leaves is found at the end of its line. One must immediately notice the point [dot] placed there, either before or after the number. If the point appears placed *before* the number, the subject of that chapter is found on the front or the prior face <note>Known as the *recto* side.</note> of the leaf designated by that number, so the index may be found quickly. If, however, the point is seen *after* the number, the subject of that chapter is found on the back or the posterior face <note>Known as the *verso* side.</note> of the leaf noted by that number, as is shown so it may be found without delay. Thus, most desirably, the labor of a long search is entirely removed from you, and you will achieve the pleasant fruit of the work.

<meta>This page marks the formal beginning of the manuscript, following the table of contents. It introduces the primary author, Haly Abenragel (Ibn Abi al-Rijal), and details the complex translation history of the text from Arabic to Old Castilian and finally into the Latin presented here.</meta>

# The most distinguished and complete book on the judgments of the stars, which Albohazen Haly, son of Abenragel, published, most happily begins; and first, the prologue to the book itself.

This is the great and complete book that Haly Abenragel, son of the highest astrologer, composed regarding the <term>judgments of the stars<note>original: "iudicijis astroꝝ"; this refers to judicial astrology, the practice of making specific predictions or "judgments" based on celestial movements.</note>). This work was translated from the Arabic language into the mother tongue—specifically the Spanish dialect—by Yehuda, son of Moshe, by order of the Lord Alfonso, the illustrious King of the Romans and Castile, by the grace of God. From that version, Egidius de Tebaldis of Parma, a notary of the Imperial Court, together with Peter de Regio, the prothonotary of the same court, translated it into Latin. This book is divided into eight parts, as the chapters will show.

->The Translators’ Prologue<-

Haly, son of Abenragel, said: Thanks be to the one God, the victorious, the honored, the powerful creator of night and day, the revealer of hidden sciences and purities; to him who created, balanced, judged, directed, brought death, and gave life; the Lord of liberty, reward, honor, and the kingdom. He is the first without a known beginning and the last without a finite end. He created the surrounding heavens, the moving stars, the covering sky, and the supporting earth. He is the one whose lordship and power are demonstrated by all things which sight reaches and which thought and sense perceive in all signs and significations. May his salvations be upon those who faithfully believe in him.

->The Author’s Prologue<-

This is the book in which I have brought together many insights concerning the science of the stars and the wonders of their secrets. I have collected from many books of the wise men of this science, and I have added to it that which I have evaluated both through my own understanding and opinion, and what I have found through experience. For this science of the stars is grand and very high; it cannot be fully embraced, nor can even one who is wise in it explain the whole of it or divide it into all its domains. This is because it is a science of separate parts, diverse judgments, and hidden secrets. Nevertheless, a wise, understanding, subtle, and sharp person can extract it through their own intellect, subtlety, and the sharpness of their nature. But the ignorant person who passes through it is overwhelmed; they stumble within it and lose the essence of it through their own ignorance and the weight of the subject. ¶ I have set forth this joined and complete book so that it encompasses all manners of this science, from the beginning of its roots to the completion of all its divisions. ¶ I began first by speaking of the <term>signs<note>The twelve signs of the Zodiac.</note></term> and their natures, and of the planets and their qualities, and of those things which must be set forth before we speak of the judgments. Then I spoke regarding <term>questions<note>original: "questionib'"; refers to Horary astrology, where a chart is cast to answer a specific question.</note></term> and arranged these in three parts. Afterward,

<column-break/>

I spoke of <term>nativities<note>original: "natiuitatib'"; birth charts or natal astrology.</note></term> and arranged them in two parts. Afterward, I spoke regarding the revolutions of the years of the person born, placing them in one part. Afterward, I spoke of the <term>revolutions of the years of the world<note>Mundane astrology, predicting events for cities, kingdoms, or the entire world based on the solar year.</note></term>, placing them in one part. And so, the parts of the book were perfected in eight parts.

The first part of the complete book on the judgments of the stars begins, which contains sixty chapters.

### Chapter One: Regarding the Signs.

<margin>Of Lordship<note>original: "del Segnory"; likely a vestige of the Old Castilian translation process.</note></margin>
There are twelve similar signs in the sky, corresponding to the members of the body, whose natures govern the four elements. These elements are the roots of bodies and are held within them. Because of the existence of the planets in the signs—and their entry into and exit from them—there occur the changes of the seasons and the air, and the increase of heat and cold in each year. ¶ The beginning of the signs is Aries; then Taurus, Gemini, Cancer, Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpio, Sagittarius, Capricorn, Aquarius, and Pisces. Six of these signs are Northern—namely from the head of Aries to the end of Virgo—and six are Southern—namely from the head of Libra to the end of Pisces. The line that passes through the head of Aries and the head of Libra is the straight circle in which the night and day are made equal and directed. When one of these signs ascends in one part, it places its opposite in the other, from East to West. Because of this diversity, the length and brevity of the day occurs, along with the increase and decrease in its hours and ascensions. ¶ Some of these signs are fiery, some earthy, some airy, and some watery. ¶ Among these, some are in the form of humans, others in the form of beasts, and others in the form of reptiles. ¶ Some of them are mute, others rational, others generative, others sterile, others whole, others broken, others masculine, others feminine, others fortunate, others unfortunate, others bitter, others false, others sweet, and others sharp. Some are increasing in their ascensions, others decreasing. Some are eastern, others western. Some are southern, others northern. ¶ Aries, Leo, and Sagittarius are fiery. Taurus, Virgo, and Capricorn are earthy. Gemini, Libra, and Aquarius are airy. Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces are watery. The masculine signs are the fiery and airy ones. The feminine ones are the earthy and watery ones. ¶ The masculine signs are signs of fortune; the feminine ones are of misfortune. Those in human form are Gemini, Libra, Aquarius, and Virgo. In the form of beasts are Aries, Taurus, Capricorn, and Sagittarius. In the form of wild beasts is Leo. In the form of reptiles are Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces. The "broken" signs are Aries, Leo, and Pisces; the others are whole. The rational signs are Libra, Aquarius, Gemini, and Virgo. ¶ Those having a voice are Aries, Leo, Taurus, Capricorn, and Sagittarius. The mute ones are Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces. ¶ Signs of many children <gloss>fruitful</gloss> are Pisces, Cancer, and Scorpio. Signs of few children are Aries, Taurus, Sagittarius, Capricorn, and Libra. The sterile signs are Leo and Gemini.

<summary>This page serves as the formal introduction to Haly Abenragel's seminal astrological treatise, outlining its translation history from Arabic to Latin and providing a foundational classification of the twelve zodiac signs by element, gender, and physical form.</summary>
<keywords>Haly Abenragel, Ibn Abi al-Rijal, Alfonso X, astrology, zodiac signs, four elements, planetary influences, judicial astrology, translation history, medieval science</keywords>

--- Page 20 ---
<meta>This page continues the introductory principles of astrology, moving from general definitions into the specific classifications of the zodiac signs as established by Ptolemy and other classical authorities. It transitions into more technical subdivisions of the signs, specifically "Terms" and "Faces."</meta>

Ptolemy stated that the signs of few children are Aries, Taurus, Libra, Sagittarius, Capricorn, and Aquarius. Those of many children are Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces. The sterile signs are Gemini, Leo, and Virgo. The signs of much interaction with women are Aries, Leo, Capricorn, and Pisces.

The Eastern signs are Aries, Leo, and Sagittarius. The Western are Gemini, Libra, and Aquarius. The Southern are Taurus, Virgo, and Capricorn. The Northern are Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces.

The sharp <note>original: "acria"; likely referring to pungent or acidic tastes associated with the signs' elemental qualities.</note> signs are Taurus, Capricorn, and Virgo. The bitter are Aries, Leo, and Sagittarius. The sweet are Gemini, Libra, and Aquarius. The salty are Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces.

The weak signs are Aries, Sagittarius, and Capricorn. The strong are Leo, Scorpio, and Aquarius.

The straight <note>original: "directa"; signs that take longer to rise over the horizon.</note> signs are from the beginning of Cancer to the end of Sagittarius. The crooked <note>original: "tortuosa"; signs that rise quickly or "obliquely."</note> signs are from the beginning of Capricorn to the end of Gemini.

The natures of these signs change due to their movement in the circumference; for their heat becomes cold, and cold becomes heat, and moisture becomes dryness, and dryness becomes moisture. Thus, Taurus in the East is lukewarm, but in the West, it is cold. Gemini is hot and dry in the East, but in the West, it is cold and moist. Cancer is hot and dry in the East, but in the West, it is cold and moist. Leo is hot and dry in the East, but in the West, it is cold and moist. Virgo is lukewarm in the East, but in the West, it is cold and moist. Sagittarius in the East is cold and moist, but in the West, it is hot and dry. Capricorn in the East is cold and dry, but in the West, it is cold and moist. Aquarius and Pisces are both cold and moist in both the East and the West.

## ¶ The Second Chapter: On the Terms

<margin>Concerning the humors</margin>
<image-desc>Ornamental drop cap 'T' with foliate patterns within a square border.</image-desc> Terms <note>original: "termini"; these are specific degree-ranges within a zodiac sign assigned to a particular planet.</note> are parts of the signs. There are five terms in every sign, and four of them correspond to the four qualities, which are heat and dryness, coldness and dryness, heat and moisture, and coldness and moisture. The fifth nature is mixed from these four natures, according to the mixture of the complexion of Mercury, who is at one time dry, another hot, another cold, and another moist. 

When any of the planets enters any of these terms, it strengthens itself if it is compatible with its nature and form; but it is weakened and worsened if it is different from its nature and form. Thus, if a term is cold and dry, and a planet is likewise cold and dry, it increases in its coldness and dryness. If it is hot and dry, it rises in its heat and dryness. If it is cold and moist, it increases in coldness and moisture. 

A term that is hot and dry changes a planet that is cold and moist because of its heat and dryness. And a term that is cold and moist changes a planet that is hot and dry because of its coldness and moisture. 

If a term is among the fortunate terms, and a fortunate planet enters it, it then increases in its goodness, profit, and fortune. If it is an unfortunate term and an unfortunate planet enters it, it increases in its evil, misfortune, and harm—especially if it is in a sign compatible with the planet in its nature and qualities. For example: if Mars is in a fiery sign and a fiery term, or Saturn in an earthy sign and an earthy term. 

According to this judgment, colors also change. For when the color of the term is compatible with the color of the sign, 

<column-break/>

that color is more strengthened and increases by thickening that tint. For example, if the term of Mars is in Aries, Leo, or Sagittarius, then its redness increases and is strengthened. If the term is of Saturn in Libra, Scorpio, or Capricorn, its blackness and darkness increase and are strengthened. But if it is in different signs, that color is diversified and diminished from the state it was in; the redness and blackness are weakened and diminished. Likewise, it is thinned, and the red becomes a weaker color—that is, of less redness; similarly, black is changed and drawn toward green, according to the mixture of the color of the term with the color of the sign.

The Lord of the Term who is in his own term has greater power in that sign than the Lord of the House <note>The primary ruling planet of a sign.</note> or the Lord of Exaltation <note>A planet that has a special position of honor in a sign.</note> if they are in "peregrine" <note>original: "peregrinis"; referring to a planet in a place where it has no specific dignity or power.</note> locations. If the Lord of the Term is in his own term and the Lord of the Sign is in another sign casting his rays upon him, the Lord of the Term will have greater power in that sign than the Lord of the Sign, and the significance will be his. 

If the Lord of the Term is in his own term and his own house, then his significance is strengthened, and he extends his action and his gift. For any planet entering any sign, the harm to it is condemned <note>minimized</note> when it is in its own term; by that sign, the harm is diminished and it is strengthened by casting the harm away from itself. If a planet enters any of the signs that bring it fortune and it is in its own term, its fortune is then completed, its action is verified, and it is strengthened in all its significations and deeds, with the help of God.

## The Third Chapter: On the Faces

<margin>Regarding the 3 Faces</margin>
<image-desc>Ornamental drop cap 'S' with foliate patterns within a square border.</image-desc> Know that in every sign there are three "Faces" <note>Also known as "decans," these are 10-degree subdivisions of a zodiac sign.</note>, and in every face are those things which the sages have said regarding forms, figures, and likenesses. These faces are divided by the planets according to their order in the heavens. When the sequence reaches the lower planet from below, it returns and begins again from the high one above. These faces have natures and figures compatible with the natures and figures of their lords. Likewise, they agree with them in their significations, properties, and deeds.

<margin>3 Faces</margin> The first face of Aries belongs to Mars; it is a face of boldness, strength, height, and shamelessness, and it is complete and firm in its properties and virtues. 

The second face of Aries belongs to the Sun; it is of nobility, the height of the kingdom, and great lordship. 

The third is of Venus; it is feminine, of subtlety in work, and of gentleness, play, joy, and brightness. 

The first face of Taurus belongs to Mercury; it is complete in its nature, and it is a face of plowing and sowing, building, populating, giving instruction, and wisdom in dividing lands and in geometry. 

The second face is of the Moon; it is of power, nobility, dignity, and of depopulating villages and necessity over people. 

The third face is of Saturn; it is of misery, servitude, ferocity, necessity, and vileness. 

The first face of Gemini belongs to Jupiter, complete in its nature; it is of writing, number, giving and receiving, petitions, and wisdoms in which there will be no utility. 

The second face is of Mars; it is of the pressure of labor and seeking things with effort and dishonest agility. 

The third face is of the Sun; it is of forgetfulness, disdain, joking, jesting, and...

### The Faces of the Signs

The first <term>face</term><note>A "face" (or decan) is a 10-degree subdivision of a zodiac sign. There are three faces in every 30-degree sign, each governed by a different planetary ruler.</note> of **Cancer** belongs to **Venus** and is complete in its nature; it is a face of vigor, of the senses, and of those who make themselves loved by men, and of subtlety and community. ¶ The second face belongs to **Mercury** and is of jesting, the cheerfulness of women, of riches and abundance. ¶ The third face belongs to the **Moon** and is of hunting, of pursuing those who flee, of obtaining things through arms and strife, and of opposing men. ¶ The first face of **Leo** belongs to **Saturn** and is of complete form; of opposing, of yielding, and of agility in evil, in quarrels, and in abhorrent things. ¶ The first face of **Capricorn** belongs to **Jupiter** and is complete in figure and nature; it is of walking, of rejoicing, of gaining, and of losing with weakness and vileness. ¶ The second face belongs to **Mars** and is of seeking things that cannot be known, and demanding things that cannot reach an end. ¶ The third face belongs to the **Sun** and is of the desire to govern substance, not being sufficient for oneself, and of suspicion. ¶ The first face of **Aquarius** belongs to **Venus** and is of always being anxious for profit and never resting, of labors, of diminishment, and of the defect of poverty and vileness. ¶ The second face belongs to **Mercury** and is of beauty, of intellect, of gentleness with modesty and not becoming angry, of good manners, of the completion of its figure

For a planet "breaks" a planet; a <term>term</term><note>A "term" is another subdivision of a sign, smaller than a face, ruled by a specific planet that can "break" or modify the influence of the sign or face ruler.</note> breaks a face; a face breaks a <term>house</term><note>A "house" refers to the entire zodiac sign as the domicile of a specific planet.</note>; and their natures enter one upon another, just as water extinguishes the heat of fire, and fire removes the coldness of water, and water which makes the dryness of the earth moist, and earth which dries the moisture of water. ## Chapter Four: On the Natures of the Planets.

<image-desc>Decorative drop cap P featuring a seated scholar or astronomer at a desk surrounded by books and tools of study.</image-desc>
<margin>Against Saturn</margin>
Planets help each other because of their agreements: and they disturb each other because of their discords and their diversities. And a <term>house</term><note>A "house" (domus) refers to the zodiac sign over which a planet has rulership; for example, Leo is the house of the Sun.</note> is an enemy to a house: and an <term>exaltation</term><note>The "exaltation" is the specific sign where a planet's influence is most potent; its opposite is the "fall" (casus), where it is weakest.</note> to an exaltation: and one heaven to another. For what is made through the heaven of **Saturn** is destroyed by the heaven of the **Moon**. And what is made through the heaven of **Jupiter** is destroyed by the heaven of **Mercury**. And what is made through the heaven of **Mars** is destroyed by the heaven of **Venus**. ¶ In the place where there is the exaltation of Saturn is the <term>fall</term><note>original: "casus"</note> of the **Sun**. And where the Sun is brought low, Saturn is exalted. Where Jupiter is exalted, Mars falls. And where Mars falls, Jupiter is exalted. Where Mercury is exalted, Venus falls: and where Mercury falls, Venus is exalted. ¶ The signs are in concord through their natures, though they may be diverse in their forms, manners, and quantities. ¶ Concordant signs are those which agree in their <term>ascensions</term><note>The way signs rise over the horizon.</note>. Discordant signs are those which differ in them. ¶ A planet is an enemy to another planet when they regard each other from the <term>fourth</term><note>A "square" aspect (90 degrees).</note> or the opposite. They love and agree with each other when they regard each other from the <term>third</term><note>A "trine" aspect (120 degrees).</note> or the <term>sixth</term><note>A "sextile" aspect (60 degrees).</note>. When a planet regards another planet from the house of its fall: it is an enemy to it and abhors it. For example: if Saturn were in the place of its 
<margin>at the house</margin>
exaltation or the house of Venus, and if then Saturn regarded Venus: that aspect is one of enmity. And when it looks from the twelfth house from its own house, it likewise abhors it. And when its own action is turned back upon it, it likewise abhors that. And when it does not receive it, it likewise abhors it. And when it is diverse from the other in its form and its action, it abhors it likewise. When planets are in enmity and abhor each other: they damage the outcome and their own significance.

### Concerning the Sun

<image-desc>Decorative drop cap S featuring a crowned figure, likely representing the Sun or a King, standing in a natural landscape.</image-desc>
Know that the **Sun** is the light and candle of heaven: the governor of the world: the maker of the seasons. Through him the planets become <term>oriental</term><note>Rising before the sun.</note> and <term>occidental</term><note>Setting after the sun.</note>: and through him they become visible and hidden: through him every moving thing is moved: through him every being that is born is born: every growing thing grows: every leaf increases and every fruit is ripened. He is the

<column-break/>

great spirit of heaven. With him the signs are given life. And any sign, when he is in it, has a majority over other signs: because he vivifies and illuminates it and gives it strength and heat, and applies the heat, strength, and virtue of that sign to the earth: because his nature and deeds appear in all things and in all beings, animate and inanimate, existing on the earth. And when he departs from the sign in which he was: that sign remains in the likeness of a dead body: since it has no spirit or motion: and so do all the other planets: because when any planet enters any sign, then that sign has an improvement over other empty signs. And that sign in which the planet is avoids other empty signs just as a living body avoids a dead one when it comes to it. Through the Sun happens the flowing of waters and the motion of winds. Through him the clouds are born and the rains come. And he is a planet of great dominion, power, nobility, height, and magnitude. ¶ And he is a fortune by <term>aspect</term><note>When the sun is at a favorable angle to another planet.</note>: but a misfortune by bodily <term>conjunction</term><note>When a planet is so close to the sun (combust) that its own power is "burned up" or hidden by the sun's rays.</note>. For you see when any planet is joined to him: he burns and overcomes it and extinguishes its light and its radiance. ¶ And in questions of petitions he is the shower of things that overcome and die, and of strong things to be sought. And any planet that joins him and enters under his rays, he makes small and base. ¶ He is the significator of fathers: his place in the firmament is the fourth: and he is compared to fathers in his forms and deeds: so that when the Moon joins him at the hour of conjunction: which is the covering and refinement of the Moon, that is in the likeness of a man and a woman: and when she is separated from him, the beginning of light and radiance is renewed in her: and that light and radiance go on increasing just as a creature grows: and it goes on increasing and kindling until she makes herself one complete round body in the likeness of her father who caused her to be born and kindled her. And he signifies concerning the body of man—because his exaltation is in Aries—that which is in his partition of man, which is the head. And he signifies among the internal members of the body the **stomach**: because it is compared to him in the processing of waters in the belly of the earth: and he makes its thickness subtle: he clarifies the turbid and matures it because of his heat, strength, nature, and property: and he transmits its subtle part to the top of trees and branches: and any tree and every plant and herb receives its part from him: just as the stomach does, which cooks the food sent into it: and transmits their good, clear, and subtle part to the liver: and the liver divides it through the veins: and every vein receives its part according to its quantity and what belongs to it. ¶ The Sun is better and more noble than all other planets and higher in nobility: because his nature works in all natures and none of the other natures work in him. ¶ His house is better, more noble, and higher in nobility than all other houses. And his exaltation likewise exceeds the exaltations of others, as do his faces and <term>triplicities</term><note>A group of three signs belonging to the same element (Fire, Earth, Air, or Water).</note>. ¶ His place: in heaven he is in the fourth, namely the middle of the seven planets: like a wise king who through his sense...

->¶ About the Moon.<-

<image-desc>Decorative initial L featuring vine and leaf motifs within a square frame.</image-desc>
The **Moon** is the lesser light and is the mistress of the world's <term>ascendant</term><note>The "ascendant" refers to the rising sign on the eastern horizon; here used to mean the mistress of the physical world's beginnings.</note>: she is likened to man above all other things in the beginning of his generation: and afterward in his diminishing: because she begins small and goes on growing, receiving light from the Sun until she stands in opposition to him: and if one of the two <term>nodes</term><note>The "nodes" are the points where the Moon's orbit crosses the ecliptic; eclipses only occur when the Moon is near these points.</note> is near that place, she is eclipsed: and similarly the Moon eclipses the Sun when she is joined to him and the conjunction is in one of the two nodes. ¶ The Moon is near the Sun just as a great **Algaçil** is near a king, to whom the king gives power and high rank and draws him close to himself. For the Sun governs the Moon with his light and strength until she puts herself in opposition. And when she is placed in that location, the Sun resists her and diminishes her light and takes away from her what he had lent and put in her power: and he leads her just as a king does when he exalts his **Algaçil** and gives him strength and power in commanding his race and people: and in supporting them: and in doing what seems [good] to him. And when the **Algaçil** is magnified: and in power he proceeds so that he is in the likeness of the king his lord, then the king begins to depress him and take away the height which he had put in his power. And in this manner is the Moon with the Sun and the Sun with the Moon.

¶ Through the Moon is the beauty of the stars: and their ugliness: because she herself moves through the stars and carries [influence] from one to another. ¶ The nature of the Moon is cold and moist: **Mars** hinders her when she is full and replete with her light: and **Saturn** hinders her when she is diminished and destroyed. She is the queen and governess of the night and powerful in the sea and in her own waxing and waning. All the fruit of the water is opened through her: through that very waxing and waning, an increase and decrease occurs in the marrow and brains of every living thing in man and beasts. And she is a participant in the <term>ascendant</term> and its lord in <term>nativity</term><note>A birth chart.</note> and <term>horary questions</term><note>original: "questione"; the practice of answering specific questions by casting an astrological chart for the moment the question is asked.</note>. And she is worth as much as the ascendant: when the degree of the ascendant is neither known nor determined. She performs the work of the Sun at the beginning of any secret, and every covered and hidden thing she uncovers and shows: she is powerful in motion and approach, agilely and strongly: and in every reborn and generated thing in which the Moon was: if she is unfortunate by a strong misfortune by day or night, there will be evil in its nurturing and misfortune.

**Saturn** is a great, old, weary planet: of contempt: of anxieties: of sorrows and of long infirmities: His nature is cold and dry: he is likened to melancholy, which is governed by all honors and none by it <note>Melancholy was one of the four humors; Saturn was traditionally its planetary ruler.</note>: he is dry: envious: he holds anger for a long time: he speaks little: he does not desire company: he wishes to stay alone and separate: he holds deep opinions: he is of good memory: subtle: he thinks and looks into ancient things: he does not have an agile intellect: he is fearful and a traitor: he performs the experiment of binding necromancy and wonders: with kings he is in the likeness of a king: because all planets send their considerations: natures and strengths to him. ## About Jupiter.

Jupiter is the planet of equality: community: improvement: intellect: sense: and piety: because he is tempered and equal: and a fortune <note>In astrology, a "fortune" or benefic is a planet that brings favorable results.</note> through

<column-break/>

aspect and bodily conjunction: he signifies goodness: improvement: law: simplicity: and chastity: he directs and does not condemn: he populates and does not destroy. He abhors Saturn and his natures: he prohibits and pulls him back from his evil works. He is of beautiful appearance and a composed person: mild: faithful: lawful: and pious: he commands and shows goodness: prohibits and abhors evil: helps the poor: governs those for whom it is expedient: truthful in his words and deeds: of good comfort and love: of good and true friendship and without fraud: complete and healthy in body and limbs: prosperous in his deeds and works: he loves judgements: decrees and justice. If he must show some matter of goodness or improvement: he strengthens: affirms and verifies it. And if he has to show some horrendous or evil thing: he pulls back and condemns it and hinders it through himself and his deeds with the good pleasure of God. And when he is strong, happy, and firm in births <note>original: *natiuitatibus*, referring to the natal chart at the moment of birth</note>: the fortune and nourishment of the newborn is fulfilled. And if he is dejected in births or damaged, the business of the newborn will be damaged: and his life is diminished. No utility or any good exists in any deed or in any thing except through him: and through his demonstration and aspect: and through him the air clears: winds run and health-giving rains [fall], namely in times bringing benefit and not harm: through his equality, community, and the temperance of his complexion <note>In medieval science, "complexion" refers to the balance of the four qualities: hot, cold, moist, and dry.</note>: the heat of summer and cold of winter are tempered: and infirmities: epidemics: and mortalities are diminished through his demonstration in the revolution <note>The annual cycle of the heavens.</note> of the year. And through his demonstration and strength in the ninth month from the conception of a creature, the newborn is delivered: and it will be for the world and for its rest: and for the air: and he is delivered from the distress of the womb and its darkness. And although God knows the secret. Yet some wise men say that Jupiter was created and made from the clarity of the air and its light: and from its clear and purged wind. He is diurnal and masculine: he signifies brothers, friends, and kinsmen. ¶ On the day when God began to create the world, he was in the ascendant house <note>The "Ascendant" is the sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of creation.</note>. ¶ He shines in **Aries**, **Taurus**, and **Gemini**: and his light is diminished in **Cancer**: **Leo**: and **Virgo**: he is obscured in **Libra**: **Scorpio**: and **Sagittarius**: and his obscurity is diminished in **Capricorn**: **Aquarius**: and **Pisces**. ¶ In all parts of **Aries**, he is cloudy: he loves vices: abundance: eating: dressing: and cleaning himself. ¶ In the first face of **Taurus**, he is a man of the science of judging: of good morals and of writing. ¶ In the second and third face, he is blinded, damaged in limbs: of a narrow neck: curved spine: of evil quality: of open poverty: and is base.

**M**ars is a hot and dry planet: fiery, burning, nocturnal, feminine <note>While Mars is usually considered masculine, some astrological traditions classify it as "feminine" in certain contexts or due to its nocturnal sect.</note>, a destroyer, angry, and victorious. He loves to kill and loves slaughter, quarrels, and litigation: and to easily oppose another. He is unfortunate, a fool, and impatient: he is quickly provoked to a strong anger: he puts his whole heart

<column-break/>

into his deeds: he does not truly perceive why he is angry, nor does he pull back his hand from doing what he has begun: he stirs up wars and deeds, makes battle, and destroys populations. ¶ His **exaltation** <note>The sign where a planet's influence is most harmoniously strengthened.</note> is in the house of Saturn <note>Capricorn</note>, which signifies outcries, impediments, foolish people, and warring. Saturn is compatible with Mars in misfortune, and resists him in coldness and darkness. ¶ He is inclined toward the **Sun** by his own love: and is defended by the Sun's help, because the Sun is exalted in his house <note>Aries</note> and governs him with the heat and dryness which he receives from the same. ¶ His property and nature are compatible with and approach the property and nature of the Sun: he is ignorant and forgetful: of modest intellect and diminished sense: nor does he consider the ends of things. ¶ Through him, and through his ascent and descent in his circle, the heat of summer and the cold of winter increase and decrease every year. And when he descends in his circle toward the earth and its vapors, he is moistened and his heat is diminished: and then he signifies infirmities and pains proceeding from the condition of the blood, which are of a hot and moist nature. ### Concerning Mercury

<image-desc>Decorative woodcut initial 'M' featuring floral or scrollwork patterns within a square frame.</image-desc>

**Mercury** is the planet of sorceries: of violences: of teachings: of writing: of calculations and sciences. He is hot and dry: he is of a changeable form and nature: masculine when with masculine planets: feminine with the feminine: a good fortune with a good fortune: a misfortune with a misfortune. He is well-reasoned: well-speaking: bold in speech: of beautiful appearance: a well-composed person: a youth. He loves books and calculations: crafts <note>original: "magistieria"</note> please him: things well done: beautiful reasons: books of romance to be verified and sciences: agile in motion: and of a burning nature: cheerful: mobile in all his affairs: through speech, reasoning, and resistance he pulls back misfortune from the unfortunate. ¶ His exaltation is in his own house <note>Virgo</note>: and his fall is in **Pisces**. And he is weakened in the house of **Venus**. He is a sharer with **Jupiter** in wisdom: teaching: science and his intellect. ### ¶ Chapter 5: On the highest matters and other things that should be set before others.

The heavens have good fortune and misfortune; the signs likewise have good and bad fortunes. The fortunes of heaven are the four angles <note>The "angles" are the four most powerful points in a chart: the Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Imum Coeli.</note>: and those houses following them. For colors are changed through the motion of the heaven: and through the change of the houses in the chart, just as they are changed by the "application" <note>When a planet moves toward an aspect with another.</note> of a planet or its "separation": or by its direct motion or its station: or by its retrogradation <note>When a planet appears to move backward in the sky.</note>. ¶ Fortunate places of the heaven are suitable for planets that are joined with others. ¶ Unfortunate places of the heaven are suitable for all unfortunate things: and for light planets that are solitary and "void of course" <note>A planet that makes no further aspects before leaving its current sign.</note>. ¶ The Ascendant is the door and the key of heaven: and it is the house through which the planet applies to its significations and deeds: and the other houses follow it: and rise after it: such as the house of substance [wealth]: of brothers: of fathers: of sons, etc. Whichever of these houses is firm, fortunate, strong, and well-disposed: received in a good state: it shows and signifies good and improvement and fortune in matters that belong to the nature of that house: and its significations. Whichever house among them is weak shows loss and misfortune in the matters of that same house. ¶ In every question <note>This refers to "horary astrology," where a chart is cast to answer a specific question.</note> in which you find the Moon strong: firm and fortunate: and the lord of her house is afflicted: unfortunate and bad: it shows strength and improvement at the beginning of that matter: and loss and weakness: and hindrance at its end. And if the Moon is unfortunate: and the lord of the Moon's house is strong and fortunate: there will be hardship and loss at the beginning of the matter: and its end will be good, complete, and easy. ¶ When the lord of the house of the question is a "fortune" <note>A benefic planet like Jupiter or Venus.</note>: and receives the lord of the Ascendant: the querent will receive more than they sought: and in which they had trust and utility, goodness and ease regarding their question. ¶ If the lord of the house is an "infortune" <note>A malefic planet like Mars or Saturn.</note> and does not receive the lord of the Ascendant or the fortifier of the chart: there will be hardship in the question: entanglement and loss: until the seeker loathes it: and regrets having asked the question and having begun it. The ancient wise men are in disagreement regarding the terms <note>subdivisions of a zodiac sign that grant a planet specific power</note>; and there are five opinions: one is of the Egyptians, another of Ptolemy, the third of those of Babylonia, the fourth of the Indians, and the fifth of Atraratyh. ¶ However, the opinion of the greater part of men—which is the most truthful and most tested—are the terms of the Egyptians; and few use the terms of Ptolemy. One is of the Greeks, which is according to the order of the heavens, beginning from Mars. Another is of the Indians, and it is begun upon the order of the triplicities <note>groupings of signs by element: Fire, Earth, Air, Water</note>. Another is of Alkindi. However, the first of these is the most truthful; and in that, the greater part of men agree and use it. ¶ And they are in disagreement regarding the masculine and feminine degrees; and there are two opinions. For Ptolemy says: I see that matters ought to be placed in three ways. First, that which is past, concerning how it shall be dissolved and condemned. Second is that which is past, whether it shall be affirmed or not. And third, that which ought to happen, whether it shall be or shall not be: and in this saying and division many of the ancients and moderns agree and work by it. ¶ And Dorotheus <note>Dorotheus of Sidon, a 1st-century astrologer</note> says: I see things divided into four parts. One, that which was: and is past. Another, that which was and is present. Another, that which is present and approaching. Fourth, that which was not and shall be. ¶ And Alvellius <note>likely Vettius Valens, a 2nd-century authority</note> said: I say that whatever is in the world is divided into two ways. One is a question for that which is past, whether it occurred or not. The other is a question for that which ought to happen, whether it shall be or not. And he says that there is nothing in the world which is not included in these two ways. ¶ And the author of the *Book of Examples* says that whatever is in this world is included in five ways. First is a question for that which is past, whether it was or was not. Second is a question for that which is to be seen: whether it shall be or not. Third is a question for that which neither was nor shall be. Fourth is a question for that which is present: whether its end is completed or if it shall be completed. Fifth is a question of at what time that which was occurred: and at what time that which shall be will happen. ¶ Masha'allah says that the heavens are established upon six parts of questions. First, if

the seeker asked for a certain thing: or did not ask. Second, after they asked for a certain thing, for which of them they asked. Third, where it is. Fourth, how much it is. Fifth, if it shall be or not be. Sixth, when it shall be. ¶ Abu 'Ali al-Khayyat says that all things of the world are in three ways: in that which is past, and is present: and is future. ¶ They are also in disagreement in knowing the thought <note>original: "cogitationem"; the hidden intent or unspoken question of the person seeking an astrological consultation</note> of the seeker: and by what manner they shall understand him and what signification they ought to have over him. ¶ Dorotheus said, when you wish to know the thought of the seeker: look to the lord of the triplicity <note>the three signs of the same element—Fire, Earth, Air, or Water</note> of the Ascendant first: and if it be in its own house or exaltation or triplicity: or its own term <note>a specific subsection of a zodiac sign</note>: judge by the place where you find it. And a planet is said to be elevated over another when it is in the tenth sign from the sign in which the other planet is. And then it is said that this planet is elevated over the other. And if you find this: judge that the question was for some of the works. And if you find no planet elevated over another: judge that the question was for one of the other three things. And when it is so, and you wish to know which of the other three it may be: look to the planet which is elevated over another of the seven planets: except the moon, and the property of that planet and the sign in which it is elevated over the other planet: and from that, judge.

Any two degrees whose distance from the start of Aries is equal to the right and left are said to be two degrees equal in power <note>This refers to 'Antiscia,' degrees that are mirror images of each other across the solstice points</note>. Know that the **Ascendant** is the significator of the property of the thing. The **second house** signifies the price of the thing. The **third** signifies that which happens in the thing and that which is joined to it in one species. The **fourth** signifies the progeny of the thing and its root. The **fifth** signifies the manner of the thing, and that which is generated from it. The **sixth** signifies the durability of the thing, and that which serves it. The **seventh** signifies the contrary of the thing existing in strength from its progeny. The **eighth** signifies the low valuation of the thing, its end, and its condemnation. The **ninth** signifies the removal of the thing, and its causes which adhere to it. The **tenth** signifies the nobility and height of the thing, and its property in deeds. The **eleventh** signifies the completion of the thing, its beauty and its convenience. The **twelfth** signifies the diversity of things and the bad accidents that happen in it. Whence, the lord of whichever of these houses is in a good state, he directs the nature of that thing according to the quantity of the reason and the improvement of that lord: if it be a **fortune** <note>fortune: a "benefic" planet like Jupiter or Venus</note>, it will be fortune: if it be strong, it will give strength: and if there be **reception** <term>reception: a condition where one planet is in a sign governed by another, indicating cooperation</term>, there will be reception: and all this is in the manner of qualities: and if it be the contrary, it will be the contrary in condemnation. And in whatever place of these an improvement or condemnation happens, there will be improvement or condemnation in that nature of the same place: and there will be improvement or condemnation according to the nature of that planet which improves or

<column-break/>

condemns it: and according to its property: and according to the nature it has by its **aspect** in the figure <note>figure: the astrological chart</note> if its deed be by aspect: or according to the place where it is if its deed be by its place in the figure: and by the nature of the sign in which it is. And the quantity of the strength of that improvement or condemnation shall be according to the quality of the strength of the planet that is the "maker." And whatever state the maker and the receiver of the deed have in heaven: according to that state it shall be in that which is demonstrated on earth. If the maker be visible in the figure: that demonstration and that deed shall be visible. And if it be hidden: it shall be hidden. And the cause of every elemental thing is the element of its place: and the cause of the fortune of a thing is the fortune of its place, which is from the planet acting in heaven, or from the one who rules over that place. And the house of completion of a thing belongs to the planet acting and reigning over the nature of its place. And when the maker **applies** <term>applies: moves toward a specific geometric aspect with another planet</term> to the one who receives the deed: the deed will happen in reception by the degree of the maker. And if the receiver applies to the maker: that deed will happen by the degree of the receiver. And if the one who receives the application is **retrograde** <term>retrograde: appearing to move backward in the sky; usually a sign of delay or trouble</term>: that accident will happen suddenly. And the one who is higher in the air (that is, who is higher in the figure—for example: a planet which is in the **Midheaven** is higher than one in the eleventh or ninth house, and so on for others) is the actor, and is always the maker of deeds. And if the application is by **opposition** <term>opposition: an aspect of 180 degrees, usually indicating conflict</term>: that which it signifies will be with contrariety and labor. And if it be from the **fourth** [a square aspect]: it will be with labor, yet firm. And if it be from the **third** [a trine aspect]: it will be with lightness, pleasant, and quiet. And if it be from a **sextile** [60 degrees] likewise: except that it will be less and weaker. And if it be from **conjunction**: it will be complete, firm, and swift. ¶ The victor of two contending [planets] is always the one higher in the air: and it is understood of him who is higher in the figure; the end is always with the higher one according to the order of the heavens. ¶ The affirmation of a thing and its durability is always with him who is closer to the **angles** <note>angles: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses; the most powerful points in a chart</note>: and this is through the dignity and lordship he has in the angles. ¶ Natural qualities (that is, health) belong always to the one who is more affirmed in the eastern part. ¶ Force and impetuosity belong always to those who are swift in their motion; understand this regarding the significators. ¶ The will belongs always to the one who has the greatest aspect in the 5 **Hylech** <term>Hylech: five specific points in a chart—Sun, Moon, Ascendant, Part of Fortune, and the previous Syzygy—used to determine life and longevity</term> according to their order. ¶ The one among them safer from misfortunes is the one who is more clear from the **infortunes** <note>infortunes: the "malefic" planets, Saturn and Mars</note>. ¶ The most noble of them all is the one in his **exaltation** <term>exaltation: a specific sign where a planet is exceptionally strong</term>, or most firm in his dignities according to his order. ¶ The one of greatest fame among them is he who has the greatest aspect with the fortunes. He who has the least malice among them is he who is most fortunated in his own property. ¶ The most strengthened conductor of his own business is he who has the greatest power in **Jupiter** by dignity or aspect. ¶ The most fortunate in his business is he whom Jupiter fortunates. And if any of the **roots** <note>foundational points in a chart</note> promise any thing, it is completed when its specific property is strengthened.

# Chapter 7: On the hour of taking the Ascendant.

The ancients were in disagreement on this, such that **Hermes** <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary founder of astrology</note> said that the hour for taking the **Ascendant** <term>Ascendant: the sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of the question</term> for a question is the moment of agreement between the seeker and the master, and then the master ought to take the Ascendant. ¶ And the Indians, those of Persia, and those of Babylonia say that questions are posed based on the will of the seeker; they say that the significations of questions change according to the shifting will of the seeker across different hours. ¶ And **Vettius** <note>Vettius Valens, a 2nd-century astrologer</note> says that the Ascendant of a question ought to be taken at the hour when the seeker approaches the master. ¶ And I see clearly that the hour for taking the Ascendant of a question ought to be: when the seeker tells the master that he should take it, and not merely when he approaches him; for if he approaches but does not say that he should take the Ascendant, it is not the Ascendant until he has spoken.

# Chapter 8: How long the signification of a question lasts.

**Ptolemy** <note>Claudius Ptolemy, the famous 2nd-century astronomer</note> says that a question lasts as long as it takes the Sun to circle the heavens once <note>one year</note>. ¶ And Vettius says that a question lasts as long as it takes the **significator** <term>significator: the planet representing the matter at hand</term> of the question to circle the heavens once, and as long as the Lord of the Ascendant can circle the whole heaven once. ¶ And the Indians and those of Persia say that the signification of a question lasts until the question itself changes. ¶ And the ancient wise men say that a question lasts until the significator and all the planets have traveled through all the signs. ¶ And what is to be believed and held as a foundational principle in this reasoning is this: that a question lasts until the matter for which it was asked is completed, or until one loses hope in it, if the question was about whether a thing will or will not be. For example, a question is: "I seek to buy an estate; I ask if the matter will be completed for

<column-break/>

me or not." The judgment of this question lasts until it is either bought or until hope for it is lost. And if the question was about a thing that is durable in the present, that signification lasts until that thing is destroyed, if God wills. For example: a question is such, "I hold an estate and I ask what profit or loss I shall have from it." The judgment of this lasts as long as the estate remains mine.

# Chapter 9: In knowing the **Almuten**—that is, the significator of the question and the seeker.

Know that the **Almuten** <note>original: "almuteç"; the planet with the most dignity or power in a specific location</note> of the seeker—who asks for himself, or for a thing he seeks, or for a matter between himself and another—is the Lord of the Ascendant, if it aspects the Ascendant. And if it is **cadent** <term>cadent: "falling" away from an angle, making the planet weak</term> from the Ascendant, look to the Moon; and if she aspects the Ascendant, take her as the significator of the seeker. And take the Lord of the **seventh house** <term>seventh house: the house of "the other," representing the person or thing asked about</term> as the significator of the person for whom he asks, if it aspects the seventh house. And if it does not aspect it, take the Lord of the Moon's house as the significator. And if the Moon does not aspect the Ascendant, and she has separated from one of the planets and applied to another: take the planet from which she is separating as the significator of the seeker, and the planet to which the Moon applies will be the significator of the person for whom he asks. And if the Lord of the Ascendant is cadent from the Ascendant, and does not aspect it, nor does the Moon likewise; and the Moon has not separated from any planet nor applied to another: take the Moon herself as the significator of the seeker, and the Lord of her house for the significator of the one for whom he asks. And if the Moon in this arrangement is in her own **dignity** <term>dignity: a place in the zodiac where a planet is particularly strong, such as its own sign</term>, take her as the significator of the seeker, and the Lord of the **triplicity** <term>triplicity: a group of three signs belonging to the same element (Fire, Earth, Air, or Water)</term> in which she is as the significator of the person for whom he asks. And if there is a planet that carries the light of the Lord of the Ascendant to the Lord of the seventh, or which connects the Moon and any other of the planets: take that planet as the significator of the person for whom he asks, and the Moon as the significator of the seeker. And assist yourself in [finding] the significator of the seeker from planets that are **peregrine** <term>peregrine: a planet with no special dignity or standing in its current position; a "wanderer"</term> in the Ascendant—that is, those which have no dignity in the Ascendant—and from the Lord of the Ascendant, even if it does not aspect the Ascendant. And similarly, assist yourself in [finding] the significator of the person for whom he asks from the peregrine planets in the seventh house and its Lord, even if it does not aspect it.

## The Almuten according to the opinion of **Al-Kindi**.

Regarding the seeker, the person for whom he asks, and the thing sought: it is the planet that has the most dignities in that house, and the planet that is of the nature of that question, and the **Lot** <note>original: "pars" (Part or Lot), a mathematical point in the chart</note> that signifies the question, and the Lord of the **Hour**. And the significator of the seeker is the planet that has the most dignities in the five **Hylegs** <term>Hyleg: a "giver of life" or a vital point in a chart</term>, which are: the Sun and the Moon; the Ascendant; the **Part of Fortune**; and the place of the **conjunction** <note>New Moon</note> or **opposition** <note>Full Moon</note> preceding the question. The dignities are in this manner: the Lord of the House has 5 dignities; the Lord of **Exaltation** has 4; the Lord of the **Term** has 3; the Lord of the Triplicity has 2; and the Lord of the **Face** <note>Decan</note> has 1. ¶ **Athabari** <note>Abu Bakr al-Hasan ibn al-Khasib, a 9th-century Persian astrologer</note> says that the Almuten significator is the planet that rules in the nature of the question, and the planet that has the most dignities there, such as the Lord of the House, Exaltation, Term, Triplicity, and Face.

And when you know this: first look to the **Lord of the Ascendant** <term>Lord of the Ascendant: the planet that rules the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon</term> and give it prerogative and strength: and if it happens that it has its lordship in the Ascendant where it also has its **exaltation** <term>exaltation: a specific sign where a planet's power is heightened</term> or **term** <term>term: an unequal division of a sign where a specific planet holds power</term> or **triplicity** <term>triplicity: a group of three signs belonging to the same element (Fire, Earth, Air, or Water)</term> or **face**: take it as the **significator** <term>significator: the planet chosen to represent the person or subject of the inquiry</term> and call it the **Almuten** <note>original: "almutez," from the Arabic "al-mubtazz," meaning the winner or the one who prevails through having the most combined dignities</note> and no other significators will have a division or share with it. And know that the angles are the roots of significations and through them their Lords are strengthened and weakened by their **falls** <term>fall: a position in the zodiac where a planet's influence is at its weakest, opposite its exaltation</term>. ¶ The Lord of the house of the Sun by day and the Lord of the house of the Moon by night or the Lord of the hour when they are equal in strength: the significator will be the Lord of the house of the Sun by day: and the Lord of the house of the Moon by night or the Lord of the hour in its hour. And judge by knowing the significator and its motion until you know the signification, whether it belongs to one planet: or two: or more than two. And if you have two planets equal in strength and sharing in the signification and you doubt which of them the signification belongs to: see if one of them is the one to which the Moon **applies** <term>application: when the Moon moves toward a geometric aspect with another planet, indicating the flow of events</term> and she herself is in the Ascendant in her own house: or if it is that planet that is the Lord of the term of the Sun by day: or of the Moon by night: or if it is the Lord of the **Part of Fortune** <term>Part of Fortune: a mathematical point in the chart representing prosperity and well-being</term>: that one will have greater strength than the other: and it will be the Almuten: especially if it is in its **Hayz** <note>original: "haic," a condition where a planet is in a favorable zodiac sign and hemisphere based on its gender and day/night sect</note>. And the Part of Fortune has power in signification in nocturnal questions. Then look to see to whom the significator applies in the sign in which it is: or who applies to it: for applications are according to the quantity of the lights of the planets which are their rays. And the lights of the **malefics** <note>original: "infortunarum," planets like Saturn and Mars considered to have a challenging influence</note> disturb and ruin the questions. And the lights of the **benefics** <note>original: "fortunarum," planets like Jupiter and Venus considered helpful</note> make them agile and hasten them. And if each of them is in the house of its partner and they are equal in their dignities, the one who is firmer in the house is the Almuten. ### Chapter 10. On knowing the Almuten of conjunction and opposition.

The **conjunction** <term>conjunction: when the Sun and Moon are in the same degree, marking a New Moon</term> of the Sun and Moon was in Virgo at 15 degrees and 10 minutes at night after 10 hours, and I looked at the significators of Virgo: I found Mercury to be the Lord of the house and the Lord of the exaltation: and the Moon the lady of the triplicity: because the conjunction was nocturnal: and Venus the lady of the term: and the victor over Virgo and over that degree was Mercury: because he was the Lord of the house and the Lord of the exaltation. ### ¶ Chapter 12. On the ascendant and the questions that are within it.

<image-desc>Decorative drop cap 'H' showing a stylized floral or geometric pattern within a square frame.</image-desc>
This house is the **Eastern Angle** <term>Eastern Angle: the Ascendant, the point of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon</term>, the gate of heaven: signifying the question of the querent which he makes concerning himself; the accidents of his body, and all things he seeks concerning himself. It signifies his nature, his height, and his thickness. It signifies necromancy, incantations, and how long the newborn remains in the mother's womb. It signifies life, nobility, and in which land one is born. It signifies impediments and the escape from them, and the things that happen. It signifies to what rank one shall ascend. Likewise, it signifies creation, birth, maintenance, and one's accidents. It signifies strong things, increasing things, and additions in deeds. It signifies the intellect and the change of one's status. It signifies reasoning, the seeking of things, and the significations of things. It signifies delightful and abhorrent things; and it signifies light and brightness, battle and wars; and this house is the **joy of Mercury** <term>joy: a specific house where a planet is said to be particularly comfortable or powerful</term>.

### ¶ Chapter 13. On knowing the life of a man through his question.

If it is in a **common sign** <note>Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces</note>, it will be months. And the lord according to the 4th house, which sets itself apart with strength and signification—that is, whoever is the greater significator in the figure—is the significator of the ends of his affairs, and of his improvements and damages. ### Chapter 14. On knowing the improvements and damages of the body.

When you are asked about the improvement or damage of someone's body, and which of their members will be stronger and more perfect, and which of them will be weaker and worse: know that what is from the **ascendant** <note>the 1st house</note> under the earth until the seventh <note>the 7th house</note> concerns the part of the body from the middle upward. And if you find fortunes in this part, judge that the upper part of his body will be strong, healthy, and perfect for him. And if misfortunes are there, judge the opposite. And from the 7th house back to the ascendant <note>the houses above the horizon</note> concerns the part of the body from the middle downward. And if you find fortunes in this part from the 7th house until the twelfth, judge that the middle of his body below will be strong, healthy, and perfect for him. And if misfortunes are there, judge the opposite. And wherever you find misfortunes, always judge that part to be weaker and worse. And know that the head belongs to **Aries** and the neck to **Taurus**, and so on according to this order until the feet are **Pisces**, just as it is divided in the books of the ancients. ¶ And others say that the head belongs to the ascendant, and the neck to the 2nd house, and so on according to this order until the feet are the 12th house. And according to this, look at which sign the fortunes are in, for there will be health and good; and in which sign the misfortunes are, for there will be damage and evil, and of those things he ought to fear and guard himself. ¶ And I say that we ought to look in this chapter and the other preceding it: when a seeker asks for himself about his body and what will happen to him in what occurs, we ought to look to the **Moon** and the **Almuten** <term>Almuten: the planet with the most dignity or power over a specific point in the chart</term>, and see which of them is stronger, and their **applications** <term>application: the movement of one planet toward another by aspect</term>—the first, second, and third—and how many there will be until it is in that sign in which it resides. And when it moves itself from that sign, it changes that judgment, and that significance is lost. ¶ And know that the **separation** <term>separation: when a planet moves away from an aspect with another, representing the past</term> of the Moon signifies that which was of the seeker before the question, and its application signifies that which will be of him after the question. And when the Moon moves from a **cadent** <term>cadent: houses that "fall away" from the angles, often considered weak</term> house and applies to another planet that is likewise falling from an **angle** <term>angle: the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, which are the most powerful positions</term>, that significance will be bad and damaging; because a fortune, when it is unfortunate, weakens itself and diminishes its good and profit. And when it is strong, it confirms that which it signifies of good

<column-break/>

and profit and strengthens it. And in this manner judge concerning the misfortunes. And do not look to what the books say—that misfortunes are worse when they are cadent from the angles. Rather, when misfortunes are firm in the angles and strong, then they are worse; because they are not falling, they are like a weak sick person who cannot move himself, nor likewise help himself by himself. And I say that in questions there are the **Hylech** and **Alchocoden** <term>Hylech and Alchocoden: technical points used to determine the length of life and the "giver of years"</term> just as they are in births <note>meaning in natal horoscopes</note>.

### Chapter 15. Concerning one who wants to go to another, whether he will find him.

When someone wishes to go to another and asks you if he will find him, look to the lord of the 7th house: if you find him in the angles, say that the man is in his own place. And if you find him in the **succedent** <term>succedent: houses 2, 5, 8, and 11, which follow the powerful angles</term> houses, say that he is near his place. And look if you find any application between the lord of the ascendant and the lord of the 7th house, or any planet beholding the 7th house and carrying the light from one to the other, or that those two luminaries are joined. And if you find this, judge that he will find him; and if not, no.

### Chapter 16. On sitting in the house and the parts of the planets.

When you wish to place yourself in your house to sit, always sit in the parts of the fortunes. And if someone comes who pleases you, place him with you in that part, or in the part of another fortune. And know that from the point of the **Midheaven** <note>the highest point of the chart</note> until the point of the East belongs to **Venus**; and that same point of the East belongs to the **Sun**; and from the point of the East until the point of the North, which is the angle of the earth <note>the IC or 4th house cusp</note>, belongs to **Jupiter**; and that same point of the North belongs to **Mercury**. And from the point of the North until the point of the West belongs to the **Moon**; and that same point of the West belongs to **Saturn**. And from the point of the West until the point of the Midheaven belongs to the **Head of the Dragon** <term>Head of the Dragon: the North Node of the Moon, traditionally considered lucky</term>; and that same point of the Midheaven belongs to **Mars**. ¶ And similarly, when you enter someone's house, look at the lord of the house, in which of the parts you find him sitting. If you find him sitting in the part of the fortunes, sit with him in that part, or in the part of another fortune. And if you find him sitting in the section of Saturn, sit in the part of the fortunes. And if you find him sitting in the part of Mars, do not sit in that house, but hasten to return; and it will be better for you than sitting in that house.

### ¶ Chapter 24. Regarding the 2nd house and its questions.

<image-desc>Ornamental drop cap 'S' with floral motifs in a square frame.</image-desc>
Know that the second house signifies things taken up, governed, and valued: substance <note>In medieval astrology, "substance" is the standard term for personal wealth, money, and movable property.</note>, lawsuits involving women, and the inheritance of women when they die; also giving or receiving loans, partnerships, silver, and writing wills at the time of death. It concerns things that will happen in the future, the sharing of goods, and special advantages in questions. It also signifies infidelity, betrayal, and the envy of friends; chests, cupboards, and places where things are stored and keys kept; the education of sons, inheritances, profits, a king’s charter that comes with a mandate, and the entering of a city. This house follows the angle of the ascendant <note>This means it is a "succedent" house, following the 1st house (the Eastern horizon) as the Earth rotates.</note>. 

¶ And if in a question there is a Fire sign in this house, and the "thought of the querent" <note>A technical calculation used to determine what is on the mind of the person asking the question.</note> is within it, judge that the question is about wealth. If it is an Earth sign, say it is about entering a city. If it is an Air sign, say it is about silver. If it is a Water sign, say it is about food and profits. 

¶ The first lord of the triplicity <note>A group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element (Fire, Earth, Air, or Water). This is the case if Cancer or Leo is in the second house. If it is the house of Saturn, it will be from sowing crops. Judge in this way for the other houses of the other planets according to their associations. 

¶ The color of this house is green mixed with vermilion.

¶ And if the lord of the house of wealth applies to the lord of the house in which the Part of Fortune <note>A calculated point in a chart representing luck and prosperity.</note> is located, and that the lord of the Part of Fortune is in such a state as with the lord of the house of wealth—especially if the Moon looks at the Part of Fortune—judge similarly that he will have that wealth. And if the lord of the ascendant does not apply to the lord of the Part of Fortune, but the state of the lord of the ascendant and the lord of the part of substance from the luminaries is as we said of the others: judge similarly that he will have the wealth. This is stronger if Jupiter is looking at the lord of the ascendant or the ascendant itself, or if the significator of wealth is any of those three we mentioned. 

The strongest position that Jupiter has regarding wealth is to be in the 2nd house with the lord of the ascendant, and the significator of wealth in the ascendant, or in the 11th house, or in the 10th, or in any of the other angles. However, if it is in the ascendant, he will enter into wealth with his own person. If it is in the 2nd house, he will enter it through his silver and with the income from his rents. If it is in the 10th house, he will have it from the king and his

counts. And if it is in the 11th, he will have it from the king's friends and from things in which he has trust. And if it is in the 8th house, he will have it from the side of marriages, and through the good inheritance of the dead, and by their wills and for their sake. And if it is in the 4th, he will have it from ancient things and inheritances, and from plowing and things hidden by his fathers. And if he is helping, it is through gifts and similar things.
