### ¶ Chapter 25. At what time riches will be gained.

<image-desc>Ornamental drop cap 'I' with floral motifs in a square frame.</image-desc>
**I**n this matter, you should place the time of the applications between the lord of the ascendant and the significator of wealth: as days, or months, or years, according to what pertains to the signs in which they are located. Nevertheless, the stability and increase of wealth will be through the application of the lord of the ascendant with a fortune <note>A "benefic" or lucky planet, like Jupiter or Venus.</note> in an angle. And similarly for the lord of wealth. 

And if the significators of wealth are applying to the lord of the ascendant, the same will happen easily, without labor, and without searching. And if the lord of the ascendant is applying to the significators, it will be by seeking and searching. And if the application occurs while the lord of the ascendant is retrograde <note>Appearing to move backward in the sky, usually indicating delays or reversals.</note>, it will be by a fortuitous accident. And if the significators are retrograde while signifying that it will happen, there will be complications in obtaining it. And if they are unfortunate <note>Afflicted by a malefic planet.</note>, they will show disturbance and lessening according to the nature of the infortune and the house in which the infortune is located, according to the aspect <note>The geometric angle between two planets.</note> it has with the significators. 

¶ And if the wealth sought is from a known man or a known city: give the ascendant to the querent and the seventh house to the one from whom he seeks or to the city. And if the lord of the house of wealth applies to the ascendant, or to the lord of the ascendant, or to the lord of the 2nd house of the lord of the ascendant, or the Part of Fortune is in the 2nd house, or the Part of Wealth is with the lord of the ascendant, or with the lord of the 2nd, or the lords of the ascendant and the lords of the Part of Wealth are with the Part of Fortune, and there are fortunes testifying as we said in the previous chapter: he will have it.

...that substance. And if it is different from this, judge the opposite. And the causes and reasons by which he will possess it: judge thus by the lords if God wills. And if someone asks you about substance—whether he will have it or attain it or not—look at the lord of the ascendant: if it is applying to the lord of the house of substance <note>The 2nd house of the zodiac.</note>, or if the lord of the house of substance is applying to the lord of the ascendant, he will possess that substance and it will come into his power. ### Chapter 26. On seeking gifts.

When someone asks you about a gift, whether he will have it soon or late: look at the ascendant and its lord, and the Part of Fortune and its lord. And if the lord of the ascendant is in a "fortune" <note>A "fortune" or benefic planet, like Jupiter or Venus.</note> or a "fortunate fortune," and the lord of the Part of Fortune is a "fortune," and both are looking at the Moon: look at what state the Moon is in with both of them and which of them it "aspects" <note>An aspect is a specific geometric angle between planets that determines their relationship.</note> more favorably and closely. Judge by this that the gift can be attained, provided a "malefic" <note>original: "infortuna"; a planet like Saturn or Mars.</note> does not diminish or impede it according to its place and strength. Judge as I have told you, and you will find the truth if God wills.

### Chapter 27. On the 3rd house and its questions.

This house is the indicator of brothers and short journeys and the taking up of matters. It holds the joys and dangers of brothers and their status, whether good or bad. It signifies friends, blood relatives, sisters, kinsmen, dreams, law, knowledge of the law, purities, and the status of sisters and friends. It also signifies dances, the mistresses of women, moving from one place to another, consideration, intellect, nobility, obedience and service to God, synagogues of the Jews, and the destructions of Christians and their churches. In this house is the "joy" of the Moon <note>In traditional astrology, each planet is said to "joy" or perform especially well in a specific house.</note>.

### Chapter 28. On inquiring about a brother and questions related to him.

When someone asks you about his brother: look at the third sign from the ascendant, which is the house of brothers, and the lord of its triplicity <note>A group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element (Fire, Earth, Air, or Water).</note>, and the Almuten <term>Almuten: the planet that holds the most power or "dignity" in a specific degree of the zodiac.</term> of that house. Look at whether fortunes or malefics aspect it and where it is located. For if you find the lord of the 3rd house in the 6th, or applying to the lord of the 6th—or if the lord of the 6th is in the 3rd, 5th, or 11th—say that his brother is sick. And if you find him in the 5th or 11th, say that his brother is not in his own place but has gone to another location. And if you find the Almuten of the 3rd house afflicted or in the 12th house, say that his brother is in anxiety and infirmity. And if you find the lord of the 3rd with Mars, both joined and "combust" <term>Combust: a planet is combust when it is so close to the Sun that its power is "burned up" or hidden.</term> under the rays of the sun: judge that he will not escape from his illness. And if both are combust, judge his death by all means—especially if the lord of the triplicity of the 3rd house is afflicted or combust like the others. And judge in this way for all his qualities through the houses and aspects, just as 

<column-break/>

we have said in the other chapter. ¶ And similarly, look in this way if you are asked about any matter regarding the nature of any other thing belonging to the houses of heaven, such as parents, children, servants, women, the king, fugitives, and enemies. Look for them just as you have looked in this chapter. From this you will find in nativities <note>A "nativity" is a birth chart.</note> the aspect of fortunes and malefics in the place where the question is, or from their aspects to the lord of that place: whether it brings health, sickness, or impediment. It is the nature of fortunes to share the celestial natures of the planets with the natures of the houses. Thus, if the question is about parents, the Sun will be a participant; if about mothers, the Moon; if about women, Venus; if about children, Jupiter; if about servants, Mercury. These have significations along with the Almutens of the houses, representing matters by the good pleasure of God.

### Chapter 29. On knowing if the advice of one who comes to consult you is honest or not.

<margin>Note</margin>
If someone comes to consult you and you wish to know if he is honest or a deceiver: look if there is a "fortune" in the Midheaven <note>The 10th house, the highest point in the chart.</note>. If so, his advice is honest and true. But if a malefic is there, he is a deceiver and a liar. And I say that if a counselor comes to you and the ascendant is one of the "common" signs <note>original: "signis coibus" (communibus); these are Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, and Pisces, known for being changeable.</note>, or the lord of the ascendant and the Moon are in common signs, he is a deceiver and wishes to deceive you; do not listen to him.

### Chapter 30. On knowing whether rumors are true or not.

If you are asked about rumors—whether they are true or false, or whether they bring good or evil—or whether they are based on trust or fear, or if the matter has a "root" <note>A "root" means the rumor has a factual basis or origin.</note> or not, or if it is based on nothing through "avastamentum." *Avastamentum* is when someone sets up another, doing or dragging them into evil, as you understand. Look at the Almuten of the ascendant and the Moon, and see which of them is in an "angle" <term>Angles: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses, considered the most powerful and active areas of a chart.</term>. If neither is in an angle, take whichever of them has more right in the ascendant and begin with that. If the rumors are ones the seeker would rejoice in, and you find the Almuten of the ascendant and the Moon and the lord of the house of the Moon in angles or "succedent" houses <note>The houses following the angles: the 2nd, 5th, 8th, and 11th.</note>, aided by fortunes and clear of malefics and damaging planets (which are the lords of the 6th and 12th in their places), then judge that the rumors are true and very good. But if you find the opposite, judge them to be false and bad. ¶ Rumors will likewise be true when fixed signs <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, and Aquarius, which represent stability.</note> are in the angles, and Mercury and the Moon are in fixed signs, separating themselves from malefics; and if a fortune is in any of the angles, rumors that are bad will be true and will be verified. If the two angles—the 10th and 4th—are fixed signs and the Moon is "received" <note>Reception occurs when a planet is in a sign governed by another planet that aspects it.</note>, those rumors will be verified in some part. And if the rumors are bad, but a fortune is in the ascendant and the Moon is fortunate, it signifies the destruction of those rumors and that they will turn into good. The retrograde motion of Mercury, or the planet to which Mercury applies, or the one to which the Moon applies—especially if it is the lord of the ascendant—signifies the destruction of rumors and that they will turn into good. ¶ The saying of Al-Kindi <note>Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Ishaq al-Kindi (c. 801–873 AD), a famous Arab philosopher and astrologer known in the West as Alkindus.</note> regarding rumors:

When you wish to know the verification of good rumors: look if there are fixed signs in the angles, and the Moon is in a fixed sign and received, and the ascendant and Moon are made fortunate by fortunes. Judge that those rumors are true by the power of God. But if the rumors are good and the angles are "movable" signs <note>original: "signa mobilia"; also called cardinal signs (Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn), which indicate change.</note>, and the lord of the ascendant and the Moon are in movable signs...

### ¶ Chapter 31: On the Fourth House and its questions

<image-desc>Decorative initial H featuring intricate foliage patterns within a square border.</image-desc>This house is the significator of fathers, the angle of the earth, the significator of the ends of things, of inheritances, of sowing, of fields, of things hidden and covered, and concealed; and it signifies the form of the thing in which a person is born. It signifies the work of buildings, the elements, and the roots of things. And that which shall be after death. It signifies the inheritance of the goods of fathers and mothers. And it signifies castles and houses and ancient years. It signifies uncles, and the diversity of places, and that which happens of good or evil in the world, and precious stones. It signifies the nature of women (that is, the womb), and the place where a theft is located. And it signifies the places where children are cared for, and treasures.

### ¶ Chapter 32: On a question regarding cultivated land or a house of inheritance, whether one will have it or not:

<image-desc>Decorative initial C featuring intricate foliage and floral patterns within a square border.</image-desc>When you are asked about cultivated land or a house or an inheritance which someone seeks, whether they shall have it or not: give the ascendant and its lord and the planet from which the moon is separating to the seeker or the buyer; and give the seventh house and its lord and the planet to which the moon is applying to the one from whom it is sought, or the seller. And give the fourth house and its lord and the planet that is in it and the moon to the thing being bought; and give the Midheaven <note>original: "mediū celi"; the 10th house, representing the peak of the sky.</note> to the price. Afterward, if you find the lord of the ascendant

<column-break/>

looking at the lord <note>of the fourth house</note>, and the lord of the house applying to the lord of the ascendant: say that the seller has a great desire to sell. And see if between the lord of the ascendant and the lord of the house there is any application, or "translation of light" <note>When a faster planet moves from an aspect with one planet to an aspect with another, "carrying" the influence between them.</note>, or bodily conjunction: say that the sale will take place between them. And if none of these is there: the matter will be prolonged and the sale will not happen. And if there is an "application" <note>An approaching aspect between two planets.</note>, and the translation of light is from the fourth or the opposite <note>Referring to a square (90°) or opposition (180°) aspect.</note>: the matter will happen, yet with labor and various words passing between them. And if it is from the third or "fertile" <note>Likely referring to a sextile (60°) or trine (120°) aspect.</note> aspect: it will be easy. And if there is "reception" <note>When two planets are in each other's signs of dignity, facilitating cooperation.</note> between them: the sale will be with the good will of the buyer and the seller. And afterward, look to see if the lord of the ascendant or the moon applies to the lord of the fourth; or if the lord of the fourth or the moon applies to the lord of the ascendant. And if only the lord of the fourth house applies to the lord of the ascendant, and he receives him, or receives both if both apply to him; or if the lord of the ascendant and the moon are in the fourth house, and the lord of the fourth is in the ascendant: this signifies that the inheritance will be bought, and that he shall have it. And if this is not so, and the moon carries the light of one of them to the other: it signifies that the matter may happen, yet through mediators and the hands of messengers. And if no application is found, nor translation of light, nor a planet that joins their lights: it signifies that the matter will not be, and he shall not buy nor have that inheritance. ¶ And if you wish to know the state of that inheritance, whether it will be populated or depopulated: look if you find in the fourth house malefics that are powerful or "peregrine" <note>A planet in a sign where it has no essential dignity, like a wanderer in a strange land.</note>: it signifies that the inheritance which he buys will be depopulated and ruined. And the lord of the fourth house signifies the same if it is retrograde or unfortunate, or in its "fall" <note>The sign where a planet's influence is most weakened.</note> from its house or exaltation. And if benefics are in the fourth house, even if peregrine, provided they are strong: it signifies that the inheritance will be populated and improved, and it is good for those inheritances and houses. And assist yourself with the "Part of Inheritance." And you take this Part by day from the degree of the lord of the fourth house to the degree of Saturn. And if Saturn is the lord of the degree of the fourth house, take it from the degree of the fourth house to the degree of Saturn. And by night, work conversely and project it from the degree of the fourth house. And this Part, according to the opinion of Hermes <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary founder of hermetic and astrological wisdom.</note>, is taken by day and night from the degree of Saturn to the degree of the moon, projecting it from the degree of the ascendant. And if this Part and its lord apply to the lord of the seventh, and he receives them: the sale will be completed. And if the degree of the Part and the degree of its lord are unfortunate: it signifies depopulation and damage to that inheritance. And if the Part of the thing and its lord are fortunate: it signifies the population of that inheritance. ¶ And if it is cultivated land, and you wish to know what kind it is: set the ascendant as the significator of the laborers and those working in it; and the fourth house as the significator of the type of land and its form. And the Midheaven as the significator of that which is in it of trees and plants that are smaller than trees. And the Midheaven <note>The text repeats "mediū celi" for both plants and fruit-bearing trees.</note> as the significator of that which is in it of trees and fruits. Afterward, look if you find in the ascendant a malefic: say that the laborers are thieves and not faithful. And if there is a benefic in the ascendant: say that the laborers are faithful and just. And if the benefic existing in the ascendant is "direct" <note>Moving forward in the zodiac.</note>: those laborers will remain in the inheritance. And if it is retrograde: say that they will move from there. And if the malefic which is in the ascendant is direct: they will remain in the land while stealing. And if it is retrograde: they will flee from it.

¶ And if you find a benefic <note>original: "fortuna"; a helpful planet like Jupiter or Venus.</note> in the **Midheaven** <note>original: "medio celi"; the 10th house, representing the highest point in the sky and the visible status of the property.</note> moving in direct motion: say that its trees are good and many. ### Chapter 33. On knowing the price of an estate:

<image-desc>Ornamental drop cap 'C' with floral motifs in a square frame.</image-desc>
When you wish to know how great the price of an estate is: look to the Lord of the Midheaven and the planet that is powerful in it: and take the stronger of these as the **significator** <note>The planet chosen to represent the specific matter being asked about.</note>: and this is "power"—that it be oriental and direct in its own **house** <note>The zodiac sign it naturally rules.</note> or **exaltation** <note>The sign where the planet is most harmoniously "uplifted."</note> or triplicity: and if a planet is found so, and you have it as the significator: take its **minor years** <note>A specific number of years assigned to each planet in ancient astrology (e.g., Saturn is 30, Jupiter is 12).</note>. And if that significator is in its own house: say that number of its minor years represents hundreds or thousands. And if it is in another of its **dignities** <note>A position of strength, such as triplicity or term.</note>, set the number as tens or units. And if the Lord of the Midheaven is not in any of its dignities and is in some **affliction** <note>original: "dānamento"; a position that weakens the planet, such as being in its fall or detriment.</note>, leave it be and do not look at it. And look for this from the planet that is "propped up" <note>original: "appodeat⁹"; perhaps meaning situated or supported.</note> in the Midheaven. And if there is no powerful planet in the Midheaven: take the Lord of the Midheaven, even if it be **cadent** <note>Falling away from an angle; a weak position.</note> from an angle or otherwise unfortunate, or retrograde, or **combust** <note>Too close to the sun, which "burns" up the planet's power.</note>: and take its minor years, setting them as the price of the estate in units: and you will find it, by the good pleasure of God.

### Chapter 34. On knowing if he will have profit from the estate or not.

<column-break/>

<image-desc>Ornamental drop cap 'S' with floral motifs in a square frame.</image-desc>
If you wish to know if the buyer will have profit from this estate or not: look at the **aspects** <note>The geometric angles between planets.</note> of the significators one with another. And if all of them apply to one another by **trine** <note>120 degrees; a very favorable aspect.</note> or **sextile** <note>60 degrees; a helpful aspect.</note>, or most of them: and if there is **reception** <note>When two planets are in each other's dignities, indicating mutual agreement or cooperation.</note> between them: it signifies that he will have the estate with respect to itself <note>Likely meaning he will gain the property as desired.</note>. And likewise look if the lord of the **fourth house** <note>The house of land and buildings.</note> applies to the lord of the **Ascendant** <note>The planet representing the buyer.</note> by trine or sextile: and if it be clear and fortunate: it signifies that he will have profit from it. And if this is not so, and the aspect of the lord of the 4th with the lord of the Ascendant—and the other aspects of the other significators with the lord of the Ascendant, or most of them—be by **square** <note>original: "quarta"; 90 degrees, indicating tension or difficulty.</note> or **opposition** <note>180 degrees; indicating conflict.</note> or bodily **conjunction** <note>Occupying the same degree.</note>: it signifies that the profit he will have from it will be with labor and pain. And with this, if there is reception between them, it will be with less labor. And assist yourself in this matter of profit with the **Part of Fortune** <note>A calculated point in a chart representing prosperity.</note> and its lord: and take them as significators. And if they are fortunate: it signifies profit from that estate. And if you find **Saturn** in any of its dignities, free from Mars and fortunate by the aspect of a friendly **Jupiter** or from an angle: and the **Moon** increasing in light aspecting Jupiter or Saturn: especially so if the Moon is in any of its dignities or in the Midheaven: this signifies the populating of the land and its fertility, by the good pleasure of God.

### Chapter 35. On knowing at what time estates ought to be bought.

<image-desc>Ornamental drop cap 'C' with floral motifs in a square frame.</image-desc>
When you wish to know the time for buying an estate: look at the application of the lord of the Ascendant with the lord of the **seventh** <note>The house of the seller.</note> by square or opposition or bodily conjunction: and if reception is found between them, at the hour that they aspect each other degree by degree, the purchase will be with labor. And if you wish to know when the estate will enter into his power: look in this for the application of the lord of the Ascendant with the lord of the fourth house: and project the time from that aspect, just as we have told you: and you will find it, God granting. ¶ **Vettius** <note>original: "Uuelli⁹"; likely referring to Vettius Valens, a famous 2nd-century astrologer.</note> disagrees in this which we have said about estates, and says: Take the Ascendant and its lord as the significators of the land and what is in it: and Jupiter and the planet from which the Moon separates as the significators of the buyer. And the fourth [house] and its lord as the significators of the inhabitants or those working it: and the planet to which the Moon applies as the significator of the end and of that which will become of that land: and look which of those significators is powerful and safe from misfortunes: for by it the signification is improved: and it signifies direction and goodness in that for which you took it as significator. And that which among them is afflicted and unfortunate ruins its signification and ruins that thing for which you took it as significator.

### Chapter 36. On leasing estates and working them and renting houses.

<image-desc>Ornamental drop cap 'S' with floral motifs in a square frame.</image-desc>
Take the significator from the one who leases or rents, which is the lord of the estate from the 7th house and the place of the Midheaven: and the end of the matter from the 4th house. And afterward, look if you find a benefic in the Ascendant: say that he who receives the estate for rent is reliable and agreeable and good, and wishes to do well. Know that the **Ascendant** <note>The zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon; it represents the beginning of any project.</note> is the significator of the beginning of growing things <note>original: "vegetabiliū."</note>, and the **Fourth House** is the significatrix of its end. And if you are asked about a plant or seed that is sown, whether it will grow or not, or what will become of it: take for this the Ascendant and its Lord, and the Moon and her Lord. And if all these are fortunate: judge that the thing will grow and be completed there for good. And if all these are unfortunate or "condemned": judge that it will be ruined. And if two are fortunate and the other two are unfortunate: judge an equality in that matter.

### ¶ Chapter 38. For ditches and waters for irrigation.

When you are asked about **canals** <note>original: "zequijs" (from the Arabic *sāqiya*); irrigation ditches or water-channels.</note>, that is, ditches and waters which someone wants to make flow, and similar things: look here at **Saturn** and the **Moon** alone, and the aspects of the benefics and malefics to them. For if you find Saturn **direct** in its motion and **oriental** <note>Rising before the Sun.</note>, and the Moon in the third, fifth, or eleventh house, and clear of Mars <note>original: "a marte limpidā"; free from the harsh influence of the planet Mars.</note> and fortunate: it signifies the safety of the thing sought, and it will be done easily. This is especially true if the Moon applies to the Lord of her own house and is received by it; or if there is a benefic Ascendant in its latitude and in a **fixed sign** <note>Signs like Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, or Aquarius, which represent stability and endurance.</note>: this is a sign that there will be much water, and that it will be directed and will last. And similarly, if one of the benefics is in the Midheaven, especially **Jupiter**: this entirely signifies the durability of the stream and the canal. And if you find Saturn strong, and that he is in the eleventh house and the Moon is looking at him with a friendly aspect, and the Lord of the Moon's house is in a fixed or common sign—and even more so if the Moon is in any of the **signs of rain**, which are Cancer, Leo, Aquarius, and Pisces <note>Leo is typically a "dry" sign; this may be a scribal error for Scorpio, or part of a specific seasonal system.</note>: for this signifies the flowing of the canals and their improvement and increase. And if you find a malefic in the Midheaven: it signifies that the canal will be broken and ruined, and likewise the stream.

### ¶ Chapter 39. On treasures and things buried underground.

When you are asked about substance or a thing buried underground, concerning what men make, such as necklaces or other things: take the Ascendant and calculate <note>original: "dirige"; to direct or calculate the position precisely.</note> it as finely as you can; and afterward, look at the nature of the seeker's question. And know if he asks for substance which he himself buried and does not know its place; or if he asks for substance which his father buried, or his son, or another whom he knows and the seeker knows that he buried it; or if he asks for a thing buried which he knows is there, but does not know who buried it, nor the place. Or if he asks for a buried thing without specifying anything: afterward, if he specifies it to you, give the Ascendant to the seeker. And if it is a thing which he himself buried and has forgotten the place: look at the Lord of the **Second House** <note>The house of personal wealth and possessions.</note> from the Ascendant. And if his brother buried it: look at the Lord of the **Fourth House** <note>The 2nd house relative to the 3rd house of brothers (3+1=4).</note> for that which is the lord of his brother’s substance. And if his father buried it: look at the lord of the substance from the father's house <note>The 5th house, being the 2nd house of possessions relative to the 4th house of the father.</note>. And thus, following this way and order for whoever the burier might be: look at the Lord of the House of substance which is the second from the house where the significator is; and look at what kind of place it is in. And if you find it in any of the **angles** of the Ascendant, or in any of the angles of the Lord of the Ascendant: say that the buried thing is in the house. And if it is in the Ascendant, or in the sign of the Lord of the Ascendant: say that the buried thing is in the main hall <note>original: "palatio"; a large room or chamber.</note> where he lives. And if it is in the Midheaven from the Ascendant, or in the tenth [house] of the Lord of the Ascendant: say that it is in the house where he occupies himself with his crafts and business <note>original: "magisteria sua & factiones."</note>. And if it is in the **Seventh House** from the Ascendant, or in the seventh of the Lord of the Ascendant: say it is in the chamber of his wife. And if it is in the **Fourth House** from the Ascendant, or in the fourth of the Lord of the Ascendant: say it is in the chamber where his father or grandfather stays, or his relatives who are older than he. And if there are no relatives: say it is in the middle of his house. And afterward, look at the **application** <note>The movement of a faster planet toward an aspect with a slower one.</note> of the Moon and the Lord of the Ascendant with the aforementioned significator. And if there is any **reception** <note>A harmonious relationship where one planet is in a sign ruled by the other.</note> between them: see if it is from friendship or enmity; for from this aspect and reception, you will know if he will have what he seeks, or not. And if the reception itself is from love: say that he will have it easily. And if it is from enmity: say he will have it with labor and pain. And if reception does not occur, but there is a **translation of light** <note>When a fast planet moves from an aspect with one planet to an aspect with another, "carrying" the influence between them.</note> or a **collection**, he will have it. And if neither an aspect, nor translation, nor collection occurs: say that he will not have that thing which he seeks. ¶ And if the question is for a buried thing not known if it is there or not, and it is not known, nor was a limit set, nor anything else about it: if you want to know if it is buried there or not, it will be known in this way. Look at the Lord of the Ascendant: if it is in an angle, or if a benefic is in an angle: say that it is there. ¶ And the ancients say, as does **Masha'allah** <note>original: "messe hala"; Masha'allah ibn Athari (c. 740–815), a Persian Jewish astrologer and astronomer.</note>: look at the Lord of the **Seventh** from the Ascendant; and if a benefic is there, the buried thing is there. And if a malefic is there and the question is about an image or buried papers <note>original: "cartis"; charters or documents.</note>: it is the truth; and if not, it is not the truth. And if the question was for buried wealth, and a malefic is in the seventh: that which was buried there has been taken out and moved elsewhere. ¶ And **Al-Kindi** <note>original: "irechindus"; likely Al-Kindi (c. 801–873), known as the "Philosopher of the Arabs."</note> says: Look nine degrees before the degree of the Ascendant; if there is any planet in that term, and if it is a benefic and is in that ninth degree: say [it is there]...

### On knowing of what nature the buried thing is.

When you know that a thing is buried in a place and you wish to know its nature: look to the planet that is the **significator** <note>The planet representing the object of the search.</note>, because the buried thing is there; and see if it is the **Almuten** <note>original: "almutęz"; the planet holding the most mathematical power or "ruling" a specific house.</note> of the seventh house. Know the nature of that planet if it is the Almuten of that house. And if it is not the Almuten of the seventh house: join it with the Lord of the seventh house, and see if there is any participation between them, and take the combined nature of both. And if none of these are found, the Lord of the house itself is the significator.

If the significator of this is the **Sun**: and it is in its own house or its **exaltation** <note>A sign where a planet's influence is especially strengthened.</note>: say that it is gold or bright and precious red stones. And if it is not in its house or exaltation: say it is of things that resemble these, such as glass and the like.

If the significatrix is the **Moon** existing in her house or exaltation: say that it is silver or crystal, or a precious white thing.

If **Mars** is the significator existing in any of his houses: say it is copper, or Syrian glass, or things like them.

If **Saturn** is the significator existing in any of his houses: say it is something black, or a black stone, or iron, or the powder called **antimony** <note>original: "coliriū"; used historically as eye makeup or medicine.</note>, or what resembles it.

If **Jupiter** is the significator existing in any of his houses: say it is silver or white cloths, or white **jargoons** <note>original: "iarganzie"; a type of pale or colorless zircon gem.</note>, or the like.

If **Venus** is the significatrix existing in any of her houses: say it is **pearls** <note>original: "aliofar"; from the Arabic term for seed pearls.</note> and coral, or things drawn from the sea, or similar to these.

If **Mercury** is the significator existing in any of his houses: say it is **quicksilver** <note>Mercury in its liquid metal form.</note>, or books, or leather, or the like. And if these planets are not in their own houses, mix the nature of the one who is the significator with the planet to which it **applies** <note>An astrological aspect where a faster planet moves toward a specific angle with a slower one.</note>, or which applies to it, and judge according to that. And if in this signification there is a mixture of Saturn with Mercury—or if one is in the house of the other and vice-versa—and one of them is the significator of the buried thing: say it is a work of **necromancy** <note>original: "nigromantie"; here implying "black magic" or dark rituals.</note> or something similar. And it is the same if there is a conjunction of Mercury with the **Dragon’s Tail** <note>original: "cauda"; the South Node of the Moon, often considered a point of depletion or "drainage."</note>.

### On knowing if the seeker will have the buried thing.

Look here to see if the planet that is the significator of the buried thing applies to the Lord of the **Ascendant** <note>The 1st House, representing the person asking the question.</note>, or if the Lord of the Ascendant applies to it; or if there is a **translation** or **collection of light** <note>Astrological conditions where a third planet moves light between two others, acting as a bridge.</note>: say that the seeker will have the buried thing. And if that aspect, or translation, or collection is from a **square** or **opposition** <note>Difficult aspects of 90 or 180 degrees.</note>: it will be with pain and labor. And if it is a physical conjunction, or from a **trine** or **sextile** <note>Harmonious aspects of 120 or 60 degrees.</note>: say that he will have that thing easily. And so if any of the **luminaries** <note>The Sun or the Moon.</note> aspects the Ascendant, or is in the Ascendant by itself: it signifies ease for the one having that thing, and that

it will be soon. And if they are **cadent** <note>In the 3rd, 6th, 9th, or 12th houses, which are considered weak or "falling away."</note> from an angle and do not aspect the Ascendant: it signifies labor and pain in obtaining the thing.

I likewise say that when the **Part of Fortune** <note>original: "pars fortune"; a calculated point in a chart representing luck and material success.</note> and its Lord are in the Ascendant or aspect it, or any of the luminaries, or the Lord of the Ascendant: this signifies the certainty of having the thing, and quickly. ### On knowing the place of the buried thing and extracting its location.

When you wish to know the location of a buried thing: look to the planet signifying what the buried thing is, and in what sign and in what **quarter** of the quarters of heaven it is. And say that the buried thing is in that part of the house or place: so that if it is in the Ascendant or in the Eastern quarter: say it is in the Eastern quarter of the house. And if it is in the **Midheaven** or the Southern quarter: it is in the Southern part of the house. And if it is in the West or the Western quarter: it is in the Western part of the house. And if it is in the **Angle of the Earth** <note>The 4th House, representing the ground and foundations.</note> or the Northern quarter: say it is in the Northern part of the house or place. 

And with this, look to see if it is in a **fixed sign**: say it is buried in the earth. And if it is in a **common sign**: it is buried in a wall. And if it is in a **movable sign**: say it is in the roof of that quarter which it has reached. 

And if you wish to know its specific place, divide the thing or place into four parts; and afterward, measure the quarter in which you judged the thing to be (whether in the earth, wall, or roof) and know how many parts are in it. Then look at the significator to see how many degrees it has passed in its sign, and in which **face** <note>A 10-degree division of a zodiac sign.</note> it is. Divide that quarter into three parts: and if the significator is in the first face of the sign, it is in the first third of that quarter. If it is in the second face, it will be in the second third. And if it is in the third, it will be in the third of that quarter. Afterward, inspect the third which you found and divide it into ten parts; look at how many degrees the planet has passed from that face in which it is, and take from those parts of that third as many quarters, and they shall be degrees; and in that place where the number ends is the buried thing, in that third of the quarter where you found it.

And if a benefic is made unfortunate by a strong malefic: the buried thing was ruined, and it has been taken away and raised from that place. But if the benefic is fortunate: the thing is in that place. ### ¶ Chapter 40: On the Fifth House and its questions.

This house is the significator of sons and daughters, of profits and returns, and of inheriting the goods of good women. It signifies gifts, joys, and messengers; it signifies the disposing of the property of those who have passed from life, and the possessing of the treasures of paternal uncles. It signifies gifts given for the sake of helping with banquets and drinks. It signifies that which will happen to a person after their death, whether good or evil, and it signifies what one leaves behind in inheritance, and whether what they lease will remain with them or not. It signifies bread and its market price in cities, and the status of the people of cities in the revolutions of the years of the world. It signifies the returns from inheritances; it signifies the conception of women; it signifies reasoning, lying with women, and having friendship and love with them. It signifies refined and fragrant things, and the love of friends.

The first lord of its **triplicity** <note>term: "triplicity"; a group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element.</note> signifies children; the second is the significator of merchandise; and the third signifies legacies, messengers, and the strength or weakness of lying with women. And if it happens in questions of this house that there is a significator of thoughts, and a **fiery sign** <note>A sign like Aries, Leo, or Sagittarius.</note> is in it, it signifies an embassy. And if there is an **earthy sign** <note>A sign like Taurus, Virgo, or Capricorn.</note> in it, it signifies vegetable seeds and the returns of inheritances. And if it is an **airy sign** <note>A sign like Gemini, Libra, or Aquarius.</note>, it signifies children. And if it is a **watery sign** <note>A sign like Cancer, Scorpio, or Pisces.</note>, it signifies gifts and drinks. And the color of this house, in whatever sign it may be, is white mixed with black.

¶ And if you are asked on behalf of a son, whether he will have a child or not: look at the application of the **Lord of the Ascendant** <note>The planet ruling the first house, representing the seeker.</note> and the Moon with the Lord of the **House of Children** <note>The Fifth House.</note>. And if an application occurs, and that planet to which it applies (which is the Lord of the House of Children) is free from **malefics** <note>original: "infortunis"; difficult planetary influences.</note> and **combustion** <note>term: "combustion"; being too close to the Sun, which weakens a planet's power.</note>, it signifies that he will have a child. And similarly, if you find the Lord of the House of Children in the Ascendant, or the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon in the House of Children, it is a great and true sign of having children. And if neither the Lord of the Ascendant nor the Moon applies to the Lord of the Fifth House, but there is a returning of light from one to the other between them, or a **translation** or **collection** <note>Technical astrological terms for when a third planet connects two planets that do not aspect each other directly.</note>, it signifies that he will have children, though late. Afterward, look to the receiver of the disposition; if it is safe from malefics, combustion, **retrogradation** <note>When a planet appears to move backward in the sky.</note>, and falling from the angles, it signifies that it will be fulfilled. And if the planet from which the Moon separates is the Lord of the fifth sign from the place of the planet to which the Moon applies, and both planets aspect each other, it signifies he will have a child. And if they do not aspect each other, no. And if they do not aspect each other, but the planet to which the Moon applies is powerful in an angle, it signifies he will have a child.

...Jupiter in a favorable position with the lord of the **triplicity** <note>original: "triplicitatis"; a group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element (Fire, Earth, Air, or Water).</note> of the **Ascendant** <note>The sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of the question.</note>: and if it is not **under the rays** <note>original: "sub radijs"; a planet so close to the Sun that its influence is hidden or weakened.</note>: it indicates that he shall have a son, or if it be a woman: that she shall conceive. And if the lord of the Ascendant is in the fourth or seventh house: and Jupiter is in a favorable position: judge that he shall have a son: however, only after a long time from the moment of his question. And if you find the Ascendant afflicted by **malefics** <note>original: "infortunis"; planets like Mars or Saturn that were thought to bring difficulty.</note>: and its lord in an unfavorable place: and Jupiter **cadent** <note>original: "cadentem"; falling away from the powerful "angles" of the chart, thus weakened.</note> from the angles: or under the rays in the house of death: it signifies few children: or that they shall not endure if he should have them. And if the Moon is afflicted in the house of children or by an aspecting planet: it signifies that he shall quickly have a son. And if there is a malefic in the house of children: or if they aspect it: it signifies that he shall not have children. And if with this you find other testimonies signifying the having of children: judge that he shall have children: yet he shall see them dying. And if you find Jupiter in the eastern angle: it signifies that he shall quickly have a son. And if it is in the western angle: and the lord of the Ascendant is in a favorable place: it signifies that he shall have a son: yet late and after a long time from the question.

### ¶ Chapter 42. For a woman, whether she is pregnant or not.

If you are asked regarding a woman whether she is pregnant or not: **Mash'allah** <note>original: "messehallah"; a famous 8th-century Persian Jewish astrologer and astronomer.</note> says this: when you are asked regarding a woman if she is pregnant or not: and whether she will complete the pregnancy itself: or not. Look to see if you find both the lord of the Ascendant and the Moon in the house of children: or if you find the lord of the house of children in the Ascendant, clear of malefics and **direct** <note>original: "directum"; moving forward in the zodiac, rather than appearing to move backward (retrograde).</note>: you may say that the woman is pregnant. And if the lord of the Ascendant or the **significator** <note>The planet that represents the person or subject of the question.</note> who is the lord of the house of children has given its power to a planet existing in an angle: say that the pregnancy is true. And if the lord of the Ascendant is **received** <note>original: "receptus"; a technical relationship where one planet is in a sign ruled by another.</note>: and the one receiving it is also received: say likewise that the pregnancy is true. And if the lord of the Ascendant has given its power to a planet cadent from an angle: it signifies that the pregnancy is nothing: or that it will be lost: and especially if the Ascendant is a **moveable sign** <note>original: "signum mobile"; Aries, Cancer, Libra, or Capricorn, which signify change.</note>: or if a malefic is in an angle: and if the Moon has given its power to a malefic so that it has no testimony in the question: these are the signs regarding the loss of the pregnancy. And if the receiver of the Moon's disposition is clear of malefics and **combustion** <note>original: "combustione"; being too close to the sun's heat.</note>: and has testimony in the question: it signifies the truth and safety of the pregnancy. If the Moon is received: or the lord of the Ascendant is in a favorable place having great testimony in the question: it signifies that she is pregnant. If the Moon has given its power to a planet existing in the fifth house: and that same planet has great testimony in the fifth house: it signifies she is pregnant. If the Moon **applies** <note>original: "applicuerit"; moves toward an aspect with another planet.</note> to the lord of the Ascendant: it signifies she is pregnant.

### ¶ Others say.

Look to the lord of the fifth house: if it is in the Ascendant or the tenth house: and is not cadent from its house or **exaltation** <note>A sign where a planet’s influence is particularly strengthened.</note>: say that she is pregnant. And if with this the lord of the house of the Moon bears witness: and is in the Ascendant: or in any of the other angles: verify the pregnancy entirely: and likewise verify it if the lord of the hour

<column-break/>

was in an angle. ¶ And likewise if you are asked whether a tree will bear fruit: or not: or for any weight if it will fall into the water or not. Look into this just as you looked into pregnancy: and in the same manner.

### ¶ Naphail son of Thomas said

Look to the luminaries and the dignities and the places of the **duodenaries** <note>original: "duodenariorum"; a division of a zodiac sign into twelve parts of 2.5 degrees each.</note> in which they are in the Ascendant. And if they are **common signs** <note>original: "signa coia"; Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, or Pisces.</note> or signs of many children and the **benefics** <note>original: "fortune"; helpful planets like Venus or Jupiter.</note> aspect them: or are within them, or if the lords of the aforesaid signs are in common signs or in signs of many children: and the **Part of Fortune** and its lord are in this manner. And look which of these has the greatest testimony in the question. If it is in any of the angles: or in the eleventh house or the fifth: and in any of the aforesaid signs: say that she is pregnant. And if any of the aforementioned planets is in the **midheaven** <note>original: "medio celi"; the highest point of the chart.</note>: and in a good state: she is pregnant. And if a benefic is in an angle safe from malefics: it signifies she is pregnant. ¶ Likewise if Jupiter is safe from the rays and the lords of its triplicity are likewise: and in good places: it signifies she is pregnant. ¶ If Jupiter and the lords of its triplicity are cadent from the angles and under the rays: and the lord of the midheaven likewise: it signifies she is not pregnant. ¶ If the lord of the midheaven: and the Sun are in good places: and the benefics aspect them: it signifies she is pregnant. ¶ If the Moon and the lords of its triplicity are in signs of many children: and in good places: it signifies she is pregnant. ¶ If the two benefics and Mercury are afflicted by the two malefics: it signifies she is not pregnant, especially if the Moon is afflicted with them. ¶ And if the two benefics are in angles: and safe from malefics, it signifies she is pregnant. ¶ When the Moon separates from the point of conjunction or opposition and applies to a malefic: it signifies she is not pregnant. ¶ The **Part of Children** <note>An "Arabic Part" or calculated mathematical point in the chart.</note> is that which you take from Jupiter to Saturn: and project from the Ascendant. ¶ If there is a benefic in its opposition or fourth house: it signifies she is pregnant. And if this Part is void of the fourth and its opposition: and likewise void of planets: it signifies she is not pregnant.

### ¶ Irechindus said.

If the Ascendant is a common sign: or its **Venbahar** <note>original: "venbahar"; likely a technical term for a specific planetary power or period, possibly of Persian or Arabic origin.</note> is at 3 degrees and 20 minutes of the Ascendant in a fixed sign or common sign: it signifies she is pregnant. And if a benefic is in any of the four angles and is not **retrograde** <note>original: "retracta"; moving backward.</note> from the determined bounds: it signifies she is pregnant. And if she is not pregnant then: it signifies she soon will be. And if there is a malefic in any of the angles and in the dignity of the duodenary of the degree of that angle: or in its own Venbahar: it signifies she is not pregnant: and if she were pregnant it would not be completed. ¶ And regarding this other wise men say. Look to the western sign: if any of the seven planets is in it: it signifies she is pregnant. And if no planet is there: she is not pregnant. ¶ And I say that this is not true: unless the question was asked by the woman herself naming herself, then if any planet is in the seventh house <margin>note</margin>: it signifies she is pregnant. And if that planet is Mars: it signifies she is newly pregnant. And if that planet is Saturn: it signifies she has miscarried <note>original: "movit"; literally "moved," often implying the movement or expulsion of the fetus.</note> or will miscarry. And if that planet is Jupiter: it signifies she is pregnant with a male. And if the western sign is the house of Jupiter: and none of the seven planets is there: it signifies she is pregnant with a daughter.

### ¶ Chapter 43. On knowing if the pregnancy will be completed or not.

<meta>This page continues the astrological instructions regarding family and children, moving from the potential to have children to the specifics of pregnancy, childbirth, and the health of the fetus. It relies heavily on the "Lord of the Fifth House" (the house of children) and the positions of the Moon and the "malefics" (Mars and Saturn).</meta>

**When you know she is pregnant** and you wish to know whether the pregnancy will reach full term or not: look to the **Lord of the Fifth House**. <note>The planet that rules the zodiac sign on the cusp of the house of children.</note> If that planet is not **retrograde** <note>appearing to move backward in the sky</note>, nor **afflicted** <note>original: "damnatus"; in a poor astrological state</note>, nor **cadent** <note>falling away from the powerful angles of the chart</note> from its house or its **exaltation** <note>a specific sign where a planet’s power is boosted</note>, and not made unfortunate by any aspect of the **malefics** <note>original: "infortunarum"; difficult planets like Mars or Saturn</note>—whether it is "received" <note>a technical relationship where planets "host" one another</note> or not—the pregnancy will reach completion. But if it is not received, and is unfortunate, or **combust** <note>too close to the Sun and thus weakened</note>, or retrograde, or cadent from its house or exaltation: it signifies that the pregnancy will fail. The Moon and the **Lord of the Hour** <note>the planet ruling the specific hour the question was asked</note> also share in this meaning. If two of these three are safe and one is afflicted: judge that the pregnancy will survive and be completed. If two are afflicted and one is safe: it signifies it will fail. If the Moon or the Lord of the **Ascendant** <note>the sign rising on the horizon</note> applies to a retrograde planet, it signifies the pregnancy will fail. If the Moon is received, or the Lord of the Ascendant is in a good place and fortunate with a great **benefic** <note>original: "fortuna"; a helpful planet like Jupiter or Venus</note>: it signifies the pregnancy will be completed. 

¶ **Nayfel** <note>likely Al-Nayrizi, a Persian mathematician and astrologer</note> says: If the Moon is full and joined to Mars by body or by aspect: it signifies that the fetus will move <note>miscarry</note> and the creature will die a sudden death. Similarly, when Mars aspects Venus while she is in one of his houses—namely, Mars in Scorpio—it signifies it will move. And if you find a malefic in the tenth house from the position of Venus, elevated above her, and Mars if he aspects her from an **angle** <note>one of the four most powerful points in a chart</note>: it signifies the pregnancy will fail through the woman's own fault. If the **Lot of Fortune** <note>original: "pars fortune"; a calculated point in the chart representing luck</note> and its lord are unfortunate in the fourth house or opposite it, and have no aspect from the benefics: it signifies the creature will perish in the mother's womb.

¶ **And other sages say:** Look to the twelfth house from the Ascendant and what is in it. If a malefic is in it, it signifies a dangerous and bad birth. If that malefic is Saturn and a benefic aspects him: she will survive, yet she will give birth in a foul place, or near a foul place. And if that malefic is Mars and a benefic aspects him, she will survive, yet she will give birth in the **kitchen** <note>original: "cogna", likely a corruption of "coquina"</note> or near it, or near the hearth of a fire or in a place where one lights 

<margin>fire</margin>

a fire. And if Mars is there and no benefic aspects him: she will give birth well and afterward she will die, or the child will be moved <note>delivered</note> dead and the mother will die afterward. And if Saturn is there and no benefic aspects him: the creature will die in the woman's womb, and the mother will die afterward before the creature comes out. 

¶ **And Al-Kindi says:** <note>original: "Irechindus"; the famous Arab philosopher and astrologer Al-Kindi.</note> If there is a malefic in any of the four angles, and it is in the **bounds** <note>original: "venba," likely a corruption of "fines"</note> of that angle or in any of its dignities: it signifies it will move. And if Mars aspects the Lord of the Ascendant or of the fourth house from the angle of the earth <note>the bottom of the chart</note> or his exaltation: it signifies the woman will give birth quickly and suddenly, and the creature will be exhausted. And if Jupiter aspects by the same aspect we mentioned for Mars: it signifies the salvation of the newborn and that she will give birth easily and quietly, and that the child will be intelligent and wise. And if the Moon is in the place of Jupiter or Mars: it will similarly survive, and the parents will be fortunate through the child and will have great good. And if it is Venus: it will similarly survive. If it is a daughter: she will be beautiful, cheerful, and of good character. If it is a son: he will be effeminate and have the manners of a woman. And if Saturn is in that aforementioned aspect: the mother and creature will be in danger. If a benefic aspects him: he will survive, yet that child will be a fornicator, and always weak in the likeness 

<column-break/>

of an old man in manners and deeds. 

¶ **And Dorotheus says:** <note>Dorotheus of Sidon, a 1st-century astrologer.</note> When you know the hour of the creature's generation in the woman's womb: Look if in that hour Mars was joined bodily with the Moon: that creature will fall <note>be miscarried</note> with much blood and will die. And if in that hour Saturn was bodily joined with the Moon: the creature will die in the mother's womb. And if at that hour malefics aspect Mercury: the mother and creature will die, or they will suffer great infirmity. And if benefics aspect the malefics which are aspecting the Moon or joined with her: the creature will survive, yet it will be sickly in the mother's womb. And if the Moon at that hour was joined to Jupiter or Venus by body: she will give birth to a healthy and safe son.

### ¶ Chapter 44: Whether she will give birth to one or more.

**When you ask yourself** regarding a pregnant woman whether she will give birth to one or two: look to the **Ascendant sign**. If it is a **mutable sign** <note>original: "signum commune"; Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, or Pisces—signs thought to represent multiplicity.</note> and a benefic planet is in it, and you find a benefic planet in the **house of children** <note>the 5th house</note>: say that she will give birth to two. And if there is not a mutable sign in the Ascendant or the house of children, nor a benefic planet in them, nor the **luminaries** <note>the Sun and Moon</note> in mutable signs: say she will give birth to one. 

¶ **One group of sages says:** You should look to the Lord of the house of children and the sign of that house itself. If both are in mutable signs, she will give birth to two; if not, one. 

¶ **And Al-Kindi says:** Look at the ninth sign from the Ascendant and its lord; if both or one of them is in a mutable sign, she will give birth to two. And if that ninth sign is also a feminine sign, and its lord is masculine and aspecting it from a mutable and masculine sign: she will give birth to two, a son and a daughter. And if Mercury also aspects that place or is in it without the aspect of a benefic: the newborn will be a **eunuch** <note>original: "castratus"</note> or effeminate. And if Venus or the Moon is in the Ascendant, or aspects the ninth from the Ascendant or its lord: she will give birth to two. And if the Lord of the ninth from the Ascendant or the Lord of the twelfth from the Ascendant aspects the ninth from the Ascendant or its lord from any **cardinal sign** <note>original: "signo mobili"; Aries, Cancer, Libra, or Capricorn</note>: she will give birth to two. 

And consider the planet that is the **significator** <note>the planet representing the child</note> and its sign: and if both are masculine: both will be boys; if feminine, both will be girls. And if they disagree, so that one of them is masculine and the other feminine: they will be a boy and a girl. And if with this constellation it is a mutable sign: there will be two sons. And if it is a **fixed sign** <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, or Aquarius</note>: there will be two daughters. And if a malefic who is the lord of a mutable sign aspects the Ascendant: she will give birth to two eunuchs or effeminate ones. 

¶ **Dorotheus says:** Look if at the hour of conception the Moon was with the Sun or with Mercury in a mutable sign: it signifies there are two, and perhaps they are from fornication. And if the Moon and the lord of its house are in mutable signs: it similarly signifies there are two.

### ¶ Chapter 45: On knowing how long the woman has been pregnant.

**If you are asked** regarding a pregnant woman how long she has been pregnant: Look to the Lord of the house of children and the Moon and the Lord of the Hour: and see which of them is closest to a **separation** <note>moving away from an aspect</note> from any planet; and look from what aspect it separated. If it separated by a **trine aspect** <note>original: "de tertio"; an aspect of 120 degrees</note>, say that she is in the fifth month of her pregnancy as in the 3rd...

And if it separates from the **quartile** <note>original: "quarto"; an aspect of 90 degrees</note>: say that it is in the fourth month. ### ¶ Chapter 46. Whether the fetus is male or female.

When you are asked on behalf of a pregnant woman if the child is male or female: look to the **Lord of the House of Children** <note>the planet ruling the 5th house</note>, the **Lord of the Hour**, and the **Moon**. If all or two of them are in **masculine signs** <note>Aries, Gemini, Leo, Libra, Sagittarius, Aquarius</note>, it is a male; and if in **feminine signs** <note>Taurus, Cancer, Virgo, Scorpio, Capricorn, Pisces</note>, it is a female. ¶ And other ancient wise men say: Look to the **Lord of the House of the Ascendant** <note>the planet ruling the sign rising on the eastern horizon</note> and the Lord of the House of Children; if both are in masculine signs, say it is a male; and if in feminine signs, say it is a female. And if they disagree, so that one is masculine and the other feminine: look to which of them the Moon agrees with, and judge according to this; or look to the "receiver of the Moon's disposition" <note>the planet ruling the sign where the Moon is currently located</note> and judge by it. ¶ And other ancient wise men say: Look at the **Ascendant** and its Lord, and the sign of children and its Lord, and the **Luminaries** <note>the Sun and Moon</note> and the Lords of their houses and the **terms** <note>specific degrees of a sign ruled by different planets</note> in which they are, and the Lord of the Hour. And if the majority of them and those with more "weight" <note>original: "appodeati"; meaning those with higher essential dignity or strength</note> are in masculine signs, it is a male. And if the majority of them and those with more weight are in feminine signs, it is a female. ¶ And Nocy, son of Thomas <note>likely a Latinized reference to an Arabic authority, possibly Masha'allah or Al-Nauvakhti</note> says: If you find the Sun in the "fourth part" <note>a quadrant of the chart</note> of children, or in its opposition in a masculine sign, it is a male; and if you find the Moon in such an aspect in a feminine sign, it is a female. And help yourself with the Lord of the **term** of the Ascendant, and with the Lord of the term in which the planet that signifies children is located. If both terms belong to masculine planets, it is a male; and if to feminine ones, it is a female. The planets signifying males are the Sun, Jupiter, and Mars. Those signifying females are Saturn, Venus, and the Moon. And Mercury, if it is **oriental** <note>rising before the Sun in the morning</note>, signifies a male; and if **occidental** <note>setting after the Sun in the evening</note>, a female. And I say in the case of Saturn and Mars, the greater part of the ancients agree on what we said before; they place Saturn as masculine and Mars as feminine. In this matter, the foresight is profitable because each of these two opinions has a reason that supports and confirms it. ¶ And **Ptolemy** <note>Claudius Ptolemy, the 2nd-century foundational authority on astrology</note> says: Although you may know the masculinity of the ascending sign and the signs of the luminaries and other significators, look also to the state of Mars and Venus; for if they are oriental, they are significators of males, and if occidental, of females. And I say that there is truth in this reasoning. ¶ And one group of the wise says: If the sign of the twelfth house and its Lord are feminine, she will give birth to a female; and if masculine, a male. And if they disagree: look to the stronger of them and judge according to that. And look in the Ascendant; if a masculine planet is strong in it, confirm the judgment of a male; and if feminine, a female. And if that strong masculine planet is in the "fourth" <note>square aspect</note> of another masculine planet, and the feminine in the fourth of another feminine planet, it strengthens and affirms the significance of the judgment in which it was, if 

<column-break/>

God wills. ¶ And others say: look to Saturn, the Sun, and Mars; if all or one of them is in the Ascendant, the third house, the fifth, the seventh, the ninth, or the eleventh: judge that she will give birth to a male. And if Venus and the Moon, both or either of them, are in the second house, the fourth, sixth, eighth, tenth, or twelfth: judge that she will give birth to a female. And if planets join together in these aforementioned places, so that they are in one or another place: look to the one that is closest to the Ascendant, for it will be more powerful in all things; judge according to it and take it as the significator. ¶ And **Al-Kindi** <note>original: "irechindus"; referring to the 9th-century Arab "Philosopher of the Arabs"</note> says: Look to Mercury and Jupiter and whether they are in their **exaltations** <note>signs where their power is most amplified</note>, and the ninth house from the Ascendant and its Lord; and if they are masculine, it signifies a male; and if feminine, it signifies she will give birth to a female. ¶ **Dorotheus** <note>Dorotheus of Sidon, a 1st-century astrological poet</note> says: Look at the hour of conception; and if at that hour the "fortunes" <note>benefic planets like Jupiter and Venus</note> are powerful and in masculine signs, and the Lord of the sign of the Moon is masculine, she is pregnant with a son. And if the Moon is in a feminine sign, and the Lord of the Moon's sign is feminine, she is pregnant with a daughter. ¶ And I say: If at that hour the Moon gives its "virtue" <note>transfers its light or influence</note> to an oriental planet that is in a masculine quadrant and a masculine sign—and especially if the Moon is likewise in a masculine sign—she is pregnant with a male; and if the contrary of this occurs, it is a female.

### ¶ Chapter 47. On knowing at what time the birth will be.

When you wish to know the time of birth: look to when Mars and the Sun join with the Lord of the House of Children, and with the Moon, and with the Lord of the Hour, or with several of them; and that will be the hour of giving birth. And help yourself in this with the "fortune" <note>benefic planet</note> that was in the question, looking at the **Lot of Children** <note>original: "partem filiorum"; a calculated mathematical point in a chart</note> when it applies to its quadrants. Direct that Lot of Children and the **athazir** <note>a Persian/Arabic term for the progression or "distribution" of a point through the degrees of the zodiac to time events</note> to the degree of the House of Children, and to the degree of Jupiter and its rays; and especially if Jupiter is between the Lot and the House of Children, because then, when that Lot reaches Jupiter by degrees of **ascension** <note>the time it takes for a sign to rise</note>, and when it is between those rays of those degrees, that is the time she will give birth, giving one day for each degree. And look at the application of the one to which it applies before the conjunction of the Lord of the House of Children with the Lord of the Ascendant in the Ascendant or in the House of Children; for that is likewise the time of giving birth. And likewise look when the significator of the question "changes its form" <note>changes sign or phase</note>; and this is likewise the time of giving birth. Look at which of all these has the greatest "testimony" <note>supporting evidence from multiple factors</note> and judge according to it. And likewise take the distance from the Lord of the House of Children to the degree of the House of Children; find how much it is and give one month for each sign. Help yourself with other testimonies, and judge according to the testimonies if they agree and join together, if God wills.

### ¶ Chapter 48. On knowing whether the birth will be by day or by night.

When you wish to know if the birth will be by day or by night: look to the ascending sign and its Lord, and the Moon, and the planet that is in the Ascendant, and the Lord of the House of Children, and the sign of the house...

If there is any **application** <note>an "application" occurs when a faster-moving planet approaches an aspect with a slower one</note> between the Lord of the Fifth and the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon; and if the Ascendant and the Moon are in **common signs** <note>also called "mutable" signs: Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, and Pisces</note> and the "significators" <note>planets representing the person or topic</note> are in the **angles** <note>the strongest houses in a chart: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th</note>; and especially if a **benefic planet** <note>original: "planeta fortuna"; usually Jupiter or Venus, which bring good luck</note> is in the Ascendant or the second house: say that she is pregnant. And if you do not find this application and these significations: say she is not pregnant. And if by chance a planet in direct motion is with the Moon, applying to the Lord of the Ascendant: it signifies she is pregnant. ¶ And **Abozebiz** <note>likely Abu Ma'shar, a famous medieval Persian astrologer</note> says that he found in the book called *Berdiraferę*: If you find the Lord of the **Third House** from the Ascendant in a common sign, she is pregnant; if not, she is not. And the signs of this matter are if the Lord of the Ascendant is in the Fifth House, and the Lord of the Fifth is in the Ascendant; for this is a sign of pregnancy. And if **Jupiter** or **Venus**, or either of them, is in the Fifth House, it likewise signifies she is pregnant. And if the Moon is in the Fifth House applying to Jupiter or Venus: it signifies she is pregnant. However, a planet that is joined in the same degree with the **Sun**, or "under its rays" <note>original: "sub radijs"; a planet obscured by the Sun's light, which usually weakens its power</note>, especially if it is a benefic, is a great sign that she is pregnant. And if in these aforementioned significations a **malefic** <note>original: "infortuna"; usually Mars or Saturn, which bring difficulty</note> is in the place of a benefic: it signifies she is not pregnant, or that [the fetus] will be lost. If **Mars** is the significator: it signifies loss because of a flow of blood. And if **Saturn**: it signifies the place of pregnancy is inflated with wind or water and is destroyed and taken away. ¶ And if it is asked how long she has been pregnant: look at how many degrees <note>original: "vnbas" or "unbas," likely a corruption for degrees or "steps"</note> have passed from the sign of the Ascendant, and give to each one month; and say that so many months have passed from the time of conception to the hour of the question. And perhaps the time of giving birth will be according to the number of degrees between the applying planet and the one it applies to; and in this signification, they will be months. And if the degrees are more in number than the possible time for giving birth, the number of days will be from those degrees; and judge according to the most testimonies you see. ¶ And when it is asked of you whether it is male or female: If the significators are masculine and in masculine signs, say it is a male; and if the contrary is true, say it is a

<column-break/>

female. And if there are many significator planets and many signs "of many children" <note>fruitful signs like Cancer, Scorpio, or Pisces</note>: say that she will give birth to more than one. ¶ And if you are asked about the status of the mother and what will happen to her after the birth: Look to the Moon and what it applies to; and according to the last application it will have in the sign in which it is, such will be the mother’s status in giving birth according to the power of that [planet] it applies to, and its nature, place, and power in the figure. ¶ And if you are asked about what has passed regarding the mother's status: you shall know this from the hour of pregnancy regarding the **Second House** and its status. And you shall know the mother's status after birth from the **Twelfth House**; and in whichever of these houses there are benefics, speak of good and indicate improvement and fortune. And in whichever there are malefics: speak of loss and evil according to the nature of the benefic or malefic. And if you find **Mars** receiving any of the significators without harming it, and a benefic aspecting Mars, it indicates an easy and safe birth, especially if it is in a hot sign, for then it is a significator of heat. And if **Saturn** is in this signification in the place of Mars: it indicates slowness and heaviness in the pregnant woman, as well as pain and labor in the birth.

## Chapter 49. On the question for a son and his 
### qualities.

When you are asked about a son and what
will become of him, and what love and friendship
will be between the father and him: look to the
Lord of the Ascendant and the Moon and the
**Fifth House** and its Lord, as well as **Jupiter**
and the Lord of the House of Children. And if you find an application and **reception** <note>original: "receptionem"; when two planets are in signs ruled by each other, showing cooperation</note> between the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the House of Children from good and strong places: it appears there will be love and good will between them, and the father will love the son and do good for him; and more strongly if the Lord of the Ascendant is the one to whom the other applies, and if the application is "friendly" <note>an aspect like a sextile or trine</note>. And likewise if Jupiter aspects the House of Children with a good aspect, or is the Lord of the House, or is received by the Lord of the House, or applies to it from a good place and is clear of malefics and safe from **retrogradation** <note>appearing to move backward</note> and **combustion** <note>being too close to the Sun</note>; and the Moon is similarly safe from malefics: it signifies the safety of the children and their good status, and agreement with the father, and of one son with another, and that they will proceed well in their deeds. And if the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the House of Children, as well as the Moon and Jupiter, are "afflicted" <note>original: "damnatus"; in a poor position or aspected by malefics</note>, and there is no aspect or reception between them: it signifies enmity and ill will of the children toward the father and between themselves, and their poor status, and that they will tend toward evil. And generally, place the degree of the House of Children in the likeness of the Ascendant <note>a technique called "derivative houses" where the 5th house is treated as the 1st house for the child</note>: and look to its Lord and in which house it is from the houses ordered according to the position of this house (which acts as the Ascendant). Look just as you look at the planets, and how the planets aspect it: and judge the status of the children according to this, just as you judge in **nativities** <note>birth charts</note> and generally in questions. And if the Lord of the House of Children is in it, or in the **Third House** from the Ascendant: it signifies the fortune of the children and their good status, and that they will have good from the father and the father from them. And if the Lord of the House of Children is in the **Tenth House** from the Ascendant: it signifies the illnesses of the children and their impediments; and judge in all other things according to this.
