### Chapter 50: On knowing the nature of a messenger or an embassy.

You should know that the **significator** <note>original: "significator"; the planet representing a specific person or topic in an astrological chart</note> of the messenger is the **Lord of the Fifth House** <note>original: "dñs quinte domus"; the planet that rules the sign on the cusp of the 5th house, which governs messengers</note> from the **Ascendant** <note>the sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of the question</note>; and the **Moon** shares in this role. The significator for the *reason* of the embassy is the planet to which the Lord of the Fifth House **applies** <note>original: "applicat"; a term for when a faster planet moves toward a meaningful alignment with another</note>, or the one to which the Moon applies, or the one to which both apply. Afterward, if this application is from a **Fortuna** <note>a "benefic" or lucky planet, such as Jupiter or Venus</note> by a **Square** <note>original: "quarto"; a 90-degree angle</note>, **Opposition** <note>an 180-degree angle</note>, or **Conjunction** <note>a 0-degree meeting</note>; and if there is **Reception** <note>when one planet is in a sign ruled by the other, indicating cooperation</note> between them, or if there is a **Translation of Light** <note>when a faster planet carries the influence from one planet to another</note> or **Collection of Light** by some planet; and if the planet that receives the application (or the one carrying or collecting the light) is the **Lord of the Tenth House** <note>the house governing kings, authority, and career</note>: say that the reason for the embassy for which the messenger was sent concerns the affairs of a King, his revenues, or some noble and high matter. And if that application is by a **Sextile** <note>original: "tertio"; a 60-degree angle</note> or a **Trine** <note>original: "fertili"; a 120-degree angle, considered very favorable</note>, the judgment shall be the same. And if the aforementioned planet—that is, the one who receives the application—is the **Lord of the Eleventh House** <note>the house of friends and hopes</note>: say that the reason for the embassy is of the nature of the eleventh house. And in this manner, you may speak regarding all other houses, whatever they may be, where that planet is the Lord. But if that application is to an **Infortuna** <note>a "malefic" or unlucky planet, like Saturn or Mars</note> and without reception: say that the reason for the embassy is for some evil related to the nature of the house where the Infortuna is located. And if it is with reception: the evil for which he goes will be less.

### On knowing the state of a messenger who goes for property or another matter.

Assign the Ascendant and its Lord to the one who sends the messenger; the **Seventh House** <note>the house of "the other"</note> and its Lord to the one to whom he is sent; the Moon to the embassy; and the Lord of the Fifth House to the messenger for his guidance; and judge according to this. Afterward, if you find the Lord of the Fifth House **separated** <note>original: "separatū"; moving away from an alignment</note> from the Lord of the Seventh House and **applying** to the Lord of the Ascendant: say that the messenger has completed his embassy, has already left the person to whom he was sent, and is returning to the one who sent him. And if, in that state, he is separated from the Lord of the **House of Substance** <note>the 2nd house, governing money and possessions</note>: say that he brings property back with him, whether the significator is a Fortuna or an Infortuna. And speak similarly regarding all other houses in this way: for the response the messenger brings will be of the nature of that house whose Lord is the planet from which he is separating, and of the nature of that planet itself. If it is a Fortuna, it will be good in its nature; if an Infortuna, it will be evil in its nature. And if that significator of the messenger applies by a Square or Opposition to an Infortuna before he separates from the Lord of the Seventh: say that the messenger encountered an obstacle in his embassy from the person to whom he went. And if that application to an Infortuna occurs before he applies to the Lord of the Seventh: say that he will have an obstacle on his journey before he reaches the one to whom he was sent. And if the application occurs after he has separated from the Lord of the Seventh: say that he will have that obstacle on his return before he reaches the sender. And if there is an Infortuna in the **Ninth House** <note>the house of long-distance travel</note>: say that the journey is fearsome and that there are thieves upon it. And if you find the opposite of this, judge the opposite. **Al-Kindi** <note>original: "alkindus"; a famous 9th-century Arab polymath and astrologer</note> says regarding messengers and travelers: when you are asked whether messengers or travelers will arrive

<column-break/>

at the place to which they are going, or not: look to the Lord of the Ascendant and the Moon. If both or either of them are in the Seventh House, or if both or one of them is applying to the Lord of the Seventh: say that they have arrived at that place. And if, along with this, they are separating from Fortunas: say that he had a good and safe journey; if from Infortunas, say the opposite. And your judgment shall be according to the nature of the Fortuna or Infortuna in this matter, and according to its dignity in the heavens, its strength, and its weakness. And if the application is to Fortunas: say that he found goodness and safety in that place where he was. If it is to Infortunas: say the opposite. And judge good or evil according to the nature of the Fortuna or Infortuna, its place and dignity in the heavens, and its strength and weakness; and you will be certain with God's help. And if you are asked for confirmation whether a messenger or traveler has arrived at a place or been there—specifically if he found the person to whom he was sent or not: look to the aforementioned significators. If both or one of them is applying to the Lord of the Seventh, or if either of them is applying to the Lord of his own place: say that he found him; and if the opposite is true: say no. And if the applying planet is **received** <note>original: "receptus"; see note above on Reception</note> by the one to whom it applies: say that the person to whom he went received him well and granted the thing for which he went to him. And if the application is by an Opposition: say that he found him and that he received him well, yet he will give some excuse because he did not wish to grant the matter for which he went to him. And it will be the same if it is by a Square, except that it will be less so. And if the question is whether the messenger is already on his return: look at these two significators; if both or one of them is withdrawn from the Seventh House or from another **angle** <note>the four most powerful points in a chart: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses</note>, separating himself from the Lord of the Seventh House, or is applying to the Lord of his own place while moving away from an angle: say that he is coming. And if the Fortunas testify in this signification: say that he will have a safe journey; if the Infortunas, say the opposite. And let your judgment turn upon the nature of the Fortuna or Infortuna, its state, place, and dignity in the heavens, and its strength and weakness. And see if the significator applies to the Lord of the Ascendant or the Lord of its own place. And if you are asked *when* he will come: speak according to the number of degrees of the application—whether hours, days, months, or years—and according to the nature of the **Fixed, Common, or Movable signs** <note>original: "signoz fixorū aut cōmuniū uel mobiliū"; the three "modalities" of zodiac signs that indicate the speed and stability of an event</note>. For you shall divide it according to this, and according to the ease of the significators in their motion or their heaviness; and especially if that number of degrees aligns with the number of degrees the Moon has left before applying to the degree of the Ascendant by **body** <note>a physical meeting or conjunction</note>, or before applying to the degree of the Lord of its place; and similarly for the Lord of the Ascendant. Or see if any planet was **under the rays** <note>original: "sub radijs"; so close to the Sun that it is invisible and weakened</note> until it appeared, or if the significators apply to the degrees of their dignities in the heavens. And if the significator is **retrograde** <note>original: "retrogradus"; appearing to move backward in the sky</note>, the time of return will be when it turns **direct** <note>original: "dirigetur"; resuming forward motion</note>; and the time—whether hours, days, months, or years—will be according to the number of degrees remaining until it turns direct. And look at these aforementioned significations, join one with another, and judge according to your own mind and according to them.

¶ **Whether a messenger who goes to kill a man will do so or not.**

Look in this matter to the **Lord of the Fifth House** <note>original: "dñm quinte"; the planet ruling the 5th house of messengers</note>: and if you find him separated from **Mars** <note>the planet of violence and war</note> and the **Lord of the Seventh House** <note>ruling the opponent or the target</note> **applying** <note>moving toward an astrological aspect</note> to him: say that he will kill him. And if the Lord of the Fifth is **received** <note>original: "receptus"; a state of astrological cooperation</note> by the Lord of the Seventh from the **House of Death** <note>the Eighth House</note>—that is, with the Lord of the Seventh being in the House of Death: say also that he will kill him; and if not, he will not.

### Chapter 51: On invitations to banquets
<note>original: "Caplm .5 .in inuitationibus ad conuiuia"; though the text says 5, it follows chapter 50 on the previous page</note>

<image-desc>A decorative ornamental initial 'C' begins this chapter.</image-desc>
When you wish to go to eat at a wedding or a banquet and you have been asked about this: give the **Ascendant** <note>the sign rising on the eastern horizon</note> and its **Lord** <note>the ruling planet of that sign</note> to yourself at the beginning of the meal. Use this to judge whether there will be much food or little, and if it is good or bad, complete or clear, or not; as well as the games that will be there.

Assign the **Second House** as the **significator** <note>indicator</note> for the person sitting near you on your left side, and for the servants of the master of the house, and those who prepare the food, as well as the cloths and things appropriate for the occasion.

Assign the **Third House** from the Ascendant as the significator for those standing over the meal but not eating, and for brothers and friends holding the banquet.

Assign the **Fourth House** as the significator of the house and the place where they stand, and the relatives of the host on his father’s side, and the goodness or badness of the things upon which they sit.

Assign the **Fifth House** as the significator of the wine, the host’s friends, his sons, nephews, and his relatives, and those coming with gifts <note>original: "exenijs"</note>.

Assign the **Sixth House** as the significator of the person sitting to the right of the host, as well as the slaves and serving-men waiting on the meal; whether they are few or many, whether they are refined or organized, or not.

Assign the **Seventh House** as the significator of the place where the host sits, and whether he is sad or happy, and whether he appears well or not; whether he is refined or base; and of those things you might find on the road; as well as the host’s women and the relatives of his women.

Assign the **Eighth House** as the significator of the room where the wine and the vessel are kept, and the **steward** <note>original: "morautiū"; likely a corruption of "moratorem" or "dispensatorem"</note> with the host's women who are helping, and the one sitting to the right of the **manager** <note>original: "expenditoris"; the one paying for or organizing the event</note> and the singers.

Assign the **Ninth House** as the significator of the door of the host's house, the entrance, and what is within it; the cooks, the bakers, and those bringing fragrant things; and those who stand by the guests while they eat; whether many or few men are present, and the doorkeepers.

Assign the **Tenth House** as the significator of the candles and the highest-ranking men who are at the meal, such as kings or others.

Assign the **Eleventh House** as the significator of those sitting around the candles, the friends and brothers of the host and the manager, and of their loyalty or fraud; and of the common people who are at the meal.

Assign the **Twelfth House** from the Ascendant as the significator of the host's own wife and the low-status people who are there; and whether those of that house love the host or not, and whether he rejoices with her or not.

¶ Assign the **Moon** as the significator of the whole lodging, and the Lord of the Moon’s sign as the indicator of the end of that stay. Assign the second sign from the Moon’s sign as the indicator of the songs. And the **Lord of the Triplicity** <note>a set of three planets ruling an element</note> of the Moon's sign: the first is the signi-

<column-break/>

-ficator of those who serve first; the second, of those who serve in the middle; and the third, of those who serve at the end.

Assign the third sign from the Moon as the indicator of those who stand over the meal from the beginning to the end.

Assign the fourth sign from the Moon as the indicator of the place where they sit.

Assign the fifth sign from the Moon as the indicator of the cloths spread out.

Assign the sixth sign from the Moon as the indicator of the vessels—that is, the apparatus of the house from which one is served.

Assign the seventh sign from the Moon as the indicator of the state of the house after the people have departed.

Assign the eighth sign from the Moon as the indicator of the latrine or the bath or the place where they wash themselves, and where they strike <note>perhaps referring to the cleaning of vessels or physical altercations</note>.

Assign the ninth sign from the Moon as the indicator of the places to which they go after they depart from the meal.

Assign the tenth sign from the Moon as the indicator of the things in which they take delight, such as games, stories, and such things.

Assign the eleventh sign from the Moon to the ornaments of the banquet itself and similar things.

Assign the twelfth sign from the Moon as the indicator of that which happens in the house regarding evil or brawls.

Afterward, judge through that specific significator which you find **fortunate** <note>in a lucky or strong position</note> that the thing will be good and cheerful, according to the power and virtue of the fortunate planets and their Lord. And through whichever one you find **unfortunate** <note>in a difficult or "malefic" position</note>, judge according to its power regarding reduction and loss, according to the power and virtue of the planet causing the damage and its dignity in the heavens.

Through whichever significator you find well-proportioned and beautiful, judge beauty and order in that matter. And through whichever you find base, judge foulness in that matter. Beauty and order come from **Venus** and her witnesses; fame and profit from **Jupiter** and his witnesses. Fear and loss come from **Mars** and his witnesses. A thing well-made and well-ordered, and of good workmanship, comes from **Mercury** and his witnesses—this is if he is fortunate. If he is unfortunate, it will be the opposite. A thing that is visible and revealed comes from the **Sun** and his witnesses; and it is similar with the **Moon**, but the Moon has less power in this than the Sun.

A matter whose significator is in its **Exaltation** <note>a sign where a planet's influence is heightened</note> will be noble and good. A matter whose significator is in its **Fall** <note>original: "casu"; a sign where a planet's influence is weakened</note>, whether in house or exaltation, will be base and bad. A matter whose significator is in the **Opposite** <note>180 degrees</note> of its own house damages itself.

When Venus is in the **Angles** <note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</note> from the Moon, and especially in her **Midheaven** <note>the 10th house, the highest point</note>, it signifies that there will be orderly and beautiful games at that banquet. If Jupiter is in this place instead of Venus, it signifies that there will be great expense and liberality there. If Mercury is fortunate in this aforementioned place, it signifies there will be beautiful speech and logic; if unfortunate, it signifies the opposite.

If the Lord of the Ascendant is made unfortunate by Mars at the hour of the departure of the person going to the banquet, the one going there will not be safe, because an occasion of blows and wounds will happen to him; and perhaps he will die if Mars is the Lord of the Eighth House. And if the Lord of the Ascendant, made unfortunate by Mars, is Mercury, brawls will happen to him, and things will be said to him that will weigh on him, and threats will be made against him. If it is made unfortunate by **Saturn**, he will be treated with contempt. If Saturn is the Lord of the Sixth House, an illness will happen to him; and what happens to him will be according to the place where the planet is, and according to the house of the significator in the heavens. And the...

If **Jupiter** <note>the planet of expansion and luck</note> should be in the place of **Saturn** <note>the planet of restriction and discipline</note>: he will have good profit and honor according to the state of Jupiter, having his place and house in the heavens. And if **Venus** <note>the planet of beauty and pleasure</note> should be in this house in the place of Jupiter, he will have joy and gladness, and charms according to the state of Venus, in her place and house in the heavens—that is, in the astrological chart. And if the **Sun** should be in this house in the place of Venus: he will have honor and fame, and they shall be ruled by him, and his words and goods will be seen as his own achievements. 

And if the **Moon** should be unfortunate <note>afflicted by "malefic" planets like Mars or Saturn</note>, she ruins that banquet, and obstacles will happen according to the power and state of the unfortunate planets. But if she is fortunate, it will be a joyful and good banquet according to the power and state of the fortunate Moon. And if the **Second House** <note>the house of possessions and food</note> of the Moon should be fortunate, the food will be good and beautiful according to the power of the fortunate planets. But if that house is unfortunate, the opposite will be true. 

¶ And if the food is good, and the **first lord of the triplicity** <note>a group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element</note> of the second house of the Moon is in a better state than the second lord: the food will be better and safer than the drinks. But if the **second lord of the triplicity** of the second house of the Moon is better and more fortunate than the first: the drinks will be better than the food; and whichever of them is fortunate signifies good fortune, and whichever is unfortunate signifies misfortune. 

And you should know that when the Moon is afflicted by the body of **Mars** <note>in a "conjunction," where planets are in the same degree</note>: it signifies a bad end and that one will repent. And if it is by the body of **Saturn**: it signifies the foulness of the food, and that one will have no desire to eat it, and it will cause sickness and evil to those who eat. 

And if this misfortune should be bodily in the sign of **Libra**: or in its fourth part <note>a square aspect of 90 degrees</note>: it signifies that this harm will be in the meat of cows. And if it is in the sign of **Virgo**: it will be in lentils and cabbages and similar things. And if in the sign of **Leo**: it will be in all kinds of meat—and you should guard yourself so that you do not eat anything. And if in **Sagittarius**: it will be in the meat of the hunt <note>venison or wild game</note> and similar things. And if in **Capricorn**: guard yourself from the meat of goats and similar things, because it will do you harm. And if in **Aquarius**: it will be in the meat of the hunt, of fallow deer and such; and guard yourself from them. And if in **Pisces**: guard yourself from fish, both fresh and salted. 

And if Venus and **Mercury** <note>the planet of communication and wit</note> should be with the Moon: it signifies games, dancing, music, and all manner of jesting and joys. And if Mercury alone should be powerful: it signifies that in that meal they will have discussions of the sciences and philosophy, especially if Mercury is in his own house. And these same things are signified by these planets when they gaze upon each other from the quarters <note>original: "aspicientes de q̄rtis"; the square aspect</note>. 

¶ **Antiochus** <note>Antiochus of Athens, an influential early astrologer</note> says on this matter: When the Moon applies <note>moves toward an aspect</note> to another planet from the place of the "fall" of Venus <note>the sign where a planet's influence is weakened</note> from the house or exaltation: it signifies that the wedding will be noble. And if **Saturn** should be in the **Ascendant** <note>the sign rising on the horizon</note> and following the first angle <note>the 1st House</note>: it signifies that the meal and the games will last a long time. 

And if the Moon should be joined bodily with Mercury and Mars, or in their quarters: it signifies that there will be brawls, controversies, and evil and foul words. And if Mars should be in his own triplicity: it signifies that contentions and words and things of which one will have fear shall happen there; the words will be foul, yet they will have a safe ending. And if the Moon should be with Mars, and Mercury in her quarter: fear will come to him from the part of the King, along with hindrance, killings, and beatings. And if she is in conjunction with Saturn, and Mercury in his quarter: the meal will be foul and bad and of little profit.

And if the Moon should be with Venus or with Jupiter, with Mars gazing at them from the fourth or third aspect <note>square or trine</note>: there will be many games, comforts, and joys there. ### ¶ Chapter 52. On letters and messengers.

When you are questioned regarding the matter of **letters** and **messengers**: give the **Lord of the Ascendant** <note>the planet ruling the sign rising on the eastern horizon</note> and the planet from which the **Moon** is separating as the significators of the one who sent the letter. And give the **Seventh House** <note>the house of the "other," or the recipient</note>, its lord, and the planet to which the Moon is applying as the significators of the one to whom it is sent. The positions of the **Moon** and **Mercury** are the significators of the good or evil that may be in the letter. And the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the Seventh, and the places where they are, and the aspects <note>the geometric angles between planets</note> they have from the "fortunes" or "infortunes," are the significators of the matters in which he has trust, and of what will happen regarding that letter, and the will of the two—the sender and the receiver—and what will one has toward the other. And any of these significators which are in the **angles** <note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, which are the most powerful positions</note>, or received in their own house in the place where they are: the matter will be noble, high, and good. And if the planet from which the Moon separates is in its **exaltation** <note>a sign where a planet’s influence is greatly strengthened</note> and is falling away from an angle: it signifies that the sender of the letter had power and high status but lost it. And if it is in its own house and in an angle: it signifies that he is a high and wealthy man, and that he has power in his own city, existing in his own right. In this signification, the **triplicity** is of less power than the house, the **term** is less than the triplicity, and the **face** <note>terms and faces are smaller subdivisions of a zodiac sign</note> is less than the term.

### ¶ Chapter 53. On knowing if letters are coming.

When you are questioned whether letters are coming: look in this matter to **Mercury**, who is the significator of the arrival of letters. If you then find him having dignity in the Ascendant, or in the significator of the question—which is the **Almuten** <note>the planet with the most combined strength and essential dignity in a specific degree</note>—say that the letters will come. And if you wish to know at what time they will arrive, look when **Mercury** applies by aspect to the degree of the Ascendant, degree by degree, from the right or the left: say that on that day the letters will arrive, especially if that application is from an angle. And if **Mercury** has no dignity in the Ascendant, nor in the significator which is the Almuten,

<column-break/>

nor in the Moon, and has no aspect with the Ascendant or the significator: say that the letters will not come at this time. And if **Mercury** does not behold the Ascendant, but beholds the significator, and has a portion or testimony in its place: judge that the letter will come, and that it will be at the time when Mercury applies to the significator degree by degree. And if you find **Mercury** beholding the Ascendant and the Moon separating from Mercury: it signifies that the letter will come on that day when the Moon is in the degree of the Ascendant. And if you find Mercury separating himself from the Lord of the Seventh and applying to the Lord of the Ascendant or to the degree of the Ascendant itself: judge that the letter has already come, and that it came on that day when Mercury applied to the degree of the Ascendant, or to the degree of the significator which is the Almuten. And if you find Mercury having no dignity in the significator, nor in the Ascendant, nor in the Moon, nor any aspect with any of them: judge that the letter will not come at that time, unless Mercury is in the **Twelfth House** <note>the house of hidden things and delays</note> quickly entering the degree of the Ascendant, which then signifies that the letters will come, and at the hour when the Moon is in the degree of the Ascendant. And if you find Mercury separating himself from the Lord of the **Second House** and applying to the degree of the Ascendant or its Lord: judge that the letter will come with substance and profit. And if you find Mercury separating himself from the Lord of the **Fifth House**, and the Lord of the Fifth is a "fortune" and receives Mercury as he applies to the Ascendant or its Lord: judge that the letter will come with **gifts** <note>original: "exeniis," meaning formal offerings or hospitality gifts</note>. And know that the Lord of the Hour, when you find him in the Midheaven or in the Eleventh House, signifies that the letter will come, if God wills.

### ¶ Chapter 54. On knowing if good or evil will come in a letter.

When questioned regarding any letter, whether good or evil will come in it: look at the planet from which **Mercury** separates. If he separates from an "infortune" <note>Mars or Saturn</note>: say that evil will come in the letter; and if from a "fortune": say the opposite. And you shall know the nature of that good or evil from the nature of that planet from which Mercury separated, and its place in the figure <note>the astrological chart</note>, and its status in the Ascendant, and whether it has dignity in the Ascendant or beholds it.

### ¶ Chapter 55. On knowing if a letter is sealed or not.

When it is asked of a letter whether it is **sealed** or not: look in this matter to **Mercury** and the **Moon**. If you find the Moon applying to Mercury: say that it is not sealed. And if you find her separated from Mercury by a few degrees, so that she has not passed the limit of the aspect: say that the letter is sealed. And in this you give the letter to Mercury, and that with which it is sealed to the Moon; judge according to this, and according to how you find the status of one toward the other. Weigh the matters in your intellect, understand them, and distinguish one from another, and you will be certain.

And if you find the Moon in the **Fourth** or **Seventh House** applying to the degree of the Ascendant or to any planet existing in the Ascendant: judge firmly that the messenger is coming. And if the Moon is in the **Ninth House** about to enter the **Tenth**: judge also the arrival of the messenger, and that by coming in...

### Chapter 57. On knowing if a messenger has come with the result for which he went or not.

When you are asked whether a messenger brings the thing for which he was sent or not: look to the **Moon** and the lord of the **fifth house**. See if you find both of them, or even one of them, separating from some planet whose nature is similar to the nature of that thing for which he was sent. And if that **significator** <term>significator: a planet representing a specific person or object in an astrological chart</term> was "received" <note>original: "receptus," an astrological condition where one planet is in a sign ruled by another</note> by that planet, and if by its separation from it, it applies to the degree of the ascendant or to the lord of the ascendant: judge that the messenger brings the thing for which he was sent. In this, look by considering the other parts of this logic, and you will be certain, with God's help.

### Chapter 58. On knowing the summary of a letter.

When you are asked about some letter in summary, whether there is good or evil in it: look [to see] from whom **Mercury** or the **Moon** separates, because letters and messages belong to Mercury and the Moon. And the lord of the **third** and **ninth** houses [relative to] the one having the letter and message provide a weak indication. Afterward, look at that aspect; if it is from a "fortune" <note>original: "fortuna," a beneficial planet like Jupiter or Venus</note>: judge that what is in the letter is good. If it is from an "infortune" <note>original: "infortuna," a difficult planet like Saturn or Mars</note>: evil.

### Chapter 59. Concerning guests, how many of them will come, and who will not.

When some have been invited and you want to know how many of them will come: direct the ascendant and look in what sign its lord is, how many degrees are between him and the degree of the ascendant, and which planet **applies** <note>original: "applicat," meaning the planets are moving toward an aspect or meeting</note> to the lord of the ascendant. And if it is the lord of the **seventh house** applying to the lord of the ascendant: look how many degrees are in the **term** <term>term: a specific subdivision of a zodiac sign ruled by a particular planet</term> in which the lord of the seventh himself is. As many men will come as is the number of degrees of that term, or as is the number of degrees which the lord of the seventh has passed from that term, or how many degrees remain for him in that term. And if the lord of the 7th does not apply to the degree of the ascendant: look how many planets are between the lord of the ascendant and the degree of the ascendant, and that many will come. And if any of those planets applies to any other planet, or any other applies to it outside that place which we mentioned (from the lord of the ascendant up to the ascending degree): if that external planet which aspects any of them in that place was **Mars**, others who were not invited will come along with those you did invite. And if the lord of the seventh was in the seventh house or aspects a planet which is in the seventh, and it applies to the degree of the ascendant: as many will come as you invited. And if you find none of these aforesaid things, none will come.

### Chapter 60. On knowing if those you invited will come or not.

When you have sent for some people and you want to know how many will come with your messenger: look how many planets were bodily joined with **Mars**, or how many aspected him by any aspect, because that many will come with your messenger. Consider this with your intellect, and you will be certain by the good pleasure of God.

### Chapter 1. On the sixth house and its actions.

<image-desc>A large ornamental woodcut drop-cap initial 'H' decorated with white scrollwork and foliate patterns on a dark background within a square frame.</image-desc> This house signifies illnesses and where they come from; the ruin of limbs; captives; male and female servants; betrayals and sorceries; movement from one place to another. [It signifies] beasts and enemies; the redemption of captives; the healing of the body; the uncovering of secrets and confrontations.

This house is **cadent** <term>cadent: a house that 'falls away' from the main angles of the chart, often considered weaker or more difficult</term> from the western angle. It signifies the first part of life; tenant farmers and laborers; beasts that have fled by themselves; lost things of vile and weak price; suspicion of women; eunuchs. It signifies things for which one has no confidence in obtaining, and the thing which a man needs but does not have. It signifies the departure from one's town; the change of will of friends; lies, false testimonies, envies, and fornications in words and deeds. It signifies worshipping devils and those initiated through **necromancy** <note>original: "nigromantiam," referring to dark magic or communication with the dead</note>; it signifies subtle and weak bodies. When in any nativity the significator of the birth is in this house: it signifies that the person born will be a **physician** <note>original: "phisicus," a doctor or student of nature</note>. The first lord of the **triplicity** <term>triplicity: a group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element (Fire, Earth, Air, Water)</term> of this house signifies illness and whether he will be healed or die from it. The 2nd lord signifies servants, laborers, and eunuchs. The 3rd lord signifies small and large beasts, and whether they are many or few, and whether good or bad. And if the sign of this house was **Fiery** in a question, the question is regarding fear. If **Earthy**, the question is about a thing which fled. If **Airy**, it is for a servant or captive. If **Watery**, it is for a sick person. The color of this house, in whatever sign it may be, is a deeply dyed black.

### Chapter 2. On observing the state of the sick person.

Know that this consideration is divided into ten parts. The **1st** is to inspect the place of the significator which indicated the illness, and to look into medicines and for the physician. The **2nd** is in observing if the illness is in the spirit or in the body or both. The **3rd** is in knowing in which place of the body the illness is. The **4th** is whether this sick person will be healed from this illness or if he will die. The **5th** is whether this illness will be short or long. The **6th** is at what time he will be healed or when the sick person will die. The **7th** is in knowing a good or bad **crisis** <term>crisis: a medical turning point or critical stage in a disease</term> and at what time it will come. The **8th** is in knowing the increase or decrease of the illness. The **9th** is in knowing the manner of the sick person in his illness—whether he will be fearful or enduring. The **10th** is in knowing the end of the illness and the sick person. Know that the significator of the state of the sick person is taken from the majority of the things of the ascendant, its lord, and its **almuten** <term>almuten: the planet with the most power or "dignity" over a specific point in a chart</term>. The 5th [consideration] is the place of the **hylech** <term>hylech: the "giver of life," a planet used to calculate a person's lifespan</term>. The end of the sick person and the illness is taken from the **tenth house**. This is the opinion of **Ptolemy**, **Alkindi**, and the majority of the ancient wise men, and I agree with it. Furthermore, **Dorotheus** says in these principles or reasons: look at the state of the sick person from the ascendant. And for the physician, look from the tenth [house], and judge the state of the sick person and what will become of him and how his case will end based on the ascendant. And afterward...

<meta>This page continues the discussion on astrological principles, moving from specific questions about messengers to a broader critique of established authorities like Dorotheus, Ptolemy, and Al-Kindi regarding the calculation of planetary houses, latitudes, and the "faces" of the zodiac signs.</meta>

The author returns to the same reasoning and the same chapter. He says that one should observe the status of the physician from the **ascendant** and the status of the sick person from the **10th house**. However, he contradicts his own sayings, and this is a manifest error; for by right, it is clear that the ascendant ought to be given to the sick person to know their state, what will become of them, and how their affairs will turn out, since it was for them that the thought and the question were raised. By what logic or in what manner should we give them any other **significator** <term>significator: a planet or house in a chart that represents a specific person or topic</term> besides the ascendant? One group of astrologers followed this path of Dorotheus <note>Dorotheus of Sidon, a 1st-century astrological poet</note>, following him in this and not challenging him; among these are Masha'allah, Abu 'Ali al-Khayyat, Ibn Ezra, Al-Faghar, Abu Ma'shar, and Sahl ibn Bishr. Although Dorotheus was a great sage and a noble man, he erred in this reasoning. This spread into judgment and resulted in something transitory in practice.

Similarly, he erred in his book on **nativities** <term>nativities: birth charts</term> when he calculated the *athazir* <note>a method of progressing a chart through time</note> of the *hylech* <term>hylech: the planet that acts as the "giver of life" in a birth chart</term>, and he calculated the *athazir* from one *hylech* to an opposing planet when the latitude of one was Southern and the other Northern. He said that this disagreement did not interfere, and that the disagreement of latitudes in two different directions does not hinder conjunctions. But in the opposition of two planets, even when they agree in degrees of longitude, if they disagree in the number of degrees of latitude—even if they disagree in direction, one being Northern and the other Southern—is it a straight and true application of the opposition?

When both are on the line of the **zodiac** <term>zodiac: the imaginary belt in the sky through which the sun and planets move</term> and neither of them has latitude in any direction, and they aspect each other in opposition from equal degrees in that longitude, that will also be a true opposition of straight aspect. However, if both have latitude in the same direction—either North or South—and the degrees of that latitude are not equal, even if they agree in degrees of longitude, it is not a true opposition; for it is diminished by as much as the difference in the degrees of latitude. And if both have latitude in opposite directions—one to the North and the other to the South—and those degrees of latitude are not equal, though they agree in longitude, it is not a complete opposition, because it lacks as much as the difference in latitude. And if one of them is on the zodiac line and the other has latitude in any direction, though they agree in longitude, it is not a complete opposition. Following this path, oppositions are worked out. This is explained and divided in the tables I have made regarding the aspects I have observed, which contain 38 chapters on the quantities of planetary applications.

Abu Ma'shar followed him in this same error and gave this same reasoning in the third part of his book called the *Book of Remembrances*. Nor is it a wonder if this man erred, because even Ptolemy—though he was the highest of the ancients in this science, better and more honorable than all other sages in his opinion, who best separated and understood his divisions and reasons, who most deeply and from the furthest distance accepted significations, who had better intellect and consideration than all others, and who was furthest from error—all others erred when he looked in the chapter on children in one place at the **fifth house**, as all other sages of this science and all astrologers do, and then in another place took the same from the **tenth** and **eleventh houses**. He says similarly in the places of their opposites concerning aspects that are the 4th and 5th, and he places the significator of the father by day in the tenth house and by night in the 4th. And he places the significator of the mother by day

<column-break/>

in the 4th and by night in the 10th. And according to this, it could happen that the significator of the mother, the significator of the father, and the significator of the son are all received from the same place. This could happen according to this reasoning many times. The error is not hidden, for it is manifest to all who understand this science. This is found in the 5th chapter of the 4th part of his book called the *Quadripartitus* <note>original: "quadripartitus," the Latin title for Ptolemy's Tetrabiblos</note>.

Similarly, regarding the **Part of Fortune**, he commanded it to be taken the same way by night as by day—in one way from the Sun to the Moon—disagreeing with all the sages of this science of all laws. He also disagreed with all the sages regarding the **triplicities** <term>triplicities: groups of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element</term>; he said in the 29th chapter of the first part of the *Quadripartitus* that Aries and its triplicity are Northern, Taurus and its triplicity are Southern, Gemini and its triplicity are Eastern, and Cancer and its triplicity are Western. He disagrees with all other sages in all of these.

Similarly, when he spoke of the *hylech*, the giver of life, and the *animodar* <term>animodar: a method used to find the exact minute of birth</term> of life, he himself contradicted himself in his later sayings with greater discord than in the other things we have mentioned; we have explained this reasoning in the 4th part of this, our book, in the chapter on the *hylech* and the *alchocoden* <term>alchocoden: the planet that determines the number of years a person might live</term>, which anyone who wishes to see may find there. Likewise, he contradicted himself in his sayings when he spoke on knowing the significator of kings and their officials; for one time he took this from the ascendant, and another time from the tenth house. This occurs in his book of the *Centiloquium* <note>original: "centiloquij," the 100 Aphorisms attributed to Ptolemy</note> in many aphorisms of that book, specifically in words 30, 3, 1, 39, 83, and 85.

And Al-Kindi, though he was a noble man and very high in this science, a complete sage of profound sayings—who was among the Moorish sages such as Ptolemy was among the Gentile sages, except that both wrote in a very closed and profound manner—spoke very secretively, with very deep reasons and long reaches of intellect. Their books are very difficult to understand, such that mid-level students of this science cannot help themselves with them, much less beginners. Thus, the usefulness of their books is very small, because they are of no value except to those who are already very wise in this science, and those whom God has helped by His grace and reward, giving them the intellect to open the locked depths and understand the difficult meanings.

Al-Kindi has among his books one book divided into two parts consisting of 8 leaves, in which he included the entire science of astronomy; yet if a good sage wished to explain it, it would not fit into 8 large volumes. But the error in which Al-Kindi erred is this: he denied the division of the ancient sages regarding the **faces** of the signs <term>faces: 10-degree segments of a zodiac sign, also known as decans</term>. He says in that book of his, in the 40th aphorism, what we wish to say word for word, just as it is in his book: "And each of the signs is divided into three parts, and in each part are ten degrees; and these parts are named 'faces' because they are the significators of the faces." Most men gave the first face of **Aries** to Mars, the second to the Sun, and the third to Venus, and so on according to this order in all the faces of the signs by the order of the planetary spheres, one after another, until the last face of **Pisces** belongs to Mars. But this division is not well-placed, nor does it agree with itself, because the last face of Pisces is followed by the first face of Aries, and thus according to this division, two faces are given one after another to the same planet [Mars].

planets: however, the division must be right and complete according to our understanding, just as we placed it in our greater book called the *Book of the Secrets of the Stars*. There, we set out the division of the rulers according to the order of the signs in this manner: we gave the first **face** <term>face: a ten-degree subdivision of a zodiac sign, also known as a decan</term> of Aries to Mars, who is the lord of Aries; the second to Venus, who is the lady of Taurus; the third to Mercury, who is the lord of Gemini; and so on until the end of the signs. We began the first face of the next fiery sign <note>Leo</note> similarly with Mars. Following this order, the last face of Scorpio returned to Jupiter, who is the lord of Pisces; and the last face of Pisces likewise fell to Jupiter, who is the lord of Pisces. Then the division of the first face returns to Mars, that is, of Aries. Here ends the statement of Al-Kindi <note>original: "alkindi"; Al-Kindi was a 9th-century Islamic philosopher and astrologer</note>. But I say that he who reproached this did not understand it correctly; for the last face of Pisces and the first face of Aries follow one after another and belong to one planet <note>Mars</note>. This does not happen in all twelve signs except for the **Sun** alone. He neither looked into nor knew this in the partition he set down: because there the faces follow each other in three places for Saturn: once in the sign of Cancer, another in the sign of Scorpio, and a third in Pisces. He erred similarly in his book in the 9th chapter of the *40 Aphorisms* when he spoke of battles and litigations.

And in the first faces which begin to rise against others, he spoke thus in that place: that when **Mars** is in the Eastern part of the sky—which is from the 10th degree of Taurus to the 10th degree of Leo, and from the 10th degree of Scorpio to the 10th degree of Aquarius—while Mars himself is in these parts, we should determine that the invaders of a dispute begin from the Eastern parts, coming from that side. And when Mars is in the Western part of the sky—which is from the 10th degree of Leo to the 10th degree of Scorpio, and from the 10th degree of Aquarius to the 10th degree of Taurus—while Mars is in these parts, we should determine that the invaders begin from the Western parts and come from that side. According to this statement, the sky with its twelve signs would be entirely Eastern or Western and nothing more. In truth, it is not so; for the sky has North, South, West, and East. Likewise, invaders have four parts from which they can come: East, West, North, and South. And perhaps very quickly the invaders might come—or a king wishing to invade—from any of these parts. Because there will perhaps be a confrontation of war between East and West, or perhaps between North and South by a king or invaders, the partition we ought to follow in this matter is as follows: Mars, so long as he is from the 10th degree of Taurus to the 10th degree of Leo, is **Eastern**. From the 10th degree of Leo to the 10th degree of Scorpio, he is **Southern**. From the 10th degree of Scorpio to the 10th degree of Aquarius, he is **Western**. And from the 10th degree of Aquarius to the 10th degree of Taurus, he is **Northern**. We ought to follow this partition and reasoning in battles and litigations; truly, it would be long to recount the errors and discords of the world. For Al-Kindi was in all ways more intelligent than all other wise men in the judgments of astronomy, and more complete than others in this science. This is excepted: that his sayings are not well explained, nor are his words, because they are very "closed" <note>meaning obscure or cryptic</note> and his intentions are very profound. In this, he is the opposite of Albumazar <note>Abu Ma'shar, a famous Persian astrologer</note>, because Albumazar has little insight despite his many words and long reasonings; he confirmed few things though he spoke much. And in his

<column-break/>

many reasonings, the meaning was lost. He is like a man making a fire at night who gathers both good and bad wood; for such are his sayings. And all the wise men of this science, the **gentiles** as well as the **Moors** <note>referring to both European/Pagan and Arabic scholars</note>, say that from the **ascendant** <term>ascendant: the sign rising on the eastern horizon at a specific moment</term> to the 10th house is "ascending," and from the 10th to the 7th is "descending," and from the 7th to the 4th is "ascending," and from the 4th to the ascendant is "descending." But I do not believe this to be true, nor do I grant this partition. The correct partition, and that which we ought to believe, is that from the 4th house to the 10th is **ascending**, and from the 10th house, passing through the 7th to the 4th, is **descending**. Indeed, we do not care nor have the need to speak much in reproaches; truly I do not believe, nor do I say, that I should apply myself to the first degree of any of them. We wish, therefore, to return to our purpose of speaking and to take from their stated opinions those which we understand to be right and true: to follow and affirm them, and to destroy the others and not look back, if God wills.

### # The first part concerning the knowledge of the location of the significator of the sick person.

The location of the **significator** <term>significator: a planet or house representing a specific person or topic</term> of the sick person is as we have said. Observe the **almuten** <term>almuten: the planet with the most combined dignity and strength at a specific point in the zodiac</term> over the ascendant, and the almuten over the Sun and over the Moon, and the lord of the **Part of Fortune** <note>a mathematical point in a chart representing well-being</note> as well as the lord of the hour. Take that one among them as the significator of the sick person which is the strongest in the figure; from that planet, you shall know their state, what shall become of them, and to what their infirmity shall lead. From the 6th house and its lord, and from the planet from which the Moon separates, you shall know the infirmity they have. From the 8th house and its lord, you shall know their death. From the 4th house and its lord, and from the lord of the Moon's house, you shall know their end. From the **term** <term>term: a specific set of degrees within a sign ruled by a planet</term> of the degree and the house, you shall determine the cause of their death and from where it shall come.

### # The second part concerning the knowledge of the infirmity, whether it is in the spirit, or in the body, or in both together.

If you find the Moon and the ascendant both **unfortunate** <note>afflicted by difficult planets like Mars or Saturn</note> and both their lords fortunate and safe from misfortunes, judge that the infirmity is in the body, not in the spirit. If you find the lord of the ascendant and the lord of the Moon's house both unfortunate, but the Moon and the ascendant both fortunate and free from misfortunes, judge that the infirmity is in the spirit <note>meaning the mind or mental health</note>, not in the body. If all are unfortunate and the misfortune is common to all, judge that the infirmity is in both, namely, the spirit and the body. Masha'allah <note>original: "messa hala"; an 8th-century Jewish-Arab astrologer</note> said that when a misfortune aspects the Moon and not the ascendant, the infirmity will be in the body. If a misfortune aspects the ascendant and not the Moon, the infirmity will be in the spirit, such as a loss of the senses and what is similar to this in matters properly pertaining to the spirit. And if a misfortune aspects both without an aspect from a **fortune** <note>a helpful planet like Jupiter or Venus</note>, it will destroy the body and the sick person shall die.

### # The third part concerning the knowledge of in which part of the body the infirmity is located.

Observe the **Almuten** <term>Almuten: from the Arabic *al-mubtazz*, this is the planet that holds the most essential power or "dignity" over a specific point in the zodiac</term> which is the **indicator of the illness**, and it will be the primary guide in this matter. You must see in which of the twelve houses of the astrological figure it has been **afflicted** <note>original: "infortunatus"; in astrology, this means being weakened or negatively influenced by "malefic" planets like Saturn or Mars</note> in this manner:

The **Ascendant** <term>Ascendant: the sign rising on the eastern horizon at a specific moment; the 1st House</term> is the indicator of the **head**; the **second house** the **neck**; the **third** the **hands** and **shoulders**; the **fourth** the **chest**, the **lungs**, and what is contained within them; the **fifth** the **stomach**, **heart**, **liver**, and those parts that resemble them or govern the limbs; the **sixth** the **belly** and **ribs**; the **seventh** the **intestines**, **viscera**, and **groin**; the **eighth** the **female womb**, the **male testicles**, and the **base of the bladder** and **kidneys**; the **ninth** the **flesh of the buttocks** and the **nature of excrement**; the **tenth** the **thighs** and **kneecaps**; the **eleventh** the **shins** from the kneecap downward; and the **twelfth house** is the indicator of the **feet**. In whichever of these houses the indicator is afflicted, judge that the illness is located in that specific member. This illness will be of the nature of the house where the affliction was seen with the clearest view.

¶ And if you wish to know on which side of the body the illness is located—the **right** or the **left**—observe that afflicted indicator: if it is afflicted **above the earth** <note>in the visible part of the sky above the horizon</note>, say that the illness is on the **right side**; if it is **below the earth**, say it is on the **left side**. And if it is afflicted in a **sign of long ascension** <term>signs of long ascension: signs that take longer to rise over the horizon (in the northern hemisphere: Cancer through Sagittarius)</term>, say the illness occupies the **whole body**. If it is in a **sign of equal ascension**, say the illness is in the **heart**. If it is in a **sign of short ascension**, say the illness is a **diminishing of a limb**.

¶ The **Part** <term>Part: a calculated mathematical point in a chart, often called an "Arabic Part" or "Lot"</term> by which the location of an illness is known is calculated from the degree of the **Lord of the Hour** <note>the planet ruling the specific planetary hour when the illness began</note> to the degree of the **Sun**, and projected from the beginning of **Aries**. Assign 30 degrees to each sign, and in the place where the number ends, say the illness is in the member assigned to that sign, beginning with the head for Aries and proceeding through the order of the signs. Another "part" is found another way: observe how many degrees of the **Ascendant sign** have risen in equal degrees and multiply them by the degrees of ascension for that sign. Project the resulting number from the degree of the Ascendant, giving 30 degrees to each sign. Where the number ends, the illness is in that member, beginning with the head at the Ascendant and following the order previously mentioned.

### ¶ The 4th part: on knowing if the patient will be healed or not.

Observe the **Moon**, the **Sun**, and the **Almuten of the Ascendant**. If they are free from **afflictions** <note>malefic planetary influences</note> and do not have a direct **aspect** <term>aspect: a specific geometric angle between planets, such as a square or opposition, believed to transmit influence</term> with the **Lord of the House of Death** <note>the planet ruling the 8th House</note>, say that the patient will escape that illness. And if two of these three indicators are free from afflictions and lack an aspect with the Lord of the House of Death, they will likewise escape, by God's good pleasure. 

And if even one of the two indicators is safe from afflictions, and the other two do not aspect the Lord of the House of Death, the patient will escape the illness—provided the affliction of the two is not by **bodily conjunction** <note>when two planets are at the same degree</note> or by a powerful malefic influence, especially if that malefic planet is the ruler of the **4th**, **8th**, or **2nd houses**. For if two indicators have such an affliction, it will be a miracle if the patient escapes. And if it is the Almuten of the Ascendant or the Moon—especially if she is the **Lord of the Time** <note>the planet ruling the current period of the patient's life</note>—or even the Sun if he is the Lord of the Time: if all these indicators, or the strongest among them, have an aspect with the Lord of the House of Death, the patient cannot be delivered from death. Every time an indicator applies to an affliction, the illness strengthens until the time it separates from it.

But if you find powerful **benefic planets** <note>original: "fortunas"; usually Jupiter or Venus</note> in the angles, it indicates health and escape.

The time of that recovery will be when the Moon reaches that benefic planet which blessed the sign of the ill member. If malefic planets are present without any aspect from a benefic, it will be a time of great severity for the illness when the Moon reaches that malefic planet; and if the Moon is then in the **term** <term>term: a small subdivision of a sign ruled by a specific planet</term> of a malefic, it signifies death.

Similarly, if at the start of the illness the Moon is in the place where **Mars** was at birth, and Mars is in that same place or aspecting her, it signifies severity of illness and heat <note>fever</note>, with danger and fear in that illness.

If the Moon at the start is where a malefic was at birth, but a **benefic planet** is with her or aspecting her, the illness will be severe, though the patient will escape and be healed. 

If the Moon at the start of the illness is in the sign of the **6th house** of the birth chart, or the **4th** or **8th**, and there was a malefic at birth in whichever of those three places the Moon now sits, it signifies a severe illness. ### ¶ Fifth part on knowing if the illness is long or short.

### ¶ Sixth part on the time when there will be health or death.

<image-desc>Decorative woodcut initial 'E' depicting a seated figure, possibly an authority or physician, in an interior setting.</image-desc>And the time of death will be when the **Almuten** of the Ascendant: or the Moon joins with the Lord of the house of death: or with the misfortune that afflicted it: or when it moves to the square or opposition of it: and then will be the time of death. And especially if that indication was through such a movement that was between them: and if it be in another way: it will be the hour of death: when it moves to that which indicated death by its movement to the degree of that which it approached bodily: or to the degree of the squares: and then will be the hour of death. And likewise when the Moon joins with the misfortunes by the body of that misfortune which indicated death: or when it moves to the house of death. And if the indication of death was because of the combustion of the indicator: when that indicator moves to the degree of combustion: then there will be death. And likewise observe how many degrees are between the mover and that which it moves toward among those which indicated death. And if they are in **movable signs** <note>Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn; these indicate fast action</note> count them as days: and in **common signs** <note>Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces</note> months: and if they are in **fixed signs** <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius</note> the indicators will testify to the length of the illness in years. And if that mover which indicated death is **Saturn**: give to each degree a month or a year: and if it be **Mars** give to each degree a day or a month: and observe in this according to the strength: the place and the indicators which you had concerning the length of the illness or its brevity: and then will be death. And if the indication of death was by a misfortune that happened in the Ascendant or through the Lord of the eighth who was in it or in another angle: when that indicator moves to the degree of that angle: then there will be death. And the time of health will be because of the movement of the Almuten and its application to the fortunes: or when it moves to its own house or exaltation: or that it changes the aspect which it had in the figure: or that it turns **direct** if it was **retrograde** <term>Retrograde: when a planet appears to move backward; it often signifies delays or reversals of fortune</term>. And if the Lord of the house of death is far from it and from its aspect, this is a sign of health. And if the sign of health was through the aspect of a fortune to the indicator, when it moves to the degree of the aspect: then there will be health. And if it was through a conjunction, when it moves to the degree of the conjunction: there will be health. And especially if that application or conjunction was in one of the angles. And if that indication was through the movement of a fortune to the degree of the Ascendant, when that fortune is in that very degree of the Ascendant: then there will be health if God wills.

## ¶ The eighth part on the increase and decrease of the illness.

And when you find this signifier separating himself from these aforesaid places, and the Moon separating herself from the infortunes and applying to the fortunes, and the signifier applying to the fortunes, or a fortune to him, then the illness is diminished and decreases.

## ¶ The tenth part of this chapter on the end of the illness and if he will die a bad death.

->### Chapter 3: On buying captives and servants.<-

<image-desc>Ornamental initial letter C with floral patterns.</image-desc>When you are asked about a servant or captive whom someone wishes to buy: whether that purchase will happen or not. And if that Lot, or the lord of its house, be in the Ascendant, or apply to the lord of the Ascendant, or the lord of the Ascendant to them: judge according to how you find these things.

->### On knowing in what place there is a mark on a person's body.<-

### ¶ Chapter 4. On the question of a captive, whether he shall be freed or not.

<image-desc>Decorative drop cap 'C' showing a foliage pattern within a square frame.</image-desc>

When a captive or a servant <note>The Latin "servus" can mean servant or slave depending on the legal context; here, the context of buying and selling suggests an enslaved status.</note>—whom a man can buy or sell—asks you whether he shall be freed or not: assign the Ascendant <note>The zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of the question.</note> and its lord to him; assign the Moon to the servant; and assign the Midheaven <note>The 10th house, representing authority.</note> and its lord and the Sun to the master of the servant. Afterward, look to the Moon and the lord of the Ascendant: and whichever of them you find to be stronger in the chart, see if you find him separated from the lord of the 10th house or from the Sun. If he is separating himself from either of them and does not apply <note>An "application" is when a faster planet moves toward a mathematical aspect with a slower one.</note> to another planet: judge that he shall be freed; otherwise, he shall not. ¶ And if the lord of the Ascendant and the Moon (or the stronger of them) applies to the lord of the 10th, or if the lord of the 10th applies to the lord of the Ascendant—or if there is a planet that joins their lights or carries the light <term>translation of light: when a third planet mediates between two that do not aspect each other</term> from one to the other—and if that application, conjunction, or carrying of light is by a square <note>An aspect of 90 degrees, usually indicating difficulty.</note> or opposition, or conjunction, and is without reception <note>Reception occurs when one planet is in a sign where the other has dignity; it suggests cooperation.</note>: judge that that master is the possessor of that servant and is cruel toward him; he will have no mercy on him, nor shall the servant be separated from him until he dies. And if there is reception there: say that the master will repent of the evil he does to the servant and it will displease him; nonetheless, he will never let him go, especially if the sign in which the significator <note>The planet representing the person in the chart.</note> resides is fixed, or if the application happens from an angle <note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, which represent the strongest areas of a chart.</note>. But if that aspect, application, carrying of light, or conjunction is by a trine or sextile <note>Harmonious aspects of 120 and 60 degrees.</note> and is with reception: it signifies that the master will be gentle and good to his servant. And being "oriental" <note>Rising before the sun.</note> alone signifies a strong separation; however, "recess" <note>Moving away from a station or the sun.</note> is firmer in signifying separation—but beware that he does not have another application while in recess, for if he does, he might perhaps return to servitude.

### ¶ Chapter 5. On the question a master makes regarding a servant, whether he will separate himself or not.

<image-desc>Decorative drop cap 'I' showing a foliage pattern within a square frame.</image-desc>

In this question, give the Ascendant to the master and the sixth house and its lord to the servant: and look for the application, or translation, or collection <note>Astrological conditions where planets transfer influence to one another.</note> that exists between them, according to what I told you in the preceding chapter. And if the application, translation, or collection is by square and without reception: it signifies the cruelty of the master toward the servant, and that he does him evil and will never free him. And if there is reception with that square: it signifies that the master will repent of the evil he does to the servant and will be brought back to doing good for him, yet he will not free him because of it. And if the lord of the 6th house separates himself from the lord of the Ascendant: it signifies that the servant shall be freed, provided the lord of the 6th has no application with another planet during that separation.

### ¶ Chapter 6. On the question a servant makes, whether he will leave the possession of his master by sale or not: and how many masters he will have after he leaves that master.

<column-break/>

<image-desc>Decorative drop cap 'D' showing a foliage pattern within a square frame.</image-desc>

In this question, give the Ascendant and its lord to the servant; the Midheaven and its lord to the master of the servant; and the eleventh house and its lord to the first buyer. And give the twelfth house and its lord to the second buyer who will have him after that. And the second house from the Ascendant to the third who will have him after that. And the third house to the fourth, and thus you shall go through the order of the houses until you find an application, until it is cut off <note>The "abscission of light," where a third planet's aspect blocks the main significators from connecting.</note>: and in this place he shall remain, where the significance was cut off, according to what we said in the chapter on the separation of the servant in the significance of the Moon. The Midheaven is the significator of his mastery <note>his trade or profession</note> and the work he has. And from the lord of the Ascendant, who is the significator of the servant, you will know what price the servant may be, according to his place in the figure and his state: whether he is in his own house, or exaltation, or fall <note>The "essential dignities" which describe the planet's inherent strength.</note>, or triplicity; or whether he is oriental or occidental. And you shall give his price according to the number of his "minor years" <note>A specific number of years assigned to each planet in traditional astrology.</note> in units or tens according to the state of that planet, as we said in the chapter on substance. If you find the lord of the Ascendant in an angle, not giving its power to a planet that is remote from an angle: judge that the servant shall not leave his master's power. And if the lord of the Ascendant gives its power to a planet that is not in an angle: it signifies that the servant shall leave his master's power. And if the Moon is of the same manner—especially if the disposition of the lord of the Ascendant or the Moon is received by the lord of the 3rd, or the lord of the 11th, or the 7th: the significance will be firmer that he shall leave his master's power. And if Saturn is combust <note>So close to the Sun that it is "burnt up" and weakened.</note>: he shall die before he leaves his master's power. And if the Moon or the lord of the Ascendant are separating themselves from the Midheaven or its lord and applying to the lord of the eleventh: the servant shall leave his master's power and enter the power of another through sale. And look then at how many planets the lord of the Ascendant or the Moon applies to in that sign: and say that he shall have that many masters after the one he has. Consider afterward those applications: and those which you find to be by opposition or square and without reception, say that that master will be bad and cruel (according to its place in the number of applications); and whichever of those applications is by trine or sextile and with reception signifies that that master will be good and gentle and will do him good. ¶ And when you wish to know at what time the sale will be: look at the time when both significators join by square or opposition or conjunction. And if there is reception between them: judge that the sale will be at that time. If there is no reception between them: say that the sale will be at that time, but with hardship and labor.

### ¶ Chapter 7. On the question of a master, whether he will sell the servant or not.

If someone asks you whether he will sell his servant or not, and how many will have him after him: give the Ascendant and its lord to the master of the servant; and the sixth house and its lord, along with the Moon, to the servant; and the second house and its lord to the buyer who buys him from him. And afterward consider if you find the Moon and the lord of the sixth (or one of them) separating itself and applying to the lord of the second house: it signifies that the sale shall take place.

### ¶ Chapter 8. On the question of a servant, whether the master he has is better for him than another.

Look in this to the lord of the Ascendant; and if you find him received in his own place, say that the master he has is better for him. And if the lord of the 7th house is similarly received in his own place, another master will be better for him than the one he has. Afterward, consider from whom the Moon is separating and to whom she applies; if she is received by the one from whom she separated, the master he has is better for him; and if she is not received by the one she separated from, but is received by the one she applies to, say that another master is better for him than the one he has. And if you find none of these significations, look to the lord of the Ascendant and the Moon; if both—or one of them—are received in the sign in which they are, or if that sign is suitable to him, say that the master he has is better for him. And if neither of them is received in that sign in which they are, nor is it suitable to him, but is received in the second sign toward which they are going, or if it is suitable to him, say that another master will be better for him than the one he has.

### ¶ Chapter 9. On the question of whether I shall have such a servant as an inheritance or not.

Look in this to the lord of the Ascendant and the Moon; and if they apply to the lord of the 7th, which is the house of the substance <note>property or assets</note> of servants, say that he shall have him. And similarly if the lord of the 7th applies to the lord of the Ascendant, or if he is in the Ascendant, or if the lord of the Ascendant or the Moon is in the 7th, or if you find any planet carrying the light <note>Translation of light: when a faster planet moves from an aspect with one planet to an aspect with another, "connecting" them</note> from one to the other, he shall have him; otherwise not. And if you are asked regarding the substance of a servant, whether the seeker shall have it, look to the third house from the Ascendant, which is the 10th from the house of servants. And if you find the lord of the Ascendant and the Moon (or one of them) applying to the lord of the 3rd from the Ascendant, or the lord of the 3rd applying to the lord of the Ascendant, say that he shall have that substance. And similarly if the lord of the Ascendant is in the 3rd, or the lord of the 3rd is in the Ascendant, or you find any planet carrying the light from one to the other—namely,

### ¶ Chapter 10. Whether a captive shall be liberated or not.

When you are asked about a captive, or a man taken because of the king’s anger, or about a servant whom his master holds captive because of anger: begin in this by looking at the Moon and Mercury. If you find them in movable signs <note>Aries, Cancer, Libra, and Capricorn; signs that indicate change and action</note> and fortified by the "fortunes" <note>Benefic planets, usually Jupiter and Venus</note>, it signifies escape. And if Mercury alone is fortified in any way by the fortunes, it signifies the escape of the captive specifically. And if you find at the beginning of the captivity Jupiter in the Ascendant, or bodily joined with the Moon, or aspecting her with a fortunate aspect, it signifies that he shall escape easily and quickly. And if Venus is with the Moon in the Ascendant, or Mercury with Jupiter aspecting the Moon (or both joined with her), it signifies that he shall escape and leave the prison quickly, and he shall have good fortune after that. And when the Moon is applied to either of the two fortunes, it similarly signifies an easy escape. And if the fortunes aspect the lord of the Moon’s house, he shall similarly escape and leave the prison; and if the lord of the Moon’s house aspects the Moon, it signifies that he shall escape, and the one who took him shall release him voluntarily, and shall repent that he took him, and shall restore him to his grace and love.

### ¶ Chapter 11. On knowing if the bewitched <note>original: "toricatus?"; likely a corruption of "toxicatus" (poisoned) or related to the following vernacular term "fechiçados"</note> shall be healed or not.

When you wish to know if the bewitched <note>original: "fechiçados"; from the Portuguese/Spanish "feitiço," meaning a spell, hex, or charm</note> shall be healed or not, consider if you find the Part of Fortune joined with the fortunes, or the fortunes applying to it, or if they have any testimony with it; say that he shall be healed. And if the "infortunes" <note>Malefic planets, usually Saturn and Mars</note> have testimony with it, it is bad for him, and he shall not be healed. And if the Moon testifies for him—such as being in her own house, exaltation, or triplicity, or in a good place for her, such as the Ascendant, the Midheaven, or the house of trust <note>the 11th house</note>—or if she applies to the fortunes and aspects them, it signifies that he shall be healed. And if you find the contrary, judge the opposite. And if you find the Ascendant in a movable sign and the fortunes aspecting it, say that he shall be healed; and if it is the contrary, he shall not be healed.
