### Chapter 13. On the seventh house and its questions

<image-desc>Decorative drop cap 'H' showing a male and female figure facing each other in an outdoor setting, likely representing marriage or partnership.</image-desc>This house signifies women, marriages, the causes of marriages, sexual relations with women, grandfathers, adversaries, the legal advocacy of cases, the state of old age, the place to which a traveler goes, the sought-after thing for which a seeker inquires, lost property and theft, a person who is not present (and information about them through signs, including how they are faring in the place where they are and what has become of them). It also signifies a thing which does not exist or has not been found, hidden matters, things concealed or denied; it signifies the withdrawing of committed evils, reproof, and great quarrels; foreign men, a lowering of status, the death of enemies, the friends of brothers, the children of friends, and killings. Furthermore, it signifies buying, selling, and hunting. ¶ The first lord of its triplicity <note>A group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element</note> is the significator of the first wife a man shall have. The second lord signifies the second wife with whom he shall contract marriage and the pleasures that shall come to him. The third lord is the significator of oppositions. Judge according to the power, status, and location of each of these. If the significator of women is looking toward the lord of the Ascendant or the Ascendant itself with a friendly aspect <note>A "sextile" or "trine" aspect, suggesting harmony</note>, it signifies joy and agreement. If that aspect is an unfriendly one—which is from the fourth <note>a "square" aspect</note> or opposition—it signifies quarrels and discords. If the question is about some woman being petitioned and the thought of the seeker falls in this house, know that this house, by its nature and property, signifies women, adversaries, the place where a person is going who is not present, the location of a thief, and theft. If you find a fire sign in the question in this house, and the significator of the question and thought is in it, say that the question is about adversaries, battles, or those who contradict. If you find an earthy sign there, say the question is about age. If you find an airy sign there, say it is about a woman. If you find a water sign there, say the question is about a person who is not present. The color of this house on its own, in whatever sign it may be, is the leopard <note>original: "pardus"; meaning a variegated or spotted pattern</note>, because it tends toward black, and within it is darkness and greenness. And if there is a sign in the seventh house

<column-break/>

signifying comeliness, beauty, and clarity—and these signs are Gemini, Libra, Virgo, and Scorpio—and after these, those which have less comeliness and clarity—Taurus, Sagittarius, and Capricorn—or if its lord, or the Part of Marriage, or its lord, or Venus or the Moon are in any of these signs signifying comeliness, it signifies that the person born shall have beautiful, well-proportioned, and clear-skinned women. In the births of women, look for this same thing, except by swapping the Moon for the Sun; for if the Sun is in the signs of comeliness, it signifies that the woman shall have a clear and handsome husband.

### Chapter 14. On knowing whether a marriage will occur or not.

<image-desc>Decorative drop cap 'C' containing a profile portrait of a man, possibly the author or an authority figure.</image-desc>When someone asks you about a marriage, whether it will happen or not: look at the Ascendant <note>The sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of the question</note>, its lord, the Moon, and the planet from which the Moon is separating; give these as significators for the person asking. Give the seventh house, its lord, and the planet to which the Moon applies as significators for the person about whom the question is asked. If the seeker is male, add the Sun to his significators and make it a participant in the meaning. If the seeker is a woman, add Venus to her significators and make it a participant. Specifically, if the seeker is a woman, give her Venus with the Moon and the lord of the Ascendant, and the planet from which the Moon separates; and for the man, give him the Sun with the seventh house and its lord, and the planet to which the Moon applies. Afterward, look at what kind of application <note>The movement of one planet toward an aspect with another</note> the lord of the Ascendant or the Moon has with the lord of the seventh. Also, look at what kind of application the planet from which the Moon separates has with the planet to which it applies, or Venus with the Sun. If the lord of the Ascendant or the Moon applies to the lord of the seventh, or the planet from which the Moon separates applies to the planet it is approaching, or the lord of the Ascendant or the Moon is in the seventh, it signifies that the seeker shall have the thing sought, though with many petitions and prayers. ### ¶ For knowing by what marriage is hindered.

<margin>If it is feminine, look to the mother's side.</margin>
<image-desc>A decorative woodcut initial 'Q' containing a grotesque mask or face.</image-desc>
**W**hen you wish to know this: look at the significators as previously described, and consider the planets receiving those significations. For if the receiver is afflicted <note>original: "infortunatus"; weakened by a harsh planetary aspect</note> or "falling from an angle" <note>original: "cadens ab angulo"; located in a weak house of the chart where it has less power to act</note>: it signifies that the matter will fail after it is nearly finished. 

If the "afflicter" causing the damage is the Lord of the Second or Eighth House: it signifies the disturbance of the marriage will be due to a disagreement over the dowry. If the afflicter is the Lord of the Sixth House: it signifies the disturbance will be due to evil things said about the man’s lineage. If the afflicter is the Lord of the Twelfth House: it will be because of evil things said about the woman’s lineage. If the afflicter is the Lord of the Fourth House: it will come from the parents. 

If the planet and the zodiac sign are masculine, it will be because of the father and his lineage. Use this same method for all other signs according to their natures and properties. And if the indication that the matter will not happen is due to a planet "cutting off" the light between them <note>An aspect that prevents two planets from completing their connection</note>: say that the disturbance will be of the nature of the house that the "cutting" planet rules. For example: if it is the Lord of the Second or Eighth House, the disturbance is for the dowry; if the Lord of the Third, it is because of brothers; if the Lord of the Fourth, it is because of parents. If it is the Lord of the Fifth House: it signifies that the woman previously had another husband and has a child, or that the man has a child by another woman, and the disturbance is by reason of the children. 

If it is the Lord of the Sixth House: the disturbance will be because of a blemish <note>original: "macula"</note> or illness she has in her body. Look at the other signs in this same way. If the indication that the marriage should not be is because of an affliction to a planet that "carries the light" from one significator to another: it signifies the disturbance is because of messengers traveling between them with ill intent. But if the planet that "cuts the light" is a "fortune" <note>original: "fortuna"; a benefic planet like Jupiter or Venus</note> and its nature is compatible with the significators: it signifies the marriage will happen with delay and will eventually be completed. The worst and greatest misfortune in a "cutting of light" occurs when the planet doing the cutting is the Lord of the Eighth, Fourth, or Twelfth house, or if it is in a fixed sign or in an angle; for

other "cuttings" that are not done in these ways are not so bad.

### ¶ Chapter 15. On the completed marriage, and whether it is better for the man than for the woman.

<image-desc>A decorative woodcut initial 'A' featuring foliage and floral motifs.</image-desc>
**O**bserve in this matter: if the Sun is afflicted by the ill-fortunes <note>The Sun represents the husband in a woman's chart</note>: say that it is bad for the man. If you find Venus afflicted <note>Venus represents the wife</note>: say that it will be bad for the woman. If you find the Moon afflicted, or falling from the angles into the eighth or twelfth houses, or "void of course" <note>original: "cursu vacuam"; making no further connections with other planets before leaving its current sign</note>: say that it will be bad for both, and they will have anxieties and hardships according to the nature of the place, the afflicting planet, and the sign. 

If the affliction of the Moon is by a square <note>original: "quartum"; a 90-degree angle</note> or an opposition from the ill-fortunes while the Moon is in an angle: it signifies they will have quarrels and [harsh] words, and that one will be separated from the other. If the same happens by a trine <note>120-degree angle</note> or a sextile <note>60-degree angle</note>: evil, anxiety, or illness will happen to them. If it occurs by a conjunction: one of them will die. It is even worse and stronger if the conjunction occurs in the Ascendant or the Midheaven. If this happens in a masculine sign, the man will die and meet an evil fate; if in a feminine sign, this will happen to the woman; if in a common sign <note>A "mutable" sign, like Gemini or Virgo</note>, the evil will happen to both. If that evil occurs by an opposition or square: look at the sign the Moon is in to see if it is masculine or feminine, and judge for the man or woman accordingly.

If in this situation you find a "fortune" <note>benefic planet</note> instead of an "ill-fortune": change your judgment. If it is by a square or opposition: judge that they will have harmony and will endure for a long time. If by a trine or sextile: it signifies that both will have good fortune, lawfulness, profits, and riches—especially if the Moon is in a fixed sign or in one of the angles. 

If the planet bringing fortune does so by a sextile: that which they receive will come from friends and brothers. If by the first square <note>The square aspect formed as a planet moves away from the Moon</note>: it will come from the inheritances of the dead and things buried underground. If it is by the first trine: it will be from children after they have them. If it is by an opposition: it will be what he gets from journeys and from women. If it is by the second trine: it will be from journeys and religion. If it is by the second square: it will be what he gets from the King's side. If it is by a conjunction: it will be from the work of hands.

If you find the significators of the man in masculine signs and the woman’s in feminine signs: it will be good for both. If you find Venus and the Moon in feminine signs: the good and improvement will be more for the woman than the man. If you find them in masculine signs: it is better for the man than the woman. If you find the Sun and Jupiter in feminine signs: it will be better for the woman. If you find them in masculine signs: it will be better for the man. When the Sun is in a masculine sign: it signifies that the marriage is good for the man and bad for the woman. If the Moon and Sun are both in a feminine sign: it signifies the marriage is good for the woman and bad for the man. If the Moon is in a feminine sign and the Sun in a masculine sign: the marriage is good for both.

### Chapter 16. On knowing the future harmony and discord between a man and a woman.

<image-desc>Ornamental woodcut initial 'S' decorated with scrolling foliage and vine motifs within a square border.</image-desc>
**S**ignificator of what happens regarding good or evil between a man and a woman is the Midheaven <note>the 10th house, representing the social status of the union</note> from the Ascendant, and the tenth house from the Moon; and the significator of the end of their negotiations and of the dowry is the fourth house from the Ascendant, its Lord, and the Lord of the Moon's house. If you find a fortune in it, it signifies concord. If you find a fortune there, say the opposite. If the Lord of the fourth house is retrograde or afflicted, it signifies evil and loss in the end. And if it aspects the significators that indicated the completion of the marriage through their applications: if that aspect is an opposition <note>planets 180 degrees apart</note>, it signifies anger, brawls, and lawsuits between them—especially if there is no "reception" <note>a condition where planets "host" each other in their home signs, easing tensions</note> between them. If the aspect is a square <note>original: "de quarta"; planets 90 degrees apart</note>, it similarly signifies brawls; however, they sometimes agree and sometimes fight. If the application is a conjunction <note>planets in the same degree</note>, it signifies that they will be angry and one will hate the other. <column-break/>

properties, except that the tenth house and the angle of the earth <note>the 4th house</note> signify "mixers" <note>meddlers or matchmakers</note> who place evil between them. Likewise, if the planet from which the Moon separates does not aspect the planet to which she applies at the start of the marriage, it signifies there will be neither love nor agreement between them. What is more, along with this, strife and enmity will happen between the relatives of the man and the woman. If both the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the seventh house are "falling" <note>cadent, or in weak houses</note> from an angle, the stronger one will have the truer significations. Consider which of those planets is stronger in the question, and judge that he shall be more weighted <note>influential</note> over the other. That is, if the Moon is in the sign in which it was at the birth of one, but in the twelfth house of the birth of the other: judge that the one whose Moon it is shall be the victor over the other, and the other shall obey him like a servant. ### ¶ Chapter 17. Regarding a man’s question: whether he will have her through marriage or fornication.

Look at the applications involving the three significators for the seeker: the Lord of the Ascendant, the Sun, and the planet from which the Moon is separating. Compare these with the three significators of the woman: the Lord of the seventh house, Venus, and the planet to which the Moon is applying. If you find these applications occur after they have had an application with the two "infortunes" <note>malefic planets</note>, Saturn and Mars, or with one of them, judge that it will be without fornication and will be a lawful marriage. But if his significators, after one has applied to the other, then apply to the infortunes (or one of them), it signifies it will be through marriage first, and afterward through fornication <note>meaning adultery or an illicit affair later in life</note>.

### ¶ Chapter 18. Regarding a question by a woman: whether she has a friend who loves her, or she a man.

Look at the *almuten* <note>term: the planet with the most combined dignity and strength at a specific point</note> of the Ascendant and the Moon. If you find one of them joined with Mars in the same degree, judge that she has a lover in the house with her who sleeps with her. If they are not in the same degree but are in the same sign, say he is her neighbor and lives near her. And if that significator has separated from Mars, say she had a lover but left him. And if that significator applies to Mars, and Mars is in one of his own houses <note>Aries or Scorpio</note>, say she has a man who seeks her out to lie

If it is to Mercury, she loves a young scribe or a merchant, or a man skilled in handiwork. If it is to Venus, he loves a woman for that same kind of work <note>possibly implying a fellow artisan or someone of similar social habits</note>. 

And if Jupiter aspects her significators, it signifies that she repented of what she was doing and removed herself from him. If the planet aspecting is the Sun, it signifies that a man of high rank had sexual relations with her, because of whom she left the first man out of fear. If the aspecting planet is Venus, it signifies that a woman had relations with her <note>or him</note>, because of which she left; and in this way you shall judge for all the planets according to their natures, provided the significators have separated from the one we mentioned. 

And know that if Saturn and Mercury are both in one sign, aspecting the Moon or the Lord of the Ascendant, it signifies that she had relations with an old man with thin hair <note>original: "tenens capillos," literally "holding hairs," possibly a reference to balding or a specific grooming style</note>, according to what I have found it resembles. If the significators apply to him, it signifies she loves a man who keeps himself such that he looks like a youth.

### ¶ Chapter 19. At what time the marriage will occur.

After you have a sign that the marriage ought to be completed, and you wish to know when it will be, look at the significators that show the marriage will happen through their application. When they are in an angle—especially in the Ascendant—say that the marriage will be at that time. Or look at the number of degrees in the application: if they are in movable signs <note>Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn</note>, take them as days; if in common signs, as months; and if in fixed signs <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius</note>, as years. 

Similarly, angles signify speed and the number of days; "succedent" houses <note>houses 2, 5, 8, 11, which follow the angles</note> signify a middle ground between slowness and speed and the number of months; and "cadent" houses <note>houses 3, 6, 9, 12</note> signify slowness and the number of years. If the sign is by translation, the event happens when the "bringer" <note>the planet carrying the light</note> applies to the one to whom it brings the light. If the application is from "hidden places," it will be sooner and in a shorter time; perhaps the number of degrees between them will be the days or months. 

Also look at the "Part of Marriage" <note>a calculated mathematical point in a chart</note> of the man (if it is a man’s question) or the woman. Look at the location of that Part for either of them, considering the distance from it to the degree of Venus by degrees of ascension; take the result as days. If you find the said Part while Venus is in an angle, it signifies brevity and that the marriage will be hastened. Look also for when Jupiter and Venus, by their own motions, transit through the degree of the said Part, and say that the marriage will be at that time. The judgment will be even more firm and certain if you verify the time when the *athazir* <note>term: a method of timing by directing a point through the zodiac, often called "profection" or "direction"</note> of the Sun applies to Venus or its rays, because this will never fail, God willing.

### Chapter 20. On the question for a man and a woman as to whether they have had intercourse through fornication or not.

<image-desc>Decorative drop cap 'C' featuring floral and vine motifs.</image-desc>
**W**hen someone asks you about a man and a woman who are suspected of having committed fornication, to know if they have had sex or not: give the Ascendant <note>the sign rising on the eastern horizon</note> to the person asking the question. Give the seventh house to the person being asked about. Assign the planet from which the Moon is separating to the woman, and the planet to which the Moon is applying <note>moving toward an aspect with</note> to the man suspected of lying with her. Afterward, look to see which of the planets are "peregrine" <note>wandering without any special dignity or strength in that sign</note> and "occidental" <note>setting in the west after the sun</note> in the seventh house, as well as the planet to which the Moon applies, for these will be the significators <note>the planetary representatives of the people involved</note>. Thus, if you find the Lord of the Ascendant applying to the Lord of the seventh house, or to a planet located in the seventh house, or to the planet to which the Moon applies—while "infortunes" <note>malefic planets like Saturn or Mars</note> are aspecting these planets—it signifies the truth of the suspicion. It means they have indeed had intercourse through fornication <note>original: "per fornicationem"</note>, as well as through legal means <note>original: "per legem," likely implying they have acted as if married or are bound by some law</note>. And if "fortunes" <note>benefic planets like Jupiter or Venus</note> aspect these three significators and no infortunes are looking at them, it signifies the querent’s suspicion was true, yet it happened through marriage. If the fortunes and infortunes aspect them equally, it signifies the act happened through both fornication and marriage. And if the question is whether several men have had sex with her, look at their names and place them in order: first, second, and third. Look at the Lord of the Ascendant and the Moon; whichever one you find aspecting the Ascendant, take as the significator for this. Then observe how many planets this significator aspects: the planet it first applies to represents the first suspect, the next represents the second, and the third for the third suspect. If that significator has no such applications, take the first Lord of the Triplicity <note>a system of three planets ruling each element</note> for the first suspect, the second for the second, and the third for the third. Then look at the application of the Lord of the Ascendant to each of their significators, noting the aspects of fortunes and infortunes, and judge according to what we said at the start of this chapter; you will be certain with God’s help.

### Chapter 21. On the question of a young woman, whether she is a virgin or not.

<image-desc>Decorative drop cap 'A' featuring floral patterns.</image-desc>

If they are in "movable" <note>Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn</note> or "common signs" <note>Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces</note>, say the woman is already "complete" <note>sexually experienced</note> and is or was married. A conjunction similarly signifies that she will return; however, if the aspect is a square or opposition without reception, it signifies she will never return. 

Some wise men say that if the Ascendant is a "fixed sign" <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, or Aquarius</note> and Saturn is in any of the "angles" <note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</note>, especially in the Midheaven <note>original: "medio celi"; the highest point of the chart</note>, it signifies that the quarrel between them will last a long time and they will remain in that state for a long duration, especially if the Moon aspects Saturn. And if Mars is in any angle where the Moon has also given him her strength—and more so if the Ascendant is a "movable sign" <note>Aries, Cancer, Libra, or Capricorn</note>—it signifies they will separate by the mutual consent of both. If either of the two "fortunes" is in an angle, especially the Midheaven, it signifies they will have peace. If that "fortune" is in the angle of the Ascendant, it signifies the agreement will come from the man’s side. If it is in the angle of the descendant <note>original: "occidentis"; the 7th house</note>, it will be from the woman’s side. And if any "infortune" aspects those "fortunes," it signifies the agreement itself will be made with fraud.

### ¶ Chapter 23. Whether he will have intercourse with a woman that night.

If someone asks you whether he will fulfill his desire with a woman that night or not: look to see if you find Venus aspecting the Ascendant in the question. If so, say that his question <note>his desire</note> will be fulfilled that night. And if the question is whether he did the thing this past night or not: judge it in the same way, neither more nor less. If Venus does not aspect the Ascendant, say he will not have intercourse with a woman that night, or did not have it.

If Venus aspects Saturn from the seventh house, say he will have intercourse with a servant or a low-born woman. If Venus aspects Jupiter from the seventh instead of Saturn—Jupiter being in whatever place you wish—say he will have intercourse with women who are chaste of body. If she aspects the Sun from the seventh, say he will have intercourse with women of high-ranking men, or of a king. If she aspects the Moon from the seventh house, say he will have intercourse with a woman who is noble, clear-skinned, sweet-smelling, and dressed in white clothes; and perhaps he will have intercourse (or did have) with his father’s wife or his son’s wife <note>This indicates the astrological potential for prohibited or scandalous relations</note>. If Venus is joined with Mercury or aspects him from the seventh, say he will have intercourse with a young

<column-break/>

virgin girl, and completely so. If Venus is in the seventh house from the Ascendant, aspecting any of the planets according to what we have said, it signifies the act has been done, or will be done by all means, and in the manners we described. If Venus is "falling" <note>in a weak or "cadent" house</note> from the Ascendant on that day, he did not have intercourse with a woman, nor will he. And if the Ascendant is a fortunate sign with "fortunes" aspecting it from good places, or if they are in it, and the Lord of the exaltation of that sign is aspecting it: say the matter sought will happen quickly and on that day; but you must consider and judge carefully.

### ¶ Chapter 24. On the question of whether he had intercourse with a woman this night or not.

<image-desc>Decorative initial C featuring a floral/leafy pattern inside a square frame.</image-desc>

When someone asks you about his lying with a woman this past or future night—how it was or will be, or in what place it was or will be, or if he had or will have intercourse with a woman that night: Look in this case to Venus. If you find her in the Ascendant in the house of Mars or Saturn, he had intercourse that night (or will have) with a woman other than his own, and he lay (or will lie) in a stranger's house and not his own. 

If Venus is in the house of Mercury or Saturn, say he lay (or will lie) in a dark house with a woman without a candle. If Venus and the Moon are joined in the seventh house from the Ascendant and it is a nighttime question, say he lay (or will lie) with a woman of good character <note>original: "sui corporis bona"</note> and in a clean place, and not with a prostitute. If Venus and the Moon are joined in the Ascendant, that man has a friendship with women and has spoken with them, or will speak with them that night. If Venus and the Moon are in the house of the Moon <note>Cancer</note>, it signifies the same. 

If Venus and the Moon are in the seventh from the Ascendant in any of the houses of Mars <note>Aries or Scorpio</note>, in whatever way it may be—whether the Lord of the house aspects them or not—he lay or will lie with a harlot <note>original: "ganea"</note>. If Mars is in Libra aspecting the degree of the Ascendant from the seventh house, that man will lie "sodomitically" <note>original: "sodomitice"; in this context, it often refers to non-procreative or anal sex</note> with boys. If Mercury aspects there from the seventh house, he will use women through a "prohibited place" <note>likely referring to anal intercourse</note> and he mocks women, and some woman has performed trickery <note>original: "pastaturam"; could imply a love charm or a deceptive act</note> upon him. 

If Mercury aspects Venus from the seventh, or if Venus is in the seventh in the house of Saturn, he will lie with women who do <gloss>not</gloss> belong to him, such as public prostitutes. If Venus in the seventh is in her own house or the house of Jupiter, he will lie with his own woman <note>his wife</note>, and he lay or will lie in his own house. If the Ascendant is a "common sign" <note>Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, or Pisces</note> and Venus aspects it from the seventh, say he will fulfill his desire with the woman and will immediately depart from her and lie alone. If the Moon aspects there from the seventh and is in a "quadruped sign" <note>signs representing four-legged animals like Aries, Taurus, Leo, Sagittarius, or Capricorn</note> in the house of Saturn, or in its own *andurungen* <note>original: "adurungen"; a technical term derived from Persian/Arabic astrology, likely *Andaruzagar*, referring to a specific division of a sign's degrees</note>. (And *andurungen* is when you divide the ascending sign into three parts, giving the first to the Lord of that house, and the second to the planet...)

### Chapter 25. On the question of how many husbands a woman will have.

If you are asked on behalf of any woman how many husbands she will have: look from the degree of the tenth house <note>the Midheaven, representing status and public life</note> even unto the degree of Mars: and however many planets you find between them, so many husbands shall she have. And if Mars should be in the tenth house, you should look from Mars even unto Jupiter in this same manner: and judge according to that: and you will be certain, with God's help.

### Chapter 26. On the question for a woman, whether she has a son or not.

In this matter, consider Venus: and if you find her in Aquarius or in Leo joined with Mercury: say that she never gives birth: and if you find her joined with Mercury in Scorpio or Taurus: she has a son. And if Mars or Venus or the Moon should be in a common sign <note>original: "signo communi"; the mutable signs: Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, or Pisces</note> provided it is not in Sagittarius: she has no son, nor will she ever give birth: and if she does give birth, the creature will die. And if the "infortunes" <note>the malefic planets Saturn or Mars</note> should be in moveable signs <note>original: "signis mobilibus"; the cardinal signs: Aries, Cancer, Libra, or Capricorn</note>: her son is from fornication and she has a lover who practices betrayal and falsehood against her husband. And if the "fortunes" <note>the beneficial planets Jupiter or Venus</note> should be in moveable signs: she has a legitimate son: and if the infortunes are mixed with both fortunes in moveable signs: she has a legitimate son: and if the infortunes are mixed with both fortunes in moveable signs: she has bad sons who cause her trouble.

### Chapter 27. On the question for a woman, whether she is pregnant or not.

Look to the Ascendant: if it should be a common sign: say that she is pregnant: and if the lord of the house of children <note>the ruler of the 5th house</note> should be in the Ascendant: say that she is pregnant. And if Mercury should be fortunate in the Ascendant: it signifies that she is pregnant. And if you find none of these significations: look to the four "angles" <note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses of the chart</note>: and if you find a fortune in any of them, especially Jupiter: say that she is pregnant: and according to the power: state: and safety and fortune

<column-break/>

of that planet: there will be safety and completion of that pregnancy: for if that planet be strong and in a good place, safe from the infortunes that might strike it: it signifies the completion of the pregnancy itself and the escape <note>the successful delivery</note> of the creature and its health: and if that planet should be retrograde <note>appearing to move backward</note> or "combust" <note>original: "combustus"; rendered invisible and weakened by being too close to the Sun</note>: or afflicted by a planet that does not "receive" it <note>a planet in a sign where the other has no dignity</note>: say that the pregnancy will be lost: it will be destroyed: and will come forth dead, having neither life nor completion: and you shall know the state of the pregnant woman from the power of her planet and its fortune and misfortune: and from its "application" <note>the movement of one planet toward another</note> to planets that help and liberate it: for if that planet should be afflicted in the house of death, or applying to the lord of the house of death: or combust or "depressed" <note>in its sign of Fall</note> in the "angle of the earth" <note>the 4th house, the lowest point of the chart</note>: that pregnancy will be hard and heavy for the mother: and the creature itself, before it comes out, will kill its mother: unless the Lord helps her through His mercy. And if Mars should be in the Ascendant, safe and "received" by the lord of the Ascendant: that pregnancy will be easy for the mother: and without any danger or evil, she will give birth easily. And if Saturn should be in this place instead of Mars: say that the pregnancy will be hard, strong, and troublesome for the woman, and because of it, sicknesses, miseries, and anxieties will happen to her: and perhaps death and destruction: unless God removes it. 

And if with this you wish to know whether she is pregnant with a male or a female: look to the masculine and feminine signs: and the masculine and feminine degrees: and the masculine and feminine "quarters" <note>the four quadrants of the zodiac</note>: and the masculine and feminine planets: afterward, look to the lord of the house of children; if it should be a masculine planet in a masculine sign: in a masculine degree: and in a masculine quarter: say that the creature will be a male. And if the planet should be feminine: and should be in a feminine sign, degree: and quarter: say it is a female. And if you find these significations mixed: look to the Ascendant and its lord: and the house of children and its lord, the Sun: and the Moon: and the lord of the hour <note>the planet ruling the specific hour of the question</note>: and if the greater part of these significators be in a masculine sign: say that the creature is a male: and if the greater part be in feminine signs: say it is a female. And you should never take any masculine planet as a significator when you find it in feminine signs: but set it aside: and look to the other significators: and judge a male from the masculine, and a female from the feminine: and you will be certain, with God's help. 

And one group of the wise says: look to the angles from the Ascendant: and if you find a masculine planet there in a masculine sign: say it is a male: and if a feminine one in a feminine sign: say it is a female. And know that this chapter on the significance of the quarters and degrees is powerful and truthful.

### ¶ Chapter 29. On the sayings of Al-Kindi regarding marriages.

And he said well: when the Lord of the Ascendant <note>original: "dominus ascendentis"; the planet ruling the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the time of the question</note> applies <note>original: "applicuerit"; when a faster-moving planet approaches an aspect with a slower one</note> to the Lord of the Seventh House <note>the house governing marriage and partnerships</note>, the marriage will be completed. And if the Moon applies to Venus: and Venus is powerful and increasing in her motion <note>moving faster than her average daily speed</note>, and the Moon likewise: the marriage will be completed. And if Venus aspects the Sun: and the Sun holds some dignity <note>essential strength, such as being in its own sign or exaltation</note> in the Ascendant: and is himself increasing in his motion: and aspects the Lord of his own house: similarly a marriage will occur. And if the applying planet and the one to which it applies are both falling from the angles <note>original: "cadentes ab angulis"; located in the 3rd, 6th, 9th, or 12th houses, which are considered weak positions</note>: and especially if their own Lords do not aspect them: it signifies that the marriage will reach almost to its completion: and afterward it will be disturbed: and it will not happen. And if the Moon, the Sun, Venus, and the Lord of the Seventh and the Lord of the Ascendant are in angles <note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, which are the strongest positions</note>: even if one does not aspect the other, if their Lords aspect them and they are powerful: the marriage will be granted and remain for a time without hope of completion: and afterward it will happen with the good pleasure of God: and the time of that completion will be when the significator showing that the marriage will be applies to an angle by <term>athaçir <note>from the Arabic "tasyir," a method of astrological timing used to determine when a predicted event will manifest</note></term>: and that time will be in days, months, or years.

### ¶ Chapter 30. For a woman, whether she will be faithful in body to her husband or not.

This likewise is a saying of Al-Kindi. Look: if you find the Lord of the Ascendant, Venus, and the Moon in fixed signs <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, or Aquarius, which represent stability and endurance</note> with the Fortunes <note>the "benefic" planets, Jupiter and Venus</note> aspecting them: say that she is a pure and chaste maiden. And if in this place of the Fortunes there be Infortunes <note>the "malefic" planets, Saturn and Mars</note>: say that she is neither a maiden nor chaste: and it is even more so if the aspecting planet is Mars. And if the two luminaries <note>the Sun and the Moon</note> aspect each other, with both of them aspecting Mars: say that she is not chaste: but a public prostitute <note>original: "meretrix palatina"; literally a palace prostitute, implying one who is publicly available</note>. And if the luminaries do not aspect each other nor Mars: say that she is not chaste: yet she does what she does in secret. And if the Ascendant and the significators are in mobile signs <note>Aries, Cancer, Libra, or Capricorn, which represent change and instability</note> with Infortunes aspecting them: say that she desires a man much and that she is amorous: nevertheless she covers herself and represses her evil desires and withdraws herself from them: and defends herself from those seeking her: yet she is not to be trusted: because she is changeable.

### ¶ The saying of Al-Kindi in knowing if a woman is ugly or beautiful.

Look to the Ascendant: and give it to her face and her head: the second house to her neck: the third to her hands and shoulders: and so every house to every member according to this order: and judge in each of these members according to the figure of that animal from which that sign is named <note>for example, Leo the Lion or Taurus the Bull</note>: and according to the beauty and ugliness of them among other animals. And look in what place of the heavens the Moon is. And if she be fortunate: say that the member signified by the sign in which the Moon is fortunate

<column-break/>

is beautiful and well-formed: and that there is a beautiful mark <note>original: "signale"; a birthmark or beauty spot</note> on that member. And if the Moon be unfortunate: say that the member given to the sign in which the Moon is unfortunate is ugly: and there is an ugly and bad mark upon it. And if the Moon in this is increased in motion: say that the ugly mark is a thing that stands out more than others: like a wart <note>original: "pozzus"; likely a growth or protrusion</note> or some such thing that is growing. And if the Moon be diminished in motion: say that there is a defect in that member: such as a finger <note>original: "dedo"; likely a stunted or missing digit</note>: or that which resembles it. If the Moon be moderate in her motion between increase and decrease: say that it is a mark in the skin: and on the surface of the member. ¶ And if you wish to know of what color the mark or that blemish is: mix the color of the sign in which the Moon is with the color of the unfortunate planet which signified that blemish: and judge from that color: and you will be certain, with God's help. ¶ And if you wish to know what kind of complexion <note>the physical balance of the four humors: blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile</note> that blemish is: Look to the sign in which the Moon is: and in which of the Infortunes it is which showed the blemish. If it be an Earthly sign: the blemish is from coldness and dryness. If Watery: from coldness and moisture. If Fiery: from heat and dryness. If Airy: from heat and moisture. And if the sign in which the Moon is be different—that is, of another complexion—than the one in which the planet of the Infortunes is: mix their natures: and judge according to the mixture: and in whatever member the Infortunes may be: in that member judge the ugliness and blemish: and when you are asked about this matter: follow this way: and judge according to the rules which you will find, with God's help.

### ¶ Chapter 31. On knowing if a woman is rich or poor.

Look in this to the Lord of the Eighth House <note>the house of shared resources, dowries, and inheritances</note>. If you find him applying to the Lord of the Seventh: and the Lord of the Eighth be a Fortune: and the Moon applying to the Eighth house: and its Lord with the Infortunes far removed from the eighth: and from their aspects: judge that she is rich and that she will enrich her husband as long as he is with her: and if you find the contrary of these constellations: say that she is poor and that the husband will become poor with her. And if you find this constellation moderate: say that she is middling between riches and poverty. And if a woman asks this of you: give her the Ascendant as her significator: and take this signification from the Ascendant and the Second House <note>the house of personal wealth</note> just as you took it from the Seventh and Eighth: and judge according to what you find and you will be certain, with God's help. ¶ And if you wish to know if love exists between them or not: consider the aspects which are between the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the Seventh: and between the Lord of the Ascendant and Venus and the Moon: and if these aspects are of friendship <note>trine or sextile aspects, which are harmonious</note> and with reception <note>when two planets are in signs ruled by each other, indicating mutual support</note>: say that they love each other and one will help the other. And if one of their significators receives the other, and the other does not receive him: say that the one receiving will love the other, and the other will not love him. And according to this order and rule in everything that is asked of you concerning this matter and the whole state of a man with a woman: judge according to these rules and you will be certain, with the good pleasure of God.

### ¶ Chapter 32. On elections for making marriages and beginning them.

When you wish to begin a union <note>original: "coiũctiõê" (coniunctionem); referring here to the formal start of a marriage</note>, ensure that the signs containing the significators—which are the Ascendant, the Seventh House, Venus, and the Moon—are fixed signs <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, and Aquarius; these were thought to provide stability</note> and signs of direct ascension <note>signs that take longer to rise over the horizon, associated with long-lasting effects</note>. And place an aspect of friendship <note>a sextile or trine aspect</note> and reception <note>a condition where one planet is in a sign ruled by another, suggesting mutual support</note> between the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the Seventh House: and do the same between the Moon and the Lord of the Seventh. Place both fortunes <note>the "benefic" planets, Jupiter and Venus</note> in the angles <note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses</note> and the misfortunes <note>the "malefic" planets, Mars and Saturn</note> falling away from the angles. And place the Lord of the House of Children <note>the 5th house</note> and Mercury applying to the significators in a fortunate state and free from misfortunes. Set the sign of the fifth house, the sign where its Lord resides, and the sign where Mercury resides, in signs of many children <note>typically water signs like Cancer or Scorpio</note> and many fortunes. You shall also make the fourth house fortunate, as well as the lights <note>the Sun and Moon</note>, the Part of Fortune, and the Part of Substance <note>calculated points in a chart representing wealth and assets</note>. And place the Moon—after her separation from the conjunction or opposition that occurred before this—applying to a fortune: and let the Lord of the house in which the Moon resides be a fortune.

->### Chapter 33. On fugitive servants or beasts and on lost things: where they are and why they were lost.<-

Otherwise, because this matter is looked upon in many ways and from many perspectives, the best method in this—which we ought to follow—is that which Dorotheus <note>Dorotheus of Sidon, a 1st-century Greek astrologer</note> spoke: and he says thus: when you wish to look into a fugitive or any lost thing, give the Ascendant and its Lord and the Moon as the significators of the fugitive and the lost item. And give the Midheaven <note>original: "mediuz celi"; the 10th house</note> and its Lord, and the Sun, as the significators of the master of the fugitive, or the person seeking the lost thing. And let the Lord of the house of the Moon and the receiver of the Moon's disposition be the significators of the end of the matter. And Messehala <note>Masha'allah, an 8th-century Persian-Jewish astrologer</note> and a great part of the wise men said: give the Ascendant and its Lord for the significators of the master of the fugitive or the one seeking the lost thing and the inquiry of the seeker: and the seventh house and its Lord for the significators of the fugitive and the lost thing. And Alkidus <note>Al-Kindi, the 9th-century Arab philosopher</note> said, when he spoke of the fugitive and the lost thing: the lost thing is either an animal or not an animal. What is sought in this, and what is desired to be known from this cause, is in what place the lost thing is: and if it shall be found or not. And if it ought to be found: whether it will be found in its entirety or only one part of it, and where it will be found: and by what reason it was lost and shall be found. And the significator of the lost thing is the Moon: hence, if you find the Moon applying to the Lord of the Ascendant, or to the Lord of the second house from the Ascendant <note>the house of personal property</note>, or to the Lord of the house of the Moon: the lost thing shall be found, if God wills. And if the Moon does not apply to any of these, nor is in the Ascendant, nor in the second house: you shall not find the lost things unless God wills. And if the Lord of the house of the Moon is in the third or in a sextile aspect to the Ascendant, have hope of finding that thing by that aspect existing toward the degree of the Ascendant itself; similarly if, separating itself from the Lord of the twelfth, or eighth, or sixth houses <note>the "evil" or weak houses</note>, it applies to the degree of the Ascendant. And similarly if it has separated itself from the Lord of the twelfth, or eighth,

<column-break/>

or sixth: and applies to the degree of the House of Substance <note>the 2nd house</note> from whatever aspect it may be: have hope of finding the lost thing if the Lord of the house of the Moon aspects the Moon. And if you find the contrary of these constellations, judge the contrary of this judgment. And if you find the Moon unfortunate <note>afflicted by malefic planets</note> by the Lord of the eighth, or sixth, or twelfth: say that the lost thing has entered into the hands and power of some evil man who will never restore it: and especially if that misfortune does not aspect the Lord of the Ascendant. And if the Moon is made fortunate by either of the two fortunes: the lost thing has entered the hands and power of someone good and faithful who is guarding it. And if that fortune applies to the Ascendant, or aspects it, or the Moon aspects the Ascendant: that faithful person will restore the thing to its master if God wills. And if the Moon is in the angles from the Sun, or joined with him: that lost thing has entered the power of the King <note>or a high official</note>: and if with this the Sun aspects the Ascendant with an aspect of friendship, and the Moon applies to the degree of the Ascendant: that thing will be restored to its master. And if the application which the Moon had to the Ascendant was by a square <note>90 degrees</note> or opposition <note>180 degrees</note> in this constellation we have described: the restoration will be with penalty and labor. And if the aspect was by a trine <note>120 degrees</note> or sextile <note>60 degrees</note>: he will restore it lightly and of good will. And if in this constellation the Moon is in the Ascendant: the restoration will be with damage. The significator of where the lost thing is located is the place of the Moon according to the nature of the sign in which she resides: for if that sign is Oriental <note>Eastern</note>: it is in the eastern part: and if it is Occidental <note>Western</note>: it is in the western part. And if Northern: it is in the north. And if Southern: in the southern part. Look at the place of the Moon in the figure <note>the birth or interrogation chart</note>: for if she is in the Ascendant: the lost thing is in the east: and if in the angle of the West <note>7th house</note>: it is in the western part. And if in the Midheaven: it is in the southern part; and if in the Angle of the Earth <note>4th house</note>: it is in the northern part. And similarly to the right and left of any of these angles. And according to this, judge and mix this signification with the signification of the sign in which the Moon is. And if the Lord of the house of the Moon is in human signs <note>Gemini, Virgo, Libra, Aquarius</note>: it is in a place where men are. And if in a sign of small beasts such as Aries or Capricorn: it is in a place where there are sheep and beasts similar to them. And if in a sign of large beasts such as Sagittarius: it is in a place where there are great beasts: such as mules, donkeys, and those similar to them. And if in Leo: it is in a place where there are evil beasts and a place to be feared. And if in Scorpio: it is in a place where there are serpents and venomous reptiles. And if in Cancer: it is in a place where there are pits, and a place of waters, springs, and aquatic beasts. And if in Pisces: it is in a place where there is much fresh water and a fishery where fish are caught. And if it is in Aquarius: the same thing. And if it is in human signs: it signifies places where there are high mountains, high rocks, and great rivers. And if it is in the last half of Capricorn: it signifies places of ships. Similarly, look at the sign in which the Moon is: if it is in a fiery sign, it signifies a place in which there is fire or around which there is fire. And if in a watery sign: it signifies a place in which there is water or near water, or a place where things are [affected] by water. And if in an airy sign: it signifies a place where there are many and strong winds.

### Chapter 35. On the question of two litigants, which of them shall win.

<image-desc>A decorative woodcut letter 'C' showing a judge or scholar in robes and a cap, gesturing as if presiding over a legal case.</image-desc>

When you are asked about a trial or dispute that occurs between two people, regarding which of them shall overcome the other: give the ascendant and its lord and the Moon to the **petitioner** <note>The person asking the question/the plaintiff.</note>, and the seventh house and its lord to the one with whom he contends. Afterward, if one significator applies to the other by a **sextile or trine** <note>Harmonious aspects of 60 or 120 degrees.</note>, they will agree and reach an accord before they come to trial or quarrels. If the application is by a **square or opposition** <note>Tense aspects of 90 or 180 degrees.</note>, there will be no peace between them except after a trial or quarrel. If they are joined in one sign without a mediator, they will agree among themselves. If the lord of the tenth house applies to them before one of them applies to the other, they will have neither agreement nor peace until the trial comes before the King. If the Moon carries the light of one to the other, the agreement will be through a messenger who travels between them. 

Afterward, look at the locations of the lord of the ascendant and the lord of the seventh house and their strengths, because from this you will have the indication to know the stronger of them and the one who will win; for that person is the victor and more powerful whose significator is in an angle. Whichever of them is **received** <note>A technical term where one planet is in a sign ruled by the other, indicating support.</note> will have more helpers. Know that the beginning of peace and agreement will come from the planet that gives its power to the other planet, or from the lighter of them, or from the one falling from an angle. Know that when the lord of the seventh is in the ascendant, it signifies the power of the petitioner. When the lord of the ascendant is in the seventh, it signifies the opposite, for they are likened to one who is submissive and defeated. 

When one of the significators is **retrograde** <note>Appearing to move backward in the sky; signifies weakness or reversal.</note>, it signifies weakness, fear, brokenness, and lying on the part of the petitioner. If the lord of the seventh is retrograde, it signifies weakness for the one with whom he contends. If the lord of the midheaven aspects that retrograde one, it signifies that the **official** <note>original: "alcaydus." Derived from the Arabic *al-qadi*, meaning a judge or magistrate.</note> will act poorly toward the person represented by that significator, and that the quarrel and trial will be greatly prolonged. Likewise, if these two significators—the lord of the ascendant and the lord of the seventh—separate from one another, it signifies the quarrel and trial will be greatly prolonged. ## ¶ Chapter 36. On buying and selling.

Look at this: if you find an application between the lord of the ascendant and the lord of the 7th house: say that the purchase will be made easily; and the ease in it comes from the faster planet going to the other. And if you do not find an application between them, but you find some planet carrying the light of one to the other: say that the sale will be made through some mediator placed between them. And if you find the lord of the ascendant in the 7th house: say that the buyer seeks the purchase from the seller. And if you find the lord of the 7th house in the ascendant: say that the seller seeks from the buyer. 

And if you find a benefic in the ascendant: it signifies the readiness and truth of the seller and the sale. And if you find a malefic there: it signifies laziness and lying. And if you find a benefic in the 7th house: it signifies speed and truth in the buyer. And if you find a malefic there: it signifies the contrary. And if you find the Moon applying to any planet without separating from another: say that the seller sells a thing which he did not buy, which he has from his inheritance or revenues; and if he did buy it, he has not yet paid its price. And if the Moon is separated from a planet and applying to no other: say that the thing was bought for a time <note>Likely meaning a temporary lease or on credit.</note>. And if the planet from which the Moon separates is entering **combustion** <note>Passing too close to the Sun, which "burns up" the planet's power.</note>: say that the seller will die before receiving the price of the thing sold. And I say that it should be considered in this chapter in this way: take the signification of the seller from the ascendant, and of the buyer from the 7th house, and of the merchandise which is sold and bought from the 4th house, and what happens between them regarding readiness or laziness from the 10th house: and judge according to this and you will be certain, with God.

## ¶ Chapter 38: Regarding the question of someone wanting to go to another, and whether they will find him in that place or not.

Look in this case to the lord of the 7th house <note>The house of "the other person."</note>. If you find him in an **angle** <note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, which indicate immediate action and presence.</note>, that person is in that place. If he is in a **succedent** house <note>The 2nd, 5th, 8th, or 11th houses, which follow the angles.</note>, he is near his place. And if he is in the **cadent** houses <note>The 3rd, 6th, 9th, or 12th houses, suggesting weakness or being far away.</note>, he is outside his place. And in all of this, look to see if there is an application between both **significators** <note>The planets representing the seeker and the person sought.</note>, or a **translation** or **collection** <note>Astrological conditions where a third planet connects the two main planets.</note> of light. And if the planet that collects or carries the light aspects the 7th house, he will find him; and if you find the opposite of this, say that he will not.

## ¶ Chapter 39: Regarding the question of soldiers going to find other soldiers or others for the sake of fighting.

When you wish to know if they will find them or have a battle or not: give the **ascendant** <note>The 1st house, representing the person asking.</note> to the seeker, and the 7th house to the soldiers for whom he asks. And if you find the <term>Almuten</term> <note>original: "almuteç"; the planet with the most essential dignity in a specific degree.</note> of these two places, or their lords, applying to one another, say that one will confront the other. And if there is a planet there that carries light between them, they will confront each other. And if Mars is not in the angles from the ascendant, nor in the angles of the significators, say that they will confront each other, yet they will not have a battle. And if they do not aspect each other, and there is no translation between them, one will not confront the other, if God wills.

## ¶ Chapter 40: Regarding a matter to be petitioned from a community or which ought to be done through a community.

Take the Almuten of the ascendant for the seeker, and move it by <term>Atazir</term> <note>original: "athaçir"; a method of calculating the progression of points in a chart over time.</note>, and look at the first, second, and third applications. In whichever of these there is **reception** <note>When a planet is in a sign where another planet has dignity, showing a cooperative relationship.</note>, the matter will be completed through that person's hand and his inquiry. And if the same Almuten of the ascendant does not apply to any house, take the Moon in its place and proceed in the same manner by looking at her applications, and judge according to this.

## ¶ Chapter 41: Regarding purchases and sales.

I say similarly regarding buyers and sellers: look to the seller from the ascendant, and to the buyer from the 7th house, and to the thing being bought from the 4th house. And that which happens between them regarding ease

or difficulty is seen from the 10th house. And if there is no application, reception, translation, or collection between them, there will be contention and discord in that sale. And if there is a planet between them that carries light from one to the other, the matter will be completed by the hand of a mediator. 

It is known to happen many times that the completion of a sale occurs with trouble for the buyer and seller; this happens if the lord of the 7th applies to the lord of the 4th and the lord of the ascendant receives the lord of the 7th. And this same thing will be true when a malefic is in the 4th house, especially if the thing sold is land or an inheritance, because then it signifies that there will be contention there, and perhaps someone will rise up to claim that inheritance.

And when benefics are in the 10th house, they signify a high price for the thing and that it sells well. And if malefics are there, it signifies the cheapness <note>original: "vilitatẽ"; lack of value or low quality.</note> of that thing, and that it will sell poorly, and there will be loss and contention in it because of the price and the sale. 

Everything we have spoken of in this reasoning applies if the thing sold is not named or specified. But if it is a named and specified thing: if it is a servant, take this from the house of servants <note>The 6th house.</note>. If it is a beast, from the 12th house. For a thing whose likeness or form you cannot find, nor take from the houses of the chart, take from the significations of the planets: such as from Jupiter, who is the significator of animals; and Venus of fragrant things, cloths, and books. And Mars of iron and minerals; and Saturn of medicinal spices. And the Sun of precious stones; and the Moon of colored cloths. It is a very long explanation to divide and determine these, yet we have stated the sum of the reasons from it, so that a wise man may understand it and by it follow the path; and he shall be made certain with God.

This judgment was stated by **Masha'allah** <note>original: "messahalla"; a prominent 8th-century Persian-Jewish astrologer and astronomer.</note>, who was an expert in this matter; and it was also made known by **Al-Fadl ibn Sahl** <note>original: "alfad fili⁹ çael"; a famous 9th-century Persian vizier and astrologer.</note> in his book. This judgment follows the principles of battles and the movements of military forces going out to war, as well as the hour of a **question** <note>A "horary" question, where a chart is cast for the moment a specific question is asked.</note> concerning two litigants and what will become of them. 

And if **Mars** occurs at the beginning of a dispute, or at the movement of a military force going out to fight, or at the entry into a city by force in a **difficult position** <note>original: "malo loco"; refers to the "unfortunate" houses in a chart, like the 6th, 8th, or 12th.</note>, and **Jupiter** or **Venus** aspects it, and the **Lord of the House** in which Mars is located is in the **Midheaven** <note>original: "medio celi"; the highest point of the chart, representing authority and public action.</note>: it signifies discord in the military among themselves, and they will disagree with their leader. Similarly, if the **Benefics** <note>original: "fortune"; the "lucky" planets, Jupiter and Venus.</note> are in difficult positions aspecting Mars, it signifies betrayal and malice in the military. 

And if Mars is in a difficult position and the Benefics aspect it from **good positions**, it signifies the lawfulness of the military, and they will be obedient to their leader. And if Mars is in a **movable sign** <note>original: "signo mobili"; also known as cardinal signs (Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn), which indicate change and action.</note> and a good position in the heavens, and planets from various places aspect it, it signifies that they will fight many times. 

And when it happens that Mars is in an **angle beneath the earth** <note>The 4th House, representing the ground or hidden matters.</note>, it signifies great slaughters. And if he lingers a long time in that sign, it will last until another revolution comes. And if he is **retrograde** in the middle of a sign, so that he is neither at the beginning nor the end, with that same durability, it signifies that they will fight many times, one after another. And if he is at the end of the sign, the dispute will last only a little while. 

And if Mars is in **Aries**, which is his own house, and is in an angle—that is, the **Ascendant** or the oriental Midheaven—it signifies a great strength of the dispute, great fame, many weapons, and that it will be cut short quickly. And if Mars is in an angle in a **fixed** or **common sign**, that dispute will last a long time and be repeated many times; it grows stronger, and they will conquer each other in turn many times. 

And if any of the planets **applies** <note>An "application" is when a faster planet moves toward an aspect with a slower one.</note> to him, or he to another, and this planet is slow-moving or retrograde, it signifies durability. ### ¶ Concerning him who departs from obedience to the king and becomes a rebel to him.

Alfodal <note>original: "alfodal"; likely referring to the scholar Sahl ibn Bishr, a famous 9th-century Jewish astrologer and mathematician who wrote in Arabic.</note> son of Abenzebhel <note>original: "abenzeb hel"; a Latinization of Ibn Bishr.</note> said to the people: when someone asks you about a man who has retreated in disobedience from the king, give the **Ascendant** <note>The sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of the question.</note> and the **Moon** to the disobedient one, and give the **Sun** and the **Midheaven** <note>The 10th house, representing authority and the ruler.</note> to the king. ### ¶ Chapter 44. On besieging and capturing towns and what shall become of their states.

<image-desc>A square woodcut decorative initial letter 'Q' with a central circular motif containing a face, surrounded by stylized foliage and floral patterns.</image-desc>

**When** you are asked about any city or castle, whether it will be besieged or not; or if it is besieged, whether it will be captured or not; and if it is captured, whether it will be through peace or violence; and whether those inside will be given security, and if they will be firm in that security, or if a betrayal will happen to them afterward. If you know the **Ascendant** <note>the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon</note> of the city and the place of the Sun in its rising, and the other planets at the "root" of its building <note>the foundation or "birth" chart of the city</note>: work according to this and according to the strength of the **fortunes** <term>fortunes: benefic planets like Jupiter and Venus</term> and **infortunes** <term>infortunes: malefic planets like Saturn and Mars</term> in that figure, and their applications and movements. And if you do not know this, and you know the **nativity** <note>birth chart</note> of its King, or the beginning of when he held dominion over that city: work according to this; for if the King’s **significator** <term>significator: the planet representing a specific person or place in the chart</term> is afflicted, the state of that city will be afflicted and it will be stormed.

¶ And if you do not know this either, set the Ascendant for the hour of the question, and give the Ascendant and the Moon to the city. Afterward, if you find a **malefic** in the degrees of the Ascendant, it signifies that it is besieged. And if that malefic is removed from the Ascendant into the **twelfth house**, it signifies that it *was* besieged, but is not now. And if the same malefic is ascending by degree in the participation of the **second house**, it signifies that it is not besieged yet, nor will it be besieged afterward. And if, along with this, a **fortune** is in the **Midheaven** <note>Latin: "medio celi," the 10th house or highest point of the chart</note>, it signifies that the city will be saved and not captured. And if a malefic is in the **tenth house**, it signifies that he will enter the city by violence. And if a fortune is in participation of the tenth, and a malefic is in the very same **angle** <note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</note>, he will enter the city, yet with a great security of peace. ¶ And if

<column-break/>

**Mercury** regards them <note>forms an aspect to them</note>, there will be conventions and pacts between them. And if Mercury is then with the malefics, betrayals will be made concerning them, and the convention will not be held for them, nor the security given to them. And if Mercury is with the fortunes, the pacts and conventions made for them will be more fully preserved. And if a fortune is in the tenth angle and a malefic follows it, it signifies that the city will be taken and the people saved from death; however, it will be plundered, and some of them will be hanged. And if the same malefic is removed from the angle of the tenth into the part of the **ninth house**, and a fortune is in the part of the Midheaven, it signifies that they will plunder and take captives and burn the settlements in the city. And if **Jupiter** is the Lord of the Ascendant and powerful in an angle where he has some **dignity** <term>dignity: a sign where a planet has specific strength, such as its home or exaltation</term>, or in a **succedent house** <note>the 2nd, 5th, 8th, or 11th houses</note> looking at the Ascendant: this signifies that the city will escape from the strife and will be taken through peace for the salvation of the people—if the indication was that it must be taken at all.

¶ And if **Saturn** is in this place instead of Jupiter, and the fortunes are **falling away** <note>cadent</note> from him so that they do not look at him, and **Mars** is looking at him, and the Moon is afflicted by Mars: it signifies that the city will be taken by violence and they will kill the people existing in it, so that none shall escape from there except a few.

¶ And when a question is made to you for a besieged city: Look at what sign is its Ascendant, and who is its Lord, and how it is regarding the aspects of the fortunes and malefics, and where the Moon is. For if the Moon is **applying** to Mars without the aspect of the fortunes, it signifies that it will be strongly stormed; and if with this the significators of the city or castle are made unfortunate by Mars, it signifies that it will be taken by violence and whatever is found in it will be plundered, and very many of those people will be killed. And if Saturn is in the place of Mars in all that we have said, it signifies that there will be long disputes between the people of the besieged city and the outsiders besieging it, and this will last until it wearies both parties. And if Jupiter looks at the Moon and the significators of the city from a strong place, it will not be captured, nor can it be had, except through peace. And if **Venus** in this matter helps Jupiter and the Moon by an aspect, or helps the Moon and the significators of the city: the people of the city will strengthen themselves against the besiegers, so that they will retreat without having the city.

And if the **Luminaries** <note>the Sun and Moon</note> are in the quartile of the malefics, whenever the Moon applies to the quartile of the malefics (specifically to Mars), the dispute will be stirred up on that day. And if the fortunes look at them at that hour, the dispute will rest and be light.

¶ And if you wish to know for how much time the dispute will be: Look at the Lord of the sign of the city, whether it is a fortune or a malefic, and count how many degrees there are from it to the Moon, and how many degrees there are also from it to the Lord of the Ascendant. And if it is a malefic, the number of degrees from it to any of the said places will be **months**. And if it is a fortune powerful in the figure, that number will be **days**. And when you find the fortunes ruling over the significators of the city, and over the Moon and the Ascendant of the question at the hour of the question: judge the salvation of the city.

### ¶ Chapter 1: Concerning the eighth house and its questions

<image-desc>A decorative drop cap 'H' featuring floral and scrollwork patterns.</image-desc>
This house is the indicator of death, killing, suffocation, the burning of men, deadly poisons, infirmity, and the condemnation of the body on account of various types of poverty. It signifies great losses, fears, and wretched men in this world, such as the blind, the lame, or the hunchbacked; long-lasting illnesses and similar fatigues; depopulated places; terrifying things; and that which happens to a man before his death regarding abundance or need of good or evil. It also concerns things entrusted in bad faith, and every thing that is lost and destroyed; reasoning about ancient things and about things that are not true; the inheritances of the dead that are inherited; ancient things that have passed; profit in journeys and in going outside one's own land. It also concerns the property of women and the infirmity of elders. ¶ The Lord of the triplicity of the eighth house: The first is the indicator of death. The second is the indicator of the substance <note>meaning wealth or property</note> which one gains from the manner we have described. The third is the indicator of the inheritances of the dead. And if in this house, during questions, there is a fire sign, and the thought of the seeker is within it, the question is for inheritances. And if it is an earth sign, the question is for a dead person. And if it is an air sign, the question is for the devil, or for a powerful evil-doer

<column-break/>

or a giant. And if it is a water sign, the question is for the substance of the man for whom the question was made; because the ascendant always represents the seeker. And the seventh house represents the one for whom he asks. And the color of this house, in whatever sign it may be, is drawn toward green, or black mixed with green.

### ¶ Chapter 2: Concerning an absent man, whether he is alive or dead

<image-desc>A decorative drop cap 'Q' with an ornate background and a small figure or head depicted within the letter.</image-desc>
When a question is put to you for a man existing elsewhere, whether he is alive or dead: Look to the lord of the ascendant and the Moon. If you find them in the fourth house from the ascendant, or in the house of death <note>the 8th house</note>, or combust <term>combust: weakened by being too close to the Sun</term>, or in their fall <term>fall: a position in the zodiac where a planet's influence is weakened</term>, or joined with the lord of the house of death, say that he is dead. ¶ And if you find the lord of the ascendant in the twelfth house joined with malefic planets <note>original: "infortunis"; usually Saturn or Mars</note>, or any of the luminaries <term>luminaries: the Sun and the Moon</term> regarding him and afflicting him, judge that he is dead. And if the malefic planets are united with the luminaries without the testimony of the fortunate planets <note>usually Jupiter or Venus</note>, it similarly signifies death; especially where the malefics are more powerful than them by regarding them and also afflicting them. ¶ This is the significance of the Moon in this reasoning: know that when the Moon applies by aspect to any planet existing in the midheaven, it signifies safety and health. ¶ And when she applies to a planet that is in the 7th, 8th, or 4th house, it signifies death. ¶ And if the Moon is in the 4th house, applying to a planet existing in the midheaven, it signifies safety. ¶ Similarly, if she is in the midheaven, applying to a planet in the 4th house, it signifies safety. ¶ However, if from the ascendant she applies to a planet which is in the 4th, it signifies death. ¶ When the Moon is afflicted and applying to the lord of the 4th, and that lord is in his fall, or his exaltation, or retrograde <term>retrograde: appearing to move backward in the sky</term>, or under the rays <note>of the Sun</note>, it similarly signifies death. ¶ And if the Moon and the lord of the 4th house, or the lord of the ascendant, are harmed, it similarly signifies death; and especially if the lord of the ascendant is harmed and afflicted, it signifies death by all means. ¶ When the Moon is in the 4th house applying to a planet existing in the ascendant, it signifies that he will die a most wretched death. And if with this the 4th house is Scorpio, he will die submerged in water. And if she applies to Mars, he will be killed and submerged. And if Mars is in Leo or Sagittarius, he will die by some occasion that happens to him on the part of animals. And if that application is to Saturn, he will die by cold and dry poisons, or by something hidden and concealed.

### ¶ Chapter 3: Concerning the ninth house and its significations

<image-desc>A decorative drop cap 'H' with foliage designs.</image-desc>
This house signifies journeys, travel from one land to another, foreign men, changes of location from one place to another, divine matters, and it signifies prophecies and prophets, brothers <note>original: "fratres"; can mean biological brothers or members of a religious order</note> and hermits, houses of prayer, philosophy, the forecasting of future things, astrology, astronomy, divination, books, the recitation of past things—such as romances—dreams and their interpretations, and any science by which it is said that such a man knows things.

### Chapter 4. On journeys.

<image-desc>A decorative woodcut initial 'Q' with a central circular floral or geometric motif within a square frame.</image-desc>
When you are asked about any journey, whether it will be completed or not: look to the Sun and the Moon and the lord of the ascendant: and the lord of the Part of Fortune: and the lord of the place of the past conjunction or opposition: if these are cadent <term>cadent: houses that 'fall away' from the main angles, often indicating movement or weakness</term> from the angles: judge that the journey will be made and completed: especially if the lord of the ascendant applies to the lordship of the 7th house: or the lordship of the 3rd: or to Mars while he is cadent from an angle: or the lordship of the 3rd: or the 9th: and let Mars be cadent from the angle of the ascendant: or as if he falls from the ascendant by entering the twelfth house: and the lord of the ascendant is in the 9th or 3rd: for all these are signs that the journey will be completed and made: and if you find the contrary of this, judge the contrary.
