### ¶ Chapter 7: For knowing what will happen to one entering a city at the hour in which he entered.
---

<image-desc>Decorative drop cap 'Q' with intricate foliate and geometric patterns inside a square frame.</image-desc>

When someone coming from a journey enters a city: look at the **ascendant** at the hour of his entry: and if you find the lord of the second house from the ascendant **retrograde** <note>Moving backward in the sky, usually a sign of delay or reversal</note>: it signifies that he will quickly depart from it without having any good there: nor will he complete anything there for which he came. 

And if the lord of the second is in its **first station** <note>The moment a planet stops before turning retrograde</note> going toward retrogradation, he will stay there for a long time and depart from there without completing any of his affairs or requests. And if the lord himself is in its **second station** <note>The moment a planet stops before turning direct</note> wishing to go direct: he will not delay much in that land: nor will he depart from there quickly: but he will fulfill his requests with labor: and he will complete them after he has despaired of them. 

And if the lord of the second is in the ascendant: or in the **Midheaven** <note>original: "medio celi"; the 10th house, representing status and success</note> or the eleventh: he will be healthy and with prosperity in that land. And if he is in the seventh: weariness and labors will happen to him. And if in the ninth or third: he will not stay there: except for a little and he will move from that land to another place. 

And if he is in the fourth: or a malefic aspects him or is bodily joined with the same: that journey will be his last: and perhaps he will die in it. 

¶ And if the Moon is joined with the lord of the second: or aspecting him: or bodily joined with Mercury: and in an aspect of Mars: blows and wounds and fractures: or other bad things will happen to him. And if the Moon with this is in an **angle of the earth** <note>The 4th house, often associated with the grave or the end of matters</note>: he will die from this: however if she is in another angle he will have signs remaining in his body from those blows and fractures. 

<margin>☞</margin>
And if the Moon aspects Mars without an aspect of a benefic: wounds will happen to him according to the nature of the sign in which he is: however if a benefic aspects the Moon: then those accidents and illnesses will have a remedy and be healed: however if she does not have the aspect of benefics: that will endure in him: until he dies.

### ¶ Chapter 8: On knowing when the king goes to a town <note>original: "villam"; can refer to a country estate or a specific municipality</note>, what will become of those whom he leaves in his place.
---

When you are questioned at the departure of kings concerning what shall become of those remaining after him: Look if you find a **malefic** <note>original: "infortunatam"; a planet like Mars or Saturn that signifies challenge or destruction.</note> in the second sign from the **Ascendant** <note>The 1st house or rising sign, representing the start of the inquiry.</note>: there will be loss among those he leaves from his company or his kingdom. If that malefic is **Mars**: it will be through the way of discord, or by killing, or by the burning of fire. And if that same malefic is **Saturn**, that loss will be through thieves, or by drowning, or by infirmity. However, if the malefic is **received** <note>A technical term for a planet being in a sign ruled by another, which mitigates its negative effects.</note>: it will not cause loss, but will instead make things fit. And if it is in the **fall** <note>original: "casu"; a sign where a planet's power is weakened.</note> of its house or its **exaltation** <note>A sign where a planet's power is greatly increased.</note>: that evil will grow; it will be fulfilled and strengthened, especially if that planet is **retrograde** <note>Moving backward through the zodiac, often signifying delays or reversals.</note>, because that will be a sign of destruction and damnation. And judge in this same way concerning **benefics** <note>original: "fortuna"; helpful planets like Jupiter or Venus.</note> when you find them in the second sign, by judging the opposite of what we have said, because that is a sign of good. 

And you should know that when the **Lord of the Ascendant** <note>The planet ruling the rising sign.</note> or the **Moon** is afflicted by a malefic: it signifies sorrows and anxieties on the journey. And if the malefic itself is above the earth between the Ascendant and the **Midheaven** <note>original: "mediu celi"; the highest point of the chart.</note>: it signifies that this shall happen to him while going. And if that same malefic is below the earth, anxiety will happen to him in his company, and similarly while going. And if the malefic is between the **fourth and seventh houses**: it will happen to him upon his return.

### ¶ Chapter 9. On knowing whether the place where he is or the place to which he goes is better for him.

When someone asks you if the land in which he is is better for him, or if it is better to depart from it: Look if you find the **Moon** separated from malefics: say that departure is better for him than staying. And if you find her separated from benefics: staying is better than departure. 

¶ And if he asks you in this manner: "I have a need to do a certain thing; I ask whether I should do it or not": Look to the Lord of the Ascendant and the Moon. And if you find them separating from malefics and **applying** <note>Moving toward an astrological aspect or connection.</note> to benefics: command him to do whatever he has thought of in his will. And if you find them separated from benefics and applying to malefics: tell him that he should not do that thing, nor apply himself to it.

### ¶ Chapter 10. Concerning one who is away, when he shall come.

When he asks you for a person who is away, [as to] when he shall come: Look to the **Almuten** <note>original: "almutē"; the planet with the most combined dignity and strength at a specific point in the chart.</note> of the Ascendant. And if you find it in the Ascendant or the Midheaven, or giving its power to some planet existing in either of these two places: it signifies that he is coming. And if the Almuten is in the **seventh house** which is in the angle of the earth: it signifies that his arrival is delayed, and that he has not yet moved himself from the place where he is to begin coming. And if the Almuten is in the **ninth house** from the

<column-break/>

Ascendant, or in the **third house** applying to a planet existing in the Ascendant: it signifies that he is on the journey for the purpose of coming. And the Lord of the Ascendant signifies this same thing if it is in the **eighth** or **second house** applying to some planet in the Midheaven; however, if the Lord of the Ascendant is **cadent** <note>Falling away from the powerful corner houses of the chart.</note> and does not apply to any planet in an **angle** <note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses.</note>, nor aspects the Ascendant: it is a sign of delay. 

And when the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon applies to a **retrograde planet**, or the Lord of the Ascendant itself is retrograde and aspects the Ascendant: the sign is that he is coming. And if the Lord of the Ascendant is afflicted by a malefic: it signifies delay and impediment in the arrival. 

¶ And if you do not find anything among what we have said regarding the Lord of the Ascendant: look to the Moon. And if the Moon gives her light to the Lord of the Ascendant while it is in the Ascendant or near the Ascendant: it signifies that he will come quickly. And if the Moon is in the **seventh, ninth, or third house** applying to the Lord of the Ascendant: it is similarly a sign that he is coming. 

And if the Moon is separated from a planet which is on the **left of the Ascendant**—I mean below the earth—and applies to another planet existing on the **right of the Ascendant**—I mean above the earth: it is a sign that he is coming. And if the Moon is on the right of the Ascendant and applies to a planet in the Midheaven: it signifies that he is coming, yet with delay; and this is because of the Moon which was on the right of the Ascendant, for if she had been on its left, the arrival would be sooner. And when the **Lord of the Moon's house** is afflicted by a malefic: it signifies delay and impediment in the arrival. 

¶ And I say that for a man who is away from a place, the Lord of the Ascendant is his **significator** <note>The planet that represents the person or subject in the chart.</note>; and this is when the question is asked generally. However, if the question is asked specifically, such as saying: "Look for me regarding a man who has made a journey," then the planet that is in the **house of the journey** <note>The 9th house.</note> will be his significator. And if he asks for a **son**, from the **fifth house**. And if for a **brother**, from the **third**. And if for a **father**, from the **fourth**.

And when the Lord of the Ascendant is in the Ascendant, or in the **twelfth house** entering the Ascendant, or if it is retrograde, or if the planet which was the significator of the journey is retrograde, or if the Lord of the Ascendant applies to the Lord of the **tenth house**, or the Lord of the Midheaven to the Lord of the Ascendant, or if the Lord of the Ascendant is in the Midheaven, or the Lord of the Midheaven in the Ascendant, or if the Moon is received, or the Lord of the Ascendant is received: all these are signs that the absent one is coming and returns quickly. And the planet from which the Lord of the Ascendant separates is the significator of the status in which he was and which has passed. And the planet to which the same Lord of the Ascendant applies is the significator of the status in which he currently is. And the planet to which it applies after this one is the significator of his status at which he shall arrive; nor should you be certain of...

If the separation <note>The moment after two planets have met in an aspect.</note> was from a **benefic**, it signifies that the news is good, concerning happiness and joy. And if the separation was from a **malefic**, it signifies they are bad, and concerning anxieties and sorrows and **aphorisms** <note>original: "aphorismi"; here likely referring to harsh truths or dire pronouncements.</note>. ## ¶ Chapter 11. On the question concerning many absent people.

**If** you are asked about many men who are not in their places—which of them will come—you should know that some of them are fortunate and some unfortunate; some return to their places and some are destroyed; some gain and some lose. All of this cannot come from a single **Ascendant**; however, the significator for this

<column-break/>

will be the **Moon**. Name them all by their names, one after another. Afterward, look at the first, second, third, and fourth **application** <note>original: "applicationez"; the Moon's movement toward an aspect with another planet.</note> of the Moon, and so on for as many as are absent, until the number of them all is complete. Give the first application to the first man, the second to the second, and the third to the third, observing the fortunes or misfortunes of those planets and their directions and **retrogradations** <note>When a planet appears to move backward, often signifying delays or errors.</note>. Through these, judge for each of them according to the one whose significator it is. And if the applications return to those same planets again as if from the beginning, do not wonder or be troubled by it, for it is no wonder that among the men themselves, two or more may be of one status and manner, as the aspects are many. He who has a good understanding in discerning and separating these matters arrives at the truth and is made certain with God’s help. And in this same manner you shall judge if you are asked about two or three or more captains of soldiers, which of them is more powerful and bolder, by looking in the way predicted above; and you shall be made certain with God’s help.

## ¶ Chapter 12. On visions of dreams and their significations.

**Know** that visions are divided into three parts: one is the vision proceeding from God on high; the second proceeding from the power of the planets; the third from the **humors** <note>The four bodily fluids—blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile—thought in medieval medicine to determine health and temperament.</note> of the body. The first, proceeding from God on high, is that which happens through prayers and divine obedience; it is of the nature of prophecy and the glory of God which comes upon the men whom He chooses. The second, which proceeds from the power of the planets, consists of many visions that all men see; their significations are found in the **nativity** <note>The birth chart.</note> or in the **Ascendant of conception**—that is, when the seed is cast. When those significators at certain times arrive at places suitable to them, or have participation with them in the figure, or when one of the significators aspects another, then the aforementioned visions will happen. 

However, the third kind, proceeding from the force of the body’s humors, has no predictive power or necessity. It is like a man in whom **choler** <note>Yellow bile, associated with fire and heat.</note> sometimes over-abounds, either in quantity or quality; for that man will then seem to see fires. And if **phlegm** <note>Associated with water and coldness.</note> prevails, he will seem to see waters. And if **melancholy** <note>Black bile, associated with earth and darkness.</note>, it will seem that he is in darkness, or he sees that which is called the **nightmare** <note>original: "pessadiella"; a term for the "heavy presser" or incubus felt during sleep paralysis or bad dreams.</note>. 

¶ And when blood is involved, the vision follows the humors which are mixed with it from the other three in quantity or quality. However, when there is no superfluous or damaged humor in the body or the blood, then the visions will be through the power that proceeds from the planets. And know that visions proceeding from the planets are of two kinds: they will be either dreams of vanities or of truths, for they signify and demonstrate what is to come. And those of vanities are those which proceed...

### ¶ Chapter 13. On the question of a dreamer saying: "What did I see in my dream?"

<image-desc>Decorative drop cap 'C' featuring a central flower-like motif surrounded by a geometric lattice design within a square frame.</image-desc>When someone asks you regarding that which they saw in their dream: look to the **Ascendant** <note>The zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment the question is asked.</note> of that hour in which the question was made to you. And if you find **Saturn** in the Ascendant: say that they saw religious men, such as hermit brothers and the like, and oratories, and nobles who are all of good law. And if you find **Mars** in the Ascendant: say that they saw captains of soldiers, and soldiers, blood, thieves, arms, and battles. And if the **Sun**: they saw gardens, trees with fruits, gold, or a king. And if **Venus**: they saw a young maiden, or eating or drinking, or lying with a woman or taking solace, or playing or walking abroad, and white and red garments. And if **Mercury**: they saw well-composed men speaking and reasoning well, palaces with hangings and floors covered with noble cloths, foods, books, and papers of salutations and accounts. And if the **Moon**: they saw rivers or water, and pearls <note>original: "aliofar"; from the Arabic 'al-jauhar', usually referring to pearls or precious stones.</note> and other stones, or eating or drinking, or their mother or their mother’s sister. 

And **Masha'allah**, **Albubather**, and **Abu Ma'shar** <note>original: "messehala ⁊ albaybat ⁊ abzier farsal"; these are Latinized names of famous Persian and Arabic astrologers whose works were fundamental to Medieval European science.</note> said: Look at this from the sign of the **Ninth House** <note>The house of the astrological chart traditionally associated with dreams, visions, and long journeys.</note> from the Ascendant. And if you find any of the seven planets in that same house: judge the vision by whichever of them it is, according to what we have said regarding the signification when they are in the Ascendant. And you shall add to the signification of the Sun that they saw themselves flying between heaven and earth, or that they saw a great light. 

And if you do not find a planet in the Ninth, look for it in the Ascendant. And if you find none in the Ascendant, look for it in the **Third House**. And if you find it there, [well]; if not, look in the **Fourth**. And if you do not find it in the Fourth, look in the **Seventh**; otherwise look for it in the **Tenth**: and judge according to the signification of each individual planet, and you shall be made certain, with God’s help. And he says that the **Sun** is an apparent vision while waking, and the **Moon** is a covered vision while sleeping. And when you are asked about any vision: you shall know the hour of the question, and if the **significator** <note>The planet that represents the dream in the chart.</note> of the vision was **fortunate** <note>Well-placed or helped by planets like Jupiter or Venus.</note>: they saw happy and good dreams, and there is a suspicion of having something good. And if the significator was **unfortunate**: the vision will not be confirmed and brings loss.

<column-break/>

And if the significator was **received** <note>A condition where the planet is in a sign governed by another planet that "welcomes" its influence.</note> **applying** <note>Moving toward an aspect (angle) with another planet.</note> to a **fortune** <note>A benefic planet like Jupiter or Venus.</note>: the vision will be truthful and easy for the one suspecting they will have good from it; and in this, the dreams are good. And the time in which it will be confirmed: that signification will be as much as the distance from the place of the significator to the one receiving its power; for that will be the time: days, months, or years. 

And when the vision was bad and the significations bad, yet you find the significator received and applying to a fortune: say that the vision will not come to pass, nor will it be verified, nor will that dream be evil. And if the significator of that bad vision was unfortunate, it will increase and be verified. And in this manner, look at the **constellation** of that hour in which the dream occurred and the vision was seen: and judge the good or evil of it as we said before. 

And I say that you should look to the **Lord of the Ascendant** or the **Almuten** <note>term: Almuten <gloss>The planet that holds the most combined dignity and strength at a specific point in the zodiac.</gloss></note> of the Ascendant and the Moon: and see which of them you find in the Ninth or the Third house. And if you find none there, see which of them you find in the Ascendant, or in any of its **angles** <note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses, which are the strongest points in a chart.</note>: and look at that planet which is in one of the predicted places. And if it was **separated** <note>Moving away from an aspect with another planet.</note> from a fortune and applying to a fortune: the vision will be good and of good signification, and of the nature of the fortune to which it applies. And the profit of that vision will be according to the nature of its house in the figure, and the nature of the house it aspects with a good aspect. 

And if it was separated from an **infortune** <note>A malefic planet like Saturn or Mars.</note> and applying to an infortune: the vision is fearful and bad, and of bad signification. And that evil and loss will be from the planet to which it applies, and from the nature of the house in which it is in the figure, and from the nature of that infortune. And if it was separated from a fortune and applied to an infortune: say that the vision was good and beautiful, but it has a bad signification. And if it was separated from an infortune and applied to a fortune: say that the vision was ugly and bad, yet it has a good signification. And the profit and fortune will be according to the nature of the planet to which it applies, and the nature of the house in which it is in the figure, as we said before. And according to this way and rule, consider it and move from one to another, and you shall be made certain, with God’s help.

### ¶ Chapter 14. On a ship and those who go in it.

*   **Libra** to that which is raised and lowered <note>original: "eleuať ⁊ desmūť"; possibly referring to the rigging, sails, or anchor mechanisms.</note> from the prow...

### Chapter 15. On the question regarding a person's knowledge or wisdom, whether it is truth or a lie.

<image-desc>Decorative woodcut drop cap 'Q' containing a human face in profile within the letter's counter.</image-desc>
**When** you are asked about someone's knowledge, whether it is truth or a lie: give the Ascendant to the person being asked about, and the Ninth House to their knowledge. From this, if they are in good fortune, or if the Lord of the Ninth is fortunate and aspects the Lord of the Ascendant, judge that the knowledge itself is within him and that he is truthful. But if malefics are in the Ninth, or the Lord of the Ninth is afflicted and aspects the Lord of the Ascendant, it signifies that the knowledge itself is a lie and is corrupted in him. 

And look at what kind of relationship the Moon has with the Lord of the Ninth; if both apply to benefics, it signifies the verification of the knowledge and that it resides in him. If they apply to malefics, they signify the condemnation and falsehood of the knowledge. And if one of them applies to benefics and the other to malefics, look at which of them is stronger in its position, and judge according to that. If one of them applies to malefics and the other to nothing, judge that the matter is condemned. If one applies to a benefic and the other to nothing, judge the verification of that matter. And if the Ninth House and its Lord are fortunate but do not aspect 

<column-break/>

the Lord of the Ascendant: the knowledge in itself is truthful, yet that person does not practice it, nor does he derive any benefit from it. And if the Ninth and its Lord are afflicted, and do not aspect the Lord of the Ascendant, it signifies that the knowledge itself is a lie, and that the person does not practice it, nor does he have any benefit from it.

### Chapter 16. On the question regarding the work of alchemy.

<image-desc>Decorative woodcut drop cap 'Q' containing a stylized human face.</image-desc>
**When** you wish to know about someone, whether they know **alchemy** <note>term: "alkimia"; the medieval forerunner of chemistry, concerned with the transmutation of metals and the discovery of an elixir of life.</note> or not: give the Ascendant and its Lord to the seeker, and the Seventh House and its Lord to the alchemist, and the Lord of the Ninth House, which is the house of the science of alchemy. 

Afterward, look to the Lord of the Ninth to see if it is fortunate or afflicted, oriental or occidental, falling from an angle, or in an angle, or in a succedent house <note>term: "houses" (angulus/succedens/cadens); houses were categorized by strength: 'angles' were strongest (1, 4, 7, 10), 'succedent' were medium (2, 5, 8, 11), and 'cadent' were weakest (3, 6, 9, 12).</note>. See if it aspects the Lord of the Seventh or not. Then, if it aspects the Lord of the Seventh and is fortunate, it signifies that the science is truthful in him, especially if that aspect is a **trine or a sextile** <note>Harmonious astrological angles of 120 and 60 degrees.</note>, and if there is **application or reception** <note>term: "application" (applicatio); when a faster planet moves toward an aspect with a slower one, indicating a future event.</note> between them. Yet if malefics aspect there, it signifies that he labored and exhausted himself much in it, but did not reach it, nor can he reach it.

# Judgment in the Hours

If the **Sun** and **Moon** are positioned with **Fortunes** <note>term: "Fortune"; a benefic or "lucky" planet, specifically Jupiter or Venus.</note> and **Infortunes** <note>term: "Infortune"; a malefic or "unlucky" planet, specifically Saturn or Mars.</note>: and if you find them both afflicted by **Saturn** and removed from **Jupiter**: judge that the person was imprisoned or captured because of a high and famous man. And if one of them has a good mixture with **Jupiter** or **Venus**: and is in a strong place in which it has some **dignity** <note>term: "Dignity"; a position in the zodiac where a planet has particular strength or influence, such as its home sign.</note>: and **Jupiter** aspects **Leo**: it signifies that he will escape lightly and quickly, nor will he remain long in prison. And that time will be according to the number of degrees that are between the **Moon** and **Jupiter** from their **application** <note>term: "Application"; the movement of a faster planet toward a mathematical aspect with a slower planet.</note> and they shall be days; yet if the application of the **Moon** and **Jupiter** is a complete application, so that there is no degree between them: the time of liberation will be when it joins him by body <note>original: "per corpus"; a physical conjunction where the two planets occupy the same degree.</note>: and then he shall be liberated, God willing. ¶ And if the **Ascendant** <note>The zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of the question or the event.</note> is **Sagittarius** or **Pisces**: and **Jupiter** is in an **Angle** <note>term: "Angle"; the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses of an astrological chart, considered the most powerful locations.</note> or outside an angle: yet safe and free from **Infortunes**: and the **Moon** likewise: he shall have no anxiety about his prison: because no evil happens to him in person or things: and he shall see what he wished for: and thereafter he shall be honored, and with good fortune. And if it has some mixture with one or both of the **Infortunes**: Look then at which is stronger: either **Jupiter** or the **Infortunes**: judge according to this: since according to this it cannot be but that the **Infortunes** will hinder in the cause of the captive in whatever manner it may be: and that they signify labors and the hardships of prison: yet they do not bring great damage because of **Jupiter** and his good significations. ¶ And if the **Ascendant** is **Capricorn**: and **Saturn** is in any of the angles in the **Ascendant**: or in a place which the **Fortunes** aspect from a **third** <note>term: "third"; a trine aspect (120 degrees), usually considered very harmonious.</note>: and the **Fortunes** aspect **Saturn** and the **Moon**: he is removed from great trouble and labor: yet through **Saturn** a long prison is signified: and that it will last there as many years as there are degrees of application between the **Moon** and **Saturn**. And when **Jupiter** is free from **Infortunes**: and has some mixture separately with the **Moon**, it signifies joys and delights which will come to the captive in prison: and that he shall go out from it, and be liberated speedily. And the time of liberation will be the number of days according to the number of degrees that are between the degree of the **Ascendant** and **Jupiter**. And when it happens that the **Moon** is in the lower part of the sky: which is the part from the middle of the sky <note>The Midheaven or 10th house.</note> unto the angle of the earth <note>The Imum Coeli or 4th house.</note>: and **Mars** is in the upper part of the sky which is from the angle of the earth unto the angle of the middle of the sky: and aspects the **Moon** from an angle: it signifies that the captive shall go out of prison through death. And if it happens that the **Moon** is in the upper part of the sky with **Jupiter** aspecting it from an angle: and **Mars** from a **third**: it signifies that he will evade and go out of prison without labor or penalty: and without paying anything. And when the **Moon** is joined to **Saturn** in the **fourth** or **tenth** [house]: it signifies a long prison: and damage to person and property unless **Jupiter** aspects them from an angle, having some dignity in it. ¶ And if **Jupiter** and **Saturn** both aspect the angle of the **fourth** or **tenth** from a strong place: and both are common in that aspect: Look at the state of the **Moon**: and if you find her with **Saturn**: judge that the captive will flee from prison by breaking the prison and the shackles: and great penalties shall happen to him: fear, beatings, and wounds: and yet he shall not be caught because of the aspect which he has from **Jupiter** from a good and strong place.

The ancient sages said that he who is captured in the **Hour of the Sun**: shall evade in the space of one month. And he in the **Hour of Venus**: shall evade at 40 days. And he in the **Hour of Mercury**: shall have a long prison. And he in the **Hour of the Moon**: the business shall be changed: and his status stands according to the applications which the **Moon** has with the **Fortune** and **Infortune** planets: and according to this shall be his business in the lightness of liberation, or slowness. And he who is captured in the **Hour of Saturn**: shall have a long prison. And he in the **Hour of Jupiter**: his prison shall not be prolonged, and he shall be liberated quickly. And he in the **Hour of Mars**: troubles shall happen to him in prison: and he shall be placed in shackles: and beaten: and he shall have strong anxieties and labors. And we have experienced and found it to be true: that when it happens in the **Revolution of the years of the world** <note>term: "Revolution of the years of the world"; a chart cast for the moment the Sun enters Aries, used to predict the events of the coming year for the whole world.</note>: that **Mars** is in any of the houses of **Saturn**: and **Saturn** is not aspecting that house: the prisons shall be opened in 그 year and the prisoners existing therein shall go out. ¶ **Messehalla** <note>Masha'allah ibn Athari (c. 740–815 AD), a famous Persian Jewish astrologer whose works were central to medieval European astrology.</note> said: when it happens in the **Revolution of the years of the world**: that the Lord of the **tenth** [house] is in the **ninth** or **third**: it signifies that the captives and prisoners who are in that **climate** <note>term: "climate"; a geographical zone or region defined by its latitude.</note> shall go out from prison that year. And if with this the **Significator** of the King aspects him from a **third** or **sextile** <note>term: "sextile"; an aspect of 60 degrees, considered helpful and harmonious.</note>: the exit shall be by the mandate and good pleasure of the King: however, if the aspect is from an **opposition** <note>180 degrees.</note> or **quartile** <note>term: "quartile"; a square aspect (90 degrees), indicating conflict or tension.</note>: they shall go out of prison without the King's good pleasure and mandate. And when the **Significator** of the King is in a place signifying a journey: and the Lord of the **fourth** gives his power to him: it signifies that the King shall draw out the prisoners and captives. And when the Lord of the **ninth** is in that same **ninth** house: and receives the power of the Lord of the **fourth**: it signifies that an enemy of the King shall draw out the prisoners and captives.

And if in the **tenth**: he will be captured in a manifest and visible place of his house: or while going through places which he was accustomed to use: wherefore if the **Fortunes** are strong in these places: and the **Infortunes** weak: he will have no evil from that matter: nor should he care about it even if he is captured: however, if the **Infortunes** are strong and the **Fortunes** weak: and the **Moon** in the **term** of the **Infortune** applying to **Infortunes**: it signifies

that he will be captured: nor will he go out from prison until he dies, unless a **Fortune** is strong in its own place aspecting the **Moon**: for then it signifies that after anxiety and pains he will escape. And if the **Fortunes** aspect the **Ascendant** or are in the **angles**: they signify salvation in the end. Afterward, look to the **Lord of the House of the Significator**, knowing that he himself is the significator of the end: wherefore if you find that **Fortune** or a fortunate planet: judge a good and safe end. ### Judgment on one who is expelled from his place.

<image-desc>Decorative drop cap 'A' featuring interlaced foliate patterns within a square border.</image-desc>

**L**ook into the cause and business of him who is expelled by a **King** from the hour in which that business happened, by considering the **Moon**. And if with this he is applying to **Infortunes**: that which he fears will happen to him. And if he applies to **Fortunes**, he will escape from it: nor will he remain in fear. And if the **Lord of the Ascendant** is in an **angle**: and **Infortunes** similarly aspect him from an **angle**: it is the worst evil and most persistent. ### ¶ Chapter 19. On the tenth house and its questions.

<image-desc>Decorative drop cap 'H' with floral patterns.</image-desc>
**T**his is the house of the king and signifies height: the king: the kingdom: and lordship: the **governorship** <note>original: "alkaydā"; from Arabic "al-qa'id," meaning a leader, commander, or local official.</note>: nobility: a good name: fame from afar: masteries: works: services: a good appearance and honor: and it signifies visible things: reigns: good intellects: good considerations: and a good memory. And it signifies noble women and the wives of kings: and the wives of fathers: and the middle of life. And concerning the king, whether he holds right and justice among his people, or if he is just in it: and it signifies the completion of questions.

¶ The first **Lord of the Triplicity** <note>term: "Triplicity"; a group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element (Fire, Earth, Air, Water).</note> of this house signifies the mastery of the **native** <note>term: "Native"; the person for whom the horoscope is cast.</note>: the second his character and health: the third what will happen to him of good or evil in the middle of his life: and according to the power and state and form of each of these three signs, and according to the dignity which it has in the figure <note>original: "figura"; the horoscope chart.</note> and the testimonies they have from the planets, you shall judge in that matter which it signified.

And if the thought of the petitioner for any matter is in this house, and in it is a **Fiery sign**: judge that the question was for a king. And if **Earthy**: for the trade of a man and his mastery. And if **Airy**: for servants. And if **Watery**: for his enemies. The color of this house in whatever sign it may be is red mixed with green and white.

### Chapter 22. On knowing the durability of kings and those having dominions, and their lives, and to what degree of height they shall reach.

This would be inappropriate. And I have experienced these judgments in many who receive offices and lordships.

And there is among the parts <note>Arabic Parts or Lots: mathematical points in an astrological chart calculated from the distance between two planets added to the Ascendant.</note> one part of time demonstrating when: he who has lost his dignity <note>original: "dignitatem"; referring to rank, office, or high status.</note> can recover it: this part is taken from the Sun to Jupiter and projected from the Ascendant: wherefore when the Sun or Jupiter applies to the place of that part: then he shall recover his dignity or lordship. ¶ There is also another part demonstrating for him who is of the nature of kings when he might be able to reign: or for anyone when they might be able to reach the dignity pertaining to them: this part is taken from the "Part of Dignity" <note>Another specific mathematical point in the chart.</note> unto the degree of Jupiter: or from the degree of the Sun to that planet which is nearer to it and projected from the Ascendant. And when Jupiter applies to the degree of this part: or when the Sun applies there by the degree of *atazir* <note>original: "athāçir"; a method of planetary direction or progression used to time events.</note>: then he who is of the nature of reigning shall reign: or that man shall reach the dignity which he is able to achieve. ¶ There is also another part demonstrating the time when a ruler loses his dignity: and this part is taken from the Sun to Jupiter and projected from the degree of Saturn. And when Mars applies to the location of this part: then he shall lose his dignity. ¶ And if you wish to know how long he shall endure in his dignity or lordship: observe how far it is from the Lord of the Ascendant <note>The planet ruling the sign rising on the eastern horizon.</note> unto the Lord of the house of the Part of Fortune: and whatever the number of those degrees is, so long shall he endure in lordship and dignity. And if the signs in which these two planets are found are fixed signs, or in angles <note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses.</note> or succeeding houses <note>The 2nd, 5th, 8th, and 11th houses.</note>: the number of degrees shall be months: and if they are in movable or cadent <note>The 3rd, 6th, 9th, and 12th houses; usually signifying weakness.</note> signs, call them days. ¶ There is also another part which is taken by day from Mars to the Moon and by night from the Moon to Mars: and it is projected from the Ascendant: and observe in which place and sign this part falls, and it shall be known what territories or cities are in the domain of the sign in which the aforesaid part fell: and it is judged that in that land and those cities he shall have lordship and dignity.

### Chapter 23. On knowing the duration of time in lordship.

<image-desc>Ornamental drop cap 'D' decorated with scrolling vine and leaf motifs inside a square frame.</image-desc>
Al-Hasan ibn Sahl <note>original: "alheçen filius sehel"; a 9th-century Persian astrologer and politician.</note> said, he who was experienced in this: and he found the truth in it, that you should look from the degree of the Midheaven <note>original: "medij celi"; the highest point in the chart, representing career and public life.</note> unto the "Infortune" <note>A malefic planet, usually Saturn or Mars.</note> nearest to the others, just as Ptolemy demonstrated in knowing the hours of the elongation of planets from the Midheaven: and give to each of these hours one year: and that shall be the time which he shall endure in 그 lordship. ¶ Another wise man said: Observe from the degree of the Midheaven unto the degree of the Lord of the Midheaven: and whatever distance is between them: that number shall be the duration in days. ¶ Al-Hasan said regarding this reasoning: Observe the Lords of the Triplicity <note>Planets that rule the three signs of an element (fire, earth, air, water).</note> of the Sun by day and the Moon by night: and whichever of them you find stronger and in a stronger place: consider and take from the degree of the Ascendant unto the degree of that Lord: and whatever number of degrees is between them, according to that he shall endure in dignity. ¶ When any ruler has been removed from his dignity or lordship by some occasion: and it is asked of you whether he shall recover it or not: observe if the Lord of the Ascendant applies to the Lord of the Midheaven:

<column-break/>

and the Lord of the Midheaven aspects its own place: judge that he shall recover the lordship: and he shall return into it. And if the Lord of the Midheaven does not aspect its own place: he shall not return to 그 dignity but shall have another dignity in another place. And if the Lord of the Ascendant should be retrograde <note>Appearing to move backward in the sky; often signifies a return to a previous state.</note> he shall return to his dignity. And if the Moon should be in a movable sign aspecting the Lord of the Midheaven: or any planet existing in the Midheaven: and the Moon is received by that same planet: he shall return to his lordship. And if the Lord of the Midheaven should be in a movable sign: and applies to a planet existing in the Midheaven: not distant from it, one receiving the other: he shall return to his lordship. And the firmest and most powerful thing that can be in this kingdom is when the Moon applies to the Lord of the Midheaven and is received by it: and it likewise is received in its own place: for then the planet will be received in three ways: by the Moon, and by the Lord of its house: and by the Lord of the house of the Lord of its house. And if more than this ascends: it shall be the state of a king. And if these receptions are multiplied further: the kingdom shall be great and high. And if the Lord of the Midheaven separates from the Lord of the Fourth House: he shall return to his lordship. And if the Lord of the Fourth House applies to the Lord of the Tenth House: it confirms the lordship in him: and it increases and grows without his seeking it. And if the Lord of the Tenth applies to the Lord of the Ninth: lordship and dignity shall be lost. If the Lord of the Tenth applies to the Lord of the house of the Lord of the Fourth: there shall come to him lordship and dignity which he neither thought of nor sought. And know that when the Lord of the Fourth gives its power to the Lord of the Tenth: it is better than when the Lord of the Tenth gives its power to the Lord of the Fourth: because one gives and the other takes away. And if the Lord of the Tenth in the question should be in an angle or a succeeding house: he shall not be removed from dignity or lordship. ¶ When the Lord of the Ascendant and the Moon apply to the Lord of the Sixth or Twelfth or Eighth House: anxieties, losses, and evils shall happen to him in his journeys. And if those planets are "Infortunes" <note>Malefic planets like Saturn or Mars.</note>: the evil shall be worse and stronger. If the Lord of the Ascendant should be in the Ninth or Third house: and the Lord of the Twelfth in the Ascendant: he shall be captured and removed from dignity. If you find the Lord of the Midheaven: and the Lord of its Term <note>original: "termini"; a specific subdivision of a zodiac sign.</note> both fortunate: and the Moon joined with them: or that it has dignity and power in its places: and the sign of the Midheaven is common <note>original: "commune"; also known as Mutable signs (Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces).</note>: he shall return to dignity and it shall be increased for him: and he shall see what he wished and loved of his greatness: and this is according to the power of the Fortune which is the Lady of the Term of the planet which is the Lord of the Tenth House.

¶ [When] the Moon beholds the fortunes <note>original: "fortunas"; referring to the benefic planets Jupiter and Venus, which bring good luck.</note>, and the Lord of Dignity is falling <note>original: "cadens"; located in a "cadent" house (the 3rd, 6th, 9th, or 12th), which was considered a weak or ineffective position in astrology.</note>, or under the rays <note>original: "sub radijs"; a planet too close to the Sun is "combust" or hidden, losing its power.</note>, or not beholding the Ascendant, or is in the 2nd or 8th house; then we ought to judge that the ruler will not be well-established in that dignity, but will always be laborious within it. Similarly, when the Lord of Dignity (that is, the planet that demonstrates status) is in its "fall" <note>A specific sign where a planet's influence is at its weakest.</note> or is unfortunate, it signifies the same thing.

¶ An example of this: when Alhazen, son of Sehel <note>original: "alhazen filius sehel"; referring to Sahl ibn Bishr, a famous 9th-century Jewish astrologer and mathematician.</note>, departed from Arasen, Leo was the Ascendant, and the Sun (its Lord) was in Leo. The Moon and Jupiter were in the Midheaven <note>The highest point of the chart, representing career and public life.</note>, and Venus (the Lady of the Midheaven) was in the 2nd house, in her fall, and not beholding the Ascendant nor its Lord. He was never in that dignity without distress or labor until he was removed from it. The presence of Jupiter and the Moon in the Midheaven in Taurus did not profit him, nor did the Sun being in the Ascendant, nor the Ascendant being Leo (which is a sign suited for lordship), because the Sun as its Lord was poorly placed. Therefore, always look into this matter and chapter diligently. And know that the foundation is the "election" <note>The practice of choosing the most auspicious time to begin an endeavor.</note> of the chosen one at the beginning.

¶ Now, when you wish to know what will happen to a ruler in his dignity regarding judgments or poverty, or if he will gather wealth or dissipate it: look in this matter to the Part of Fortune <note>A mathematical point in a horoscope representing material well-being.</note> and its Lord, as well as to the Moon and the degree of the House of Substance <note>The 2nd house of the zodiac, governing money and possessions.</note>. And if the Moon applies to the degree of the Part of Fortune, and she is fortunate herself, and the degree of the House of Substance is similarly fortunate, it signifies that he will have much substance and will be powerful in gathering it. And when the unfortunates <note>original: "infortune"; referring to the malefic planets Mars and Saturn.</note> are falling away from the Moon and from the Lord of the Part of Fortune along with what we have said before, it signifies the salvation and increase of his substance.

And when an unfortunate planet is in the 2nd house, and the Part of Fortune is unfortunate, and the Moon is applying to an unfortunate and carrying light from one unfortunate to another, it signifies that he will have little substance, and he will not be firm nor stable in it, and he will dissipate it on things that will come to nothing, nor return to his benefit. And when the Moon and the fortunes are falling away from the Part of Fortune, it signifies that he will lose the greatest part of his substance and dissipate it. And if, with this, Mars unfortunates it, he will take it from him by violence, and they will give him pain because of it. And if Saturn unfortunates it, he will spend it in the defense of his body, and in removing evil from himself, and in paying collections <note>Likely referring to taxes, fines, or tribute.</note>, such as for calumnies and similar things.

And if either of these two unfortunates is joined with the Part of Fortune or with its Lord, or aspects it from a square <note>original: "quarta"; a 90-degree angle, considered a stressful aspect.</note> or opposition, especially if that same aspect is from one of the "angles" <note>The four most powerful houses in a chart: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th.</note> of the Ascendant, or if the Moon beholds the Part of Fortune while it is unfortunate: he will have opponents and those demanding the substance he has gathered, and they will take the greater part of it. And if that same unfortunate is Mars, his robbers will be his enemies, thieves, and evildoers. And if the Part of Fortune applies to an unfortunate, and the Moon to that same unfortunate, but the Lord of the Part is not unfortunate, it signifies the salvation of his substance and his honor; and afterward, he shall not lose from that which he has gathered, except what he spends and draws out

<column-break/>

by his own good pleasure and will for his own uses. And if the unfortunates and fortunes behold the Part of Fortune and its Lord with an equal aspect, so that one does not have a better aspect than the other, then look to the state of the Moon: to which group (the fortunes or the unfortunates) she is more closely joined, and which of them she beholds, and how she is powerful in her place, and if she has testimony or power or dignity in the part she beholds; and give the judgment and power to that side which the Moon beholds; and according to her, judge of misfortune or fortune.

### Chapter 27. On the eleventh house and its actions

<image-desc>A large ornamental woodcut initial 'H' featuring a figure in a landscape with architectural elements and foliage.</image-desc>

This house is of trust, hope, fortune, and gratitude. It signifies helpful children, rewards, and the friendships of high-ranking men, and having secrets with them, and being loved and well-regarded among them. It signifies trade and gifts "given under the cloak" <note>original: "dona data sub cappa"; an idiom for private gifts, tips, or bribes.</note> such as those given to judges <note>original: "alcaldis"; from the Arabic 'al-qadi'.</note> and advocates so that they might help. It also signifies the quantity of enemies <note>While the 12th house usually governs enemies, this text attributes their quantity to the 11th.</note>, and it is the house of the king's wealth. It signifies those who are absent, profitable things, populations, and high

<column-break/>

and great lineages. It is also the significator of the end of the middle part of a man's life, and what happens to him during that time of good or evil. 

The first lord of its <term>triplicity</term> <note>One of three planets that govern a sign based on its element (Fire, Earth, Air, or Water).</note> is the significator of things in which one has trust. The second is the significator of fortune. The third is of friends, friendship, gratitude, and good fame. And when you find the significator of the thought in this house in a question, and it is a **fire sign**: say that the question is for a thing in which he has trust, and for a thing which he fears he does not have. And if it is a **water sign**: say the question is for fortune. And if **air**: for friends. And if **earth**: for his predecessors. The color of this house, in whatever sign it may be, is saffron <note>A deep yellow-orange.</note> tending somewhat toward white.

### Chapter 28. On a question regarding a thing in which one has trust.

<image-desc>A large ornamental woodcut initial 'C' containing decorative foliate patterns.</image-desc>

When someone asks you about a thing in which they have trust, or for some dignity which they trust to have from the king: look if the Lord of the 11th house <term>applies</term> <note>Moves toward a mathematical relationship (aspect) with another planet.</note> to the Lord of the Ascendant, or the Lord of the Ascendant to the Lord of the 11th. Judge that he will have the thing in which he has trust, and that he will move toward it. 

And if the aspect is a <term>trine</term> or <term>sextile</term> <note>Harmonious aspects of 120 or 60 degrees.</note>: he will have it quickly, easily, and in a good manner. And if it is a <term>square</term> or <term>opposition</term> <note>Tense aspects of 90 or 180 degrees.</note>: he will have it with weariness and labor. And if you find the Lord of the 11th in an angle and "received" <note>A planet is "received" when it is in a sign governed by the planet it is aspecting, implying hospitality or assistance.</note>: judge that the thing in which he has trust will be completed just as the petitioner wished. 

And if you find the receiver of the Moon's disposition in a <term>common sign</term> <note>Also called "mutable" signs (Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces).</note>: judge that the seeker will have only a small part of the thing he hopes for. And if that same receiver of the Moon is in a <term>moveable sign</term> <note>Also called "cardinal" signs (Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn).</note>: he will have only the name of it, or very little of it. And if it is in a **fixed sign**: he will have the hoped-for thing totally and completely. 

And if you find the receiver of the Moon "infortunate" <note>Afflicted by harsh aspects from Mars or Saturn.</note>: that thing will be ruined after he has it and is in possession of it. And if you find the receiver of the Moon is himself received: he will likewise have it, and even more than he hoped for. And if you find the Lord of the Ascendant received: he will have whatever he hoped for according to his wish. 

And if someone asks you if he will be joined with some friend of his or not: look to the Lord of the Ascendant and the Moon; if you find them applying to the Lord of the 11th, they will both be joined. And if the application is a trine or sextile in conjunction: they will have joy, agreement, and love. And if the application is a square or opposition in conjunction: they will disagree and bicker, and one will grow weary of the other. And know that an application from an opposition is worse than from a square. 

And if someone asks you about a "covered" thing <note>A hidden matter or a question where the petitioner does not name the specific object.</note>, saying: "Look for me regarding a thing in which I have trust, whether I shall have it or not": consider if you find the Lord of the Ascendant and the Moon applying to <term>fortunes</term> <note>Beneficial planets, usually Jupiter or Venus.</note> and in angles or "succeding" houses <note>The houses following the angles: the 2nd, 5th, 8th, and 11th.</note>: he will have the thing; otherwise not. However, this is for when the seeker has explained the question and named the thing he trusts to have. Look to it...

...in the place pertaining to those things in the figure: just as we declared to you regarding the natures of the 12 houses and their properties.

### ¶ Chapter 29. On love.

When you are asked about the love between two people, whether they love each other or not: Look at the <term>Lord</term> <note>The planet that rules a specific house in the zodiac chart.</note> of the 1st and the 7th. If the Lords of these houses behold the Lord of the <term>Ascendant</term> <note>The sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of the question; it represents the person asking.</note> from a <term>trine</term> <note>original: "de tertio"; an angle of 120 degrees, considered very harmonious.</note> or a fertile aspect, they love each other. And if from a <term>square</term> <note>original: "quarta"; an angle of 90 degrees, considered tense or difficult.</note> or an <term>opposition</term> <note>An angle of 180 degrees, indicating conflict.</note>: they do not love each other: especially if one of them is the Lord of the 12th house. And if two others behold them there: the love will be stronger and firmer. And if all three behold them there: the love will be firmer and stronger: especially if the aspect is from <term>fixed signs</term> <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, and Aquarius, which represent stability and endurance.</note>.

### ¶ Chapter 30. On friendships, enmities, and harmonies.

Look in this matter at the Ascendant and the 7th house and their Lords: and at the planets that are in these two places: and at the <term>applications</term> <note>When a faster planet moves toward an aspect with a slower one.</note> and <term>separations</term> <note>When a faster planet moves away from an aspect.</note> of them. Make the **Moon** a participant in the significance with them: if she has a separation or application: and if she does not have one, leave her aside. And if she does, join the planet from which she separates with the Lord of the Ascendant in meaning, and the one to which she applies with the Lord of the 7th in meaning. Similarly, look afterward how and by what aspects they apply to one another: namely, by trine or <term>sextile</term> <note>An angle of 60 degrees, considered helpful and friendly.</note>, or <term>conjunction</term> <note>When two planets are in the same degree of the same sign.</note>: and if there is <term>reception</term> <note>A condition where one planet is in a sign ruled by the other, indicating mutual support or hospitality.</note> between them. If these applications are in a good manner: the affection between them will be good and healthy. And if the aspect is from a square or opposition, and there is no reception between them: there is no love between them, but discord, quarrels, and losses. And if with this square or opposite aspect there is reception: it will be less and lighter. Look similarly at the planet from which the Moon separates and to which she applies, and in what manner one applies to the other or separates: and judge from them just as you judged from the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the 7th. Similarly, judge from the planets you find in the Ascendant and in the 7th: and from their applications and separations. And if the said <term>significators</term> <note>The planets representing the people involved in the inquiry.</note> or any of them have no application or separation, nor does any planet carry the light from one to the other, nor is there a planet that collects their lights: those people do not know each other, nor does one know anything of the other.

### ¶ Chapter 31. On knowing what happens between two people, whether good or evil.

Look at the Lord of the 10th house <note>The house of status, success, and authority.</note> [and see] to whom he applies, or who applies to him: and which of the <term>peregrine</term> <note>A planet that has no specific dignity or strength in its current position, like a traveler in a foreign land.</note> planets is in it: and to whom that same planet applies, or who applies to him. For if it is the Lord of the Ascendant or the 10th, there is profit for that lord: since if any planet that is in the 10th applies to the Lord of the Ascendant, or the Lord

<column-break/>

of the Ascendant applies to that planet: or that planet to the Lord of the 10th: or the Lord of the 10th to the Lord of the Ascendant: or to a planet that is in the Ascendant: or a planet that is in the Ascendant to the Lord of the 10th: and that aspect is by trine or sextile or conjunction: it will be a benefit and good for the seeker. And judge in this way concerning the Lord of the 7th if you find aspects and applications of this kind for him. And if the application is by square or opposition: judge loss, evil, and sadness in the part where those aspects are found.

### ¶ Chapter 32. On knowing at what time good or evil will occur, and when it is.

You shall know this from the conjunctions of the two significators of the seeker and of the one for whom he asks: for when they join in one of the signs in one degree: in that conjunction the matter will happen. However, if the question is explained and distinct—so that he says he asks for his brother or father, or for his servant or his wife—then look to the house that belongs to the reason of that question, and what suits it, and consider the Lord of that house and the planet you find in it: and take it in place of the 7th house and its Lord: and you shall judge by it just as you judged by the 7th house and its Lord.

### ¶ Chapter 33. On the 12th House and the questions that are in it.

This house is the significator of enemies, labors, pains, sorrows, prisons, captives, envies, grumblings, deceptions, bad habits, anxieties, and punishments. And it is the significator of beasts and animals, and of fears, hindrances, and the loss of limbs; of substance, thieves, and evildoers; of enchanters and of servants who do not obey their masters; and of outcasts and the foot-soldiers of justice. And it signifies what is lost of one's substance, and men who are not in their own places but outside; and those wishing to be officials for others; contempt; and long and hidden anger; and vile and despised men who change the law and do evil deeds; and what happens to the child while it is in the mother's womb; and it signifies the lightness and heaviness of birth. Thus, when this house is a <term>crooked sign</term> <note>The signs from Capricorn to Cancer; these were traditionally thought to cause more difficulty in certain calculations.</note> and is unfortunate, or its Lord is in a crooked sign and unfortunate, or the Moon is in a crooked sign—then those planets beholding it in any of the <term>angles</term> <note>The most powerful houses: 1, 4, 7, and 10.</note> signifies difficulty in birth. And it is the significator of all terrestrial, four-footed beasts. ¶ The first <term>Lord of the Triplicity</term> <note>A system where three planets rule a specific element (Fire, Earth, Air, Water) depending on the time of day.</note> is the significator of labor, prison, pain, and sorrow; the second, of enemies; the third, of animals and beasts. And when it happens in questions that the significator of the question is in this house, and the house itself is a <term>fiery sign</term> <note>Aries, Leo, or Sagittarius.</note>, the question was about misery and pain. And if it is an <term>earthy sign</term> <note>Taurus, Virgo, or Capricorn.</note>: about prison or being captured. And if a <term>watery sign</term> <note>Cancer, Scorpio, or Pisces.</note>: about beasts. And if an <term>airy sign</term> <note>Gemini, Libra, or Aquarius.</note>: about enemies. The color of this house, in whatever sign it may be, is green tending toward white.

# Chapter 34. On the racing of horses and on knowing which of them will win. &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; ¶ Chapter 35. On a question regarding enemies.

When you are asked about two animals running, which of them will win in the race: and the seeker has their own animal in the race, or another for which they are concerned: look at the <term>Lord</term> <note>The planet ruling the specific hour or sign.</note> of that hour in which the question was made. And if you find it in the sign of the <term>Ascendant</term> <note>The zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of the question, representing the person asking or their interests.</note>: their animal or the other for which they are concerned will win. <margin>¶</margin> And if the Lord of the hour is in the <term>Midheaven</term> <note>original: "medio celi"; the 10th house, representing the highest point in the sky.</note>: say that it will be second after the first. And say the same if it is in the eleventh or the third house. And if you find it in the seventh: it will be between the first and the last. And if in the fourth: say that it will be the last of all. And if it is in its <term>fall</term> <note>original: "casu"; a position in the zodiac where a planet's influence is weakened.</note>, the rider will have fear while running upon that animal, and perhaps will fall from it. And if, in addition to this, the <term>malefics</term> <note>original: "infortune"; planets like Mars or Saturn that were traditionally thought to bring hardship.</note> behold it, the rider will break some member of his body which corresponds to the sign in which the significator is placed. <note>In medieval astrology, each zodiac sign ruled a specific part of the human body (e.g., Aries rules the head, Taurus the neck).</note> And if the aspect of the malefic is from an <term>opposition</term> <note>An angle of 180 degrees, the most tense astrological relationship.</note>: the runner will die from that fall. And the worst that can happen in this is if, along with what we have said, the Lord of that sign is afflicted, and the **Moon** likewise is afflicted. <margin>¶</margin> And if the seeker has no animal in that race, and asks which animal will win the race: Look at the Lord of the hour: and if you find it in the Ascendant or another favorable place, or in the Midheaven or the eleventh house: say that the animal which wins the race will be the color of the planet you found in any of the aforesaid places. And if the significator which indicated victory is in its <term>exaltation</term> <note>A specific sign where a planet is most powerful.</note>, or its own house, or <term>triplicity</term>, or its <term>term</term> or <term>face</term> <note>Sub-divisions of zodiac signs that give planets varying degrees of strength.</note>: the animal that wins is well-known and famous. And the strongest indicator in this is when it is in its exaltation. After this, its own house; however, the others have only a little fame. And if the significator is not in any of the aforesaid places: that animal is a stranger and unknown. And if along with this it is in its fall: it is a bad animal, ugly and of ill-temper. And if it is in its exaltation or its house, it will be personally known and famous. And if in its triplicity, it is named in its own land, but not personally famous. And if in its term or face, it is named in the town where it is from, yet not personally, nor is it known from which land it comes. <margin>¶</margin> And if you are asked what the age of the animal is: Look if it is <term>oriental</term> <note>Rising before the sun.</note>; the significator indicates it has two teeth. <note>Medieval horsemen judged a horse's age by its teeth; "two teeth" indicates a young horse, about two years old.</note> And if it is <term>occidental</term> <note>Setting after the sun.</note>, it is old; and if it is <term>northern</term>, it has four teeth. <margin>¶</comment> And if you are asked what kind of man the owner of the winning animal is: Look if the sign of the Ascendant is the house of the **Sun**: he is of the kings' animals. And if the Lord is **Saturn**: he is an old man or a servant, or a low-born man who is not of good lineage—unless **Saturn** is in an <term>angle</term> <note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, which are the most powerful positions.</note> and a good place. And if it is the house of **Jupiter**: he is an honored man of good offspring. And if the house of **Mars**: he is a man who involves himself in arms, military service, and strife. And if the Lord of **Venus** or **Mercury**: he is a king's man, or a lord, or a king's scribe, or perhaps a woman. And if the house of the **Moon**: he is a merchant whose animal is brought to be sold. And if that same significator of victory is in the Ascendant, the animal is known and famous for its goodness; and if descending: it has neither fame nor goodness.

If a question is made to you for enemies with none named: look for this from the twelfth house and its Lord; but if someone is named to you, look from the seventh and its Lord, considering their <term>applications</term> <note>When a faster planet moves toward an aspect with a slower one.</note>; and whatever is between them according to what we have told and distinguished for you in the questions of the twelve signs, judge according to this and you will be certain, with God’s help.

### ¶ Chapter 36. On revenge.

When a question is made to you on this, look at the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the house of the end. <note>The 8th house, associated with death and the "end of things."</note> And if both are <term>received</term> <note>A state where planets occupy each other's signs, indicating cooperation or mutual influence.</note> and the **Moon** is in a <term>movable sign</term> <note>Aries, Cancer, Libra, or Capricorn; signs that indicate action and change.</note>, he will not be able to escape. And it will be worse if the Lord of the house of the **Moon** does not behold the **Moon**, nor the Lord of the Ascendant behold the Ascendant; for then the murderer will be captured and killed, unless the **Moon** applies to a <term>fortune</term> <note>A benefic planet like Jupiter or Venus.</note>; for if it applies to a fortune, he will escape by ransoming himself through his possessions. And if after the fortune it applies to a malefic, they will take revenge on him without any ransom.

### ¶ Chapter 37. On the question of one wishing to adhere to one of two people, which of them will be better for him.

When someone asks you to which of two named people it will be better for him to adhere: give the first Ascendant to the seeker. Afterward, look at what rank those two are: and if they are kings: look at which of them is greater; give him the **Sun** and the other the **Moon**, judging one of them by **Leo** and the other by **Cancer**. And if they are <term>alcaydis</term> <note>original: "alcaydi"; from the Arabic *al-qā’id*, meaning a military commander, governor, or judge.</note> or judges, or those who involve themselves in the law, or what is similar to it: give to one of them **Gemini** and to the other **Virgo**. And if they are lords of soldiers or the king's or emperor's alcaydis or his powerful men, or those who farm his revenues: give one **Aries** and the other **Scorpio**. And if they are the king's entertainers or guardians of his women or children, or those who involve themselves with precious stones: give one **Libra** and the other **Taurus**. And if they are men of old secrets, or guardians of treasures, or those inheriting from the dead or hiders of substance: give one **Capricorn** and the other **Aquarius**. And if one of them is on the part of **Saturn** and the other on the part of **Mars**; or one on the part of **Jupiter** and the other on the part of **Venus**; or one on the part of **Sun** and the other on the part of **Mercury**; or one on the part of the **Moon** and the other on the part of **Mercury**: in this manner you shall always combine them. And look at the Lords of the houses, and those who behold them from the fortunes or malefics, and the Lord of the Ascendant, and what kind of participation or friendship or enmity he has with each of the Lords of the houses: and the aspect of the Lords of the houses to the other, and their aspect to the Ascendant regarding friendship or enmity. And when you have examined all this, join them together...

In this book, I have added rare and noble matters that were scattered and hidden through the books of the ancients; and they were spoken of through signs in all manners of the judgments of the stars. And if the Sun is in the seventh house in this manner: it signifies the son will not be reared. ¶ When a malefic is in the ascendant, and has some dignity in it and some fortune looks upon it: it signifies that nursing will be completed; because when malefics are in their own dignities, their malice is diminished—Mars, especially if it be by night in feminine signs; and Saturn, by day in masculine signs.

And when it is not in its dignity, its fortune and goodness descend and diminish. ¶ When the **Moon** is diminished in light and "obsessed" <note>original: "obsessa"; an astrological term meaning the planet is trapped between two harmful planets (malefics)</note>, and has no aspect from a benefic, the child will die and will not be reared; and perhaps he will be blind. The mother will also be in danger and perhaps will die. ¶ When the lords of the triplicities <note>original: "triplicitatum"; groups of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element (Fire, Earth, Air, Water)</note>, namely the <term>Hyleg</term> <note>The planet designated as the "giver of life" in a birth chart</note>, are strong and firm, but a **malefic** <note>original: "infortuna"; referring to Saturn or Mars</note> is in the **ascendant** <note>The zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</note> and the lord of the second house is a malefic, it signifies that the child will live and be reared, yet in evil, anxiety, infirmities, and labors. ¶ When **Venus** and **Mercury** are joined in one degree in the ascendant, it signifies that the child will not live, because both are contrary and cannot be joined for good. ¶ The conjunction of planets does not signify humanity; I mean to say that when four or five planets are joined in the ascendant of someone born, that person will not live. ¶ The commentator said: the King of our city called me, for one of his women had given birth to a son. The ascendant was **Libra** at 8 degrees, in the **term** <note>A specific subdivision of a zodiac sign ruled by a particular planet</note> of **Mercury**. In it were **Jupiter** and **Venus**, **Mars** and **Mercury**. A company of astrologers gathered there, and each of them gave their opinion; I remained silent. The King said to me, "Why do you have nothing to say?" I replied to him: "Give me the space of three days; for if your son passes the third day, it will be a great miracle." And when the child had completed 24 hours of life, he sat himself up and spoke and made signs with his hand. The King was greatly terrified, and I said it was possible that he might speak some prophecy or some miracle. And the King went to the child and we with him to hear what he would say; and the infant said: "I am born unfortunate, and I am born to indicate the loss of the kingdom that shall happen and the destruction of the people of **Al-Mansur** <note>original: "gentis almanaç"; likely referring to the Al-Mansur dynasty or family in the context of the original Arabic text</note>." And immediately the child fell back and died. ¶ For the wise say that the life of those born and the diversity of their movements exist only through the expansion <note>The separation or distance between planets</note> of the planets. However, when they are joined together and their lights are joined together, they do not live, nor do they signify life. ¶ When both **luminaries** <note>The Sun and the Moon</note> and the ascendant and its lord are joined bodily with malefics, or by a "square" or "opposition" <note>original: "quarta aut oppositioē"; harsh angles of 90 or 180 degrees between planets</note> and without an aspect from a benefic, it signifies that he will not be reared, unless the lords of the triplicity are fortunate and supported and well-fixed in the **angles** <note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses of the chart, considered the most powerful</note>; then indeed he may live, yet a life that is bad and anxious. ¶ When the **Moon** is in any angle and any malefics aspect her—and most strongly **Mars** from a square or opposition—and the Moon is not "received" <note>Reception occurs when a planet is in a sign ruled by the planet it is aspecting</note> by that malefic, nor does a benefic aspect her, it signifies that the child will not taste anything; and if he does taste, he will not be nourished. ¶ When the **Part of Fortune** and the **Part of the Secret** are in the term of a benefic or in the house of a benefic, or in good places from the ascendant, and the Moon is with them and some malefic "receiving" her aspects her, it signifies that the child will be reared and have a long life; and he will be fortunate and have a good and great name. ¶ When the lord of the ascendant is **combust** <note>Too close to the Sun, which "burns up" the planet's power</note>, it does not signify nourishment, and especially if the ascendant is **Capricorn**, or if that combustion

<column-break/>

occurs in the **eighth house** <note>The house associated with death</note>. ¶ When the lord of the ascendant and the <term>Almuten</term> <note>original: "almutez"; the planet with the most combined dignity and strength in a specific place in the chart</note> are to the right of the ascendant, and benefics aspect and receive them, and the degree of the ascendant is with a benefic having some testimony in the ascendant, it signifies that the child will be reared and have fortune and prosperity in his town and in his place. However, if these two—namely the Almuten and the lord of the ascendant—are unfortunate, he will be expelled from his land and his place, and will always live with burdens and fear. ¶ When the **Moon** is increasing in light and bodily joined with **Mars**, especially in **Aries**, it signifies a short life. And it signifies the same when she is with **Saturn** at the end of the month, with both of them existing under the rays of the Sun. ¶ When the lords of the triplicity of the ascendant are in the **third house**, made unfortunate by any planet, it signifies a short life—unless the lord of the triplicity is the Moon, because the Moon is strong in the third house because of her "joy" there. Look at the place of the Moon at the hour of birth, and to that degree in which she is, add 26 degrees: and look at who aspects that degree, and in which term it falls. For if it is in the term of a benefic and a benefic aspects it there, it signifies good nourishment, and especially if that term belongs to a powerful benefic. And direct the Almuten by <term>Atazir</term> <note>original: "athaçir"; a method of advancing planetary positions to predict timing</note>, and give to each sign one day, or a month, or a year. ¶ And know that the malefics prohibit life by afflicting the ascendant, or the luminaries, or the Part of Fortune. And look similarly at how far it is from that malefic to a benefic at any time. And set the degrees as years or months or days or hours. ¶ When the lords of the triplicities (namely the Hyleg) are firm and strong, and there is a malefic in the ascendant and a malefic in the **second house**, and the lord of the second house is in a square or opposition to the malefics: the child will live and be reared in infirmities; however, he will be weak and thin, and in his rearing, obstacles, wants, hunger, and misery will happen to him. ¶ The greatest power <margin>no</margin> that **Mars** has in cutting off life is when he is in **Aries** in daytime births above the earth; and **Saturn** when he is in **Capricorn** above the earth in nighttime births. ¶ When **Mars** aspects the luminaries from an opposition or a square by day, or **Saturn** by night from a "foreign sign" <note>original: "signo pegrino"; a sign where the planet has no essential dignity or strength</note>, and they have no aspect of any benefic, it signifies that the parents will abhor the child and expel him from their power. And if the **Sun** is more afflicted, he will be expelled on the part of the father. And if the **Moon** is more afflicted, this will be on the part of the mother. And if it afflicts both, it will be on the part of both.
