### ¶ Chapter Three: On the Hylech, who is the giver of life.

IN this chapter, the ancient sages were in great disagreement with one another, for this matter is very subtle and deep. We shall state here the reasoning for this according to the opinion of the Greeks, the opinion of the Moors <note>referring to Islamic or Arabic-speaking astrologers</note>, and the opinion of the people of **Layrach** <note>original: "layrach"; likely referring to Al-Iraq (the Iraqis)</note>. We shall state each in its proper place; however, we will first state the opinion of **Ptolemy** <note>Claudius Ptolemy, the 2nd-century scholar whose work "Tetrabiblos" formed the foundation of Western astrology</note>. Ptolemy proceeded in this manner: he adjusted the degree of the ascendant, and afterwards subtracted five degrees from it, and then formed the **houses** <note>divisions of the sky</note> upon that. Then he looked at the five <term>Hylech</term> <note>The "giver of life," a planet or point used to calculate life span</note> candidates, which are the Sun, the Moon, the degree of the ascendant, the **Part of Fortune** <note>a calculated point representing health and prosperity</note>, and the location of the conjunction or opposition <note>the New Moon or Full Moon</note> preceding the birth. He also looked at the planets having power in their places; and if any of them were found in the ascendant, the **Midheaven** <note>original: "medio celi"; the highest point in the sky at birth</note>, or the 11th, 7th, or 9th house, he took that for the Hylech. He did not accept any other locations for this, nor did he in any way accept a planet existing below the earth as the Hylech, unless it was within those 25 degrees that follow the degree of the ascendant, even if they were below the earth. And for a day birth, he took the Sun first; and if he did not find it fit for this, he took the Moon. And if the Moon was not fit, he took the planet having power in the place of the Sun, or in the place of the preceding conjunction or opposition, or in the ascendant. I mean to say that it should have three **dignities** <note>types of astrological authority</note> there, whatever they may be, so that it shall be called the lord and power of that place; or more than three dignities in the predicted places. And if he found none of these, he took the degree of the ascendant. However, if it was a night birth, he took the Moon first if it was fit; otherwise the Sun if it was fit; otherwise the planet having dignity in the place of the Moon, or in the place of the preceding opposition, or in the place of the Part of Fortune. And if we find none of these to be fit, we take at last—if the birth was following a conjunction <note>New Moon</note>—the degree of the ascendant; and if it followed an opposition <note>Full Moon</note>, the Part of Fortune. And if both **luminaries** <note>original: "luminaria"; the Sun and the Moon</note> and the lord of the conjunction (if it was by day) or opposition (if it was by night) were in fit places to be the Hylech, it is proper for you 

<column-break/>

first to take the stronger and more suitable of the luminaries; and that one has the greater lordship who is first in the Midheaven; and afterwards the one in the ascendant; then the one in the 11th house, and afterwards the one in the 7th, and finally the one in the 9th house. This is the opinion of Ptolemy regarding the Hylech. ¶ But other sages have disagreed greatly on this; however, that which the majority have agreed upon is that for day births, they start first with the Sun. They look to see if it is in one of the **angles** <note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</note> or in a **succedent** <note>the 2nd, 5th, 8th, or 11th houses</note> house, and in a masculine sign and a masculine quadrant, and if it aspects any of its own dignities, then it shall be the Hylech. And if it is not so, and does not aspect any of its dignities, it will not be fit for the Hylech; and you shall seek the Hylech from the Moon. And if you find it in an angle or succedent house, and in a feminine sign and feminine quadrant, and it aspects any of its dignities, take it for the Hylech; otherwise it will not be a fit Hylech. And then look at the birth: if it followed a New Moon, take the Hylech from the degree of the ascendant. And if any lord having some dignity there aspects that degree, you should take it for the Hylech. And if the ascendant is not fit, seek the Hylech from the Part of Fortune. And if the Part of Fortune is not fit, seek the Hylech from the place of the conjunction or opposition preceding the birth. And if these are not fit, the birth will have no Hylech; and it will be necessary for you to return to directing by the <term>Athazir</term> <note>A method of "moving" planets through time to predict events; here used to find the end of life</note> the Hylech locations to the places of the **malefics** <note>original: "infortunarum"; harmful planets like Saturn or Mars</note> and their rays; and there you will find the place of the end [of life]. And if the birth was at night: seek the Hylech first from the Moon, just as you began to seek it from the Sun by day. And if you find it in an angle or succedent house in a feminine sign and feminine quadrant, and any of its dignities aspect it, that will be the Hylech. Otherwise, seek the Hylech from the Sun. And if you find it in an angle or succedent house in a masculine sign and masculine quadrant, and anyone having dignities there aspects it, take it for the Hylech; otherwise it will not be fit for the Hylech. And then if the birth followed a Full Moon, seek the Hylech from the Part of Fortune, just as you sought it from the Moon and Sun. And if the Part of Fortune is not fit for the Hylech, seek the Hylech from the degree of the ascendant. And if none of these are fit for the Hylech, seek the Hylech from the degree of the conjunction or opposition preceding the birth. And if it is in an angle or succedent house and is aspected by something having any of the five dignities there, take it for the Hylech. And when the Sun is the Hylech but has no <term>Alchocoden</term> <note>The planet that "gives the years," used to calculate the actual number of years a person will live once the Hylech is identified</note>, seek the Hylech from the degree of the Moon. And if that should be the Hylech and has no Alchocoden, seek the Hylech from the degree of the ascendant, if the birth followed a New Moon. And if that degree is the Hylech and has no Alchocoden, seek the Hylech from the Part of Fortune; however, if the birth followed a Full Moon, begin first from the Part of Fortune. And if that is the Hylech and has no Alchocoden, seek the Hylech from the degree of the ascendant. And if it is the Hylech and none of these has an Alchocoden, seek the Hylech from the degree of the conjunction or opposition preceding the birth. And if none of them has an Alchocoden, since the newborn has neither Hylech nor Alchocoden, it is...

And Dorotheus said that when the Sun is in a feminine sign and in a feminine **fourth part** <note>a quadrant of the zodiac</note>, it is not fit to be the hylech; for he says that it is "effeminated" twice and thus weakened. And he says similarly of the Moon: when it is in a masculine sign and in a masculine fourth part, it is not fit to be the hylech, for he says it is "masculinized" twice and weakened. However, when the Sun is found in a feminine sign and in a feminine fourth, it is not fit to be hylech. And it is the same way for the Moon. The sons of one nation say that the ninth house is not fit for the hylech, and they place the eighth house as fit for the hylech. And in my book, which I have named the *Book of Signs*, which speaks through signs, there are 5 chapters on the hylech and alcochoden. ### Chapter Four: On the Alcochoden.

<image-desc>Decorative initial D featuring a floral/leafy pattern within a square frame.</image-desc>

Ptolemy says that the **alcochoden** is the planet having the greatest dominion in the hylech; and that planet which has more dignities in the hylech is the alcochoden, whether it **aspects** <note>forms a geometric relationship</note> there or does not aspect. However, Dorotheus does not appoint an alcochoden except for one who has dominion in the hylech and who aspects it; and he places the dominion of the **term** be-

<column-break/>

-fore the lord of the house and the lord of the triplicity. And if there are two, three, or four who aspect there, the fittest of them is the one having more dignities there. For example: let us suppose that there is one planet which is the lord of the house, and another of the exaltation and term, and another of the term, triplicity, and **face** <note>a 10-degree division of a sign</note>. Thus, the one who has three dignities is more fit than the one who has two. And the one who has four is more fit than the one who has three. And if they are equal in the number of dignities, the fittest of them is the one who has dignities in two hylechs, or in more than two; especially if by day the dignities are in the Sun, in the degree of the ascendant, and in the degree of the conjunction; and by night in the Moon, in the Part of Fortune, and in the degree of the **prevention** <note>the full moon preceding birth</note>. And that one will be fit for the alcochoden if it aspects, or nearly so. And Ptolemy alone separately appoints the one who has the greatest dominion and the greatest dignity in the hylech as the alcochoden, even if it does not aspect. And if they are equal in all that we have said, he takes the one that is closer to an angle and direct, or the one that is in its **hayz** <term>original: "haic"; a condition where a planet is in a sign and hemisphere that matches its own nature</term> or in its dignity; for he takes that one rather than a "stranger" <note>a planet with no dignities in that place</note>. And if it is by day, he takes an **oriental** <note>rising before the Sun</note> planet rather than an occidental one. And by night, the opposite. And he takes the one that is closer to the east or west accordingly, as we have said. And when any of the **luminaries** <note>the Sun or Moon</note> is fit to be the hylech and is in its own house or exaltation, that planet will have the dominion of both hylech and alcochoden. And know that the alcochoden does not give the "full gift" <note>the maximum number of years for that planet</note> unless five dignities are joined in it. And if any of these are missing, one-fifth shall be subtracted from its full gift. According to this, one of these dignities is being in angles and succedents; and of the angles, the ascendant is the most noble, then the midheaven. Another dignity is that it be in its own dignity; and of the dignities, the house is the most noble. Next is the exaltation; for these are clearly "clean," but the triplicity and term can occur with **fall** <note>a position of weakness</note> or from fall. Another dignity is *hayz*, of which the best is that it be above the earth. The fourth dignity is **direct motion** <note>moving forward through the zodiac</note>. The fifth is being oriental; and each of these has its opposite. And when the alcochoden is in that opposite, one-fifth of its gift shall be subtracted. These contraries are: falling from an angle, opposition to an angle, being **peregrine** <note>having no essential dignity</note>, opposition to its dignity, not being in its *hayz* (which is the contrary of *hayz*), **retrograde motion** <note>appearing to move backward</note> (the contrary of direct motion), and being **occidental** <note>setting after the Sun</note> (the contrary of being oriental). And a great part of the wise say that when the alcochoden is in an angle, it gives its **greater years**. And when in a succedent, it gives its **middle years**. And when falling from an angle, it gives its **lesser years**. And another part of the wise say (and one of them is **Albategnus** <note>Al-Battani, a 9th-century Arab astronomer</note>, and I agree with him and work according to this in this chapter on the alcochoden) that when the alcochoden is in the ascendant or in the midheaven and is in its dignities and in what suits it regarding masculinity or femininity and day or night, and it is "clean" of retrograde motion or **combustion** <note>being so close to the Sun that its influence is "burned up"</note>; or when it is in the 11th or 5th house and has these good qualities we mentioned plus one more: then it gives its greater years. And if the alcochoden is in the 7th house or in...

<meta>This page continues the technical instructions for calculating the "Alchochoden" (the giver of years), which determines the length of a person's life based on their birth chart. It transitions from general rules to specific expert opinions and case studies.</meta>

If it has the four <note>original: "4^or"</note> qualities <term>bonitates; beneficial conditions like being in a strong house or favorable alignment</term> that we described in the **ascendant** <note>the eastern horizon; the 1st house</note> and the **Midheaven** <note>original: "medio celi"; the highest point of the sky; the 10th house</note>; or if it is in the ninth house or the third, and has the qualities we mentioned for the eleventh and second houses, it gives its **middle years**. And if the **alchochoden** <term>the planet that determines the number of years a person will live</term> is in the second or eighth house and has the honors <note>original: "dignitates"</note> we described for the ascendant and Midheaven; or if it is in the sixth or twelfth house and has the qualities we mentioned for the eleventh and fifth houses, then it gives its **minor years**.

And others say—and there is a similar opinion regarding the truth—that when the **alchochoden** is in the ascendant or the Midheaven, or in the eleventh or fifth house, and possesses all five honors we mentioned, then it gives its **major years**. And if it is in the seventh, fourth, ninth, or third house and has the full complement of qualities, then it gives its **middle years**. And if it is in the second, eighth, sixth, or twelfth house and has the aforementioned qualities, it gives its **minor years**. And its "full complement" is reached when it is granted four qualities: such as being "direct" <note>moving forward, not retrograde</note>, in its own honor, in its own **domicile** <note>original: "baiç", from the Arabic 'bayt'</note>, and **oriental** <note>rising before the sun</note>. If one of these is missing, a quarter of its gift is reduced. It adds and subtracts according to this method.

And he who wrote *Pndidech* <note>possibly a corruption of a Persian or Arabic name like 'Andarzaghar'</note>, who was among the strong authorities, says: when both **luminaries** <note>the Sun and Moon</note> are in the **term** <note>a specific small segment of a zodiac sign ruled by a planet</note> of a single planet, and that planet is in the degrees of the ascendant such that there are fewer than 15 degrees between it and the degree of the ascendant, and it is oriental of the Sun—or occidental of the Moon and in its third aspect—then that planet will be fit to be the **alchochoden**.

And I say that a planet having one honor that is oriental is more fit than one having two honors that is occidental; yet one having three honors is more fit than an oriental one having only one—unless it is "falling" from an angle <note>in a weak house like the 6th, 8th, or 12th</note> or entering under the sun’s rays <note>becoming invisible due to proximity to the sun</note> before seven days have passed. It is not suitable to take the Moon as the **hylech** <term>the giver of life</term> nor as the **alchochoden** when she is entering **combustion** <note>within 8.5 degrees of the Sun, which "burns" the planet's power</note>; and the same applies to other planets.

Nor is it suitable for one looking into this science to judge life in a hurried manner until he knows for a truth whether the newborn can complete its "nutrition" <note>the early period of infancy where survival is uncertain</note>, and whether it can have life or not; for it is the mark of a sound mind and good judgment to look and judge the chapter on **Nutrition** before seeking out the **hylech** or the **alchochoden**.
<margin>note</margin>
And similarly, it is the mark of good sense and sound judgment to look first at the birth charts of the parents of the newborn, and what kind of children and generation they shall have. For I have seen many who had the "house of children" <note>the 5th house</note> condemned, and as many as were born to them died, even though the newborn's chart itself had no sign of dying. Therefore, do not forget this: consider this before nutrition, and before you look into the life-span or the **hylech**.
<margin>note</margin>
And know that the judgment of astronomy is of two modes: one is deep and subtle, the end of which a person cannot easily reach. The other is manifest and great, in which a man cannot be sure that he will not err.
<margin>note</margin>
For the wise are of two types: one is the perceptive, patient, and sharp man who forgets nothing and is cautious in his words and judgments; for this reason, he escapes error and is saved. The other is lazy and weak, taking things in a coarse way and not considering all parts, because of which he stumbles and errs. And the science of astronomy has a friend and an enemy. The friend is he who believes in

<column-break/>

it and that it is truthful, even if it leads him to difficult things that he cannot endure or fulfill. And the enemy is he who speaks falsely of it, neither believing nor valuing it, even though it is proven true in many things.

And when one of those holding honors in the **hylech** aspects the **hylech** by a degree of "equal days" <note>degrees that have the same amount of daylight</note> or degrees having "equal ascensions," he will be fit to be the **alchochoden**. And one group of the ancient wise men held this opinion. And I did this and gave judgment in a certain daytime birth: the Sun was in the 21st degree of Aries, and all the lords of the honors of Aries were far from its aspect; but I found the lord of Aries <note>Mars</note> in the 9th degree of Aries, and I took him for the **alchochoden** and gave judgment for him; and this judgment resulted in the experience of truth.

And they brought me a certain birth chart from **Seville** <note>original: "zezilla"</note>, those who brought it telling me that the astrologers of that city could not find its **alchochoden**. It was a daytime birth, and the Sun was in Gemini and the ascendant was Gemini; none of the lords of the honors aspected the hylechs. However, I found Mercury, who is the lord of the house of the Sun, in Cancer in the degree making an "equal day" with the degree in which the Sun was; and I judged that Mercury was the **alchochoden** and would give 20 years of life, which are its **minor years**, and that Venus would add 8 years to him, because she was near him by a few degrees. Do not despise or forget this reasoning, for it is verified and certified by the nature of the heavens and its form.

And the greater part of the wise of this science say that when the **alchochoden** is in the "angles" <note>1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</note>, it gives its **major years**; when in "succedent" houses <note>2nd, 5th, 8th, or 11th houses</note>, it gives its **middle years**; and when in "cadent" houses <note>3rd, 6th, 9th, or 12th houses</note>, it gives its **minor years**. Nor do they give preference to one angle over another, nor one succedent over another—and this is an error. However, the arrangement we mentioned before is truthful, and with it I work and proceed.

**Zaradešt** <note>Zoroaster</note> said that when none of the lords of the honors of the **hylech** is fit to be the **alchochoden**, and the birth is a daytime one, and the **hylech** is the degree of the ascendant or the **Part of Fortune**; look to see if you find any planet that is oriental at the beginning of its orientality, such that no other planet is closer to orientality than it, nor one separated from the Sun for a shorter time. And if that planet is in an angle or a succedent house, or aspects the **hylech** or the ascendant, it is worth as much as the **alchochoden**; judge by it as if by the **alchochoden**. And this is among the deep secrets of this science, for the suitability of this planet exists only because its nature accords with the nature of the ascendant and the nature of the Sun in its orientality separately, and not in anything else.

**Ptolemy**, as we said before, did not accept the **hylech** in any way except above the earth and in the five aforementioned places. He excluded from those above the earth the twelfth and eighth houses, saying that they do not "align" with the ascendant. He means that between the twelfth house and the ascendant there are 30 degrees, and 30 does not have a proportional part of 360, which are all the degrees of the heaven. Similarly, from the eighth house to the ascendant there are 150 degrees, and these 150 degrees likewise have no proportion to the 360 degrees of the heaven. And this reasoning is truthful and manifest. Similarly...

### Chapter Five: On what the alchochoden signifies when it does not have complete strengths.

<image-desc>Decorative drop cap initial "Q" with floral patterns inside a square frame.</image-desc>
When the **alchochoden** is **combust** <term>original: "combustus"; a planet is "combust" when it is too close to the Sun, which is thought to burn up its power</term> and is moving toward the Sun so that it does not appear, it loses its entire "gift" <note>the years it would otherwise grant to the person's life</note>; for when it is in this state, it gives only days or hours, or things that have no name.

And the limit of **combustion** for the planets is this: after Saturn is "occidental" <note>setting after the Sun</note> from the Sun and the Sun moves toward it, and there are 15 degrees between them, until it remains "oriental" <note>rising before the Sun</note> from the Sun and there are 10 full degrees between them. And Jupiter is the same.

Mars, however, after there are 15 degrees between it and the Sun in the west, until it is oriental and there are 9 degrees between them. Mercury, however, performs its deeds and gives its full gifts as long as it is **direct** <note>moving forward</note>, provided it is not closer to the Sun than 7 degrees. From 7 degrees down to 5 degrees it gives, but not completely. But from the beginning of 5 degrees until the Sun passes it by five degrees, it loses its gift; and from five degrees until the completion of 7 degrees, it gives a little. However, after it passes 7 degrees, it gives its full gift. And Venus does the same, except that when she appears visibly at at least 5 degrees, she then gives her full gift.

The Moon, however, when it applies to the Sun <note>moves toward an alignment</note> and there are 15 degrees between them, its power is weakened and it gives a small thing—that is, days or something similar. And when it has applied within 12 degrees of the Sun, it loses its entire gift until it has passed the degrees of the Sun by 10 degrees; and then it will give a small gift, namely days or something similar, until it has passed the Sun by 12 degrees, and then it will give its full gift.

A **fall** <term>original: "casus"; a sign where a planet's influence is at its weakest</term> is the opposite of an **exaltation** <note>a sign where a planet is at its strongest</note>; it takes away half the gift. The limit of this "fall" is as follows: the Sun, after it is in the 5th degree of Libra until it passes 

<column-break/>

the 25th degree of that same sign in its fall; and the remainder of the sign shall be judged according to the **detriment** <term>original: "detrimentum"; a sign where a planet is uncomfortable because it is opposite its home sign</term> in which it is, which is the sign opposite its own house. And the fall of the Moon is after it is at the beginning of the 22nd degree of Libra until it passes the end of the "term" <note>a specific subdivision of a zodiac sign</note> of Mars in Scorpio; and what remains of the sign of Scorpio shall be judged as a detriment. Saturn, however, is in its fall from the beginning of the 12th degree of Aries until it passes the 26th degree of that same Aries; and the rest of the sign is judged as a detriment. Jupiter is in its fall from the first degree of Capricorn until the completion of the 20th degree of the same, and the rest of the sign is judged as a detriment. And Venus is in her fall after she passes the term of Jupiter, which is up to the 21st degree of Virgo. And Mars is in his fall from the 19th degree of Cancer until the end of the same; and in the beginning of the sign, he is judged as being in detriment. And Mercury is in his fall from the beginning of the 8th degree of Pisces until the completion of the 19th degree of the same; and in the remainder of that sign, he is judged as if he were in his detriment.

<margin>#</margin>
**Retrogradation** <term>original: "retrogradatio"; when a planet appears to move backward in the sky</term> of the three superior planets <note>Saturn, Jupiter, and Mars</note>: from the beginning of their retrogradation until they are opposite the Sun, it takes away half of the gift, and the other half remains. And when it has passed the opposition of the Sun, look at how many degrees and minutes it will go backward until it becomes **direct** <note>moves forward again</note>; and whatever that is, see what proportional part it has to all the degrees it must go retrograde from the opposition until it is direct. And add that much to the half of the gift, and direct those degrees correctly in their minutes in such a way that when the planet is at the beginning of its direct motion, it will correctly give its full gift.

<margin>B</margin>
Then Venus and Mercury, after either of them begins to go retrograde, lose half of what they give when they are direct. And afterward, look at how many degrees and minutes remain for them until **occultation** <note>when the planet is hidden by the Sun's light</note>; and calculate their occultation as accurately as you can, because Venus might appear even if there are fewer than 5 degrees between her and the Sun. And when she is visible, she will give half her gift, unless she appears while being closer than 5 degrees to the Sun; for then that appearance does not help her in this state. Afterward, direct those degrees and minutes after she began to go retrograde until she hides herself, subtly and correctly; and divide the half of the gift that remained in the aforesaid manner. For when she is hidden, she loses her entire gift as we said before, because nothing remains to her. And when Venus has passed the Sun while going retrograde toward the east by 5 degrees and appears, give her half her gift then. And if she does not appear, do not give this to her until she passes 7 and a half degrees. And when she has passed them, give her the half gift, not caring whether she appears or not. And afterward, divide that half gift over the degrees and minutes that remain from that place until she becomes direct, so that when she is direct, you will give her full gift.

Concerning Mercury, however, you cannot be well-certified by sight; therefore proceed in this way: when he is elongated from the Sun by 7 and a half degrees (which is the diameter of the Sun), and going retrograde toward the Sun, his entire gift is ruined; nor does he give anything until he passes the Sun toward the east by 7 degrees, and then he gives his half gift. And make the proportion for him just as you proportioned for Venus, so that when he is at the beginning of his direct motion, he gives his full gift.

### Chapter six: concerning what adds to the alchochoden and
### subtracts from it.

<margin>#</margin>
<image-desc>Decorative initial letter A inside a square frame featuring foliage and floral patterns.</image-desc>
**Add** the fortunate planets Jupiter and Venus when they look upon the alchochoden from a **trine** <note>original: "tertio"; a 120-degree angle</note> or **sextile** <note>original: "sextili"; a 60-degree angle</note>, or are bodily joined with it: they add to it a number of years according to their minor years, or months, or days, or hours, according to their strengths or weaknesses. However, both unfortunate planets, Saturn and Mars, when they are bodily joined with the alchochoden or look upon it from an opposition or a square, they subtract from it the number of their minor years. But when Mercury is with the fortunate planets that are adding to the alchochoden: he himself likewise adds the number of his minor years. And when he is with the unfortunate planets that are subtracting from the alchochoden: he also subtracts his own part. And when Mars and Saturn look upon it from a trine in signs of **short ascension** or from a sextile in signs of **long ascension** <term>signs that take more or less time to rise over the horizon</term>: they subtract. And I say that an unfortunate planet will not be able to show its [harmful] work when both **luminaries** <note>the Sun and the Moon</note> constrain it from above and below; and especially Saturn, which is the planet of darkness and blackness. And it is said that the fortunate planets add from an opposition and square. However, the greater part of the perfected wise men did not agree with these two aphorisms. And I say that the Sun subtracts the number of its minor years in a square and opposition; and it adds in a trine or sextile likewise; and more than the Sun subtracting from the alchochoden and cutting it off is when it is joined with Mars: and this is because of the conjunction of their heat. And many of the ancient and modern astrologers say among themselves that a fortunate Moon adds its minor years from a trine or sextile. Yet regarding the **Head and Tail** <note>original: "capite 7 cauda"; the North and South Nodes of the Moon</note>, they are in great disagreement: for one of them says that when the Head is with the alchochoden, and there are up to 12 degrees between it and the alchochoden, it adds as much as a 4th part of the years that the alchochoden signifies. And the Tail subtracts

<column-break/>

in this same manner. And **Albumasar** <note>Abu Ma'shar, a famous 9th-century Persian astrologer</note> disagrees with his own sayings on this: so that in his book *On the Hylech and Alchochoden* he says that the Head and Tail add and subtract; but in his *Lesser Book of Nativities* he does not speak of them, nor does he assign them addition or subtraction. And in his *Book of Aphorisms* he says that they add or subtract in no way at all. And he likewise says in that book that when unfortunate planets "receive" the significator: they do not subtract from it but add to it. And when they look upon the significator from the **angles** <note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses of a chart</note> without applying to it, they do not subtract. They do, however, cause the person to enter into perils and labors. And when fortunate planets look from the angles, they do not add unless they have received the significator or the significator has received them; and because addition or subtraction shall not happen except through **application** <note>when a faster planet moves toward an aspect with a slower one</note>. And he says that when the significator is strong in an angle, and unfortunate planets apply to it, and the unfortunate planet applying to it is "falling" from an angle: it will not have the power to subtract anything. And he says that when the significator is bodily joined with the Sun: it adds its minor years to it, and this if it is in a good place; however, if it is not in a good place, they subtract a third of the years that the significator was signifying. And **Atabari** <note>Umar al-Tabari, an 8th-century Persian astrologer</note> says that if the significator is in **combustion** <term>too close to the Sun</term>: it is pushed down from major years to mean years. And if with that same combustion it is in the place of its "fall," it descends from mean years to minor years; however, if
<margin>nourishment</margin>
combustion, fall, and **retrogradation** <note>appearing to move backward</note> were joined to it: that newborn will not taste [life] nor live. And all the wise men of this science confess that if the newborn does not have a **hylech** <term>original: "hylech"; the "Giver of Life" planet</term>, but has either of the two fortunate planets in the Ascendant or the Midheaven: it is possible that he will live according to the quantity of the minor years of that fortunate planet which signified the life; unless the degree of the Ascendant and the Moon were unfortunate, or that same fortunate planet was the lord of the **house of death** <note>the 8th house</note>: for then it signifies a small durability and a short life. And the **son of Arfashan** says that when the hylech is harmed by an eclipse and by unfortunate planets: let us look at the degrees that were between the hylech and the thing that eclipsed it; or between the hylech and the unfortunate planet that harmed it; or the unfortunate planet that joined itself bodily with it. And if we see that the child will be **nourished** <note>will survive infancy</note>, we will multiply those degrees by 12, and whatever comes out will be the number of years for that child. And this same thing happened in the birth of **Jafar son of Jessie** <note>likely referring to Ja'far ibn Yahya, whose life ended prematurely</note>: for the Moon was the hylech and it was eclipsed in the Tail, and there were 3 degrees between them (that is, between the harming factor and the Moon); 3 multiplied by 12 made 36, and thus his life was 36 years. And **Yahya son of Abi Mansur** said, following Arfashan and Aztaratuz and those who made the *Book of Experiments*, that when they found a planet in its own **term** <note>a specific division of a zodiac sign</note> of its own house, and it was from the degree of the Midheaven up to the completion of 5 degrees of the "house of confidence" <note>the 11th house</note>; or above the degree of the Ascendant by 2 and a half degrees up to 5 degrees from it, they looked at how much remained for it of the degrees of its term, and they added to the giver what it gave—one year for every degree. And if it were in the 4th or 5th house, they gave one month to each degree. And in the 9th and 3rd houses, days. And in the 2nd and 8th houses, hours. And the wise men of the regions say that additions shall be by **aspects** and not by applications of the Sun; and according to the quantity of degrees of distance by which the alchochoden was applied or distanced from it, it shall add; he means to say...

¶ When the year-giver is in its third or **sextile** degree <note>original: "sextili gradu"; an aspect of 60 degrees, usually considered harmonious</note> by degree, it adds its full **minor years** <term>original: "annos minores"; the shortest base lifespan assigned to a planet</term>. And if it is removed from that point by 10 degrees, it shall subtract from those minor years according to the proportion of 10 to 30, which is one-third. And similarly in this way, if the degrees are more or less, the reduction of its years will be according to the proportion of those degrees to 30. ¶ The saying of **Ptolemy** <note>Claudius Ptolemy, the foundational 2nd-century authority on astronomy and astrology</note> is that the addition will be according to the quantity of the planet's light from the **Ascendant** <term>original: "ascendente"; the point of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at birth</term>: he means to say that if it is in the degrees of the Ascendant, it adds its full minor years, and the amount decreases until it reaches the degrees of the **tenth house** <note>the "Midheaven," the highest point in the sky</note>; and then, in those degrees of the tenth house, it shall add half of its minor years. And so you shall subtract in this manner until it is in the degrees of the **7th house** <note>the western horizon where the sun sets</note>, and there the addition ceases, because the 7th house adds nothing. And he said that if the **Alchochoden** <term>original: "alchochoden"; the planet chosen to determine the length of the native's life</term> is in the house of another planet, and an **infortune** <term>original: "infortuna"; a "malefic" planet, usually Saturn or Mars</term> is in the 4th house from the Alchochoden in the other house of that same planet—such as Gemini or Virgo, or Pisces and Sagittarius—then the infortune subtracts nothing. And when the Alchochoden is "under the rays" of the Sun <note>original: "sub radijs solis"; too close to the Sun to be seen, which usually weakens a planet</note>, it cannot receive the addition of the **fortunes** <term>original: "fortunaru"; "benefic" planets, usually Jupiter or Venus</term> unless it is in **tazyid** <note>original: "taziuū"; likely referring to a planet increasing in number or strength, or perhaps "cazimi" (in the heart of the sun)</note>, for then it is in the most fortunate state possible: if it is a fortune, it is very fortunate; if an infortune, it is very unfortunate. But I do not agree with this; rather, I say that *tazyid* is the most unfortunate state that can be. The **Sons of Mitregitum** say that an **opposition** <note>original: "oppositio"; an aspect of 180 degrees, often considered difficult</note> takes away half of what is given by a benefic planet; he means to say, for example: if the Ascendant is Libra and the **Part of Fortune** is the **Hylech** <term>original: "hylech"; the "giver of life" or the point that represents the vital force</term> and it is in Leo, and Jupiter is the Alchochoden in Sagittarius, and Venus is in the 7th house from the Ascendant: then because Venus is opposite the Ascendant, she loses half of what she adds, and she adds only four years; and no one else holds this opinion except them. And I say that the **Head or Tail of the Dragon** <note>the lunar nodes</note> do not add or subtract; however, they do strengthen and weaken and nothing else. For example, the wise and intelligible masters of the **Luminaries** <note>original: "nayrac," from the Arabic "nayyirayn" for the Sun and Moon</note> in astronomy—among them **Yahya ibn Abi Mansur**, and **Muhammad al-Battani**, and **Al-Zarqali**, and others agreeing with them—place both luminaries as the Hylech in the 3rd and 9th houses. And they say that when the Alchochoden is in the 7th, it gives only its **mean years** <note>original: "annos medios"; the middle-value lifespan assigned to a planet</note>. 
¶ **Azaroen** <note>likely Ibn Ezra or a similar Andalusian authority</note> said regarding a certain birth whose Ascendant was at 15 degrees of Libra, the Moon at 25 degrees of Capricorn, and Venus and Saturn both at the 14th degree of Pisces, that the Moon was its Hylech and Saturn was the Alchochoden, because he was the lord of the **term** <note>original: "termini"; a specific subdivision of a zodiac sign</note> and the house; and he designated the Moon as Hylech even though it was in the 4th house. And he said of another birth whose Ascendant was Gemini and the Part of Fortune was in the 4th house in Virgo, and its lord Mercury was looking at it from Sagittarius: he designated that Part as the Hylech and its lord as the Alchochoden, since the Sun was **effeminate** <note>original: "effeminatū"; technically weakened or placed in a sign of the opposite gender</note> in Capricorn, and the Moon was masculine in Aries; and he took the Part of Fortune for the Hylech before the luminaries even though it was in the fourth house, and took Mercury its lord as the Alchochoden, and it gave its **major years** <term>original: "annos suos maiores"; the longest lifespan value a planet can grant</term>. ¶ And he said: I have experienced, and others have told me they experienced, that the giver of years (which is the Alchochoden) in the 7th house does not give more than its mean years, unless the fortunes add to it or the infortunes subtract from it; and he himself did not accept the Moon as Hylech when it was in the ninth house in a masculine sign.

For every planet that has fewer than 25 degrees between itself and the degree of the Ascendant is named as being in the Ascendant. For example: if the Ascendant were the second degree of any sign and some planet were in the 28th degree of that sign, that planet would be named as being in the second house and not in the Ascendant. Alcabitius <note>original: "alchabarany"; refers to the 10th-century Arab astrologer Al-Qabisi</note> and he was the one who taught astronomy to Al-Ma'mun <note>original: "memonē"; the 9th-century Abbasid caliph known for his patronage of the House of Wisdom</note>: the Head <note>the North Node of the Moon, associated with increase and gain</note> does not harm the Sun because of the suitability of their heat. And when the Head joins with Saturn, it signifies the same as Jupiter <note>meaning it turns a difficult planet like Saturn into a more beneficial influence</note>. And if it should be in the 2nd house <note>the house of wealth and resources</note> from the Ascendant of any person's birth: it will be the greatest house of a king or an official of great power. And when it joins with Mars: it signifies the same as Venus and manages its business. But the Tail <note>original: "Lauda," a corruption of "Cauda" or the South Node; associated with decrease and loss</note> diminishes fortune from fortune and adds misfortune to misfortune. The Head adds fortune to fortune: and both nodes together harm and bring misfortune to the Moon.

### Chapter Seven on Athazir.

After we have spoken and completed the reasons for the **Hylech** <term>the "giver of life," a specific point in a birth chart used to determine longevity</term> and the **Alcochoden** <term>the "giver of years," the planet that rules the Hylech and dictates the length of life</term>: and what was necessary in this matter: we wish now to speak of the **Athazir** <term>a technique of "direction" where a planet is moved mathematically to see when it will encounter other planets, used for timing events</term>, which is the end and completion of this matter: and from it comes judgment and operation in life. And this is especially according to the opinion of **Ptolemy** <note>the 2nd-century authority on astronomy</note> and those who follow him. ¶ For the things in which it is fitting to perform an *Athazir* are, namely, the *Hylech*. And we ought to begin first from that which was chosen as the *Hylech*. When the Sun is the *Hylech*, one shall know from its *Athazir* the life and impediments, as well as the status and dignity of the person born—his dominion and his good when it joins a **fortune** <note>a "benefic" or lucky planet like Jupiter or Venus</note>: and concerning evil when it joins an **infortune** <note>a "malefic" or difficult planet like Saturn or Mars</note>: or by its rays <note>aspects or angles of light</note> from a fixed or movable sign: and from this, one shall know the status of the native. And when the Moon is the *Hylech*, by its *Athazir* one shall know the life: the strength: the weakness and the status of mothers. ¶ Truly, an *Athazir* must be performed for the degree of the **Ascendant** <term>the sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</term> whether it is the *Hylech* or not: since from it one shall know the status of the native in his body and in his health or infirmity: because it is the significator of life and the soul. And the lord of the **term** <term>a specific subdivision of a zodiac sign</term> of that degree is the "divider" and is named the *Alteriustar* <note>a Latinization of the Arabic "Jarbakhtar," the planet that "distributes" the years of life as time passes</note>. And an *Athazir* is made for the **Part of Fortune** <note>a calculated point representing prosperity</note> when it is the *Hylech*: and one shall know from it just as we said one knows from the Moon: health: impediments and gains in substance, as well as troubles concerning them.

<margin>
Fortune and misfortune
</margin>
¶ Similarly, an *Athazir* is made for the degree of conjunction or opposition <note>the New or Full Moon that occurred just before birth</note> to know impediments and fortune. 

<margin>
Athazir for all principal significations of the native
</margin>
And I say that similarly an *Athazir* ought to be made for the significator of substance <note>wealth</note>: and the significator of brothers: and the significator of parents: and the significator of children: just as is done for the Ascendant and the two **luminaries** <note>the Sun and the Moon</note>. And when any of them applies to a fortune or its rays: judge good and fortune in the matter which it signifies. And when to an infortune or its rays: judge the contrary in that matter.

<margin>
Of the Earth, that is, in oblique spheres. Of the Right Circle. Ascendant [directed] in oblique spheres.
</margin>
¶ Similarly, an *Athazir* is made for the degree of the **tenth house** <note>the Midheaven, representing career and public standing</note> to know the business and work of the native and his status in dominion. And for those of these which are in the Ascendant or 7th house, the *Athazir* ought to be made by the **ascensions of the Earth** <note>oblique ascensions, which account for the local latitude</note> in which that birth occurred: and for those which are in the tenth or 4th house, the *Athazir* ought to be made by the **ascensions of the right circle** <note>right ascension, which is independent of local latitude</note>: and for those which are between these two locations: an *Athazir* ought to be made by the ascensions calculated between those two places just as we have distinguished and divided in our tables: which we made by our own skill, which are called the **tables for loosening nodes and explaining aspects**: and there ascensions of this kind are distinct. And here we wish to speak in brief and composed words: which in this reasoning are as powerful as the tables themselves.

<column-break/>

¶ When you wish to know the ascensions of any sign in whatever house of the houses of heaven. Know that every sign which rises in a land of any latitude with the ascensions of some degrees: that sign sets in that latitude with the degrees of its opposite. ¶ Wherefore when you wish to know the ascensions of the sign of Aries through all houses: take the difference which is between its ascensions in the east: and its descension in the west: and divide that difference into six parts: and add one of those parts, which is a sixth of the ascension of Aries in the east: and they will be its ascensions in the 12th house. And you shall add another sixth to the ascension of the twelfth house: and they will be the ascensions of the 11th house. And you shall add another sixth to the ascension of the 11th: and you will have the ascensions of the 10th, which are of the right circle. Afterwards add another sixth to the ascensions of the 10th and you will have the ascensions of the ninth. And also add another sixth to the ascensions of the ninth: and you will have the ascensions of the 8th. Afterwards you shall add to them another sixth and you will have the ascensions of the 7th house. Afterwards subtract from those ascensions one sixth: and there will remain for you the ascensions of the sixth house. And from those subtract another sixth: and you will have the ascensions of the 5th. And from those subtract another sixth: and you will have the ascensions of the 4th. And from those subtract another sixth: and you will have its ascensions in the 3rd house. And from those subtract another sixth: and you will have its ascensions in the 2nd house. And from those subtract another sixth: and you will have its ascensions in the Ascendant: just as you previously had those same ones. ¶ And in this way you shall do for Taurus and Gemini because their ascensions in the east are less than their descensions in the west. However, because the ascensions of Cancer are greater in the east than its descensions in the west: you shall subtract the smaller from the larger. And you shall know the difference by dividing it into six parts: and you shall subtract one sixth from the ascensions of Cancer in the Ascendant: and what remains will be its ascensions in the 12th house. And you shall subtract from those another sixth and you will have its ascensions in the 11th house: and so you shall go on doing and subtracting until you reach the seventh house. Afterwards you shall add to the ascensions of the 7th house one sixth: and you will have its ascensions in the sixth house: and another sixth you shall add to those: and you will have its ascensions in the 5th house. And so you shall go on adding until you reach the Ascendant. ¶ And you shall do the same for Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpio, and Sagittarius: by subtracting sixths from the ascensions of the Ascendant all the way to the seventh, passing through the **midheaven** <note>original: "mediū celi"</note>: and by adding those from the 7th up to the Ascendant, passing through the fourth house. And you shall do for Capricorn, Aquarius, and Pisces just as you did for Aries, Taurus, and Gemini equally. ¶ Afterwards if your calculation should be between the Ascendant and the midheaven: take the ascensions of the sign which you wish in that land: and its ascensions in the right circle by knowing the difference which was between them and reducing it to a third: and you shall subtract that third from the ascensions of the rising sign or add to them as is fitting for the lengths of ascensions and their shortness: and the ascensions of that sign in the 12th and 11th house will result for you. And similarly you shall do from the 10th house all the way to the seventh. And from the 7th all the way to the 4th. And from the 4th all the way [to the Ascendant].

<meta>This page continues the technical instructions for Athazir (astrological direction), moving from general definitions of planetary power to the specific mathematical methods used to project a person's fate over time.</meta>

<margin>
What **Athazir** <term>an astrological technique of "direction" where a planet is moved mathematically to time future events</term> is.
</margin>

<margin>
Otherwise... <unclear>dis[...]</unclear>
</margin>

And you should know that the **Athazir** <note>original: "athazir"; from the Arabic *at-tasyīr*, meaning "guidance" or "direction"</note> of the **Hylech** <term>the planet or point in a birth chart that acts as the "giver of life"</term> and of the planets follows the order of the signs, from the beginning of a sign to its end. The exception is for retrograde planets <note>planets that appear to move backward in the sky from our perspective on Earth</note>, for their **Athazir** moves against the order of the signs, starting from the end of the signs and proceeding toward their beginning. It is the opinion of Ptolemy <note>Claudius Ptolemy, the influential 2nd-century Greco-Egyptian astronomer</note> and those who follow him that if the **Hylech** is in the 8th or 9th house, its **Athazir** is likewise against the order of the signs. However, other wise men do not agree on this; rather, they direct it in the forward way. 

And whenever it joins with the body of a **malefic** <term>an "infortune" or planet like Saturn or Mars that traditionally brings challenges</term> or its opposition or its square aspect, judge it to be a hindrance and a "severing" <note>original: "abscisionē"; a technical term for the end of a life period or a major crisis</note>, unless a **benefic** <term>a "fortune" or planet like Jupiter or Venus that brings luck</term> aspects it there by body or ray—and especially if the planet undergoing the **Athazir** is in a "term" belonging to a malefic at the boundaries of the signs. 

Furthermore, the "string" of fixed stars <note>referring to constellations or specific star alignments</note> and others like them that share the nature of the malefics can "kill" <note>bring about the end of life or a period of vitality</note> and demonstrate powerful and great impediments when a benefic does not look upon them. The square aspect of the Sun and its opposition do the same. Likewise, the body of the Sun is a "severer" and a giver of great misfortune. The Moon, when it is unfortunate, "severs" the Ascendant <note>the sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth</note>, and the Ascendant severs the Moon because of the discord between their natures.

The order of the **Athazir** is varied in this way: for the **Athazir** of the Ascendant, used to know the length of life, you shall give one year to each degree. You shall do the same for the other **Hylechs** and parts. However, for the **Athazir** of "revolutions" <term>annual charts or solar returns that predict the year ahead</term>, you shall give one year to every 30 degrees. 

For example: if someone’s Ascendant was the 1st degree of Aries, and in the seventh year it reached the 1st degree of Virgo, then the entire sign of Virgo will be the ruler of that whole year from its beginning to its end. And when the "rays" <note>astrological aspects or influences</note> of many planets fall in that sign, we proceed as follows: Let us say that the rays of Venus strike the beginning of Virgo from an opposition; Venus will therefore rule the beginning of that year until the degree of the direction reaches the ray of another planet. 

And let us say that the rays of Mars fall at the 5th degree of Virgo: you shall then multiply the four degrees passed by the rays of Venus by 12 and one-sixth; this will give you 48 days and two-thirds of a day. Thus, Venus will rule the person for that much of the year. Afterward, Mars will rule through its rays which fall at the 5th degree, until it reaches the rays of others. Let us say the fertile rays of Jupiter fall at the 11th degree of Virgo: you will look at the degrees over which Mars ruled—which is 6—and multiply by 12 and one-sixth, which gives you 83 days. You will continue working in this way until the year is completed by the rays falling in that sign.

And know that there is a great difference between the direction of a degree toward a malefic (or its rays) and the direction of the malefic itself toward a degree or "part." The movement of a degree toward a malefic is worse, stronger, and more damaging than the movement of a malefic toward a degree; nonetheless, the latter still brings harm, though not as much. The majority of the wise say that the work of a malefic does not appear unless the degree undergoing the direction and the degree toward which it is directed are "in one line" <note>aligned by celestial latitude</note>; if they are diverse, the significance is weakened, and perhaps little or nothing will appear of it.

<margin>
An example... <unclear>[...]</unclear>
</margin>

<margin>
Consider well... <unclear>[...]</unclear> about the **Hylech** and... signs and... not... it is of great moment... if... although... judge... signify... and degrees... joined... now... remember...
</margin>

<column-break/>

This alignment is only necessary in the **Athazir** of the Moon and the five planets <note>Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn</note>, which have "latitudes" <term>distances North or South from the ecliptic, the Sun's path</term> outside the circle of the signs. However, for the degrees of the Sun, the Ascendant, and the "parts," this is not necessary, because their **Athazir** is done by longitude and the degrees of ascension as we said before, for these always look upon the line of the zodiac and never separate from it.

When, however, you wish to know if the degree you are directing is in the same path as the target degree, determine the degree of the planet you wish to direct—whether it be the Moon or another planet—by its longitude in the sign where it was at birth or in any other figure; this is its fit and correct place. Afterward, find the "declination" <term>the distance of a point North or South of the celestial equator</term> of 그 degree. Also find the "latitude" of that planet. 

If both are in one direction—either North or South—add them together. If they disagree—so that one is North and the other South—subtract the smaller from the larger. What remains (or the sum if added) is the distance from the equinoctial circle <note>the celestial equator</note> toward the side of the larger value. 

With the result, you shall enter the "Table of Declinations," and where you find a similar value, take what is directly across from it in the "line of numbers," and in that degree the planet makes its "circumference" <note>its projected true position on the zodiacal sphere</note>. 

For example: Let the Moon be at 10 degrees of Taurus, and the declination of that degree is 15 degrees and 12 minutes. Let the latitude of the Moon be 4 degrees North. We add them together because both are North. (If one had been South, we would have subtracted one from the other). After adding, the result is 19 degrees and 12 minutes. This is the Moon's distance from the equinoctial line in this case. 

We then looked for its equivalent in the Table of Declinations and found it across from the end of 24 degrees of Taurus. Because of this, the degree of the Moon's "circumference"—which was at 10 degrees of Taurus in longitude—became 24 degrees. Therefore, when we direct the degree of the Ascendant, or a part, or the Sun toward the Moon, if we intend to direct it toward its "body" which is at 10 degrees of Taurus, we will not be certain of hitting the body of the Moon. This is because the Moon, with its "circumference," is removed from the path of the **Athazir** by an arc of 14 degrees. 

Consequently, it will not signify then what the body of the Moon would signify if the **Athazir** fell directly upon it. If the Moon had been in this place without latitude, its circumference would be in that same degree where it was in longitude on the circle of the signs, and its **Athazir** would fall correctly upon its circumference. The smaller its latitude, the smaller that arc will be. If its latitude had been South, we would have subtracted the degrees of latitude from the declination, and what remained would be 11 degrees and 12 minutes. If we placed that in the Table of Declinations, its circumference would be at 28 degrees of Aries. 

According to this, if the Moon is the **Hylech** and you wish to perform an **Athazir** toward the body of a benefic or malefic, extract the circumference of the Moon as we said. Similarly, find the circumference of the planet toward which we are directing the Moon. If they disagree in their circumference, the malefic will do no harm, nor will the benefic bring profit. But if they agree in one circumference, the result will be verified.

<meta>This page continues the technical instructions regarding the "Athazir" (mathematical directions) and the influence of the planets on the length of life, specifically focusing on how the malefic planets Saturn and Mars "cut" or terminate the life-force (the Hylech) under specific conditions.</meta>

$\P$ Mars damages the planets existing above him more than those that are below him. $\P$ And Saturn? He damages the planets existing below him. $\P$ When Mercury is in the likeness and nature of Saturn, he damages the Moon more than the planets existing above him. $\P$ A slight "reception" <note>original: "receptio"; a technical term where one planet "welcomes" another into its territory, softening bad effects</note> of Saturn is a great thing. If the place in which Saturn and Mars are joined together happens to be between the conjunction or opposition preceding a birth and the birth itself, it "cuts" the **Hylech** <term>the "giver of life," a point in the chart used to determine lifespan</term> of that native; and the locations of their oppositions do the same. And similarly, it happens at the place where a "square" aspect <note>an angle of 90 degrees, considered a stressful or difficult relationship between planets</note> of either of these two "infortunes" <note>the "malefics" or unlucky planets, Saturn and Mars</note> occurs toward the Sun or the Moon. And similarly, if either of these two infortunes joins with the Sun or Moon before the birth, or after the conjunction or opposition in which the birth occurred, it "cuts" the life.

$\P$ When the aspect of Saturn, the aspect of the Sun, and the aspect of the Moon join by a square or opposition so that all look toward a single place, they do not "cut" the life. This is because the heat of the Sun and the moisture of the Moon temper the coldness and dryness of Saturn, especially if he is in a water sign <note>Cancer, Scorpio, or Pisces</note>.

$\P$ When Saturn is "occidental" <note>setting after the Sun in the evening</note> and with the Sun in one sign, but not yet entering "under the rays" <note>hidden by the Sun's brightness</note>, this is the greatest occidentality that can be. The smallest occidentality of this type is when he is in the same degree as the Sun. And less than this is when the Sun has separated itself from his "fertility." Thus, when Saturn is occidental in a masculine sign and "peregrine" <note>original: "pgrin?"; meaning a planet that has no dignity or "home" where it is currently located, like a traveler in a foreign land</note> and the sign is of the element of water or earth, and he casts his rays into a water or earth sign: death will occur when the native’s **Hylech** reaches the projection of those rays. However, if Saturn is "oriental" <note>rising before the Sun in the morning</note> in a water sign and is at the beginning of his orientality and casts his rays into a water or fire sign: those rays do not offend, nor will any damage befall the native from them until there are 30 degrees between him and the Sun; and then he will leave the nature of orientality and return to his own proper nature.

$\P$ When there are 30 degrees between the Sun and Jupiter in the west, and he is in a sign suitable to him, he is weakened and does not correctly carry out his significance.

$\P$ When Mars is oriental in Scorpio or Pisces and at the beginning of his orientality, he casts his rays in a water sign and neither offends nor does any damage.

$\P$ When comets appearing in the air happen to be in the **Ascendant** <term>the sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</term> of any native, or with the Moon at night in a birth where the Moon has dominion and power: it "cuts" the life of that native and they shall not live. However, if they happen to be in the "Midheaven" <note>original: "medio celi"; the highest point of the chart, relating to career and status</note> of the birth and the Sun or Mars looks upon it there: the native will come to a kingdom, if they live.

$\P$ The **Ascendant** is the significator of life, the body, the spirit, movements, durability, and good fame. And the Lord of the Ascendant—namely, the one who is most powerful over it with the testimony of Mercury and the Moon—is the significator of the soul: that is, whether the person will be angry or peaceful, and of the native's deeds. Afterward, we wish to follow entirely in this "house" <note>referring to the 1st House of the zodiac</note> according to what is fitting and pertains to it. While it might have suited us to speak in the natural order by starting with the fathers, and afterward the brothers, following that order, we have instead chosen and held it better to proceed by the order of the signs, starting from the **Ascendant**. And afterward from the 2nd, the 3rd, and to go through this order until we reach the 12th house, speaking of each house regarding the things fitting to it and whatever is named after it.

### Chapter Nine: On knowing the form and character of the native; and in this chapter enter the forms of the planets and signs.

<column-break/>

When we wish to know the form of the native, as well as their character, deeds, status, and the accidents of the spirit: first, we ought to consider the form of the native’s body and its state. This matter and judgment is very strong and has powerful entries, and it is a grave thing to apply oneself to it. Indeed, the greater part of the wise men excused themselves from speaking on it. But I wish to expand and broaden the discourse on it, because it is very subtle and strong. It is necessary to take evidence in it in many ways and from many parts: to know the forms of the parents, their colors, and their villages. 

For if someone showed us the figure of a native who was born in Ethiopia <note>original: "ethiopia"; used here as a general term for sub-Saharan Africa</note>, and the natural parents were of that land, and we found in his **Ascendant** a planet dominating his form, and that planet signified yellowness and whiteness: if we were to judge this native according to the form which this planet signifies before we inquired about the parents or his land, we would fall into error and ignorance. However, when we know his root and the land in which he was born, and the color and form of the parents, we can judge from such significations that the native will be fairer than his father and of less blackness. 

Afterward, when we wish to know the form of the native, we must look to the **Ascendant**. If we find in it its Lord, or the Lord of its Exaltation, or the Lord of its Term, or the Lord of its Triplicity <note>these are different "ranks" of planetary ownership over a specific sign</note>, judge that native according to the form and nature of that planet. And if you find many planets in the **Ascendant**, consider which of them is closer to the degree of the **Ascendant**, or which has the greatest power in the **Ascendant**, and judge the native according to it; and mix with it the Lord of the "Face" <note>original: "faciei"; also known as the Decan, a 10-degree division of a sign</note> and the planet to which the Lord of the Face gives its strength. 

And if you find the Lords of the dignities of the **Ascendant** far from the **Ascendant**, and not one of them is in the **Ascendant**, but you find a "peregrine" planet in the **Ascendant**: judge the native according to the form and nature of the planet that is in the **Ascendant**. However, if there is no planet in the **Ascendant**, judge the native from the nature and form of the Lord of the Face, especially if it looks upon the **Ascendant**. And if it is "falling" <note>placed in a weak house where it cannot "see" the Ascendant</note> from its aspect so that it does not look there: see which planet is closer to the **Ascendant** and which looks upon it with the best aspect among those having dignity in it; and judge the native from the nature and form of that planet. 

Mix with that color and form the color and form of the sign in which it is, and its "bounds" <note>original: "vni"; likely referring to the boundaries or terms</note>, and the Lord of its Term; and judge according to that. Judge the form and face of the native from the planet, and the form of the body from the sign in which the planet is. And know that the shapeliness of all the limbs is from Jupiter, and the shapeliness of appearing well is from Venus, and the clarity and light of color is from the Sun and Moon. Ugliness is from Mars and Saturn. Mercury mixes himself with those signifying shapeliness in his good appearance and beauty, and with planets signifying ugliness in their ugliness. The "houses of fortunes" <note>the 1st, 4th, 5th, 7th, 9th, 10th, and 11th houses</note> signify beauty, and the "houses of infortunes" <note>the 6th, 8th, and 12th houses</note> signify foulness. And the day helps planets signifying clarity and light, while the night helps planets signifying blackness and obscurity.

$\P$ **Jupiter** is white and slightly yellowish; he has large eyes with small pupils and medium hair that is neither curly nor straight. His beard is curly and of good appearance, his cheekbones are high, and his nostrils are thick. He is of good physical stature, neither very fat nor very thin, and the same applies to his height. If he is oriental, moisture will predominate in his **complexion** <term>the balance of "humors" or bodily fluids that determines health and personality</term>. If he is occidental, he is handsomer and his eyes are of medium size; his body is somewhat smaller, and moisture will be more apparent in his complexion.

$\P$ **Mars**, if he is oriental, will be between white and red in color, of medium body, and in a beautiful state. He has "zarchus" <note>original: "zarcho[rum]"; likely bright blue or grey-green</note> eyes and thick hair that is between curly and straight; heat and dryness will predominate in his complexion. If he is occidental, he will be of a simple red color, with small eyes and a medium body. His hair tends toward whiteness, and dryness will be the most dominant trait in his complexion. He will have a completely round face, perhaps with spots or marks upon it, a large forehead, and a scar or mark on his brow. He has large nostrils and a sharp gaze; he is prone to anger and quick to react. He has long teeth and little flesh; he takes long strides in his gait, and men do not enjoy his company.

$\P$ **The Sun** is saffron-colored, thick, and white around the eyes; his face is round and shining, his head large, and his hair straight. He has bulging eyes, a pious look, and a hoarse voice. He is of medium height and walks with a steady gait; he is firm in his reasoning and does not doubt himself.

$\P$ **Venus** resembles Jupiter, except that she happens to be handsomer and of greater presence; she is more welcoming and of a more beautiful form. She signifies a beauty appropriate to the beauty of women; she is more mild and has a softer body. Her eyes specifically are between blue-grey and black, and very beautiful. Some say she is sometimes slightly swarthy <note>original: "bazus"</note> mixed with redness, weak, yet of a beautiful look. The black of her eyes is greater than the white; she has thin, joined eyebrows and thin lips. She has much flesh in her face, a narrow chest, short ribs, and thick legs. She has a sweet and pleasant look and a beautiful face; she plays with her eyes to appear well, and has slightly curly hair.

$\P$ **Mercury**, when he is oriental, has a color like that of fresh honey; he is of medium body, with small eyes and medium hair. He is composed in his reasoning and fond of books; heat will be the most apparent quality in his complexion. If he is occidental, his color will be between swarthy and saffron; he is thin with a high-pitched voice. His eyes are deep-set, and his pupils resemble those of a goat, tending somewhat toward redness; dryness predominates in his complexion. It is also said of Mercury that he is of a green color mixed with swarthiness, with medium, hairy hair. He has a narrow forehead, large ears, a beautiful face, and a well-formed nose. His eyebrows are joined; he has wide, soft limbs, small teeth, a sparse beard, and is thin. He is of good stature and walks with smaller steps and has smaller limbs. He is patient, possessing much sense, intellect, and learning. When he is "fortunate" <note>placed in a helpful astrological position</note> and the "fortunes" <note>lucky planets like Jupiter and Venus</note>

$\P$ **The Moon** is white with a beautiful face and a lovely look; she is a lover of quiet, with a beautiful beard <note>this may refer to the "fuzz" or soft hair on the face, or a metaphorical "shining" appearance</note>, a clear color, a healthy body, and good morals. She is tall and of a moist complexion.

$\P$ Consider these aforementioned forms and mix them with the states of the planets; for when the planets appear in their "first station" <note>the point where a planet appears to stop before moving backward</note>, they produce strong and patient bodies.
<margin>Retrograde planet</margin>
And when they are "retrograde" <note>appearing to move backward through the zodiac</note>, they produce unequal bodies, such that the limbs do not correspond to the rest of the body. When they are in their "second station" <note>stopping before moving forward again</note>, they make the bodies weaker. And when they are "hidden" <note>too close to the Sun to be seen</note>, they make them base and prone to receiving misfortunes and anxieties.

$\P$ When a birth occurs in the first quarter of the year—from the spring equinox to the summer solstice—it makes the native of good bodily status in height and thickness, tending more toward thickness, with good color and medium beauty, and beautiful hair; heat and moisture predominate in the complexion. If the birth is in the second quarter—from the summer solstice to the autumnal equinox—it makes the native medium in height and body size, tending toward thickness, with large eyes and much hair; he is hairy, and heat and dryness predominate. If the birth is in the third quarter—

from the autumnal equinox to the winter solstice—it makes the native honey-colored, with a thin voice and wide shoulders; he is thin with straight hair and beautiful eyes, and coldness <margin>and dryness</margin> predominate. If the birth is in the fourth quarter—from the winter solstice to the spring equinox—he is of a black color, average in body size, with straight and sparse hair and well-proportioned limbs; coldness and moisture predominate.

$\P$ Similarly, the regions of the heaven that have forms similar to human forms <note>the "humanoid" zodiac signs like Gemini or Virgo</note> create composed and well-proportioned bodies. Other forms of different types diversify the bodies and make them unequal, causing the limbs to resemble the limbs of that specific form—perhaps making them very large, strong, or weak; or giving them beautiful or ugly proportions, or making them sensible or foolish. 
<margin>Signs</margin>
The forms that tend toward greatness are **Leo**, **Virgo**, and **Sagittarius**. Those that tend toward smallness are **Pisces**, **Cancer**, and **Capricorn**. Know that the beginnings of the signs of **Aries**, **Leo**, and **Taurus** make bodies tend toward thickness, while the ends of these signs make them tend toward thinness and weakness. The beginnings of **Sagittarius**, **Gemini**, and **Scorpio** make bodies tend toward thinness and weakness, while their ends lead to thickness and strength. Similarly, **Virgo**, **Libra**, and **Sagittarius** pull bodies toward equality and good proportion. **Taurus**, **Scorpio**, and **Pisces** cause bodies to tend toward diversity and different proportions. When any planet is upon the degree of the **Ascendant** <note>the sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth</note>—provided it is understood to be in the Ascendant even if it is not its ruler—it demonstrates its effect and work on the native according to its nature, drawing him toward its own form, manners, and nature.

Whenever you wish to know the state of the spirit of the native regarding his senses and reason, you shall always know this from the state of **Mercury**.
