<meta>This page continues the discussion of astrological influences on the human character, moving from the physical appearance of the Zodiac signs (on the previous page) to the internal "spirit" or disposition as determined by planetary alignments and "dominion."</meta>

One planet may be dominant in some significance and another planet may have dominion over it—such as if it were the lord of its house, its exaltation, or even its <term>triplicity</term><note>A group of three signs belonging to the same element (Fire, Earth, Air, or Water).</note>, or something similar. This is what is meant by "agreement" <note>original: "conuenientia"</note>. You should understand it in this way: when it is said that its status is in a "good state," it means there is a good agreement between them, such as both having dominion in one place, or one giving its strength to the other by a natural gift, or if they look upon each other by a <term>trine</term><note>An auspicious astrological aspect where planets are 120 degrees apart.</note> or <term>sextile</term><note>A harmonious aspect where planets are 60 degrees apart.</note> aspect, and both are in a good position in the heavens. However, when they are not in this manner we have described, or are in places not suited to their nature in spirit, they will be hidden, neither appearing nor complete.

But the natures of the planets which are rulers over those that signify the natures of the spirit—and are elevated above them—make the natures of the spirit strong and powerful. They make them doers of evil to those less powerful than themselves, or similarly doers of good, according to whether these planets are powerful. For when the ruling planets have an agreement with <term>infortunate</term><note>Also known as "malefics," typically Saturn and Mars, associated with challenges.</note> planets, they then direct their movements and virtues toward doing evil to others; they will move toward this easily without any prohibition, hindrance, or labor. And if they are <term>fortunes</term><note>Also known as "benefics," typically Jupiter and Venus, associated with luck and harmony.</note>, they cause good to be done naturally. 

When other planets strengthen themselves over these aforementioned planets—those which are of a different nature—they make the <term>native</term><note>The person born under this specific astrological configuration.</note> a person of little reputation who does not improve, and he will fall into trouble with authorities. And when the fortunate planets have agreement with them and are elevated above them, they make the native just and joyful in doing good to others; he loves those who do good and neither desires nor seeks a reward for the good he does. But if these fortunate planets in agreement are not elevated above them, the good he does is only done to receive a reward or to cast off some evil from himself, rather than from a true will to do good. 

And when the planets having dominion over these are contrary to them, the result will be the opposite of what we said: it makes the natives mild, quiet, loving of men, and pious. Yet they will be so mild that men will despise them and run over them, taking what they have and doing whatever they wish with them. ¶ This is the general way and method of investigating this part of the human spirit; however, we wish to speak here of the particular properties and states occurring through the natures of the planets according to their dominion, speaking first of their mixtures and the things that appear through them.

### Let us begin first with Saturn.

I say that when Saturn is the lord of the significance and king of the spirit by itself separately, and is the lord of the house of Mercury and the Moon: if it is in a good position in the sky, such as in the <term>angles</term><note>The four most powerful houses in a chart: the 1st (Ascendant), 4th (Imum Coeli), 7th (Descendant), and 10th (Midheaven).</note>, it makes the native well-mannered, of good counsel, and of profound intellect. He draws counsel for his affairs from within himself; he is wealthy, loved by kings and high-ranking men, a master of treasures, composed, neither prone to laughter nor sad, nor envious. But if Saturn is different from this, it makes the native ugly, weak, and despised; he does not value himself,

<column-break/>

is not known, and only consults with himself. He is envious, fearful, solitary from all people, a deceiver, and loves to go to places of weeping and labor. Without shame, he always loves miseries and brings betrayal and fraud upon his companions; joy and clarity will never be in him; he hates friends, equals, and associates.

¶ And if Saturn is in agreement with Jupiter and in the good state we described—and likewise Jupiter is in a good state—it makes the native religious. He honors and loves the elderly; he is mild and quiet, of good counsel and good reputation, a helper, known by kings and nobles, and honest. He wishes to show this; he is a giver, a good chooser, a lover of certain people, intelligent, patient, and a philosopher. 

But if these planets, namely Saturn and Jupiter, are in a different state from what we said, they make the native one who does not love to do good. He is deficient in his senses, meddles with <term>phantasms</term><note>Illusions, ghosts, or deceptive mental images.</note>, loves to dwell in churches, and predicts the future. He hates children, cannot keep a friend, and does not associate with men. No one trusts him; he is ignorant, a betrayer in his reasoning, and glories without reason. He does not love honor; he loves to weep; he is poor at receiving advice or making choices; he is solitary, patient, hardworking, and tedious.

¶ And if Saturn has agreement with Mars and both are in a good state as we said: they make the native bold, though poor at receiving others, impious, and coarse in his affairs and deeds. He is a litigator, exposing himself to great dangers and misfortunes. He does not look at the cause or the words he speaks; he is a retainer of anger and enmity and does not excuse himself for things that happen to him. He makes men labor and loves to conquer; he is disobedient and sets himself above kings and princes. He loves to argue and win; he is of deep thoughts, stingy in doing favors or service or in socializing. He is an affronter, heavy, a doer of evil, hurting men, weakened, firm, and unchangeable. He puts himself in great and strong dangers, yet quickly returns from them; he is hasty in his affairs and deeds, and generally prosperous. 

But if these planets are in a different state from what we said: they make the native a highwayman, evil, despised, of bad status, and one who profits from evil. He does not fear God, nor has he friendship with anyone. He is a deceiver of friends, unfaithful, a murderer, a brawler, given to vile fornications, a necromancer, one who steals church vestments and robs the dead; and generally, he is evil from an evil state.

¶ And if Saturn has agreement with Venus and both are in a good state as we described: it makes the native a lover of the secrets of the law <note>Likely referring to religious or divine law/theology.</note>; he seeks hidden things and is a diviner. He loves to worship the things of the gods; he is rich, modest, very mild, a lover of ornament, a faithful explainer of reason, a restrainer of his own will, of good thoughts, and very jealous of women. 

But if these planets are in a different state from what we said: they make the native follow his own desires, a fornicator of vile and foul lusts. He will not be known; he is a jester/trickster; he commits fornication with his own kin through deception. He hates good things and deeds; he is solitary and of bad speech and reasoning. He meddles with concealed and hidden things; he commits fornications that are vile by nature and prefers to do them with the elderly rather than the young, and in base matters. He lives his law in a beastly manner; he does not fear God; he despises the law and churches and mocks them and their judgments.

However, if she is there in a state different from what we have said, it is a bad sign.

¶ If **Saturn** is in the Ascendant: it signifies damage to the body and spirit, and that accidents and troubles will happen to him according to the nature of the house he occupies in the division of the heavens.

¶ And if **Venus** is in the Ascendant, safe and clear: it makes the native beloved by people and of good conversation; he will be mild and good, and he will have a life of pleasure <note>original: "vitiosam vitam," which can mean "vicious" in a modern sense, but in medieval astrology often implies a life of sensory indulgence or luxury.</note> and a good reputation.

¶ If **Mercury** is in the Ascendant: the native will be just, full of much joy, and will drive away all sadness and anxiety from himself—especially if he is fortunate and clear from the gaze of the "Infortunes" <note>The "malefic" planets, traditionally Saturn and Mars, which were thought to bring challenges.</note>. He will be faithful; men will trust him and deposit their goods in his keeping. And if Mercury appears with the "Luminaries" <note>The Sun and the Moon.</note> in a feminine sign and in feminine degrees: it signifies that the native will be in a good state.

¶ When the lord of the **sixth house** and the lord of the "Lot of Accidents" <note>A mathematical point in a chart used to predict specific types of events or misfortunes.</note> are in the Ascendant: it signifies that the native and his parents will come to poverty and to begging, especially if they are in a "movable" <note>Also called "cardinal" signs (Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn), associated with change and initiation.</note> sign.

¶ When **Jupiter** is in the Ascendant: it signifies praise for the native, and that he will wish to be valued and worthy for doing good and just things; he will be agreeable and lovable to men. This is if it is a daytime birth; however, if it is a nocturnal birth, and he has no dignity <note>A position of strength or "essential dignity" in a sign.</note> in the Ascendant: he will waste his family inheritance and will be a "good eater" <note>A euphemism for a glutton.</note>.

¶ When **Jupiter** is in the Ascendant with the Luminaries and Venus: the native will be noble, especially if the Infortunes are far from them; however, if the Luminaries gaze upon them but are not physically there: he will be even more noble and high.

¶ When **Mercury** and the **Sun** are unfortunate in the Ascendant: it signifies that the native will be an advocate <note>A lawyer or legal representative.</note>, and that evil will happen to his parents, and trouble for the same reason.

¶ When the "Fortunes" <note>The "benefic" planets, Jupiter and Venus.</note> are in the Ascendant with the **Tail** <note>The "Dragon’s Tail" or South Node of the Moon, usually considered a point of decrease or loss.</note>: it signifies destruction.

¶ When **Saturn** is in the Ascendant in daytime births: it weakens the native’s strength and name. And if it is a nocturnal birth: he will have many enemies, will dwell in bad houses, and will do evil and shameful deeds. However, if the Ascendant is a sign ruled by Saturn, he will be of high name and honored; and this is also true if he is in the other "angles" <note>The four most powerful points of a chart: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses.</note>.

¶ When **Mars** is in the Ascendant and in the "house of his joy" <note>A specific house where a planet is said to be particularly happy or effective; for Mars, this is the 6th house, though here it implies strength in the 1st.</note>: he will be a leader of armies, happy in this, and in taking towns; they will commit great slaughters with him. But if the Ascendant is not his joy, but he is in his "triplicity" <note>A group of three signs of the same element.</note> or has some other dignity: he will associate with kings and commanders <note>original: "alcaydis," a term derived from Arabic meaning a governor or military leader.</note>, and will have offices and lordship from them. For if it is in the tenth house, it will be concerning the king. And if the Lord of the Ascendant is in its **exaltation** <term>Exaltation: a specific sign where a planet’s influence is most harmoniously and powerfully expressed</term>, or in an **angle** <term>Angle: the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, considered the most active areas of a chart</term>, that native <note>The person for whom the chart is cast</note> will be of good stock and will attain nobility and high rank. However, if he is not in an angle, he will attain rank and nobility, but he will not be of good stock.

And if there is **reception** <note>original: "receptus"; a condition where two planets are in each other's signs, indicating mutual support</note>, he will be favored, and people will speak well of him. And if the Lord of the Ascendant, or the planet to which the "significator of nobility" applies, is in its own house, his status will be less than what we have said, because an exaltation is a higher and greater degree. And if it is in neither of those but is in its **triplicity** <note>A group of three signs belonging to the same element: Fire, Earth, Air, or Water</note>, it will be less than both. Therefore, look upon this ordering subtly, and judge according to it; nor should you forget to mix the influences of the planets, and look to their conditions. 

¶ When the Lord of the Ascendant applies to a planet existing in the "fall" <note>original: "casus"; the sign opposite a planet's exaltation, where it is weakened</note> of its exaltation, or that planet applies to him, it signifies that the native draws losses upon himself. And if any planet applies to the Lord of the Ascendant, and the Lord of the Ascendant is in the fall of that planet’s exaltation, it signifies that anxieties and labors will happen to that native. 

And if both or one of them is in an angle, that condition will be worse and more intense. And if that angle is the **Midheaven** <note>original: "medium celi"; the highest point in the chart, representing career and public life</note>, that evil will come from the king’s side. And if it is in the Ascendant, an infirmity or some other trial will happen to his body. And if it is the seventh house, it will come from the side of women and his adversaries, and those who argue with him. And if it is the fourth house, it will be from kinsmen, parents, and inheritances. 

And if a planet applying from its "fall" to the Lord of the Ascendant is a **fortune** <note>A "benefic" planet like Jupiter or Venus</note>, it signifies that his parents will fall upon him, just as one falls from a high place. And if **Aries** is in the Ascendant and **Mars** is in its exaltation <note>Mars is exalted in Capricorn</note>, the native will be full of anxieties and many thoughts; nor is he content with what he has, nor with his status. 

And if the Ascendant is Aries and the **Moon** is in **Gemini**, it signifies that the native will have a long life in anxiety and misery. And if it is in **Scorpio**, he will be a slaughterer <note>original: "degulator"</note> and a spreader of bad blood <note>A reference to a butcher or a medical bloodletter</note>. 

And I say that this judgment was spoken obscurely, just as the ancient wise men spoke obscurely in their aphorisms. Because what is said of Mars in its exaltation and Aries rising must be understood to happen when it is at night and he is beneath the earth, outside his **hayz** <term>Hayz: a condition of strength when a planet is in a sign and hemisphere matching its own nature</term> and unfortunate. And that which is said of the Moon in Gemini: that likewise is said when she is unfortunate there; then she signifies anxieties and miseries. 

¶ What is said of the Moon when she is in Scorpio, concerning slaughter and blood, is said because Scorpio is the eighth house from Aries and the "fall" of the Moon; and it signifies the shedding of the blood of beasts, as if he were a butcher of beasts and a letter of blood, since a "fall" does not signify a noble profession in this regard.

## ¶ Chapter 10. On knowing the parts of the Ascendant: and its judgments.

<image-desc>A large decorative woodcut initial 'Q' containing a human face, possibly representing a celestial or scholarly figure.</image-desc>When the **Part of Fortune** <term>Part of Fortune: a mathematical point representing prosperity and well-being</term> is protected and "outside the rays" <note>meaning the planet is not so close to the Sun that its influence is burned away or hidden</note> of the Sun, and its Lord is likewise, it signifies that the native will be healthy and will have good nourishment. And if it is unfortunate and "under the rays," it signifies that he will be miserable with poor nourishment. And if the Lord of the Part is in this manner in various parts, he will have many anxieties. And if with this it is in the Ascendant, he will have a stronger and worse status. And if it is free from the **malefics** <note>original: "infortūiis"; usually Saturn and Mars</note> and outside the rays, he will be of healthy body, good form, virtuous, a helper of the good, and will have a complete life in his livelihood. 

¶ When the **Part of Law** <note>original: "pars legis"; often referring to the Part of Religion or Faith</note> is in **Capricorn**, it signifies that the native will be of good character, nor will there be any malice in him. And if it is in Aries, or Leo, or Scorpio, it signifies that the native will be of swift and strong anger, nor will he be in harmony with men. 

¶ When the Moon does not apply to **Jupiter** in any aspect, it signifies that the native will be lowly, poor, and of a base life. And if she does not apply to **Venus** in any aspect, it signifies that he will have no joy, especially in marriage and because of women. And if she does not apply to **Mercury** in any aspect, it signifies that the native will not be a doer of good things, nor intelligent; these judgments will be especially strong if both are in signs of unequal ascension.

And if it is **retrograde** <note>Appearing to move backward in the sky</note>, it signifies that he will be among the wasteful, though strongly received by men, especially if Mercury is the significator of his status and the spirit of his deeds.

¶ The **Part of the Hyleg** <term>Hyleg: the "Giver of Life," a point in the chart used to determine the native's vitality and life span</term>, if the birth was **conjunctional** <note>original: "coniunctionalis"; referring to a birth that occurred during a Waxing Moon, following a New Moon</note>, is taken from the degree of the conjunction preceding the birth to the degree of the moon by day and night, and is projected from the ascendant. And if the birth was **preventional** <note>original: "preuentionionalis"; referring to a birth occurring during a Waning Moon, following a Full Moon</note>, this part is taken from the degree where the opposition (Full Moon) preceded the birth to the degree of the moon, and is projected from the ascendant.

¶ The wise man who wrote the book named **Enzirech** <note>Likely referring to a "Zij," a set of Islamic astronomical tables, or a specific author like Al-Zarqali</note> said that the signs of the Sun are masculine, and the signs of the Moon are feminine: therefore, when you have prepared its place, look to see if it falls in a sign of the Sun, which are: Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpio, Sagittarius, and Capricorn. And if it is in any of these, the Sun shall be the significator and shall have dominion. And if it is in any of the signs of the Moon, which are the remaining signs, the Moon shall be the significatrix and she shall have dominion. And if the lord of the term in which the part falls is with it, or aspects it, it will be the **Alcochoden** <term>Alcochoden: the "Giver of Years," the planet that determines the actual length of a person's life based on its position</term>. native will have a modest life. Afterward, if the lord of that sign is **cadent** <note>Cadent: falling away from the "angles" of the chart, usually meaning the 3rd, 6th, 9th, or 12th houses, suggesting weakness</note>, and the lord of the term is separating itself from aspects in the twelfth house, the native will be without a significator and without an Alcochoden, and will be of short life. Then perform the **Athacir** <term>Athacir: a method of "directing" a point through the zodiac at a rate of one degree per year to predict timing</term> of the degrees, and you shall direct it to the degrees of the fortunes and misfortunes and their rays, just as you do the *athacir* for the Hyleg itself: one year for every degree, just as I showed you in the chapter on *athacir* and as is named for you in our tables, which are named the **Tables for Dissolving Nodes** and dividing aspects; and there we distinguished in what manner the *athacir* is of every degree when it is in the quarters of heaven, and going through the signs similarly giving one year to each sign. And when it applies to misfortunes, it signifies evil according to the power of the planet to which it applies and according to the signification of the sign in which that same planet is; and when it applies to the "cutting off," it cuts off life.

¶ The **Part of the Hidden** <term>Part of the Hidden: also known as the "Part of Spirit" or "Pars Celati," representing the soul, intellect, and spiritual life</term> is taken by day from the Moon to the Sun, and by night the opposite, and is projected from the ascendant. This part signifies righteousness, law, the spirit of the body, religion, secrets, hidden and concealed things, thoughts, good fame, perfection, and clarity. And this part takes the place of the **Part of Fortune** by night. When the Sun aspects this part, it signifies few children, or that the children will be separated from the father. And if Jupiter aspects it, it signifies that the native will be a preacher of divine law, and just and good; however, if that aspect is a **quartile** <note>original: "de quarta"; a 90-degree angle, often considered a challenging or tense aspect</note>, he will not believe in what he preaches. And if it is in the **angles** <note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</note>, the native will be firm and constant in the law he holds, nor will he doubt it.

And if he is not received in his place, but the **fortunes** <note>Fortunes: the beneficial planets, Jupiter and Venus</note> aspect him while the **misfortunes** <note>Misfortunes: the challenging planets, Saturn and Mars</note> are cadent from him, the native will show good and beautiful deeds, and will desire to be adorned by them, even if he does not do deeds consistent with truth or goodness. And if the lord of the Part is **retrograde** <note>Retrograde: appearing to move backward in the sky, signifying a reversal or internalizing of energy</note> and unfortunate, it signifies that the native will change his law (religion) and will doubt it. And this will be according to the planet aspecting and afflicting it.

¶ And you shall know the cause of the change of his law in this way: if it is **Mars** that makes it unfortunate, it will be because of perfections, quarrels, and disputes that will be between him and another belonging to a more powerful law. ### Chapter 11. On the Second House and its significations.

**H**ere is the house that is the significator of the dignity and lordship of the native, and of fortune in **substance** <note>Wealth and possessions</note>, and the time in which he will have fortune, and of those who later raise him from misery and those who depress him into misery. ¶ I speak in the name of God, who directs us onto the good path. ¶ When we wish to look at the dignity and lordship of the native, we must first look at the stars: the **Beibenie** <term>Beibenie: Important fixed stars, usually of the first or second magnitude (the brightest)</term> which are of the first and second magnitude. Afterward, see if we find any of them in the degree of the ascendant, or in the degree of the **tenth house** <note>The Midheaven, representing career and public status</note>, or in the degree of the **seventh**, or in the degree of the **fourth**, or the degree of the Sun if the birth was by day, or with the degree of the Moon if it was by night. And the best of all these places is the degree of the ascendant, then the tenth, then the seventh, and then the fourth. And if these aforementioned stars are in two or three or more places—if the native is of royal lineage, he will be a high king. And if he is not of royal lineage, he will have power and command...

...with power and mandate similar to a king: and he will attain great nobility and high dominion. And know that the **Behenian stars** <term>Behenian stars: A selection of fifteen fixed stars considered especially powerful in medieval astrology, such as Aldebaran or Regulus, believed to provide the "root" of planetary power</term> elevate a person to a high rank and great dignity, and change them from the lowest to the highest status.
And when the **luminary of the time** <term>Luminary of the time: The Sun in a daytime birth, or the Moon in a nighttime birth</term> is in its **exaltation** <term>Exaltation: A specific sign where a planet's influence is most harmoniously strengthened</term> and in the **Midheaven** <term>Midheaven: The highest point of the zodiac at the moment of birth, associated with career, public status, and authority</term>; and the **Ascendant** <term>Ascendant: The zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</term> is one of the royal signs, and the lord of the luminary's sign or the Lord of the Ascendant is in the Ascendant or in the eleventh house: it signifies that he will attain a great and high rank, or he will be a royal counselor of high standing. And if he is of royal lineage <note>original: stirpere gali, likely a typo for stirpe regali</note>, he will be a king.
And look to the "planetary guides"—the solar guide by day and the lunar guide by night. A "guide" <note>original: ductoria</note> means that planets are oriental to the Sun or occidental to the Moon.
Next, if you find these planets in their own houses or exaltations, whether by day or night, and in the **angles** <term>Angles: The four most powerful houses in a chart (1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses), which represent the pillars of a person's life</term> aspecting one another: it signifies that the native will be a king or like a king. However, if they are in the aforementioned dignities but not in the angles, he will be an *alchaydus* <note>original: alchaydus, from Arabic 'al-qāʾid', meaning a leader, commander, or governor</note> or hold great dominion. And if neither luminary has any planetary "guides" that belong to its own **hayyiz** <term>Hayyiz: A condition where a planet is in a compatible 'sect' (day or night) and in a compatible hemisphere, significantly boosting its strength</term>, the native will be of the lowest reputation <note>original: nois (nominis)</note>.
When the Lord of the Ascendant is in its exaltation at the degree of the Midheaven: it signifies the native will be a king.
When the Moon, after its separation from a conjunction with any planet, **applies** <term>Application: When a faster-moving planet approaches a geometric aspect with a slower one, indicating an event about to happen</term> to a planet in its exaltation or one located in the Midheaven: it is a sign of kingship.
When planets rise by day before the Sun, or set by night after the Moon, or rise after her if they are likewise "fortunate" <note>meaning they are benefic planets like Venus or Jupiter</note>: it signifies kingship.
When the degree of a **Great Conjunction** <term>Great Conjunction: The meeting of Jupiter and Saturn, which medieval astrologers believed signaled major historical shifts and the rise of new empires</term> occurs in the year of that conjunction in the Midheaven of any native, and any of its lords or the Lord of the Ascendant aspects it there: the native will attain a great and manifest kingdom if he lives.
When **Venus** and **Jupiter** are in their exaltations and in the tenth house from the **Part of Fortune**, or if the Part itself is in the Midheaven from the Ascendant, and the lord of the house where the Part is located is Jupiter or Venus and they are in any of their dignities in the Ascendant: they signify kingship.
When the Lord of the Midheaven applies to the Lord of the Ascendant, and both are oriental in their exaltations: it likewise signifies kingship.
When the four "fortunes" <note>The benefic planets or points, usually Jupiter, Venus, the Sun, and the Moon</note> are in the angles: it signifies kingship.
When the Sun is in a royal sign and in the Midheaven and **received** <term>Reception: A supportive relationship where one planet is in a sign or degree ruled by another planet</term> by the Moon in its third part <note>its decan or triplicity</note>: it likewise signifies kingship.
When all planets apply to Jupiter, and Jupiter by agreement gives its power to Saturn, and Saturn is oriental, fortunate, and received: it signifies a great kingdom.
And I found from one of the wise men that **King Al-Fadl ibn Sahl** <note>A famous Persian vizier and politician (d. 818 AD) under the Caliph al-Ma'mun</note> had a Behenian star at the degree of his Ascendant—specifically the one called the "Two Rays of **Canopus**" <note>original: zoheyl (Suhayl). Canopus is the second brightest star in the sky</note>—and he held an ample and manifest kingdom and great reputation <note>original: nois (nominis)</note>.
When you wish to know the state of a native and his whole life day by day, one after the other: look to the **Lords of the Triplicity** <term>Triplicity: A group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element; each triplicity is governed by three specific planets called its 'lords'</term> of the luminary that rules the time of birth. And know that the first of them

is the significator of the first half of life; the second is the significator of the third part of life following this half; the third is the significator of the final third part that remains.
Next, look at the place where each of these planets resides and the lords of the triplicity of that place; divide their time among these lords as you did before, and proceed in this manner of dividing until you reach days and hours; and if you wish, judge according to what you find.
**Zoroaster** <note>original: Zaradest</note> said: he who has in his birth the degree with which the Moon rises in a fortunate state will have lasting fortune with him, because he will have honor through it as long as he lives.

### Chapter 12: On knowing the fortune of substance <note>Wealth and material possessions</note>.

<image-desc>Decorative drop cap 'A' within a square border featuring a floral pattern and a cross-hatched background.</image-desc>
Look first to the first Lord of the Triplicity of the **House of Substance** <note>The Second House of the birth chart, which governs money, assets, and livelihood</note>; and if you find it moving directly in its course, in a good path and a good state, firm in the angles, ascending in the circle of its **apogee** <term>Apogee: The point in a planet's orbit where it is furthest from the Earth, often associated with a peak of power or influence</term>, increasing in light and speed, and received by the lord of its house or in the house of its **term** <term>Term: An Egyptian subdivision of a zodiac sign where a specific planet holds essential power</term> with other planets giving it light and power: it signifies that the native will be wealthy and abundant in substance. The further he proceeds in his life, the more his substance grows, his status improves, and his wealth, honor, and goodness increase. But if it is in a state opposite to what we have said—such that it is remote, "falling" <note>in a weak house</note>, and unfortunate—he will be a poor, wretched beggar, of obvious poverty and low status.
And if the second Lord of the Triplicity of the House of Substance is fortunate and strong, and in a place of its dignity, received by planets aspecting it and agreeing with it: it signifies that the native will have a good and abundant life, and he will give well from his substance and do good with it for all who are close to him. But if this significator is in a different state: the native will have a narrow life, very poor and lowly, seeking his food from men, and he will be more often hungry than full.
And if the third Lord of the Triplicity of the House of Substance is in a good state, strong, and fortunate: the native will be faithful; people will speak well of him and trust him. He will be known and manifest for his good truthfulness and will be law-abiding in his words, and in buying, selling, giving, and receiving. But if this significator is in a different state: he will be disgraced, abhorrent, and hateful; known as a traitor and a deceiver, both for evil in giving and receiving, and for being lawless and a liar.
When the **Part of Fortune** is in its own house, and is in a strong place from the Ascendant, and its lord aspects it from a place well-aspected by the Ascendant, and it is in its own house or exaltation, or term or triplicity, or in its **hayyiz**, and the Moon is received by the Lord of the Second House: it signifies that the native will be wealthy and abundant in substance to a high degree. He will live a good life, and others will live with him and associate with him, and others will become wealthy through him.
And if the Part of Fortune is falling and in a bad place, or is in the rays of the Sun, or in the rays of an "unfortune" <note>A malefic planet like Saturn or Mars</note>, and its lord is in a foreign place, and the Lord of the Second House does not aspect the Ascendant: the native will be hard-working and poor.

...he will live a narrow and miserable life, begging from other men. 

$\P$ Neither the Sun, nor Mars, nor Saturn is good when placed in the **second house** <term>Second House: Known as the "House of Substance" or "House of Lucre," it governs a person's movable goods, money, and livelihood</term> in any birth chart. Nor will one born under such a placement possess good fortune, because the Sun destroys the planets and takes away their light <note>original: 'sol destruit planetas' — this refers to 'combustion,' where a planet is so close to the Sun that its influence is overwhelmed or 'burned up'</note>, and Mars is the significator of obstacles, labors, and a lack of substance. Saturn signifies emptiness, poverty, and want. And worse than all of this is if the **Lord of the House of Substance** <term>Lord of the House: The specific planet that rules the zodiac sign located on the cusp (boundary) of a particular house</term> is **combust** <term>Combust: A planet within 8.5 degrees of the Sun, considered weakened or 'blinded' by the Sun's heat</term> along with the affliction of the **Part of Fortune** <term>Part of Fortune: A mathematical point in the chart representing worldly success and physical well-being</term>; for the one born under such a constellation and state will have nothing with which to sustain himself; he will be hardworking but will live a life that is vile, miserable, and narrow. 

$\P$ When the Lord of the House of Substance is fortunate and strong, placed in the **circle of the apogee** <note>original: 'circulo augis' — the point where a planet is furthest from the Earth and moves most slowly, often associated with higher status</note>, and increased in light and number with many planets **applying** <term>Application: When a faster-moving planet approaches an aspect with a slower one, indicating an event about to happen</term> to it and giving their power and light to it—and if it is **received** <term>Reception: A dignifying relationship where one planet is in a sign ruled by another, suggesting mutual support or 'hospitality'</term> by them—it signifies that the native will gain much substance in many ways and from many sources according to the fortunes of the planets giving their light to him. He will gain the fortunes of their houses by taking them from the Ascendant, and the fortunes of the places in which they are located, and from those things they grant power and light; and it shall be according to that. Look to the first planet that enters the place of the Moon in nighttime births, or the place of the Sun in daytime births, because that planet will be the significator of the final state of the native regarding riches and poverty. 

$\P$ When the Lord of the House of Substance moves toward an application with the Lord of the **Ascendant** <term>Ascendant: The sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth, representing the person themselves</term>, it signifies that the native will gain substance from a source he did not suspect or believe possible, and he will have gains in good peace and honor, in a good manner, and from good things—especially when the Lord of the House of Substance is a **benefic** <term>Fortuna (Benefic): A planet that naturally brings harmony and success, primarily Jupiter or Venus</term>. 

$\P$ When the **malefics** <term>Infortunae (Malefics): Planets that naturally cause difficulty or disruption, primarily Saturn or Mars</term> grant gain, they signify only modest profits; and the substance which the native gains will be from fearful and terrifying places, such as through theft, or the denial of things, or through conflict and violence, or whatever resembles these things. 

$\P$ When the Lord of the Ascendant applies to the Lord of the Second House while receiving him, it signifies that the native will gain substance with labor, and he will always be oppressed in the pursuit of it, nor will he grant himself any rest in this. 

$\P$ And if the Lord of the House of Substance is a benefic along with this, he achieves success by his own efforts and gathers much substance through his own profit and sharpness. 

$\P$ But if it is a malefic, what he has of substance will be modest, and he will possess it with labor and great sharpness; and in seeking it, anxieties, labors, and fears will befall him. 

$\P$ When the Lord of the Ascendant is **separated** <term>Separation: When two planets move away from an aspect, indicating a past event or a diminishing influence</term> from the Lord of the Second House, it signifies that the native will seek little substance, and will be content with what he has, and will wait kindly and quietly for what comes to him. 

$\P$ When the Lord of the Second House is separated from the Lord of the Ascendant, it signifies that he will have a great desire to seek substance and will be very solicitous in this, involving himself in it frequently; nevertheless, he will not be fortunate in it, and will hardly attain what he seeks, nor will he have what he hopes for. 

$\P$ And when the Lord of the Ascendant applies to the Lord of the House of Substance, and the Lord of the House of Substance is **retrograde** <term>Retrograde: The apparent backward motion of a planet, usually signifying delays, reversals, or things not going as planned</term>, returning its light and power to him: the native will be solicitous in seeking substance and will involve himself in this; he will, however, be unfortunate, and whenever a way for profit appears to him...

<column-break/>

...it turns back and fails him; and troubles and labors will befall him in this. 

$\P$ And if the Lord of the Ascendant is retrograde, returning his light to the Lord of the Second House, and the Lord of the Second House applies to him: gains will come to the native, and the path will be open for him to gain much substance, yet he himself is inherently lazy in earning those things and completing the task; he withdraws into himself and does not finish it. 

$\P$ When the Lord of the Ascendant is in **opposition** <term>Opposition: An aspect of 180 degrees, often signifying conflict or total separation</term> to the Lord of the House of Substance, or in **square** <term>Quarta (Square): An aspect of 90 degrees, indicating tension and obstacles</term> to it without reception—or if the nature of either of them is contrary to the other, or their forms are similarly contrary—the native will be a dissipator and a destroyer of substance. He will spend beyond the limits of what is right, nor does he guard what he has. However, if he is in **trine** <term>Tertio (Trine): A harmonious aspect of 120 degrees</term> or **sextile** <term>Sextili: A harmonious aspect of 60 degrees</term> to it, with mutual reception, or if their forms are mutually agreeable, the native will be a miser; he will love substance, guard it, and live a greedy life. Neither will he have enjoyment from his substance, nor will others benefit through him. 

$\P$ When the Lord of the Second House is in any **angle** <term>Angle: The 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, which are the most powerful positions in a chart</term> by its sign, yet is **cadent** <term>Cadent: Falling away from an angle (the 3rd, 6th, 9th, or 12th houses), usually indicating weakness</term> by its degree: it signifies that he will be named and famous for being wealthy and will make an appearance that it is so, but in his secret life he is in want, and he will make greater expenses than the substance he actually possesses. However, if he is in an angle by degree but removed from the angle by sign: the native will be without pomp and orderly in his deeds; he will not be famous, nor will he show off his riches, and he will have greater wealth than he makes an appearance of having. His wealth will be greatest if that planet is **occidental** <term>Occidental: Setting in the west after the sun, or positioned in the western half of the chart</term> or in the **Angle of the Earth** <term>Angle of the Earth: The Fourth House, associated with the ground, hidden things, and the end of life</term>; then he will have greater riches and will cover himself more, and will hide what he possesses. 

$\P$ And when the significator of substance is in a covered and hidden place, it signifies great substance and riches—especially if the Lord of the Second House is a planet like Jupiter, who is of the nature and form of substance. However, if the significator of substance is Saturn or Mars and they are similarly hidden, it signifies great substance, but with labors, pains, and heaviness in seeking and gaining it; and obstacles will befall him, because the malefics signify obstacles, anxieties, and labors, and every thing that is lost or is gained and sought with difficulty, and every matter of despair. 

$\P$ When the **Lords of the Triplicity** <term>Lords of the Triplicity: Three planets that govern the zodiac signs of a specific element (Fire, Earth, Air, Water). They are used to divide life into three major stages</term> of the Sun in daytime births are all fortunate, strong, and received in good places and in their own dignities: the native will be rich and abundant for the whole time of his life. And if one of them is fortunate, good, and strong, and the others are unfortunate and evil: he will have substance and riches in the portion of life belonging to that fortunate planet, and he will have poverty and want in the portion of the other planet which was unfortunate. For the first of these significators signifies the beginning of life, which is the first third. The second signifies the second third, and the third signifies the remaining third. And in this manner you shall judge from the Lords of the Triplicity of the Moon in nighttime births. 

$\P$ And **Zoroaster** <note>original: 'zaradest' — a reference to the legendary Persian sage Zoroaster, often cited in medieval astrology as an ultimate authority</note> divides life through the Lords of the Triplicity in this way: he gives the first Lord of the Triplicity of the sign the first half of the whole life; and to the second he gives one-third of the whole life; and to the third he gives the remaining sixth of the whole life. 

$\P$ And know that when the Lord of the House of Substance is in the Ascendant, and in that birth there is a sign that the native will have riches, he will have them in his infancy and in the beginning of his life. And if he is between the Ascendant and the Midheaven, he will have them in his childhood. And if he is in the Angle of the Midheaven, he will have them...

However, if neither Jupiter nor Venus aspects there, the one born will gather substance, guard it, and increase it: nor will he make any good for himself from it, and he will be a miser in his whole life: nor will he remake anything from it on account of which he might have utility in this world or the next. $\P$ When the Lord of the Ascendant is strong and fortunate and in a good state and firm in the **angles** <term>Angles: The four most powerful points in a chart: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses</term>, and received by the Lord of the House of Substance: and that Lord of the House of Substance is **cadent** <term>Cadent: Positions in the sky (the 3rd, 6th, 9th, and 12th houses) where planets are considered weaker or 'falling away'</term>, unfortunate, and in a bad state, and damned: it signifies that the one born will be strong and solicitous in seeking substance: and he will seek it with many modes and ways, yet in a good manner: nor will he be lazy or weak in this: and with all this, it will be but a little that he will have from it, because when a planet is cadent it has no power: nor can it profit nor give except a small thing. However, if the Lord of the House of Substance is fortunate and strong and receives the Lord of the House of the Ascendant, and the Lord of the Ascendant himself is weak and cadent, the one born will be weak and lazy: yet he will be rich and abundant and gains will happen to him even though he does not labor for them: because when a receiving planet is strong and fortunate: its Lord will strengthen him, and God will give him a good state, riches, and good things. $\P$ When the **Dragon's Head** <term>Dragon's Head: Also known as the North Node, usually considered a point of increase and good fortune</term> is in the House of Substance going toward the Ascendant to the degree of the Ascendant: it signifies to the one born: riches, good, abundance, and profit: and he will have this from kings and nobles, and from men having power and dominion. And if the **Tail** <note>original: 'cauda' — the Dragon's Tail or South Node, usually associated with decrease or loss</note> is there in this state: it signifies diminution, poverty, and manifest misery, and he will dissipate and throw to a bad end what he has. $\P$ In whosever root of nativity Jupiter has any dignity or power or testimony: he cannot be very poor. $\P$ When the **Part of Fortune** <term>Part of Fortune: A calculated point in the horoscope representing prosperity and well-being</term> is cadent from the Ascendant and the **Luminary of the Time** <term>Luminary of the Time: The Sun in a daytime birth, or the Moon in a nighttime birth</term> does not look there: and its Lord is weak, unfortunate, and remote from the angles and not looking at the Part, and the Lord of the House of Substance is damned by the malefics or by the rays of the Sun which destroy and scatter: it signifies that the one born will be poor and miserable: nor will he be able to earn his full living: and perhaps he will live on alms. And if the Lord of the Ascendant is strong and fortunate, yet is an enemy to the Lord of the House of Substance: it does not hinder him though the Lord of the House of Substance be cadent: because the one born will have some substance: mediocre riches and mediocre gains. $\P$ When the Part of Fortune is powerful, fortunate, and in a good place: and the Lords of its **Triplicity** <term>Triplicity: A group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element (Fire, Earth, Air, or Water)</term> look upon it

from good and strong places: it signifies that the one born will be a gainer of substance: and rich, powerful, abundant, happy, full of life's habits, virtuous, and fortunate. And if any unfortunate planet damns it from the **opposite** or the **fourth** <note>original: '4$^a$' — referring to the square aspect, a 90-degree angle associated with tension</note> place while looking at it with this: his state will change and diversify: and he will have at one time indigence, and at another abundance and riches: and labors and anxieties will happen to him in earning and seeking substance. $\P$ When the Part of Fortune is in the **Term** <term>Term: Also called 'Bounds,' these are specific degrees within a sign ruled by a particular planet</term> of a malefic: and its Lord looks upon it from a good, strong, and fortunate place: and the malefics do not look upon it or its Lord: it signifies that the one born will involve himself in vile things for the sake of profit, thinking little of himself: yet he will gain and he will be the guardian of what he earns. $\P$ When the Sun in daytime births, or the Moon in nighttime births, is in the houses of the fortunes: and especially in the house of Jupiter: and Jupiter is in a good place and in a good state from the Ascendant: and the Lord of the House of Substance is safe from aspect, combustion, retrogradation, and the conjunction of malefics: he will have great riches, much substance, abundance, and high rank. And it will be the same if the planet receiving and joining the testimonies of substance applies to the Lord of the Ascendant: and the Ascendant is increased in light and number: yet if it applies and is descending and diminished in light and number: it signifies mediocre riches in substance. And if it is much misfortuned and damned: it signifies diminution and poverty and he will have little substance. $\P$ When the Part of Fortune is in the House of Substance with the malefics not looking at it nor casting their rays upon it: and the Lord of its house looks at it from a good and fortunate place: and in a good, strong, clear state, and free from the malefics that damn and destroy: it signifies that the one born will be rich and abundant: and substance, riches, and gains will come to him without any weariness or labor. And if the Lord of its house does not look at it, and the Luminaries look at it and its Lord without the aspect or testimony of malefics: he will be fortunate and of a good life: he will gather substance and riches from the king and from the high and noble ones having dominion. And if neither the Lord of its house nor any Luminary looks at it: he will be of little substance and a weak life: he will live his life by the labor of his body: nor will he earn more than what is for the day. And if with this it is misfortuned and weak and under the rays of the sun in the rays of malefics: he will be very poor, in need of life: nor will he have anything from which to live unless from seeking alms: and in this he will be ill-fortuned: because to whomever he begs, they will give him nothing: indeed, they will dishonor him, nor will they have pity for him. $\P$ When the Lord of the House of Substance is strong, safe, and fortunate: and in an angle and the Ascendant: all these virtues are not cast upon him: nor will the fortune of the one born be complete or perfect in substance: yet the one born will earn substance and in earning and having it he will be fortunate: but he will damn and scatter it: nor will it remain in him: nor will he know how to guard or maintain it.

When the **Part of Fortune** <term>Part of Fortune: A calculated point in a birth chart representing where an individual might find success and prosperity</term> is fortunate and strong in its location: the person born will be rich and will gain and gather substance, and will be sharp and wise in entering into its acquisition, and fortunate in working toward this, and will gain it in many ways and modes. ¶ When it happens that **Mars** is the **Lord of the Ascendant** <term>Lord of the Ascendant: The planet that rules the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</term> and is also himself the Lord of the Part of Fortune, and he falls in the **House of Substance** <term>House of Substance: The second house of a zodiac chart, which governs personal finances, possessions, and livelihood</term>, and no **fortune** <term>Fortune: A "benefic" or helpful planet, typically Jupiter or Venus</term> aspects <note>original: 'aspexerit' — refers to a geometric relationship between planets</note> him: it signifies that the person born will dissipate and ruin his substance and the inheritance of his parents, and will lead himself to poverty and want. And the occasion for which he will dissipate and lose it will be of the nature of the Lord of the sign; for if it is **Venus**, he will spend it on songs, games, women, and pleasures. And if it is Mars, he will lose it in quarrels, enmities, and legal cases. ¶ When Mars ruins the House of Substance, it signifies anxiety, poverty, labors, and impediments. And if **Mercury** ruins it: he will spend his substance on learning science and writing. And if **Jupiter** ruins it: he will spend it on good deeds of freedom and alms. And if with this he joins <note>original: 'applicuerit' — an astrological "application" where a faster planet approaches an aspect with a slower one</note> any fortune, or any good and strong planet: the trouble of his labor is diminished; yet if he does not join a fortune, but joins an infortune: he is laborious and very much so until he dies. ¶ When the Part of Fortune and the **Almuten** <term>Almuten: The planet that has the most essential dignity or "power" over a specific degree or house in the chart</term> of the Ascendant are in one quadrant: it signifies lasting and firm fortune. And if it is with the Lord of Travel: his fortune will be in travels. And if this part, and the **Part of Kingship**, and the **Part of Secrets** are fortunate: it signifies that the fortune of that person born will be manifest and apparent. ¶ When the Part of Fortune is in one quadrant and its Lord in another: it signifies that the person's fortune will come from many parts. ¶ When the Part of Fortune and its Lord are in the fourth house, or one of them is in the fourth house: it signifies that the person's fortune will be from treasures or from guarding treasures. And when they are in the tenth house or the twelfth, it signifies that he will have lordship and power over prisoners and captives. In whichever house the Part of Fortune and its Lord fall—provided they are fortunate and free from the aspects of the infortunes—it signifies the improvement and suitability of the things which 그 house signifies. signifier of substance more than the others; and from the nature and from the things of the house in which he is found, the gains and gifts shall be given to him. ### ¶ Chapter 13. On the third house and its significations.

This house signifies brothers and sisters together. And the **Sun** and **Saturn** with the first Lord of the "triplicity" <term>Triplicity: A group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element (fire, earth, air, or water)</term> of this house: signify elder brothers. And if **Jupiter** and **Mars** are with the second Lord of the triplicity of this house: they signify middle brothers; **Mercury** and **Venus** with the third Lord of the triplicity of this house: signify younger brothers. ¶ The **Part of Brothers and Sisters**: signifies all brothers and sisters, both great and small. ¶ When the Sun is the Lord of the 3rd house from the Ascendant and "burns" <term>Combust: A planet is "burnt" when it is too close to the Sun, weakening its influence</term> the Lord of the 2nd house or the Part of Substance: it signifies that the person born will lose his substance on account of his brothers, and will pay for them in taxes, losses, and many damages. ¶ When the Lord of the House of Brothers and the Part of Brothers are in the angles and in good and strong places: and they are fortunate and strong, and safe from "combustion" and other damages—especially if the Lord of the House of Brothers is increasing in light and ascending in his circle: it signifies that the person born will have many brothers. And if he is in a different state than we have said: it signifies he will have few brothers or none. ¶ Whichever signifier among the signifiers of brothers is fortunate, powerful, and in a good place, it will rise: it will endure and proceed toward good, and there will be goodness in that group of brothers for which it is the signifier. And those whose signifier is weak, burnt, and unfortunate: it signifies destruction and lack of love for that group for which it is the signifier. ¶ When the Lord of the 3rd house and the Part of Brothers or Jupiter are in "common" signs <note>original: 'signis cōib'' — Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, or Pisces</note> or in signs of "many children": and the fortunes aspect them with an aspect of friendship and strength, and with "reception" <term>Reception: A favorable relationship where one planet is in a sign ruled by the other</term>: it signifies that the person is the firstborn among his brothers, and that he will have powerful and good brothers. And if the "infortunes" aspect them with a contrary and inimical aspect, and without reception: it signifies they will be destroyed, and that one will despise the other, and the person born will see this. And if the Lord of the Ascendant does not aspect the Lord of the House of their brothers: those who remain will be evil and disobedient, and will leave by fleeing the town in which the person was born for another place. If the Lord of the House of Brothers is burnt, or the Part of Brothers is burnt, or if the Sun is in the House of Brothers, or in opposition to Jupiter: these are signs of few brothers, and that they will be unloved, destroyed, and pushed out. ¶ When the Lord of the House of Brothers is unfortunate above the earth: it signifies that damage and trouble will come to the brothers who were born before him. And if he has that misfortune while being below the earth: that evil and damage will come to the brothers who are born after him. And in this way you shall speak... [if the Lord of the 1st] joins with the 3rd in the 3rd house, or in the 6th, 9th, or 12th: and some "infortune" aspects them or does not aspect them: it signifies that the person born will not have brothers, or that his brothers will be so few that he remains alone, or they will depart from the land in which he was born, and he will remain. ¶ The person born will have utility from his brothers, and they from him, when the Lord of the House of Brothers is bodily joined with the **Part of Fortune** or its Lord in good and strong places. The person born will labor for his brothers, and they for him.

When the Lord of the house of brothers <note>original: 'dñs dom⁹ fratrū' — the ruler of the 3rd house</note> and the Moon are joined with Mars, and Mercury is joined with them, or if they aspect them from a square <note>original: '4ᵃ' — a 90-degree aspect, usually considered stressful</note> or opposition: ¶ When the Part of Fortune <term>Part of Fortune: A calculated point in a chart representing prosperity and well-being</term> is in the 3rd house from the Ascendant, and its Lord aspects it from a good place with a benevolent aspect: it signifies that the native <note>original: 'nat⁹' — the person whose birth chart is being read</note> will have good brothers, and he will love them and be loved by them; he will have utility from them and they from him, especially if the Lord of the Ascendant aspects that place: for then it will be a sign of great utility and firmness of love, and a complete and perfect agreement through God. ¶ When the Part of Brothers <term>Part of Brothers: A mathematical point (Lot) used to specifically predict matters concerning siblings</term> is in the tenth house, and the Lord of Jupiter <note>original: 'dñs io⁹' — likely referring to the ruler of the sign Jupiter is in, or Jupiter itself as a Lord</note> joins with it separately by itself, and the "fortunes" <note>benefic planets like Jupiter or Venus</note> aspect them from benevolent places: it signifies that the brothers of the native will have dominion, great fortune, and a high and noble status, and they will be of manifest name <note>famous</note>. And if that Part is in the "angle of the earth" <note>original: 'angulo terre' — the 4th house cusp, the lowest point of the chart</note> and the "infortunes" <note>malefic planets like Saturn or Mars</note> aspect it there, nor does it have any help from the fortunes: it signifies depression, [lack of] utility, poverty, an evil state, and the misfortune that the brothers of the native will have. ¶ When Jupiter is joined with Saturn in the house of brothers, and the Dragon’s Tail <note>original: 'cauda' — the South Node of the Moon, associated with loss or decrease</note> and Venus are there, or they aspect it from a square or opposition: it signifies that the native will fall into anxiety and loss because of his brothers, nor will he ever rejoice in them; rather, sorrows and many burdens will happen to him because of them. ¶ When Saturn is in opposition to the Part of Brothers, or in opposition to the Lord of the house of brothers, or both, or is joined with both or one of them, or both or one of them is in the third house from the Ascendant—especially if Mars aspects it there and is heavy and slow of course: it signifies that the brothers will kill that native, and will destroy and scatter him, and many burdens and losses will happen to them. ¶ The number of brothers is known from the planets aspecting the house of brothers, and from the movement of the Lord of the house of minor brothers, and from the aspect which the Lord of the Triplicity <term>Triplicity: A group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element (Fire, Earth, Air, or Water)</term> of the third house has to the Ascendant, if it is above the earth; or from the Ascendant to it if it is below the earth: giving one to each sign. And if any of those signs is "common" <note>original: 'cōmune' — a mutable sign like Gemini or Pisces, which often signifies doubling</note>, you shall double the number. ¶ When the Lord of the triplicity of the third house is in the Ascendant: it signifies that the native is the firstborn of his father and mother, or that he was born of diverse peoples, such as from a Moor and a Christian <note>original: 'mauro ꝛ x̄piano'</note> or vice versa. And if it is in the 10th house: it signifies he is the firstborn or the fourth. And if it is in the 7th: it signifies he is the firstborn or the seventh. Similarly, if the Lord of the house of brothers is in the Ascendant: it signifies the native is the firstborn, or that he will be alone, or that he will never have brothers or sisters. And when there is no planet between the Ascendant and the Midheaven <note>original: 'medium celi'</note>: it signifies similarly that the native is the firstborn. And if any brothers are born after him, they will be lost. And if by chance any of them remain: he will always be the greater and better. ### ¶ On knowing the worth of brothers.

<margin>¶ On knowing the worth of brothers</margin>
Look to the Lords of the triplicity <term>Triplicity: A group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element (Fire, Earth, Air, or Water)</term> of the house of brothers: to the first, the second, and the third; and to their locations in the heavens; and whether they are direct or retrograde. The first signifies the elder brothers, the second the middle, and the third the younger. Whichever of them is in its house or its exaltation <note>places where a planet is "strongest"</note>, free from misfortunes <note>malefic planets like Saturn or Mars</note>, in a good state, in a favorable place in the sky, and in a good relationship with the Sun: these signify the nobility and worth of whichever brother that planet represents. If the Lord of the 3rd house <note>original: 'dñs dom⁹ 3ᵃ'</note> joins with any planet existing in its exaltation or its own house: it signifies the nobility and worth of the brothers, and that they will go to and cling to the noble and the powerful. And if it joins with a planet existing in its "fall" <note>original: 'casu' — a position of planetary weakness</note>: it signifies the lowliness of the brothers and that they will cling to low men of little worth. If the Moon is separated from a planet in its exaltation or its house: it signifies the nobility of the elder brothers and great praise for them. And when she joins with any planet that is in its house or its exaltation: it signifies the nobility of the native, and great worth and nobility for the brothers who are born after him. When the Head <note>original: 'caput' — the North Node of the Moon, generally considered positive</note> is in the house of brothers: it signifies that the native will be in a worse and lowlier state than his brothers. And if the Tail <note>original: 'cauda' — the South Node of the Moon, generally considered negative</note> is there: it signifies that the native will be in a better and more noble state than his brothers. When the Lord of the 3rd house is a "fortune" <note>a benefic planet like Jupiter or Venus</note>, and is safe from misfortunes, joining with a safe fortune: it signifies the good state of the brothers, and that the native will be of the good Law <note>original: 'bone legis' — likely meaning a faithful or observant religious person</note> and a guardian of his law. And when it is a misfortune joining with another misfortune: it signifies the ruin of the brothers' status and the native's law. Similarly, when a fortune is in the house of brothers, or in the fourth house, or opposite to it: it signifies the good state and prosperity of the brothers and a good law for the native. And when a misfortune is there, or in the fourth, or opposite to it: it signifies the ruin of the brothers and misfortune for the native's law. ¶ When you wish to know if the native is of greater worth than his brothers, or vice versa: look to the Lords of the triplicity of the Ascendant <note>the 1st house</note> and to the Lords of the triplicity of the third house; whichever of them you find in a better state and place, that one will be of greater worth and nobility. And know that the first Lord of the triplicity of the house of brothers signifies the elder brothers; the second the middle; and the third the younger. Similarly, the Sun and Saturn signify the elders; Jupiter and Mars the middle; and Venus and Mercury the younger. And the Moon signifies the elders, and especially the sisters. Afterwards, whichever of them you find in the better state: judge the nobility and worth of the one that planet signifies. ¶ Mars is the significator of brothers: therefore, when he is strong and in his dignities: you shall judge prosperity, power, and fortune for the brothers. And if he is falling from his house or exaltation: you shall judge the opposite. And if Mars is between the Ascendant and the tenth house: judge the fortune and misfortune of the brothers according to the power he has in that place. Look at this from the Sun by day: and if it is not suitable, take Saturn in its place: and by night from Saturn: and if it is not suitable: take the Sun in its place. The significator <note>A 'significator' is a planet or point in a chart that represents a specific person or area of life.</note> of the mother is the Moon by night. And if she is not suitable: take Venus in her place: and by day take Venus. And if she is not suitable take the Moon: wherefore if the "fortunes" <note>The 'fortunes' or benefics are the helpful planets, Jupiter and Venus.</note> are joined with these significators: and are favorable to them: it signifies the good fortune of the father: and prosperity and a long life. And if the "infortunes" <note>The 'infortunes' or malefics are the challenging planets, Saturn and Mars.</note> should regard <note>In astrology, to 'regard' or 'aspect' means to be at a specific mathematical distance from another point.</note> these significators: and are favorable to them: and the significators are "cadent" <term>Cadent: The 3rd, 6th, 9th, or 12th houses, considered the weakest positions where a planet's influence is diminished.</term> from the angles and succedents, judge a bad state for the parents: misfortune: worthlessness: and a short life. And the greater reasoning which Ptolemy holds in this is that a "distribution" <note>original: 'athacir' — a technique of progressing a planet through the zodiac to predict the timing of events.</note> should be made to the significators by "ascensions" <note>A mathematical method of measuring the rotation of the sky.</note> by giving one year to each degree: then the fortune and impediments of the parents are judged, nor is an *alcocoden* <term>Alcocoden: The 'Giver of Years,' a planet used to calculate the length of a person's life.</term> made for them, as Dorotheus and others with him do. For Dorotheus says: look at the Sun in daytime births: and if you find it in an angle or succedent: or if it regards any of the lords of its dignities: it will be the *hyleg* <term>Hyleg: The 'Life-Giver,' the primary point in a chart used to determine physical vitality.</term>: and you shall make for it a distribution to know the state of the parents: and that planet which regards it shall be the *alcocoden* and the giver of time. And if you find the Sun cadent: or not aspected: look to Saturn: and if you find it in an angle or succedent and some of its lords regard it: it will be the *hyleg*: and a distribution shall be made for it: and that which regards it shall be the *alcocoden*: and the giver of life by the good pleasure of God. And if the Sun and Saturn are both cadent and not suitable: look to the "Lot of the Father": and if you find it in an angle or succedent: and some of its lords regard it: it shall be the *hyleg*: and the one regarding it the *alcocoden*. And if the Lot is cadent and not suitable: take the degree of the fourth house for the *hyleg*: and the one regarding it for the *alcocoden*: and a distribution is made for it: and it is judged according to that. And you should look for the mother in this way by beginning at night from the Moon: and afterward from Venus: then from the Lot of the Mother: and afterward from the degree of the 10th house: and you shall begin for the father in nocturnal births from Saturn: afterward from the Sun: then from the Lot of the Father: then from the degree of the fourth house: and you shall begin for the mother in daytime births from Venus: then from the Moon: and afterward from the Lot of the Mother: then from the degree of the 10th house. When by this way you have known the *hyleg* and *alcocoden*: look at the *alcocoden*: if you find it in an angle, direct in its course: and free from "combustion" <note>Combustion occurs when a planet is too close to the Sun, which was thought to weaken its power.</note> and "fall" <note>A sign where a planet's influence is at its weakest.</note>: and from the aspects of the infortunes: then it will give its middle years: or perhaps half of its greater years: and you shall add to it what the fortunes add to it: when they regard it from good places and when they have "received" <note>Reception is a favorable relationship where one planet is in a sign or dignity ruled by the planet it aspects.</note> it: however, the planets do not have the power of giving the parents their greatest years after the children have been born. And if any infortune regards the *alcocoden*, it diminishes as much as three-fifths of its lesser years. And if it is combust, it will diminish months according to the number of its lesser years. And if it is retrograde along with combustion: the diminution will be in days. And if with this it is in its fall: the diminution will be in hours. And there are some wise men who do not look to the lords of the *hyleg*: and they take the *hyleg* of the father and mother: and make for it a distribution: and judge by

him. And there are some who take the *almuten* <term>Almuten: The planet that holds the most combined dignity and power over a specific point or house.</term> of the father, which is the Sun or Saturn, for the *alcocoden*: and for the significator and for the giver of life and years: and they make for it a distribution. And similarly they look for the mother from the Moon and Venus: and whichever of them they find as the *almuten*: they take for the *alcocoden* and for the significator: and giver of life and years: and for it they make a distribution to know the being of the mother. And I say that when the *almuten* is strong and fortunate and "oriental" <note>A planet that rises before the Sun is 'oriental' and was considered more active and masculine.</note>: and in its own house or "exaltation" <note>A specific sign where a planet is honored and highly effective.</note> and in an angle: it can well give its greater years: especially if the father was a youth around the age of 20 years: because this judgment can well happen in this way. And there are other wise men of the ancients: such as Cima: and Belha: and Acciton: and Antiochus: and others who agree with them who extracted the life of the father from the remaining ascensions of the lords of the dignities of the significator of the father according to the time in their signs. For example: the significator of the father according to the time was Saturn: and we found it in the 15th degree and 16th minute of Pisces, which is the house of Jupiter and his "term" and his "form" (that is, "face") and the exaltation of Venus and the "triplicity" <note>The triplicity refers to the grouping of signs by element (Fire, Earth, Air, Water).</note> of Mars: wherefore from the ascensions which remain to these three planets in their signs, which are Jupiter, Venus, and Mars, they extract the life of the father: so that we found there remained to Jupiter in his sign 16 degrees of ascensions, and that which remained to Venus in her sign of ascensions was 19 degrees and 3 minutes. And that which remained to Mars in his sign through ascensions was 4 degrees and 35 minutes. And this whole amount joined together makes 39 degrees and 38 minutes. And by giving one year to each degree there would be 39 years and 7 months and 12 days: and this is the life of the father according to the opinion of the said wise men. And other wise men say that the life of the father shall be known from the number of years of the planet which is closer by degree to the degree of the 4th house, provided it regards the 4th house. And Hermes and Albategnius <note>A Latinized name for the 9th-century astronomer al-Battani.</note> say that the life of the father shall be known from the ascensions of the sign of the Sun in daytime births: and the sign of Saturn in nighttime ones. And the life of the mother from the ascensions of the sign of the Moon in nighttime births. And from the ascensions of the sign of Venus in daytime ones. Abenragel <note>The 11th-century court astrologer Ibn Abi al-Rijal, the primary author or source of this text.</note> says, "I have tested this by example in many births: and I found this judgment true: and I tested this in my own birth and the life of my father was according to the ascensions of the sign of Saturn: neither more nor less by a single point."

¶ Al-Hasan son of Al-Khasib <note>Original: "al besen filius al besçieb" – A 9th-century Persian astrologer.</note> said: One day when I was with Abu Ma'shar <note>Original: "abolabeç" – A famous Persian astrologer (787–886 AD).</note>, and he was with Himeraeus, an old man came to me and gave me a scroll in which a birth chart <note>Original: "figura vnius natiuitatis"</note> was written, and he told me to look at the chart. And I asked him whose birth it was; he replied that it was that of a certain son of his. And while I was looking and thinking about it, Abu Ma'shar took it from my hand, looked at it for a little while, and said: "The first thing we must judge in this birth is that this native was born of adultery; for he is not the son of the one who says he is his son."

I said: "From where do you have this?" And he replied: "This old man says this birth is of his son; but for the father of the native whose birth this is, it is already four years since he passed away; he died in the same year the native was born." And I asked how he knew this. And he said: "I looked at the degree of the **Part of the Father** <term>Part of the Father: A mathematical point calculated to reveal details about the father's life.</term>, and I found it in opposition to Mars, and there was not more than one degree between them; and I found the Part in the 11th house from the Ascendant, which is the 8th from the 4th <note>The 8th house from any starting point represents death; the 8th house counted from the 4th (father) is the 11th.</note> and the house of the father's death, and there was one degree between the Part and Saturn. Because of this, I judged that the father of this native died in the year the native was born. And this old man says he is his son; therefore the native is adulterous." Then the old man said: "I am not the father of this native; but he is my grandson, the son of my son; and my son, his father, died in the same year as this birth, just as this good man now said."

### ¶ On the time when the native will have children.

When Jupiter applies to the Ascendant or the Lord of the House of Children: it is a time for having children. Or look at the number of degrees that are between Jupiter and the Lord of the Ascendant: or when the Sun enters any of the angles: or when it applies to the Part of Children: these are the times for having children. And if the Lord of the House of Children is in the Ascendant: he will have a child in his youth. And if it is in the 10th: he will have one in the middle of life. And if in the 4th or 7th, he will have one in his old age: or near his end.

### ¶ On knowing the number of children.

The number of children is known in this way: look at the two Lords of the Triplicity of Jupiter: the first and the second: and whichever of them you find to be stronger and more fortunate: and in a better place. See how many signs are between it and the Ascendant: and judge that he will have as many children as there are signs. And if there is a common sign between them: give two: and according to that number you shall judge.

### Significations of the Lords of the Triplicity of the 5th House.

<image-desc>A historiated initial 'Q' with a central floral or sun-like motif.</image-desc> When the first **lord of the triplicity** <term>Lord of the Triplicity: The planets that rule the three signs of a particular element (Fire, Earth, Air, Water).
