And if it is in a different state: perhaps he will be a sodomite and a bad fornicator, performing evil and shameful fornications in an evil manner. <margin>Part of Children</margin> The **Part of Children** <note>An Arabic Lot used specifically to predict offspring.</note> is taken by day from Jupiter to Saturn, and by night the reverse, and it is projected from the ascendant. This Part signifies children: and whether they will be male or female, and if there will be more males than females or more females than males. And the number of children and the time in which they will be born is taken by day and night from Mars to Jupiter and is projected from the ascendant.

## Sayings on this reasoning.

When you wish to know illnesses and their occasions and causes, look at the **sixth house** <note>The house traditionally associated with illness, service, and small animals.</note>, the **part of illness** and its lord, and the fortunate and unfortunate planets existing in the 6th house; and look at the Moon and the lord of its house, for it similarly has significance in illnesses. And if the majority of these are fortunate and well-placed, or if that one which has the greatest significance and lordship in the figure <note>The "figure" refers to the birth chart or horoscope.</note> is fortunate, or well-placed and strong, the person born will have minor illnesses, but will be of a healthy and clear body. And if the majority of them are unfortunate or poorly placed, or if that one which has the greatest significance and power in the figure is unfortunate or poorly placed and has some mixture with the lord of the Ascendant, the person born will be damaged in body by many illnesses and pains, especially if it is in any of the **angles** <term>angles: the four strongest points of a chart—the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses.</term>. ¶ And if the strongest of these indicators is Saturn, or one made unfortunate by Saturn, the majority of the person's illnesses will be of the nature of **palsy** or paraly-

<column-break/>

-sis, or hemorrhoids, or **dropsy** <note>original: "hydropisis," an old term for edema or swelling caused by fluid.</note>, and of every illness that arises from coldness and dryness, and which is healed with difficulty. ¶ And if the strongest of these indicators is Mars, or one made unfortunate by him, the majority of illnesses will be from heat: bile or blood, and the **frenzy** <note>original: "frenesis," a state of delirium or brain inflammation.</note> of fevers and wounds. ¶ When Saturn is in the sixth from the Ascendant, or in the sixth from the Moon, or in the fourth or the opposite of either of them, the illnesses of the person born will be of the nature of coldness, especially if he is in a humid sign. ¶ And if Mars is in the sixth from the Ascendant, or in the sixth from the Moon, or in the fourth or the opposite of either of them, the illnesses of the person born will be from heat; and such will they be that they will either be liberated quickly or kill quickly. ¶ When the Moon and the lord of its house are free from unfortunate planets, and no misfortune is in the sixth house, the person born will be safe from illnesses and harms. When the Moon and the lord of its house are unfortunate, and there is an unfortunate planet in the 6th from the Ascendant, the person born will suffer many illnesses and pains in the body. ¶ When Mars is in the Ascendant as an unfortunate planet, if it is the same Mars as an unfortunate planet in a daytime birth, or Saturn in a nighttime birth, and it is joined bodily with the Moon or the Sun, it signifies weakness of sight or the damage of the entire vision. ¶ When the Moon is joined bodily with unfortunate planets, or in the quarters or opposites of them, and is in a dry sign, the majority of illnesses the person born will have will be from heat and dryness. ¶ When a planet signifying illness is in the Ascendant, the illness will be in the beginning of their life. You shall look for the matter of male and female servants from the sign of the **Sixth House** and its lord, and from its place in the figure, and the fortunate and unfortunate planets existing in the same; and in what place the **Part of Servants** <term>Part of Servants: a specific calculated point in a birth chart used to predict matters concerning one's employees or helpers.</term> is; and of what kind of nature the place of **Mercury** is, since he himself is the indicator <note>original: "significator"</note> of male and female servants. <image-desc>Decorative woodcut initial 'O' begins the text in the first column. Within the circle of the letter is an intricate diagram consisting of several concentric rings and geometric lines, likely representing an astrological chart or armillary sphere.</image-desc>

**The eighth house** <note>In traditional astrology, the Eighth House governs death, inheritance, taxes, and shared resources.</note> is the indicator of death; and from this house it is known in what manner, for what cause, and by what kind of infirmities the native <note>The person whose birth chart is being read.</note> shall die. It also shows whether he will die in comfort and wealth, or in poverty and labor; and whether he will die in his own house or abroad, or among his relatives or elsewhere. ¶ When the **first lord of the triplicity** <note>Each zodiac sign belongs to an element (Fire, Earth, Air, Water) and is ruled by a set of three planets called "lords of the triplicity." These were used to divide a person's life into stages.</note> of the house of death is fortunate and strong, the native will die in wealth and honor. And if he is unfortunate, falling, and peregrine <note>original: "peregrinus"; a planet that has no essential dignity or strength in its current position, like a traveler in a strange land.</note>, he will die a bad, shameful, and public death, and in indignity and disgrace. ¶ And if the **second lord of the triplicity** of this house is strong, firm, and fortunate, the native shall inherit from parents and ancestors, and will be fortunate in the ancient inheritances of the dead. And if his state is the opposite of this, the native will leave his goods to those who will feel no grief at his death, to his enemies, and to those who have no relation to him. ¶ And if the **third lord of the triplicity** of this house is strong, fortunate, and received <note>original: "receptus"; a technical term where one planet is in a sign ruled by another, creating a supportive relationship.</note>, the native will follow the works and ways of the ancestors of his lineage, and the nobility and good fame of them shall live again. And if he is in a contrary state, the native will damage the works of his ancestors and do the opposite of his kin, and he will be cursed for his own deeds. ¶ When the sign of the eighth house is fortunate, and its lord is in a house and term of fortune <note>Terms are specific degrees within a sign ruled by different planets.</note>, and is in height and good state, the native will die in a good manner, in riches, nobility, and high status, and his death will be celebrated. When the eighth house is unfortunate and its lord is in its "fall" <note>The sign where a planet's influence is weakest.</note>, and in a falling place, and peregrine, the native will die in misery and disgrace; his death will not be celebrated, nor will it trouble anyone. ¶ When the **Part of Death** <note>An "Arabic Part" or Lot—a mathematical point in the chart calculated to signify a specific theme, in this case, the end of life.</note> is in the house of journeys, or when **Saturn** is the lord of the house of death, or when Saturn is in the eighth even if he is peregrine, or if he is in Sagittarius; or when the Part of Death and its lord and the lord of the eighth house are in the **Ascendant** <note>The First House, representing the self and physical body.</note>, or if they are in signs in which the lord of the Ascendant has no dignity; or if the lord of the "angle of the earth" <note>The Fourth House, representing the grave and the end of matters.</note> is in the eighth or the lord of the eighth is in the third: all these signify that the native will die outside his own land, despised and poor. ¶ When the **Dragon’s Head** <note>The North Node of the Moon, often seen as an intensifier of either good or bad fortune.</note> is in the eighth from the Ascendant and **Mars** is joined to it, or aspects it from the fourth house, or by an opposite aspect that is contrary and hostile without being received by any of the fortunes; or if the **Moon** is with Mars in the eighth, especially in a nocturnal birth; or if the Moon is in any of the angles or succeeding houses, and Mars beholds her with a contrary and hostile aspect without the aspect of **Jupiter**: these are signs that the native will be killed by iron <note>original: "ferro"; implying a sword, blade, or weapon.</note>, or his head will be cut off, or he will die a bad and shameful death. ...in the **eighth house**, he will die a natural death according to the **complexion** <note>original: "complexionem"; referring to the balance of bodily humors (blood, phlegm, etc.) which was believed to determine health.</note> and the nature of the sign in which its lord [ruler] was located.

¶ The **Lot of the Killing Planet** <note>original: "Pars planete interfientis"; a calculated mathematical point in a birth chart used to predict the cause of death.</note> is calculated by day from the degree of the **Moon** to the degree of the **Ascendant**, and by night conversely; it is then projected from the Ascendant. Thus, if the Moon itself aspects <note>Forms a geometric relationship with.</note> this Lot while the Moon is in an unfortunate state, it shall kill the native. And if, along with this, it is in a sign representing "cut members"—which are **Aries**, **Taurus**, **Leo**, and **Pisces**—he shall be killed by the sword, or they shall cut off his limbs. If the Moon is not unfortunate in this regard, his limbs shall be cut off, but he will not be killed. If the lord of this Lot and the lord of the eighth house are unfortunate to one another, the native will be killed by a sword. 

¶ The **Lot of the Year** in which the killing of the native is feared—or when poverty, loss, or trouble shall befall him—is taken by day and night from **Saturn** to the lord of the **conjunction** or **prevention** <note>The New Moon or Full Moon immediately preceding the birth.</note> preceding the birth, and is projected from the Ascendant. This Lot and the **Lot of the End of Things** are one and the same. When this Lot or the lord of its house are joined with the lord of the Ascendant, and both are unfortunate, the native shall suffer many infirmities and many impediments in his body and his substance [wealth]; perhaps he will even destroy himself or come to the point of self-destruction. And when the year of revolution <note>The annual birthday chart.</note> or the degree of the division of years reaches this Lot or its lord, it signifies evil and loss in substance and body. 

¶ The **Lot of Captivity and Imprisonment**: this is the very same as the **Lot of Plowing and Sowing**, and it is the **Lot of Saturn**. It is calculated by day from the degree of Saturn to the degree of the **Lot of Fortune**, and by night conversely, and is projected from the Ascendant. This Lot signifies deep thoughts, ancient sciences and wisdoms, prisons, captivities (and how one might escape them), and the ability to retain things and keep them in mind. It also signifies the fugitive, the thief, and every thing that falls into a well or the sea; the nature of lands, plowing, sowing, and buildings; falsehood, concealment, and the keeping of secrets; and it signifies old age, idols, and the causes of death. 

¶ When the **lord of the Ascendant** <note>The planet ruling the first house, representing the native's life and vitality.</note> is in the eighth house, the native will be of ill-will, a deceiver, full of many sorrows, and weak of heart. If the lord of the eighth house **applies** <note>original: "applicuerit"; moves toward a geometric aspect.</note> to him, he will die a sudden and swift death. If it is **separated** from him, he will not fear death but will have many infirmities at the end of his life. If the lord of the Ascendant applies to the lord of the eighth, the native shall be the cause of his own death: such as one who exposes himself to fortune in a violent struggle, or in such a matter, or one who drinks and eats excessively, or who does some other thing through which he dies. And know that when the lord of the Ascendant applies to the lord of the eighth house, its significance and testimony is complete in having a short life and failing to thrive, nor is anything else necessary in this judgment. If the lord of the eighth house **receives** <note>A technical term where one planet is in a sign ruled by the other, showing a cooperative link.</note> him, he may be nourished, yet he will not have [long] life. The **retrogradation** <note>When a planet appears to move backward in the sky, usually considered a sign of weakness or irregularity.</note> of the lord of the Ascendant likewise completes this judgment, except for **Mercury**, whom retrogradation does not harm much. And if the lord of the Ascendant moves toward a retrograde planet, or is in his **first station** <note>The moment a planet stops to turn retrograde.</note> and does not receive him, it likewise completes this [judgment of short life]; this is a true testimony and a complete judgment. When the Moon is in the degree of the Ascendant, it harms and kills equally as **Mars** does, especially if it has any **dignity** <note>Traditional strength or "rank" within a zodiac sign.</note> in the sign of the eighth house.

<column-break/>

When the lord of the **Lot of Fortune** is **under the rays** <note>original: "sub radijs"; so close to the Sun that it is invisible, signifying weakness or being "hidden."</note>, it kills the native according to the nature of the sign in which it fell nearby; especially if the lord of the Lot is **combust** <note>Extremely close to the sun.</note> or **in extremis** <note>original: "itazimi"; likely a Latinization of the Arabic 'al-tazimi' referring to 'Cazimi' or being in the heart of the sun.</note>. But if it is removed from combustion in any way, it does not kill. 

¶ From the lord of the **term** <note>A subdivision of a zodiac sign.</note> of the degree of the **seventh house**, and from the lord of the term of the degree which is opposite the **Hylech** <note>The "Giver of Life" planet in a chart.</note>, the cause of death is taken; and from their lords, the manner of death is known. Thus, if it be in the tenth or eleventh house: he shall die from a fall from a high place. If it be in the ninth: he shall die on a journey outside his own place. If in the Ascendant: he shall die a natural death in his own house. If **Mars** is in the fourth house or in conjunction with it while being above the earth: he shall die by the sword. If Mars is also in a **fiery sign**: he shall die by fire. If in a **watery sign**: he shall suffer wounds. If that sign is in the fourth house: he shall be drowned in water. If it is in the sixth and in a **human sign** <note>Signs depicting humans, such as Gemini, Virgo, or Aquarius.</note>: he shall be killed by servants. If it is in the eighth: he shall die poor and indigent. 

¶ The native whose degree of the seventh house is the term of a **malefic** <note>original: "infortune"; specifically Mars or Saturn.</note> shall die a foul death. And he whose seventh house term belongs to a **benefic** <note>original: "fortune"; specifically Jupiter or Venus.</note> shall die a beautiful death. 

¶ The degree of the **fourth house** signifies what shall become of the body after death: whether it will be buried in the earth, or hung on a gallows, or cut into pieces, or cast away, or stinking, or if its garments will be stolen from the grave. Thus, if the degree of the fourth house is safe from the malefics: he shall be buried and remain safe there. If the lord of that same degree is **Mercury** and he is **cadent** <note>Falling away from the powerful angles of the chart, signifying weakness.</note> and unfortunate: his garments will be stolen after he is buried. And I say that any native having the eighth house and its lord good and safe from Mars shall not be killed. And whoever has them safe from the **Sun** shall not be burned. If it is a nocturnal birth, look to the degree with which the Moon sets: if you find it in a **square** <note>original: "recta 4^a^"; an aspect of 90 degrees, considered tense or difficult.</note> to Mars, the native will be killed. He who has benefics in his eighth house shall scarcely or never die an evil death. When the Moon is the Hylech, its opposite degree will be the signifier of death.

The other planets were there, and the lord of the house of the Moon was joined with the other planets in the house of death. Yet, because the Moon was free from the rays of the malefics, elevated and strong in her own place (being in her exaltation), and the other signifiers were safe from the rays of the malefics, it signified that he must have a long life. ### Chapter 8: Regarding the 9th House and its Significations.

Look into the journeys of the native first by the **lords of the triplicities** <note>original: "dnis triplicitatū"; in medieval astrology, each house was governed by three planets based on the element of the sign. Here, they govern different aspects of the 9th house.</note> of the house of journeying. For if the **first** lord is in a good state, strong, fortunate, and "received" <note>original: "receptus"; a condition where one planet is in a sign or dignity of another, creating a supportive relationship.</note>, it signifies that the native will go on journeys and move himself from one place to another, and he will be fortunate and happy in his journeys and movements. And if he is in a contrary state, he will have impediments and grievances in his journeys and movements; he will be despised in them, and he will be dragged out and expelled from his land and place, nor will he have any utility or profit in his travels.

¶ And if the **second** lord of the triplicity of the house of journeying is in a good state—powerful, fortunate, and received—the native will be of good law <note>Follow a righteous religion or legal code.</note>, named for being good and just, religious, and a guardian of the law. And if he is in a contrary state, he will be of bad law, named as evil, and of evil works and unbelief. And if the **third** lord of the triplicity is fortunate, firm, and safe from misfortunes and damages, and remote from contrary planets, the native will have **truthful dreams**: and whatever he sees in dreams will be true, nor will it lie; and those very things he sees in sleep, he will see in the open, or he will be an expositor and interpreter of dreams and will be truthful in them, so that whatever he says thereof will be true. And if he is in a contrary state, the native will be a liar in dreams and for the most part will see terrifying dreams; whatever he dreams will be false, and his dreams will rarely be truthful.

¶ When the lord of the house of journeying is strong and fortunate, and in his own house, exaltation, or triplicity, and is received by the lord of his house; and the **Lot of Travel** <note>original: "ps itineris"; a mathematical point calculated to predict travel.</note> is likewise in a good place in the figure; and some "fortune" [planet] is in the house of journeying or in the 3rd house: the native will make good, safe, and joyful journeys in which he will gain substance, riches, a good standing, and a name. And when the lord of the house of journeying is evil, "falling" <note>original: "cadens"; located in a weak house, like the 6th, 8th, or 12th.</note>, not received, unfortunate, and outside of his dignities, the native will have bad journeys—anxious and laborious—and he will be far from his land and place without any utility or profit.

<margin>aspect</margin>
¶ When the lord of journeying goes and applies to the lord of the Ascendant, journeys will happen to the native that he will not expect nor think of. And if with this there is a "fortune" or the lord of the Ascendant receives him, he will have utility, honor, and profit in those journeys; however, if there is a "misfortune" and the lord does not receive him, he will have damage, loss, and labor in those journeys. And if the lord of the Ascendant applies to the lord of the house of journeying, the native will be a traveler of journeys, mobile, and will move himself from one place to another. And if with this the lord of the house of journeying is a "fortune," he will have many utilities and profits in his journeys and movements. And if it is a "misfortune" and there is no reception between it and the lord of the Ascendant, he will have labors and anxieties in his journeys without any utility or profit. And if the lord of the house of journeying is separated from the lord of the Ascendant, the native will love and desire to make journeys, yet he will not make them; instead he will stay quiet and make few journeys and movements. And if the lord of the Ascendant is separated from the lord of the house of journeying, the native will be lazy.

### Chapter 9: Regarding the observation of the cause of law and legality.

<image-desc>Large decorative drop cap 'A' featuring a leafy design within a square frame.</image-desc>
You shall observe these two things from two houses by which law and legality are known: and they are the 3rd and 9th houses. And you should know what kind of signs are in them: and which planets are in those signs: and which ones aspect them from the third <note>Sextile aspect.</note>, fourth <note>Square aspect.</note>, and opposition: and who is the lord of the houses of their exaltation, of their terms, and of their triplicities <note>These are different levels of "essential dignity" or planetary strength based on their position in the zodiac.</note> and in what places in the figure <note>The astrological chart or "map" of the sky.</note> these lords are: and who is the lord of the part of law <note>A calculated point related to faith or jurisprudence.</note>: and in what place that part falls: whether it falls in a movable, common, or fixed sign: and if it falls in an angle, a succedent, or a cadent house <note>These categories describe how active or passive a house’s influence is.</note>. And if the lord of the part is oriental or occidental, direct or retrograde, or under the rays <note>Hidden by the Sun's light, making the planet weak.</note> or escaped. ¶ And you should know that **Mercury** has power and a proper significance in the cause of law and legality separately from the other planets. Wherefore observe in him also the mixture which he has with the planets and in which of them he has the greater part. ¶ And know that when he should be in the house of **Saturn** or in his aspect: the native will be of profound thoughts: firm in belief: he praises the things of the other world more than this one: and believes them and thinks much on them and loves them: and holds that they are better than those of this world: he abhors games, jests, and solaces: humble, patient, of need and of labor: especially if the "fortunes" <note>Benefic planets like Jupiter or Venus.</note> should be cadent <note>Placed in weak houses.</note> not aspecting the ascendant. ¶ And if **Mercury** should be in the house of **Jupiter** or in his aspect the native will be of a good name, complete and grateful: of good law, legality, and an observer of the law in which he was. And if he should be in the house of **Mars** or his aspect and it should be the same aspect from the 4th <note>A square aspect, usually indicating tension.</note> or opposition: the native will be a murderer, irascible, a malefactor of bad law: and he despises it and is a gatherer of lies and of those who color them: he will recite new things that never were. ¶ If **Mercury** should be in the house of the **Sun** or in the aspect of the **Sun**: the native will be humble and mild and of good law: wise in judgments and decrees: obedient to God: he will praise divine things and commands. ¶ If **Mercury** should be in the house of **Venus**: the native will be of free will: very cheerful: he will love and praise hilarities, jests, and vices. And if with this **Mars** should aspect him he will be incredulous and will despise his law.

And if he should be cadent from an angle and from there should aspect a planet which is not cadent receiving him: the native will have prosperity and fortune after [certain] causes: and he will be victorious and named after his death more than in life: and he will leave books and a name among men who will follow the works he was accustomed to do. And if the sign of the 9th house should be the house of **Jupiter** and the **Moon** in it and the birth is nocturnal: the native will be an astrologer: a narrator of hidden things: and he will predict future things: and this same thing will be if the lord of the 9th should be **Mercury**: or there should be a star of the nature of **Mercury** in the 9th. ¶ When the **Moon** should be in the ascendant in a human sign: the native will be beloved by men: and he himself will love them: and this same thing will be if it should be in any of the angles in a human sign...

### ¶ Chapter Ten: Concerning the Tenth House and its Significations.

<image-desc>A large ornamental woodcut initial Q containing a seated figure, likely a scholar or judge, surrounded by decorative floral patterns.</image-desc>When you wish to know those things which will happen to the native regarding kings, high status, nobility, offices, and masteries: First, look at this from the first **Lord of the Triplicity** <note>In astrology, each zodiac element (Fire, Earth, Air, Water) is ruled by a set of three planets known as the Triplicity Lords.</note> of the tenth house. If you find him in a good state, strong, high, and fortunate—and if he is in the **Midheaven** <note>original: "medio celi"; the highest point of the chart, representing career and public life.</note> or in the **Ascendant**—the native will have dignity, offices, and lordships; he will rule peoples and have power over them, and he will have dominion, a high rank, and profit from the king and from his affairs and from being close to him. But if the significator is in a different [poor] state, obstacles and anxieties will happen to the native on the part of the king because of his affairs and by being close to him; and for a time he will be condemned and fearful on the part of the king and despised, and through this he will lose his things. ¶ And if you find the second **Lord of the Triplicity** of this house strong and free, the native will be a man of good and great deeds and well-known, and he will be successful in his deeds. But if he is "falling" <note>original: "cadens"; located in a weak house of the chart.</note> and bad in a bad state, he will be fearful and will do evil and shameful deeds. ¶ And if the third **Lord of the Triplicity** is fortunate, strong, firm, and clear, the native will be noble, high-ranking, praised, and well-known according to his nature. And if he is in a different state, he will be low, weak, and despised according to his nature. ¶ When the sign of the **Midheaven** is one of the fiery signs—especially if it is **Leo** or **Aries** and the **Sun** is in it—and the **Part of the King** is in aspect to the "fortunes" <note>Benefic planets, usually Jupiter or Venus.</note>, the native will without any doubt be a king. Similarly, when the **Part of Fortune** has escaped from being under the Sun's rays and is clear and free from "unfortunes" and from planets that are enemies and contrary to the place in which it sits, and is in a complete and strong aspect of a "fortune" without any

<column-break/>

aspect of an "unfortune" cutting off or condemning it, the native will be a king who is safe, secure, mild, and pious. ¶ When the **Part of Fortune** is in a good place and in one of the regal signs, and the **Sun** is in the **Midheaven** in the place of height, and in a good position relative to the **Ascendant**—and similarly if the **Part of the King** is good and well-placed, and the "fortunes" aspect it there—the native will be a king. And if the "unfortunes" aspect it there, as long as the aforementioned constellations are present, they cannot greatly depress the status of the native nor make him worthless; nevertheless, they will depress him from the status of a king [to something slightly lower]: he will still have lordship, he will command peoples, or he will be the *Alcaide* <note>original: "alcayd"; a governor or administrative judge, from the Arabic 'al-qāḍī'.</note> of certain cities or castles, having the power and lordship to command and forbid. ¶ When the **Part of the King** is in any of the houses of **Mars**, and **Mars** aspects it from a good and strong place—and both are in high places of kings—and the **Sun** aspects them, and the **Part of Fortune** is in a good place with "fortunes" aspecting it from good and strong places, the native will be a lord of knights and a leader of armies and battles; he will go with knights and armies to battle with the enemies of the kingdom; he will be secure and of good counsel in his works, victorious and happy in his battles, and in them wise and mild. ### Chapter 11. On knowing the mastery of the native and what he will involve himself in.

You shall know the status of the native and his health in his masteries <note>original: "magisteriis"; refers to one's vocation, trade, or professional skill.</note> and works from the planet signifying those things: for his status in his masteries and works will be according to the status of their significator and its fortune. Know that the planets signifying masteries are: the planet found in the Ascendant or the Midheaven—specifically one that is "oriental" to the Sun <note>Rising before the Sun.</note> and "occidental" to the Moon <note>Setting after the Moon.</note>—and the planet to which the Moon applies when she separates from a conjunction in daytime births, or from the Part of Fortune in nighttime births; and likewise the planet to which the Moon applies at the hour of birth. ¶ The planets that signify masteries by their own nature are Mars, Venus, and Mercury. Therefore, when you find any of these three in the Ascendant or Midheaven in the east, having some dignity in that place or some lordship of the Sun or Moon, it signifies a noble, great, and good mastery; the native will be a leader and praised in it, and that mastery will be according to the nature of the planet that is the significator. And if none of these three

planets is in the Ascendant or Midheaven, but is instead in the "angle of the earth" <note>The 4th House, the lowest point in the sky.</note> or the west <note>The 7th House.</note>, it signifies a mastery of less height than what we have said, and that he will be more idle. ¶ And if none of these planets are in any of the said places, take the significance of the native’s mastery from the Lord of the Midheaven, if the birth was by day; or from the planet to which the Moon applies, if it was by night—especially if it has any lordship over the Part of Fortune. And if he is received <note>original: 'receptus', a condition where the planet ruling the sign of one planet is in aspect to it.</note>, he shall have the things he wants and many friends and good from them: and they from him: and if he has children, he will rejoice in them. ¶ And if he is in the 2nd [House], he will have good, profit, and riches through his friends and companions. ¶ And if he is in the 3rd [House], he will have brothers who are noted and known and in a good state, who will possess riches in their youth. ¶ And if in the 4th [House], his parents will be **afflicted** <term>azemena <note>original: 'azemena', an Arabic-derived term referring to chronic illness or physical disability.</note></term> and they will be in a good state but live for a short time. ¶ And if in the 5th [House], he will have children in whom he will rejoice, and good things and riches throughout his whole life from the beginning even to the end. ¶ And if in the 6th [House], he will be in a bad state and a bad life: he will live by the sweat of his brow and have a short life. ¶ And if in the 7th [House], he will have a fortunate wife and will love her, and will have riches and good with her. ¶ And if in the 8th [House], he will be unfortunate: he will involve himself in trade: yet he will not have fortune in this. ¶ And if in the 9th [House], he will have fortune and good in journeys: and he will be fortunate until the end of life. ¶ And if in the 10th [House], he will have power and dominion in his youth: yet his dominion will be only over his progeny and his company. ¶ And if in the 11th [House]: he will be a victor: he will have many friends and a good and great name. ¶ And if in the 12th [House], he will have little good and few friends: he will be of a bad life and will have many enemies.

When this Part is fortunate: the native will have things in which he will have confidence and whatever he desires: and if it is unfortunate, he will have none of these things.

### ¶ Chapter 14 on the 12th House and its significations

<image-desc>Ornamental woodcut initial 'A' featuring foliate patterns and cross-hatching inside a square frame.</image-desc>
Look in the judgments of this house first at the first lord of its **triplicity** <note>The three signs associated with an element (Fire, Earth, Air, or Water).</note>: and if you find him fortunate, strong, and high: judge that the enemies of the native will overpower him and do with him whatever they wish. And if he is falling, condemned, **combust** <term>combust <note>When a planet is so close to the Sun that its influence is overwhelmed or hidden.</note></term>, and **peregrine** <term>peregrine <note>A planet that is in a sign where it has no special dignity or strength, like a stranger in a foreign land.</note></term>: the native will overpower his enemies: and they will be hindered, and evil will happen to them, even that which they believed they were doing as evil to the native. ¶ And if the second lord of the triplicity of this house is safe, powerful, fortunate, and elevated: the native will have little sadness and anxiety and will be cheerful and content with what he has. And if he is in a different state: he will have many anxieties and sadnesses: and labors and obstacles and great losses will happen to him in what he possesses and in his body. ¶ And if the third lord of the triplicity of this house is powerful, fortunate, and firm: the native will be a **dialectician** <note>A person skilled in logical argument and debate.</note> and of good eloquence and reasoning: happy in his reasons and causes, and he shall prosper against any adversary. And if he is in a different state, he will be of weak reasoning and hindered speech: he will not have justice against his adversaries nor his evildoers. ¶ You shall know the state of the native with his enemies from the **Part of Enemies** and from the Lord of the 12th House: from the Lord of the Ascendant and from the Moon and from the planets having testimonies and lordships. ¶ And when the Lord of the Ascendant and his helpers are in good condition and supported: the native will be happy and the victor over his enemies. ¶ And when the Lord of the House of Enemies and the Part [of Enemies] are in good condition and supported, the enemies of the native will overpower him and conquer him.

## ¶ Concerning the Aspects of the Planets and first regarding the Trine. Saturn.

<image-desc>Ornamental woodcut initial 'Q' containing a miniature of a scholar at a desk with astronomical instruments.</image-desc>
When you find in a birth chart **Saturn** looking at **Jupiter** from the third <note>original: "de tertio"; this refers to the Trine aspect, where planets are 120 degrees apart, or four zodiac signs away from each other</note> while Jupiter is in a good position: the native <note>The "native" is the person whose birth chart is being read.</note> will have much substance: lands, trees, and will build houses and houses of prayer; and perhaps he will have dominion in his own town; he will have a company serving him; he will be obedient and agreeable to his parents; he will have an inheritance of working land and gain from strangers; and he will be trusted, faithful, and honored by kings and high-ranking men. ¶ When **Saturn** looks at **Jupiter** and **Mercury** from the third: the native will be a hider and keeper of secrets, and wise in hidden and covered matters; and perhaps he will be a counselor to a king, and will have dominion in the town where he was born; and with all this, he will be religious and of good law, and will nourish those he has brought up; but he will have no benefit from his children, because they will die or flee from him. ¶ And if **Mars** looks at the aforementioned planets: it diminishes the predicted good and signifies hardships, misfortune, and labors. ¶ When **Saturn** looks at **Mars** from the third without the aspect of Jupiter or Mercury: the native will be rich, powerful, and will have dominion; and he will be renowned in cities and lands in the likeness of a king; and his brothers will die during the days of this native. ¶ When **Saturn** looks at **Jupiter** from the third in a daytime birth: it is good in all things; ### The Opposite Aspect.

**W**hen **Saturn** looks upon **Jupiter** from an opposition <note>An alignment of 180 degrees, where planets are on opposite sides of the earth.</note> it does not signify any good for the native in business or his works: and sadness will happen to him on the part of his sons. And if **Saturn** in this aspect is in the Ascendant <note>The 1st House, representing the self and beginnings.</note>: and **Jupiter** is in the West <note>The 7th House, representing the end of life or partnerships.</note>: he will be a wretch in the beginning of his life: and fortunate at the end. ¶ When **Saturn** is in opposition to **Mars**: it signifies to the native distress and anxieties in his life, sadness: and infirmities: loss: indigence: few children: many enemies: quarrels and killings that will happen to him with his own kinsmen: and it signifies that his father will die quickly and by a sudden death: and misery upon miseries. And if these two planets are in water signs <note>Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces.</note>: the native will be hardworking on rivers or the sea or things similar to these: and moist infirmities <note>In humorism, diseases caused by an excess of phlegm or water.</note> will happen to him

<column-break/>

from which he will suffer damage in his body. And if they are in the signs of four-footed beasts <note>Signs like Aries (the Ram), Taurus (the Bull), or Leo (the Lion).</note>: strikes from beasts will happen to him: or the bite of a wolf or dog: or a "torica" <note>original: "torica"; likely referring to tormina (colic) or a twisting of the bowels.</note> from which he will die. ¶ And if they are in such signs in the fourth house, they signify that same thing: and they signify the depression of the native until he is destroyed. ¶ And if these two infortunes are in this aspect, afflicting the **Moon** without the aspect of the **Sun**, if they are in the angles: it will be a sign that the native will die in a foreign place, remote and far from his land and his kinsmen: and perhaps he will be oppressed: and removed from every good so much that it will be necessary for him to live by begging from men: yet if these infortunes are opposite in the "succedent" houses <note>The 2nd, 5th, 8th, and 11th houses, which follow ## The Sextile Aspect and Conjunctions

<margin><unclear>Amon</unclear></margin>
Concerning the **sextile aspect** <note>An angle of 60 degrees, generally considered a harmonious alignment.</note>, judge as you judged regarding the third <note>The "Trine" aspect (120 degrees).</note>, except that the significations of the sextile are weaker. ¶ **Conjunctions.** ¶ When **Saturn** is in conjunction with **Jupiter**: the native will have many lands to be worked, and will hold the labors of kings and nobles. They will entrust their substances to him, and in this he will be faithful and honored for this reason, provided that **Mars** does not look upon <note>Does not "aspect" or cast its influence upon.</note> them. ¶ And when **Saturn** and **Mars** are joined: the native will be patient and mild, yet he will not have good fortune; he will be slow to complete what he desires, and only with pain and labor. It will weaken his body, and melancholy will overcome him. His father will die before his mother, and he will destroy his father's substance. Great infirmities will befall his brothers, and they will die before him. It signifies that he will be hardworking and sorrowful; many impediments and labors will happen to him, yet he will always be patient. And if **Jupiter** looks upon them there, it will direct and resolve all this evil. ¶ And when **Saturn** is joined with the **Sun**, he loses his father's substance, and his good fortune turns into labor and bad fortune. And if the birth is nocturnal, it is worse, whether **Saturn** is oriental or occidental <note>Rising before or setting after the Sun.</note>. It signifies evil for the father and his brothers, and especially for the native himself. And if the **Sun** is within a few degrees of him, it is worse and the evil is more certain, because his father will die a bad death, and the native will be depressed and undervalued;

<column-break/>

and moist infirmities and weakness of the body will happen to him. He will love to depopulate lands, and perhaps he will gain a treasure in this, and his livelihood will come from it; but afterward, with all this, he will be in labor. And if this conjunction occurs in the house of the **Sun** or in the house of **Saturn**: it signifies that the father of the native will be of good legality, yet he is not rich; and the native will hate his parents; and other significations [will be] as we have told you. ¶ And when **Saturn** is joined with **Venus**: it signifies that he will marry a singing woman <note>A woman associated with public performance or entertainment, often viewed with suspicion in medieval texts.</note> and she will not conceive by him. He will play with sterile or injured women, and he himself will be accused and depreciated for this reason. He will have no son; and if by chance he has any, he will not have a male, nor will the child live. ### The Presence of One Planet in the House of Another

<margin>Saturn</margin>
When **Saturn** is in the house of **Jupiter**: it signifies a good status and honor. It indicates that the person will nourish his own children, love his wife, stand among nobles, and be like a counselor; along with this, he will have a good life and a good name. This same thing is indicated when he is in the **term** <note>A "term" (Latin: *terminus*) is a specific segment of a zodiac sign ruled by a particular planet.</note> of **Jupiter**. ¶ And when **Saturn** is in the house of **Mars**: the person born will be heavy-natured and full of worry regarding both his own deeds and those of others. ¶ And when **Saturn** is in the house of **Venus**: he can have no good in marriage, for if he weds, it will be to a servant, an old woman, or a harlot; obstacles and worries will happen to him because of women, and perhaps he will live in infirmity his entire life. ¶ And when **Saturn** is in the house of **Mercury**: the person born will be very cautious, yet also sensible and wise; he will understand the secrets of books, but will suffer heaviness in this regard, being ponderous in speech or of an impeded tongue. ¶ And when **Jupiter** is in the 
<margin>Jupiter</margin>
house of **Saturn**: the person born will be rich, but neither famous nor honored; yet he will have hidden wealth and riches, though he will not rise to lordship or high rank. In this, you shall judge according to the status of his lineage. He will be of good company and well-received; he does not labor, nor does he care for fame or pomp, nor for praising himself; but obstacles and thoughts of shameful things will happen to him. ¶ And when **Jupiter** is in the house of **Mars**: the person born will be a **commander** <note>original: *alcaydys*, from the Arabic *al-qā'id*, meaning a governor, judge, or military leader.</note>, a lord of soldiers, or an astrologer, understanding the natures of the stars. If, in addition to this, he is in an **angle** <note>The four most powerful houses in a chart: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th.</note> aspecting the **Moon** and **Sun**, and they themselves are in angles, he will arrive at great value and high rank. ¶ And if both luminaries <note>The Sun and Moon.</note> are in masculine signs, he will be a **commander** of many soldiers by land and sea, and powerful in both attacking and defending. ¶ And when **Jupiter** is in the house of **Venus**: the person born will be honored in the houses of kings and be their counselor, or a holder of revenues; his life will be sustained by this and by noble men. Perhaps he will dally with a prized and noble woman in secret; at that time he will have riches and great honor. Perhaps he will be a steward or the master of a house of honorable women, and he will live and be honored for it. ¶ And when **Jupiter** is in the house of **Mercury**: he will be the **commander** of a town and will be righteous; or he will be a divider of towns, or a diviner, understanding all manner of difficult things. He will be of good sense and intellect and will be praised for this; men will benefit from him because of his beauty. # This is the sixth part of the "Complete Book on the Judgment of the Stars" which Abenragel <note>Albohazen Haly (Ibn Abi al-Rijal), the 11th-century author of this work.</note> composed regarding the revolutions of the years of those born. And there are 15 chapters in it.

---

### Chapter 1: On the distribution <note>original: "appodeamento," from an Arabic concept of "releasing" time-lords or planetary periods.</note> of each of the 7 planets throughout the times of the years of the person born.

<margin>++</margin>

![Woodcut of an armillary sphere]
<note>This diagram shows the celestial spheres encircling the Earth, used here to visualize the movement of time and planetary influence.</note>
It is fitting in this matter for us to begin from the first years of the person born, and similarly from the first sphere nearest to us which is most closely around the sphere of the Earth; and to go through this order until we reach the end of the years of the person born, and similarly reach the last of the planets which is appropriate to those final years. In this matter, it is fitting for you to look closely, for through it you shall know the status of the person born...

<summary>This page concludes Book 5 with aphorisms on planetary aspects and a critique of the astrologer Messehalah's theory of retrogradation, then begins Book 6 by Abenragel, focusing on the timing of planetary influences over a human lifespan.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the discussion of life cycles and planetary influences from the previous page, moving from specific planetary combinations to a general overview of the "Ages of Man" governed by the seven planets, followed by a new chapter on the "division" of time in predictive astrology.</meta>

<margin>horoscope of the person born</margin>
...through the spans of the years of his life generally; however, you shall know the specific and separate state of the person born from the properties of the planets and the figures in the <term>root<note>The "root" (radix) refers to the natal chart, or the positions of the planets at the exact moment of birth.</note></term> and the <term>revolution<note>The "revolution" refers to a Solar Return chart, cast annually to predict the events of a specific year.</note></term>. But in this general sense of which we wish to speak, I say that the **Moon** governs the person born in the years of infancy, which are the first four years; and these are called by many the "years of nutrition." During this time, the infant’s body is moist, not yet fully formed, and grows easily. The greater part of its governance at this stage is watery and liquid; because of this, the body is soft and weak, easily altered, and its limbs are neither complete nor strong. The infant cannot do with them what must be done, nor can it remove the accidents <note>In medieval philosophy, "accidents" are external events or physical conditions that happen to a person.</note> that may befall it. ¶ After these four years, the governance passes to the second planet, which is **Mercury**, and it governs in the years of childhood, which are ten years <note>From age 4 to 14.</note>. In the person born at this time, the intellect, speech, and reason are strengthened, and during this time, he takes root in the sciences, wisdoms, morals, and <term>masteries<note>Technical skills or professional trades.</note></term>, and in every manner of learning. ¶ And after these years, the third planet governs, which is **Venus**, in the years of adolescence, which are eight years following the others <note>From age 14 to 22.</note>; and this is the number of the "minor years" of Venus. At this time, the pathways of the seed and the <term>seminal vessels<note>original: "algadi"; a term derived from Arabic referring to the reproductive anatomy.</note></term> begin to move, and the taste for or delight in lying with a woman is stirred. At this time, the person born has "canine manners" <note>An old expression meaning shameless or driven by raw appetite, like a dog.</note> because he does not restrain himself from fulfilling his desires. For the greater part of this time, he is in love. He longs to use refined things pertaining to fornication, and he deceives himself in whatever happens to him regarding these matters. ¶ After these, the middle planet governs, which is the **Sun**, in the middle years which are called the years of youth; he governs for 19 years according to the number of his revolution in conjunctions with the Moon <note>From age 22 to 41; 19 years refers to the Metonic cycle.</note>. Then the person born is powerful in his deeds, bold and sharp in seeking and demanding profit and his livelihood. He will make himself upright and withdraw from games, labors, and errors; he abstains from fornication, being diligent and seeking honor and fame. ¶ After this, the governance passes to the fifth planet, which is **Mars**; he governs for 15 years in the fifth stage and the completed state of the person born, according to the number of his own minor years <note>From age 41 to 56.</note>. In this time, hardships in his livelihood and afflictions in his body will happen to him, as well as sadness in his spirit. The body begins to fail, and for the most part, he must labor and do deeds that he will eventually have to leave behind; he will involve himself much in sharp dealings for the sake of profit, and he labors in this before he reaches the time of death. ¶ After this, the governance passes to the sixth planet, which is **Jupiter**, and this is the sixth order of years: these are the years of old age, which are 12 years according to the number of his own minor years <note>From age 56 to 68.</note>. Then a man separates himself from labors and pain, and gives himself over to quiet, not wishing to expose himself to danger or toil. He draws himself toward the law and good faith, reflecting on things and withdrawing from shameful deeds and words; at this time, he loves and studies the pursuit of honor and praise; he makes himself chaste, modest, and honors himself. ¶ After this, the final order passes to **Saturn** in the seventh order of life, which is the end of life and the decrepit age...

...and then the body weakens; life retreats, strength is lost, and movement and actions are altered. He loses joy and the desire for women; all his actions grow cold, and he devalues himself, caring nothing for himself; he lacks confidence in what he sees, according to the coldness and heaviness of **Saturn**. ¶ The time in which each of these planets governs shall be according to what its status was [at birth]; for if, at the time it governs, the planet was <term>fortunate<note>A planet is "fortunate" (benefic) if it is well-placed in the zodiac and making helpful aspects.</note></term> and in a good state, its governance will be completely good. And if it was <term>unfortunate<note>A planet is "unfortunate" (malefic) if it is poorly placed or afflicted.</note></term> and in a bad or condemned state, damage will happen during its governance according to that and according to its nature. And by this, you shall judge the deeds and status of the person born; for these are the properties of the times according to the general order and according to nature. ¶ And we began the governances of this order with the **Moon** and gave her the minor portion, and to the others their own; for we gave a tenth of her minor years <note>The Moon's minor years are 25; a tenth is 2.5, but the text calculates 4 based on the cycle with the Sun.</note> according to her revolutions with the Sun through conjunctions. After this, we increased it by giving **Mercury** the middle of his minor years <note>Mercury's minor years are 20; half is 10.</note>. Afterward, we gave the other five planets their full minor years; and according to this number and ordering, the total becomes 98 years. ¶ And if the person born should pass all these years, it returns to the years of the **Moon**. And if he passes these, to the years of **Mercury**. And if by chance he passes these, to the years of **Venus**; and with these, 120 years are completed, which are the "greater years" of the **Sun** and a complete life.

->¶ Chapter 2: On the Division and the Divider.<-

Consider if the Lord of the Partition or <term>Division<note>A "Division" (divisio) is a predictive technique where a specific point in the chart, like the Ascendant, is moved through the zodiac over time to see which planets it encounters.</note></term> should be a malefic: it signifies labor and poverty in that year; unless the Lord of the Year, the Lord of the sign of the Division, and the Moon are in good places, and have the testimony of the benefics; or unless that malefic itself is <term>oriental<note>Rising before the Sun, which was often considered a source of strength or productivity for a planet.</note></term>, and in a good place, and likewise in the root of the birth—so that the Ascendant of the root is not condemned—for this signifies an improvement of the Division. They draw back its damage and labor, and signify progress of the nature of that malefic, because the Lord of the Year will be improved. And if the Lord of the Year should be a benefic, it similarly directs and brings benefit where it is under the Sun’s rays, because then it confers that to the <term>term<note>The "terms" or "bounds" (termini) are specific degrees of a sign ruled by a particular planet.</note></term> in which the partition resides. ¶ And when the Lord of the Year is a malefic, and in a good place in the root of the birth: it signifies that it gives good to the person born; especially if it is also oriental, with malefics not casting their rays into that term; and provided that the Moon, the Ascending sign of the year, and its Lords are safe from malefics and in the testimony of the benefics; for this is the sign of good and progress in that year according to the nature and property of the planet ruling in that year and the Division. ¶ When the Lord of the Division is a benefic and in a bad and unfortunate place in the root of the birth: it signifies neither utility nor good; especially if the Lord of the Year is condemned, for then it signifies nothing but evil and loss in that year. And when the Lord of the Division is a benefic, and in a good place in the root of the birth and in the rays of the benefics: it multiplies and increases that good which it signified, and it will be more and greater; especially if with this the Lord of the Year should be supported, oriental, and a benefic, because then it signifies much good according to nature.

<summary>This page details the "Seven Ages of Man," a system where the stages of a human life (infancy to old age) are governed by specific planets, totaling a theoretical lifespan of 98 to 120 years. It then transitions into the technical rules for "Divisions," a predictive method used to determine the fortune or hardship of a specific year based on planetary placements.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the technical instructions for calculating annual predictions, focusing on "divisions" (the distribution of time periods among planets) and how the aspects of the planets in both the natal chart ("the root") and the annual "revolution" chart indicate health, status, and family events.</meta>

...its place. And when the place of division in the <term>root<note>The natal chart or birth map.</note></term> of the birth or the <term>revolution<note>The solar return chart cast for the specific year being studied.</note></term> is <term>unfortunate<note>Afflicted by "malefic" planets (Saturn or Mars) or placed in a difficult house.</note></term> through a <term>conjunction<note>When two planets are in the same degree of the zodiac.</note></term> or <term>square<note>original: "quarta"; an aspect of 90 degrees, considered challenging.</note></term> or <term>opposition<note>An aspect of 180 degrees, considered very difficult.</note></term>, or by the malefic planets; for if the division in this year belongs to a planet of <term>fortune<note>A "benefic" planet, specifically Jupiter or Venus.</note></term>, but that benefic is aspecting it with these unfortunate projections of rays, it signifies evil and loss in all ways. This is especially true if the <term>Lord of the Year<note>The planet ruling the Ascendant of the annual solar return chart.</note></term> and the **Moon** are afflicted, because the **Moon** in every manner is the one that completes all significations and deeds. 

And when the division is handed to a <term>malefic<note>Saturn or Mars.</note></term>, and the place of division in the root and the revolution is afflicted and has no rays from a benefic in either the revolution or the root; and the **Moon** is afflicted in the root; and no benefic aspects the <term>Ascendant<note>The eastern horizon at the moment of birth or the year's start.</note></term>; and the malefics aspect that place by opposition or square: it signifies the cutting off of life <note>A prediction of death.</note> for the person born in that year. 

But if the rays of the benefics are in that <term>term<note>A specific subdivision of a zodiac sign ruled by a particular planet.</note></term>, even though the **Moon** and the Ascendant of that year are afflicted, he shall not fear dying that year; however, an impediment shall befall him. 

And when a malefic <term>applies<note>The movement of a faster planet toward an aspect with a slower one.</note></term> to the place <margin>the continuous infortunes</margin> of the **Moon**, or the **Moon** applies to it in the revolution—especially if the significator of the year is in a bad house, such as the **House of Infirmity** <note>The Sixth House, which governs illness.</note>—it signifies labor and great sickness. This same thing is signified when the **Moon** applies to the place of a malefic in the natal root; the matter will be even more pronounced if this application occurs in the natal Ascendant, or in the sixth or twelfth house of the revolution, and especially if the **Moon** was afflicted in the natal root. 

And you should know that every planet, when it is in its own division and projects its rays to the term in which it was located in the root, signifies in that year the specific qualities of that planet. For example: if **Jupiter** has dominion in the year of the revolution and is the "divisor," and projects its rays into the term where it was at birth, and is not afflicted in the root nor in the natal chart, and is in a good house: it signifies in that year marriage and children, and that he will associate with and join the company of nobles; and he shall rise to nobility and power according to the promise of the natal root.

If Jupiter is more strengthened than the Sun, the loss will be less and lighter. ¶ And if **Venus** (♀) is joined with the same, or looks upon him with some good aspect and in a good state, it signifies to him an increase in substance, and joy from the part of women or effeminate men, good clothing, and that he will be occupied with fragrant things, entertainers, and gaieties. He will have gains from quiet deeds and skills, and he will be abundant and honored by men. ¶ And if **Mercury** (☿) is joined with him, or looks upon him with a good aspect in both times, and they are in a good state: it signifies that the native will rise that year in credibility, law, and liberty—doing good, reasoning, and having good thoughts. He will associate with scribes and hold an office from the king in revenues, or from the nobles. He will be fulfilled in that year, of good fame, and trusted by nobles. He will involve himself in prayers and matters of the law, and he will have utility and gains from whatever he does with his hands, or through his own character and thoughts. ¶ And if the **Moon** (☽) is joined with the same or looks upon him with a good aspect in both times: it signifies an increase in the value and worth of the native that year, and that he will do deeds from which he will have utility. He will desire righteousness and will possess wealth, gains, and profit from merchandise and other things. His hopes and trusts will be fulfilled, and every thing he begins and involves himself in will be completed for him; he will possess it and reach a high dignity. And if the Moon in this aspect is increased in light <note>Waxing toward a full moon.</note>, these significations will be greater; he will labor to have a son that year and will have him, as well as good and improvement in all things. ¶ And when Jupiter is in a bad state through retrogradation, or combustion, or misfortune, or by being occidental or <term>peregrine<note>A planet in a sign where it has no traditional dignity or strength, like a stranger in a foreign land.</note></term>, or in the house of an infortune, or falling from an angle, or in a "pit" <note>original: "gradu putei" — specific degrees of the zodiac considered to be "pits" that weaken a planet.</note> or dark degree, his fortune is diminished. His significations are damaged in all things that are of his nature and property, and small hardships and sorrows will happen to the native, and he will be <term>troubled<note>original: "balderus" — a difficult term likely meaning afflicted, sickly, or confused.</note></term>. And for any planet that is in a square, opposition, or conjunction with him while he is in this damaged state, it signifies loss in all things that are of the nature and property of that planet and of the house of the figure in which it has dominion in the birth and revolution. And if it is in a regal sign, the loss will be in kings; and if in a human sign, it will be from men. And if in an animal sign, the loss will be from the animal that corresponds to that sign. ¶ And if **Saturn** (♄) should make him unfortunate, it signifies losses and bad illnesses for old men and fathers, which are grave and difficult to heal, as well as imprisonment and want.

### ¶ Judgment of the Sun when it is the Lord of the Year.

When the **Sun** (☉) is the <term>Alcocoden<note>original: "alcecadeny" — The planet that acts as the "giver of years," determining the length of life and general fortune in a chart.</note></term>: in that year the judgment will be according to the state of the Lord of the <term>Sign<note>The zodiac sign.</note></term> in which the division of life by the <term>Hyleg<note>original: "hylech" — The planet considered the "Giver of Life" in a horoscope.</note></term> is found: whether the Sun itself is the Hyleg or another planet. And the planet that was in Leo in both the <term>natal chart<note>original: "radice" — The birth horoscope.</note></term> and the <term>revolution<note>The chart cast for the start of the year.</note></term> will be a partner with it in this division. Also consider the planet to which the Sun gives its power. And consider then where the Sun is located: and from that place you shall take testimony along with the other planet.

¶ And if the Lord of the Sign in which the division of life occurs gives its power to the Sun: and similarly if the planet that was in Leo in the birth chart and the revolution gives its power to the Sun: then the Sun’s power is fulfilled, and its lordship for that year is affirmed. Therefore, when it is in this condition and in a good state in its own <term>house<note>The zodiac sign a planet rules (for the Sun, this is Leo).</note></term> or its <term>exaltation<note>The sign where a planet is most powerful (for the Sun, this is Aries).</note></term>, or in any other sign suitable to it, and it is "received" <note>An astrological condition where planets are in each other's signs, indicating cooperation.</note> and above the earth and in an <term>angle<note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, which are the strongest areas of a chart.</note></term> of the <term>ascendant<note>The Eastern horizon.</note></term> or the <term>Midheaven<note>original: "medij celi" — The highest point of the chart, signifying career and public life.</note></term>: it signifies that the person will have dealings with kings and lords that year and will hold great and manifest dignity. He will increase in price, value, and riches, with a good reputation, sense, and intellect. It also signifies a good state for fathers and brothers of middle rank; and he will adhere to just men and men of the law, and he will do things for the sake of receiving a reward from God.

¶ And if the Sun is in the **seventh** or **fourth** house: it signifies profit for friends, and he will achieve what he desires and will rejoice on account of his children and even strangers; and he will involve himself in business and masteries. 

¶ And if it is in the **third** or **ninth** house: it signifies knowledge of the law and journeys from which he will gain utility and hope for a reward from God; he will rejoice because of his brothers and will have true dreams. 

¶ And if it is in the **second** or **eighth** house: it signifies that he will be accustomed to rest, with moderate labor; and he will have gains without searching and without toil; however, they will be small, and he will maintain his living in a strict manner.

¶ And if **Jupiter** (♃) looks upon it from a <term>trine<note>original: "tertio" — an aspect of 120 degrees.</note></term> or <term>sextile<note>An aspect of 60 degrees.</note></term>: or if **Venus** (♀) applies to it in a good state, specifically with Jupiter in both charts, his thoughts and intellect will be well-ordered, and his sense and understanding will grow. He will be certain in his thoughts for the most part and in his deeds, and his dreams will be true. 

¶ And if **Venus** (♀) is joined with it and she is <term>occidental<note>Setting after the Sun.</note></term> in a night revolution, or <term>oriental<note>Rising before the Sun.</note></term> in a day revolution, and has escaped the <term>rays<note>original: "radijs" — The "combust" zone near the sun where a planet's power is usually weakened.</note></term>: it signifies that he will receive things from kings and their sons that year in which he will rejoice. He will be of good fame and complete in his deeds and thoughts, and he will delight in the things of Venus <note>Such as love, art, or luxury.</note>.

¶ And if **Mercury** (☿) is joined with it in both charts, provided it is far from the Sun's rays whether in the east or the west: it signifies that he will have lordship that year over the society of men; he will grow in his character and wisdom, and he will be complete in his deeds and content with his status. He will profit in his possessions and rejoice over his servants and other Mercurial things <note>Such as commerce or writing.</note>.

¶ And if the **Moon** (☾) looks upon it in both charts from a sextile, trine, or <term>square<note>original: "quarto" — an aspect of 90 degrees.</note></term>: and both are in a good and fortunate state: it signifies an increase in the value of possessions and children, and that he will have honors and profits in diverse ways, and a good reputation in his deeds. 

¶ And if the Moon looks upon it from an **opposition**: he will have many adversaries and legal disputes, yet he will be the victor over his enemies.

<column-break/>

And if the Moon is joined with the Sun, yet escaped from its rays: it signifies an improvement in his state, and that he will involve himself in good deeds—both those done openly and those hidden—and though sorrows may happen to him, he will have a good end. And if the Moon is <term>under the rays<note>Combust, or very close to the Sun, usually a weakening position.</note></term> but in a good sign: it signifies that he will involve himself in bad habits and deceptions and persist in his business; however, he will escape from all this and come to a good end. And if any planet is in <term>cazimi<note>original: "taçimi" — literally "in the heart of the Sun," a position of extreme strength within 17 minutes of the Sun's center.</note></term> in a good and fortunate state: it signifies good and improvement according to its own nature and properties. But if it is in a bad state in these regards: it signifies loss.

¶ And when the **Sun** (☉) is the Lord of the Year and is in a bad state due to any downfall: either by falling from an angle, or by conjunction with the <term>Dragon's Tail<note>original: "cauda" — the South Node of the Moon, associated with loss or purging.</note></term>, or by an eclipse, or any other damaging thing: it signifies losses, hardships, and setbacks in all the things we previously said it signified. It signifies harm from kings and a bad state for one's father; fear, anxieties, a bad reputation, and bad journeys in which there is loss; illnesses of brothers and friends, hot sicknesses <note>Fevers or inflammatory conditions.</note>, pains of the eyes and head, imprisonment, and leaving one's land and place. And all these significations will be according to the nature of the house in which the Sun is located.

¶ And when any planet is joined with the Sun, or looks upon it while the Sun is in said bad state: it signifies loss and evil in the things belonging to the nature and signification of that planet. For if it is **Venus** (♀): there will be loss in marriage, and in perfumes, and in clothing and amusements. And if **Mercury** (☿): through writings, merchandise, and for one's living. And if the **Moon** (☾): there will be loss (instead of the improvement we mentioned) through legal disputes, illnesses, envy, the anger of a king, sadness of the mother and the household, through great fear, losses, and sorrows in various ways.

## Judgment of the Moon when she is Lady of the Year.

And when the Moon is the <term>Alcecadeni<note>original: "alcecadeni" — A Persian-derived term for the planet that governs the length of life or the specific year.</note></term>, the judgment that year shall be according to the state of the division in the revolution, and according to the state of the lord of the sign in which the division of the <term>hyleg<note>original: "hilech" — The planet that acts as the "giver of life" in the chart.</note></term> falls. The planet that was in the natal chart or the revolution in Cancer also participates in this significance, as does the planet to which the Moon <term>applies<note>Moves toward an aspect with another planet.</note></term> while she is in that sign of hers where she currently resides. And if in that same sign she applies to many planets, divide the year equally among those planets, giving to each planet its own portion of that year. You shall judge each part as good or bad according to the state of that planet to which the Moon applies, whether in fortune or misfortune. 

And if the Moon should be <term>void of course<note>original: "vacua cursu" — When the Moon makes no more major aspects before leaving her current sign.</note></term>, the significance of that year will belong to the lord of her house, whether he looks upon her or not; and mix the Moon with him similarly in that significance. And if the Moon is in a good state, fortunate and in a good house, it signifies goodness and improvement in things belonging to her property and significance. But if she is "damned," it signifies harm in those things: the illness of the mother and a bad state for the body. And if the Moon is northern, increasing in light and motion, it signifies power and improvement in her significations. But if she is in diverse states from these, it signifies harm and weakness. 

Look also to the sign of the Moon in the revolution, because the power of that sign is close to the power of the <term>ascendant<note>The sign rising on the eastern horizon.</note></term> of that year. But if she is unfortunate and not received, judge the contrary of this. And if she is void of course in that sign, take the judgment and significance from the lord of her house, and judge according to his property and nature, and according to the location of the houses in the figure. 

You shall judge good or evil thus: if Saturn is the lord of the house, it signifies good or harm to crops, and through lands, watery places, and old men. ### Chapter 4. On judgments concerning Firdaria.

<image-desc>Decorative drop cap 'S' within a rectangular frame featuring floral and leaf motifs.</image-desc>
->S<- Know that each of the seven planets has its own <term>Firdaria<note>A system of planetary periods used to divide a human life into blocks of years ruled by specific planets.</note></term>; and the <term>Head and Tail<note>original: "caput & cauda" — The North and South Nodes of the Moon.</note></term> likewise have their own Firdaria. And each of these Firdaria consists of fixed and known years. And that planet governs the native in those years of his life

<column-break/>

and gives him good or evil during that time. Therefore, the Firdaria of the Sun is ten years; the Firdaria of the Moon, nine; the Firdaria of Saturn, eleven; the Firdaria of Jupiter, twelve; the Firdaria of Mars, seven; the Firdaria of Venus, eight; and the Firdaria of Mercury, thirteen. The Firdaria of the Head is three years, and the Firdaria of the Tail is two years. And the sum of all these is 75 years. For in <term>diurnal births<note>Births occurring during the day.</note></term>, it begins from the Sun, wherever he may be in the figure; and afterward, the years of Venus follow, then the years of Mercury and the other planets, and so on according to the order of the heavens. However, in <term>nocturnal births<note>Births occurring at night.</note></term>, the Firdaria begins from the years of the Moon, and Saturn follows, then Jupiter, and so on according to the order of the heavens. Yet when any of these governs the native during the years of his Firdaria, he governs separately and signifies a seventh part of all the years of his Firdaria. And afterward, he has a partnership with another planet—each of these planets one after the other—and signifies good or evil with him; likewise, each of these in his seventh part of the years of that first planet’s Firdaria, beginning first from the planet whose Firdaria it is. He will have a partnership with him the first time, then the planet who is after him in the heaven, and then the rest who follow him. ¶ And according to this order, all the planets will have a partnership with him in his Firdaria in this manner. And this participation, in which one planet is associated with another in this judgment, is because these years of their Firdaria are drawn from the dignities they have in the 12 signs; for the 12 signs are their houses, and because of this, they have participation with one another in the governance or defense of these years. However, the Head and Tail govern their years separately, and this happens after the seven planets have completed their years. And this is after the native has completed 70 years; and they have no participation with any of the others, nor does any planet with them, because they have no houses in the signs. And these years given to them are drawn out through another method. Whence the native of a diurnal birth, from the hour he is born until the completion of 10 years, is in the Firdaria of the Sun. And he alone governs him for a seventh part of those 10 years; and afterward with the other planets, each in its seventh part. Whence, if the <term>root of the birth<note>The natal chart.</note></term> was good and had significations of the fortunes, the Sun signifies that in his division, the native will be excellently nourished with an honorable, royal upbringing; and his parents will have much good, except that in the first and second months, sadness and hardships will happen to the parents; yet he will remove that and return to happiness and joy. ¶ And if the Firdaria of the Sun occurs in his youth—and this can happen in nocturnal births—it signifies that he will have good from kings and nobles, and he will have praise and honor above his other kinsmen, and his possessions, riches, happiness, and joys will increase.
