### ¶ The Firdaria of Mercury

After the <term>firdaria<note>original: "fridaria" — A system of planetary periods where each planet rules a block of years in a person's life.</note></term> of Venus follows the firdaria of Mercury. It lasts 13 years and governs separately, signifying a seventh part of these years, which is one year, 10 months, 8 days, 13 hours, and fractions. This signifies that the <term>native<note>The person for whom the astrological chart is cast.</note></term> born in the first half of this division will have good, and in the other, evil and heaviness; he will travel from one land to another. And when he performs his works and deeds, loss will happen to him; and all his words and sayings will turn to his detriment. Some of his company or his beasts will die; he will fall ill and find little benefit from medicines and spices. And if, in this time, Saturn is in a bad state and aspects Mercury with a malicious <term>aspect<note>The geometric angle between two planets in the sky, believed to transmit influence.</note></term> and in an unfortunate house, he shall surely die. However, if Mercury is in a good state, these losses we have mentioned will decrease and things will improve. ¶ After this, the Moon divides a portion in the firdaria of Mercury for one year, 10 months, 8 days, 13 hours, and fractions. The total becomes three years, 8 months, 17 days, and 3 hours or thereabouts. This signifies that in this division he will be abundant in eating and drinking; he will expose himself to dangers and burdens. If he buys a male servant, he will flee, or likewise a female footman or servant. And if he begins to build a structure, he will not complete it. If he was married, his wife will die, or he will separate from her. And if he was not married and should take a spouse in this division, that marriage will not be completed, and he will fall ill with a powerful sickness; or perhaps he will fall from a height and run into great dangers of death. ¶ After this, Saturn has a part in the firdaria of Mercury for one year, 10 months, 8 days, 13 hours, and fractions. This total makes 5 years, 6 months, 15 days, and 17 hours or thereabouts. This signifies that in this division his substance <note>Wealth or property.</note> will increase, but he will not eat nor drink from it, nor do good to anyone. ¶ Afterward, it will be stolen from him by thieves; he will become poor and have few friends. His wife will die, and he will go from one land to another; hardships and labors will happen to him in his journeys. ¶ After this, Jupiter will have a part in the firdaria of Mercury for one year, 10 months, 8 days, 13 hours, and fractions. This total makes 7 years, 5 months, 4 days, and 7 hours or thereabouts. This signifies that in this division he will gain substance from diverse lands; he will associate with the likes of kings. Vile men will go against him and litigate against him, yet he will escape from them; he will gather gold and silver, and perhaps ascend to great dignity. He will build a noble building in which he will rejoice; he will love lies and liars, and make great expenses. ¶ Afterward, Mars divides a portion in the firdaria of Mercury for one year, 10 months, 8 days, 13 hours, and fractions. This total makes 9 years, 3 months, 12 days, and 20 hours or thereabouts. But if the Moon is in a good state, it signifies that in this division he will be healthy in body and of good manners; his parents will love and honor him and do good for him. ¶ And all the states of daytime births are different from the states of nighttime ones at the time we have mentioned. It is agreed that for a birth by day, the significations we have spoken of appear: because this <term>firdaria<note>A system of time-lords where specific planets rule certain years of a person's life.</note></term> comes to them after many years have passed. This is because their firdaria begins with the Sun. When they reach this point, they will be fit to hold the status of those significations we mentioned. However, the signification is different for those born by night, because their firdaria and its divisions begin with the Moon. At that time, the <term>native<note>The person born under this astrological chart.</note></term> is small and weak, as is his governance and status at the beginning; thus, he is not as fit to hold possessions as when he is an adult. For this reason, we have stated different significations for the Sun and Venus for those born by day compared to those born by night. 

If we wish to do the same for the Moon and Saturn—and speak of different significations and statuses for those born by day versus those born by night—for those born by day, the firdaria of the Sun begins, and it is the first part until the firdaria of Venus passes. Similarly, for one born at night, the firdaria begins from the Moon, and it is the first part until the firdaria of Saturn passes. You ought to consider the matters and statuses pertaining to that age of the native, whether young or old, and judge according to that. 

However, we shall speak of the significations and statuses of the other planets—Mercury, Jupiter, and Mars—in a single way.

### ¶ The Firdaria of Saturn.

After the Moon, Saturn governs its <term>firdaria<note>A system of "time-lords" where specific planets rule certain years of a person's life.</note></term> for 11 years, and it governs separately and signifies a seventh part of its years, which is 1 year, 6 months, 25 days, 17 hours, and fractions. It signifies that in this division he will perform deeds that will be imputed to him as folly; and he will have legal cases in which he will hold false arguments. He will be confronted on account of his daughters, if he has them, and he will have great sadness and anxieties for them. He will spend more than he earns; he will dissipate his property, and he will receive possessions from the inheritances of the dead or he will incur debt. He will involve himself in ancient matters, and a hindrance will happen to him regarding his value and worth. He will be sick with a great illness from which he will have sadness and anxiety. And if in this he is <term>ill-fortuned by Mars<note>Meaning Mars is in a difficult mathematical relationship to Saturn in the person's birth chart.</note></term>, the damage to him will be greater and stronger; and he will have loss through fire and heat or the strike of iron, or that which resembles it; and medicines or physical treatments will be of little use to him. And if the birth was by night, hardships and sadness will happen to him in many and diverse ways, or some of his relatives will die. He will receive possessions from the inheritances of the dead, and one part of his clothing will be stolen, and he will be sick with a powerful illness. He will do many deeds which will turn back on him for evil and loss, and he will do all his deeds foolishly, and for the most part, he will stand in vain. 
¶ Afterward, Jupiter will divide 1 year, 6 months, 25 days, 17 hours, and fractions within the firdaria of Saturn. And this total becomes 3 years, 1 month, 21 days, 10 hours or thereabouts. It signifies that in this division kings and their sons will honor him, and from them he will have profit of possessions and from other men, and he will change from one nobility to another. He will buy servants; he will have many delights and joys. He will fall ill; he will go on journeys, and perhaps that illness and journey will be at the end of that division. And if the birth was by night, things will happen to him from which he will have profit and perfection; and he will come to and associate with men of good character, from whom he will have good. He will fall ill, yet he will have good in another matter; and perhaps he will increase in servants, or he will take a wife if he is fit for this. 
¶ Afterward, Mars will divide 1 year, 6 months, 25 days, 17 hours, and fractions within the firdaria of Saturn. And this total becomes 4 years, 8 months, 17 days, 3 hours or thereabouts. It signifies that in this division he will be in a bad state, and hardships will come to him; and perhaps he will fall from the height of a house or from a beast; and because of this, he will have sadness and anxiety and a lawsuit with his wife and other women; and they will wish him evil, and men will overcome him and take advantage of him. His wife will fall ill with a powerful illness, or perhaps she will die. 
¶ Afterward, the Sun will divide one year, 6 months, 25 days, 17 hours, and fractions within the firdaria of Saturn. And this total becomes 6 years,

3 months, 12 days, 20 hours or thereabouts. He will be glad and rejoice in his house, society, and his sons. He will make journeys. And if the birth was by night, many of these significations and statuses we have mentioned will happen to him according to what is appropriate for his age.

It signifies that in this division he will have weakness in all his business. He will go on journeys in which he will have hardship and loss. His wife will fall ill and he will have hardships from this or on account of women; and some of his relatives will die. His possessions will increase, and he will lose something from them. He will rejoice in his brothers and friends; he will have good from his sons and their company and from servants. He will involve himself with beasts and with writing. His intellect and thoughts will ascend, and he will involve himself in society and diverse matters. 
¶ Afterward, the Moon has a part in the firdaria of Saturn for one year, 6 months, 25 days, 17 hours, and fractions: and this total becomes 11 years, and it is the completion of Saturn's firdaria. It signifies that in this partition he will have sadnesses; he himself or his male sons will fall ill, and some of them will die. He will be in a mediocre state between good and evil, profit and loss. He will go on long journeys in which he will profit in possessions; and perhaps in this partition he will be in a foreign place, or this will happen to him at the end of this partition; and when he departs from this partition he will gather great possessions and perhaps will be joined to another woman.

### ¶ The Firdaria of Jupiter.

<margin>Three... [shorthand notes]</margin>
After the firdaria of Saturn, Jupiter maintains his own firdaria, which is of 12 years. He maintains and signifies a seventh part of the years, which is one year, 8 months, 17 days, 3 hours or thereabouts. It signifies that in this division he will change from a low state to a good one; and he will depart from every hardship toward every good and joy. His fortune and possessions will ascend, and he will be named among kings; and good will be said of him; and he will have an honored and great dignity. And if Jupiter was in the <term>radix<note>The original birth chart.</note></term> in its own <term>term<note>A specific subdivision of a zodiac sign ruled by a planet.</note></term> or in the term of Venus or in any sign of its <term>triplicity<note>A group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element (Fire, in this case).</note></term>, which are Aries, Leo, and Sagittarius, then it signifies better in its significations and will signify greater good and fortune. And if the native was of high lineage, perhaps he will be a king or he will have power in cities and lands; and he will have many servants and his own possessions; or he will marry a noblewoman.

### ¶ Chapter 7: On the significations when certain planets occur in the revolutions in places where other planets were in the root.

<margin>Saturn on Saturn</margin>
When Saturn is in the revolution in the sign in which it was in the root: it signifies that he will move from one dignity to another. And if it falls in the revolution of the year in any of the angles <note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</note>: it signifies good and dignity, and the best of the angles in this is the Midheaven <note>original: "mediū celi"; the 10th house of career and public status</note>, because it signifies a kingdom or dominion. In the 7th, it signifies that he will have good from women regarding his affairs. And judge in the other houses according to this reasoning and according to what its power, weakness, fortune, or misfortune may be.

### Significations of Saturn.

<margin>Saturn on Jupiter</margin>
And when Saturn in the revolution comes to the place where Jupiter was in the root, and it is the lord of the ascendant in the root or revolution, or the lord of the Part of Fortune, or the lord of the place of the Sun in a day birth, or the place of the Moon in a night birth: it signifies a good state for the native and improvement in all things. ### Chapter 10. On the significations of the lord of the circle.

The specific one is that which is named according to the name of the house corresponding to it in signification: so that the Lord of the first hour is called the Lord of the Hour of the Ascendant: and the Lord of the 2nd is called the Lord of the Hour of the House of Substance: and that of the third is called the Lord of the Hour of the House of Brothers: and that of the 4th is called the Lord of the Hour of the House of Fathers: and thus all are named according to the significations of the houses. However, if the ruling planet is unfortunate, separated from the angles, and remote from receptions, it cannot have any good in its significations; and there will happen to the one whose revolution it is in that year an obstacle, depression, and misfortune in his affairs until the same planet enters a sign from which it may aspect its first place with an aspect of friendship; for when that happens, the Lord of the Revolution is fortified, and his affairs will be directed—the cause of livelihood and honor—and his fortune will appear. ¶ When the Lord of the Ascendant of the root of the birth was unfortunate, and afterwards in the revolution reaches the sign of the ascendant, and that same planet is the Lord and significator of that year, and aspects that sign of application in the revolution by square or opposition: it signifies to the native infirmities, pains, and sorrows of the nature of that sign and of the nature of that planet and the sign in which it is from which it looks upon its [own] sign. 
<margin>#</margin> ¶ When a planet in the root of birth applied to another planet making it fortunate and strengthening it, and in the revolution it is <term>void of course<note>original: "vacuus cursu"</note></term> and without the rays of others: it demonstrates what it had signified in the root and its power and fortune; neither does the void of course nor the fall in which it is in the revolution hinder it; unless the Moon is cadent in the root and revolution similarly and remote from benefics: for it signifies to the one whose revolution it is that he will be empty, slow, and lazy in his affairs that year. ¶ When the Lord of the <term>House of Substance<note>original: "domus substantie"; the Second House, governing money and assets.</note></term> in the revolution applies to the Lord of the Ascendant: he will have substance easily and without labor. <margin>#</margin> And if the Lord of the Ascendant applies to the Lord of the House of Substance: he will labor for substance and seek it. And if the Lord of the House of Substance is <term>separated<note>Moving away from an aspect rather than toward it.</note></term> from the Lord of the Ascendant: he will not gain substance. And if the Lord of the Ascendant is separated from the Lord of the House of Substance: he will not concern himself with procuring substance.

### ¶ Chapter 14. On knowing the state of the father through the birth of the son.

### ¶ Chapter 15. On dividing days and months.

<image-desc>Decorative woodcut initial Q containing stylized foliage within a double-lined square border.</image-desc>
When you wish to know the beginning of any month from the months of the revolution: look at how many complete months have passed: and enter that number into the table in the rule of months, and take what you find across from it in the table of days, hours, and fractions: and add what you find to the days, hours, and fractions of the hour of the root of the birth, or of the revolution of his year—namely, that which you wish to begin. And from all that results from this: make <term>Latin months<note>original: "menses latinos"; referring to the solar calendar months (January, February, etc.) used in the Western tradition.</note></term>: because the root of the revolutions is with them: and begin from that month in which the birth or the revolution occurred—namely, from that one from which you began—and cast out the completed months. And look at what remains to you of the days: hours and fractions: for in that many days of the Latin month will be the revolution of the month you sought. And count through the order of the <term>signs<note>The signs of the Zodiac.</note></term> from the <term>application<note>When planets or points move toward one another in the chart.</note></term> of that year and from any <term>Hylech<note>original: "hylech"; a Persian/Arabic term for the "giver of life," a planet or point that determines the vitality and lifespan.</note></term>: and give to each completed month one sign. And the Hylechs are: the Ascendant, the Sun, the Moon, the Part of Fortune, and the <term>Midheaven<note>original: "medium celi"; the highest point in the sky at the time of the chart.</note></term>. Therefore, the sign to which the number arrives will be the governor of that month, starting from any of those places: and according to the state of that sign, you shall judge in that month in each of the said matters: and this is the table.

¶ And other wise men divided the year into 12 months according to the motion of the sun: and they placed the beginning of each month in as many degrees as the sun was in its sign in the <term>root<note>original: "radice"; the natal or birth chart.</note></term>. ¶ And other wise men said: look at how far it is from the sun to the moon on any given day: and how much it was, subtract it from the ascendant of the birth: and set this down like the <term>Part of Fortune<note>An Arabic part or mathematical point in a chart representing prosperity and well-being.</note></term>, and by that same thing you shall judge on that day. ¶ Others said: look at the places of the planets in the hour of birth and the <term>revolution<note>original: "reuolutiōis"; the solar return chart for the current year.</note></term> and give [it] to the planet which strengthens in the degree of the ascendant or in the degree of the sign of profection according to the motion of the sun on whatever day until it applies to another planet or to its rays: and in others you shall do that same thing according to this. ¶ Other ancient wise men said regarding the revolution of years: you should begin in the revolution of the year to know the root of the birth: and from the root you shall know the work of the person born and his being and value and the increase and decrease of his <term>worth<note>original: "preciʐ"; likely "pretii" meaning value or status.</note></term> and health in the times of his life.
<margin>his [life]</margin>
You shall know from the planets that are the <term>lords of the triplicities<note>Planets that rule over the three signs belonging to a specific element (Fire, Earth, Air, Water).</note></term> about the age in which that person born is: for these have a great and rooted significance in nobility and lowliness, greater than what might appear to them in the revolution: nevertheless, the significations of the revolutions adapt and improve the state or ruin it according to what the places of the planets were in the root. However, the birth which signified in its root a great height and high status: when in the revolution it has significations concordant in this: they increase and augment it. And when it has significations there contrary to that: they do not ruin it much, except that they diminish it somewhat in substance: or his being will be empty: or he will go outside of his place: or he will not work at his task in that year: yet in nobility and rank he is not diminished much, provided the root was firm. Likewise, births which did not signify height in the root, nor nobility, do not much improve the signification of the revolution, even if they were good, except that they increase somewhat in that which they signified in the root: and evil significations in the revolution ruin much there when they were not good in the root: wherefore when you have well considered these things and adapted them subtly, you should track them by the <term>athaçir<note>original: "athaçir"; an Arabic-derived term (at-tasyīr) referring to the "distribution" or "direction" of points in the chart over time.</note></term>, that is, the hyleg: just as I told you in the beginning: and as it is explained in our tables which are named the "Tables for Dissolving Knots and Explaining Aspects": and when they apply to the <term>fortunes<note>Benefic planets like Jupiter and Venus.</note></term> and their rays: they signify improvement in those matters. And when they apply to the <term>infortunes<note>Malefic planets like Saturn and Mars.</note></term> and their rays: they signify loss and hindrance in those matters: especially if the rays be from <term>squares<note>original: "quartis"; an astrological aspect of 90 degrees, often considered challenging.</note></term> or oppositions. And know that the <term>trines<note>An aspect of 120 degrees.</note></term> and <term>sextiles<note>An aspect of 60 degrees.</note></term> of the infortunes show less damage: and they increase much in good and fortune for the fortunes. And when you have looked well at all that we have told you and have looked at the natures and times of the years and the ordinations of births and revolutions and the applications of the planets and their rays: you shall judge the good and evil in that matter and in any year according to what you have found: and you shall be certain, with God’s help.

### ¶ Here begins the seventh part of the Complete Book on the Judgments of the Stars regarding Elections, which Hali Abenragel made: and there are 103 chapters in this part.

#### ¶ Prologue to the book.

<margin>Election</margin>
<image-desc>A large historiated woodcut initial letter 'D' showing a bearded face in profile, integrated into ornate acanthus-leaf and scrollwork designs.</image-desc>
**D**id Hali Abenragel the son say: praised be God and thanks be given, because He is the Lord of good, of bounty, of wisdoms, and of sciences: He Himself is the Maker and Creator of all things through His will, and they are maintained by His governance: He Himself is the beginning of all things and the changer of times: by His power He erected the heavens and established them: He pressed down the earth and situated it: He created all creatures and knew all secrets: He created things and gave them an end: and afterward He created them again. May He be praised and blessed as befits His great nobility and height.

#### ¶ Author’s Prologue

**I**n this book I have gathered all the elections of the stars and the beginnings of things: and I have joined and established them as best as I could and as my sense reached: know that the ancient wise men disagreed in the reasoning of elections: for there are some of them who affirm them and their effects: and there is one part of them that denies and condemns them and their effects and judgments. And I have already divided and explained these disagreements and others in the beginning of this book, namely, in the first part on questions: and in this I have spoken as best as I knew: and I wish to say in this place that which I believe concerning their sayings, and that which is truthful and sound: and here I begin with the help of God.

<margin>perfections</margin>
**C**oncerning elections: Some are effective <note>original: "pfectuose"; meaning they achieve their intended goal.</note> with the help of God without any doubt: and their perfection and their good are manifest. And others are those that do not appear [effective], nor do their significations receive perfection: For example, if some man had in his birth manifest, truthful, and firm significations that he would not have a son: or if he should have one, he would not live, nor be nourished: because he had the <term>house<note>The 5th House of the zodiac, which governs children.</note></term> and the significators of sons ruined: or they have in the birth the house and significators of marriage ruined: such as if Venus and other significators were <term>combust<note>Too close to the sun, weakening the planet's power.</note></term>: or in their <term>falls<note>A position in the zodiac where a planet is at its weakest.</note></term>: or in bad places remote from the aspects of the significator of the native: or because the
<margin>perfection</margin>
infortunes rule in the house of Venus in the root of the birth and the significators of that house, damaging the significator of the native: and so if any of these was ruined in the root of the birth—namely, concerning sons, marriage, or a journey—if you wish to look for an election for making a son, or an hour for marriage, or for making a journey, perfection will not appear in this election: because an election is not of such power that it is able to pull back or remove that which the planets signified in the root of the birth: and you should understand the contrary of this in good and fortune. Nevertheless, elections appear and help themselves for those who have significations of them in the birth.

<meta>This page continues the introduction to Book 7 of Albohazen Haly Abenragel’s work on "elections"—the art of choosing the most auspicious astrological moment to begin an undertaking. <margin>common</margin>
¶ It is possible for them to be mediators, that is, significators that are either <term>common<note>original: "communerales"; points or planets that are neutral or mediocre in their influence.</note></term> or good. For if the <term>election<note>original: "electio"; the practice of choosing a specific time to act based on the stars.</note></term> is good, and the significators of the <term>root<note>original: "radicis"; the natal or birth chart.</note></term> are mediocre or not greatly afflicted, the election directs and draws this toward a good outcome. And if the significators are good, a good election confirms that good and it grows, raising it to a great degree; for the goodness of the election aids the significators of the root. Indeed, if the significators in the root are good and powerful, they signify good things. Similarly, if the election is powerful, good, and fortunate, that matter grows, is made powerful and affirmed, and fortune and every good appear in it more than might be expected. And following this path and opinion, there is but one way in elections; this is confirmed by the saying of **Ptolemy**, who said in the sixth word of his *Book of 100 Sayings*: "One can help oneself through elections when the power of the rising time is strong and aids two powers; yet if it is remote from them, nothing of the election appears, even if it is gathered from good significations." This is what I hold to be true, what I agree with, and according to which I work.

I caution you not to make an election for someone whose <term>nativity<note>original: "nativitatem"; the birth chart.</note></term> you do not know. For when you make an election for someone whose nativity and <term>annual revolution<note>original: "reuolutionem anni"; the solar return chart for the current year.</note></term> you know, it will be good and advantageous for them by the grace of God. ¶ But when you make an election for someone whose nativity and annual revolution you do not know—or at least if you do not have the <term>ascendant<note>The zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of the inquiry.</note></term> of their <term>question<note>original: "questionis"; in horary astrology, a chart cast for the moment a question is asked.</note></term>—you may be in danger because of this. For you might quickly choose an ascendant that is an enemy or contrary to the root of their birth, such as giving them the twelfth, eighth, or sixth house of their root <note>These houses in astrology are traditionally associated with enmity, death, and illness.</note>. Thus their enemies will be strengthened, and perhaps it will destroy or kill them, or perhaps you will stir up loss and evil for them, and the <term>fortunes<note>original: "fortune"; benefic planets like Jupiter or Venus.</note></term> you gathered for them will not be able to hold it back. Or perhaps those fortunes will be enemies and contrary to their root, or they will be masters of evil and damaging places. Or perhaps that <term>infortune<note>original: "infortuna"; a malefic planet like Mars or Saturn.</note></term> which you caused to fall and weakened in your election was, unbeknownst to you, the significator and ruler in their root.

¶ Likewise, beware of making elections for evil people or enemies unless you know their birth. You see this clearly with those who travel by sea or land: they all depart, or go out on the same day, and arrive at the city to which they go at the same hour. Yet some of them return quickly with profit, good status, and good fortune; some are delayed; some return sick; some gain nothing and have no utility from that journey; some lose what they held; and some lose themselves and are destroyed on that journey. ¶ Likewise for those who enter a ship at the same hour: some perhaps will drown, while others escape; and perhaps all will arrive at the place to which they go at the same hour, and some of them return to their city and home with profit and good, while others return without profit, and others lose so much that they never return to their home. This happens only because of the discordance of their births; the departure they made on the same day and hour does not benefit them all equally. ¶ Similarly, a person may begin a journey on an ill-fortuned and evil day, yet be delivered and gain profit. And someone who goes out on a chosen, fortunate, and good day may be hindered and lose. This happens only through the discordances of their births. And there are some for whom the fortunes

<column-break/>

bring good and utility, and the infortunes bring evil and loss. And others for whom the infortunes bring good and utility, and the fortunes bring evil and loss. All this happens through the will and power of the High God—blessed be He.

¶ Know that God, whose names are blessed, created all creatures and made them all from the four natures <note>The four elements: fire, air, earth, and water.</note>. And all is the same on earth and in the world regarding generation and corruption: the rational and the mute, the mobile and the fixed. He caused them to be joined to the heavens and set for them causes and subtle proportions which the wise of this science understand and know. Other naturalists and prudent, noble philosophers know the cause and subtle proportion He placed between the magnet and iron, between father and son, and between the lover and the beloved; from which you should understand and set your mind to this. And know that through the concordance and agreement between two properties—the high and the low—things are tempered and directed; and through discordance and disagreement between these two properties, things are damaged and destroyed.

¶ Know that the fortunes are of temperate natures and good complexions, while the infortunes are of wicked and fraudulent complexions. And although they may receive [influence], they are not secured from their evil properties and fraudulent natures, for they are like thieves and evil men. ¶ Know that the books of elections are many. Among them, the ancient books are the books of **Dorotheus** and **Vettius Valens** <note>original: "uellij"; Vettius Valens was a 2nd-century astrologer.</note> and others whom we have already named when we spoke of the disagreements of the wise in the first part of this book. Each of the Moorish wise men followed and loved one path of the ancients and abhorred another, according to his own intellect and knowledge in what appeared to him true and right, while setting aside the rest. And I am one of those who have done so, because I proceeded by the path that seemed to me to be true and sound, and I set aside the others. For I looked into the elections of all of them, and from their sayings, I took what seemed to me to be true and right, and what I saw could be verified through reason or experience. Those who took it upon themselves to write books of elections are **Messahala**, **Abimegech**, **Theophilus son of Thomas**, **Al-Hayat**, and **Al-Kindi**. These were the greatest among them, who spoke best and distinguished things most clearly. And **Abu'ayash**, **Zael**, **Benbiz**, **Albumasar**, **Haly son of Ahmad**, **Benbizany**, and **Alobaz son of Zaet** did not speak as well as the others. Nevertheless, I took the best reasons from each of them and joined to them what seemed to me true and right; and I pray to God that He directs me in the path of truth.

### Chapter 2: On the Beginnings of Deeds.

<image-desc>Ornamental woodcut initial 'C' featuring scrolling foliage within a double-line square border.</image-desc>
It is proper in the beginnings of deeds to adapt the Ascendant and its lord to fortune. And it is a "fortune" when the Ascendant is of the nature of the <insert>matter</insert> and suitable to the thing in quality and reason. "Quality" is like what we choose for journeys that we want to be completed quickly and have light movements: [we use] <term>fiery signs<note>Aries, Leo, and Sagittarius.</note></term> when we seek reasons or honor from a king. "Reason" is like what we choose in lawsuits using the signs of Mars. It is necessary that you adapt the place of the house, the lord of the matter, and the lord of the lord of the matter; because the place of the matter signifies that which will be at the beginning of the matter, the lord of the matter signifies the middle, and the lord of the lord of the matter signifies the end of the matter. <margin>Note</margin> ¶ Similarly, the Ascendant signifies the beginning of the person to whom the matter belongs, the lord of the Ascendant the middle, and the lord of the lord of the Ascendant signifies the end for that person. ¶ Similarly, look to the Part of Fortune and its lord, and to the lord of its lord; for if you can improve and fortify all of them, it is the completion [of the election]. You fortify them by placing fortunes in them by aspect or application, and by suitability of natures; and from these places you should cast out the ill-fortunes. ¶ Beware lest the lord of the Ascendant be <term>retrograde<note>When a planet appears to move backward in the sky, usually signaling delays or reversals.</note></term>, for its retrogradation signifies impediment, prohibition, and 

<column-break/>

slowness in matters. Even if all the significators are good and signify the success of the matter, so long as the lord of the Ascendant is retrograde, there will first be distrust in the matter and slowness, and it will not be completed except with labor. ¶ Beware lest the <term>Tail<note>original: "cauda"; the South Node of the Moon, traditionally considered a point of depletion or misfortune.</note></term> be with either of the <term>luminaries<note>The Sun and the Moon.</note></term> when they are in conjunction or opposition, or that the luminaries themselves are not in conjunction or opposition [at the start]. And beware lest the Tail be in the Ascendant, nor in the place of the matter, nor with the Part of the matter; because it ruins things through worthlessness, mismanagement, and labor. And it is of little use to place a fortune in the Ascendant, or in the place of the matter, or in the angles [if the Tail is there]. ¶ Know that the <term>Greater Fortune<note>Jupiter.</note></term> is powerful in all things and in all matters we wish to improve; and the <term>Lesser Fortune<note>Venus.</note></term> is powerful in all causes of games, joys, vices, adornments, friendships, and the like. ¶ In all things, beware of placing the Moon in the Ascendant, for she is an enemy to the Ascendant; the Sun, however, is not contrary to the Ascendant, yet he disrupts matters and scatters them, dissolving what has been settled. ¶ Guard yourself as much as you can so that the ill-fortunes are not in the Ascendant, nor in any of the angles. Especially if they are the lords of "bad places"; for when an ill-fortune is the lady of the eighth house, it signifies ruin through death and the helpers of adversaries, and through great imprisonments. ¶ And when it is the lady of the sixth house, it signifies harm from enemies, servants, illnesses, loss of limbs, short imprisonments, and four-footed beasts. ¶ And when it is the lady of the twelfth house, it signifies harm from labors, distrust of enemies, and moderate imprisonments. ¶ And when it is the lady of the second house, it signifies the occasion through which you have help or a helper, or through eating and drinking; therefore guard yourself as much as you can. ¶ Procure that in the day the Ascendant is from the diurnal signs, and in the night from the nocturnal signs; and that it be from signs that ascend directly, not from <term>crooked signs<note>original: "tortuosis"; signs that take less time to rise over the horizon (in the northern hemisphere, Capricorn through Gemini), often associated with difficulty.</note></term>; and if you can, that the luminaries be in similar signs, and that they be the lords of the hours of the aforementioned places; thus we predict them to be powerful. ¶ And power is divided into two parts: one natural, and the other accidental. "Natural" is when a planet appears outside the [Sun's] rays, is oriental, and in its own house, exaltation, term, triplicity, or face, and is northern in the motion of its latitude, and is direct or directing itself. "Accidental" power is when it is fortunate through a fortune applied by conjunction, or by a trine, square, opposition, or sextile aspect, and that it be safe and clear from ill-fortunes in all aspects. ¶ One group of the wise say that to ensure a fortunate end to a matter, five things must be inspected: first, the lord of the fourth house; second, the lord of the Moon's house; third, the last planet toward which the Moon goes in the sign in which she is; fourth, the lord of the house of the Part of Fortune; fifth, the fourth sign [from the Ascendant] and the sign in which the Moon is. ¶ Others say that they similarly look to the lord of the fourth sign from the place where the Part of Fortune is located. ¶ <term>Masha'allah<note>original: "Messehala"; an influential 8th-century Persian Jewish astrologer and astronomer.</note></term> and his associates say that the Moon in the Ascendant is bad and to be dreaded, and <term>Al-Kindi<note>original: "alkindus"; a 9th-century Arab philosopher and astrologer.</note></term> says the same; they say this because she is cold and moist, while the Ascendant is hot, and they do not agree. But <term>Albumasar<note>original: "albumasar"; a 9th-century Persian astrologer, often cited as one of the greatest of the Middle Ages.</note></term> does not dread the Moon in the Ascendant; it seems he adheres to the saying of <term>Ptolemy<note>The 2nd-century Greco-Egyptian polymath whose works formed the basis of medieval astrology.</note></term> that she is hot and moist, and therefore does not hold her as contrary to the Ascendant. But I say that she is bad and to be dreaded there, and I do not agree with the statement of Albumasar; for he contradicts his own words when speaking of the <term>Hyleg<note>original: "hylech"; the planet or point that acts as the giver of life in a chart.</note></term> and the "cutter" of life, where he says the Moon cuts...

¶ Know that the thing which greatly increases the luck of beginnings and improves it with a grand improvement and great fortune—likewise in a <term>nativity<note>A birth chart.</note></term> and in all <term>elections<note>The practice of choosing an auspicious time to start a project.</note></term>—is that the place of the conjunction at the hour of the conjunction (if the beginning was conjunctional), or the place of the opposition at the hour of the opposition (if the beginning was oppositional), should be safe from ill-fortunes and damages, and be fortunate; and likewise the lord of the sign of the conjunction, or the lord of the sign of the opposition.

¶ And know that the sign of the opposition is the sign of the <term>luminary<note>The Sun or the Moon.</note></term> which was above the earth. And if one luminary is in the angle of the east and the other in the angle of the west, the place will be for the one <gloss>that is</gloss> in the east.

¶ When the Moon separates from a conjunction or opposition and goes toward an ill-fortune, be careful in all beginnings, because all starts that are of this sort are bad and to be abhorred; for if the place of the conjunction or opposition was unfortunate, it signifies that the beginning of the matter will be bad.

¶ When the Moon separates from the conjunction or opposition of the Sun and goes toward an ill-fortune, it signifies that the end of that beginning will be bad and abhorrent.

¶ Conversely, when the place of conjunction or opposition is good and fortunate, and the Moon, in separating herself from it, joins with ill-fortunes, it signifies that the beginning of that matter will be good and its end bad. And when the place of conjunction and opposition is unfortunate, and the Moon, in separating herself from there, joins with <term>fortunes<note>original: "fortunis"; the "benefic" planets, Jupiter or Venus, which bring success.</note></term>, it signifies that the beginning of that matter will be bad and the end good.

¶ And when the place of conjunction or <term>prevention<note>original: "preuentionis"; a term for the Full Moon or the opposition of the Sun and Moon.</note></term> is fortunate, and the Moon, in separating, joins with a fortune, it signifies that the beginning and the end will both be fortunate.

¶ And when an ill-fortune is in the place of conjunction or prevention, and the Moon, in separating from there, joins with an ill-fortune, it signifies that the beginning and end of the matter will be bad and abhorrent.

¶ And when the conjunction or <term>puncture<note>original: "pūctio"; refers to the exact point or moment of the planetary alignment.</note></term> or its lord is in a <term>succedent house<note>Houses 2, 5, 8, and 11, which "follow" the powerful corner houses or "angles." They represent stability and middle-stages.</note></term>, it signifies that the good and improvement which appears in that matter will be at its end and its completion.

¶ And if the conjunction or opposition is <term>cadent<note>original: "cadens"; falling away from an angle, traditionally considered a weak or ineffective position for a planet.</note></term> from the angle of the ascendant—this is said regarding the ascendant of the beginning of that matter, or of an election or nativity—it signifies that the matter will be ruined and will have no good; and this is the saying of <term>Alkindi<note>Yaʿqūb ibn Isḥāq al-Kindī (c. 801–873), an influential Arab philosopher and astrologer.</note></term>, and I confirm it.

¶ And you should strive in all beginnings to improve the place of the conjunction or prevention that occurred before the beginning, and likewise the lord of the house of that conjunction or prevention.

¶ Know that the lord of the house of conjunction or prevention is more specific than the lord of the quarters of the year, and the lord of the quarter of the year is more specific than the lord of the year. And if you can improve all these, it will be better and firmer.

¶ <term>Albumasar<note>Abū Maʿshar (787–886), one of the most famous Persian astrologers of the Middle Ages.</note></term> said that when the lord of the election is the lord of the sign of the luminaries

And if at the hour of the start they are in a different state, they signify evil.

¶ <term>Alaqmin<note>Possibly Al-Qabisi (Alcabitius), a 10th-century authority on judicial astrology.</note></term> said that when the luminaries aspect each other with a good aspect, they signify good and improvement in every matter begun, and especially when the Moon is in the beginning of her joy—that is to say, when she is in the sign in which the <term>Head<note>original: "caput"; the North Node of the Moon, traditionally considered a point of increase and luck.</note></term> is.

¶ When the Moon is below the earth by day, and above the earth by night, the power and goodness of the ascendant increases.

¶ And when you have a hurried election, and do not have time to improve the Moon, place <term>Jupiter</term> or <term>Venus</term> in the ascendant or Midheaven, because they cause great improvement in the matter.

¶ The ancient sages say that this can be in things that are not meant for lasting and remaining for a long time; however, in things which they wish to last and remain for a long time, such as marriage or building and things similar to these, it is necessary to improve the Moon; and when she is ruined, you should strive to place her in a place falling from an angle and a succedent; and if you cannot do this, at least [keep her] from the angles; and especially [ensure] that the Moon does not aspect the ascendant, nor its lord, nor the lord of the house of the matter, nor its lord, nor the planet signifying that matter by its nature and property. And if you cannot withdraw her from all these places, withdraw her from as many of them as you can.

And if it receives the Moon from the ascendant, it will likewise be better. ¶ Take care that the significators are not applying to ill-fortunes by **opposition** or **quartile** <note>An aspect of 90 degrees, considered a "hard" or stressful relationship between planets.</note>; however, if the application is by **trine** <note>An aspect of 120 degrees, considered very harmonious.</note> or **sextile** <note>original: "fertili" (fertile); an aspect of 60 degrees, considered helpful.</note>, it is not evil, especially if it occurs with **reception** <note>A condition where one planet is in the sign ruled by the other, facilitating cooperation.</note>. ¶ **Masha'allah** <note>A leading 8th-century Persian Jewish astrologer and astronomer.</note> says that the aspects of ill-fortunes from a trine or sextile are good and fortunate; in which I do not agree with him. Rather, I say that such aspects neither fortify nor weaken, nor do they prohibit their own evil and damage. ¶ And it is appropriate that you beware the **conjunction** of the **Sun**, because it is very evil and damnable. ¶ And I do not agree with those who say that ***tasim*** <note>original: "tasim," likely a corruption of the Arabic "cazimi," meaning "in the heart of the Sun." Most astrologers consider this a position of great strength, but the author disagrees.</note> is good; rather, I say it is worse and of greater damage. ¶ Likewise, beware of its quartile and opposition; and if there is reception in this, the evil and damage will be less. ¶ And take care that the ascendant is not the sign in which there was an ill-fortune, or which was made unfortunate in the **revolution of the year** <note>A chart cast for the moment the Sun returns to its birth position, used to predict the year's events.</note>. Similarly, it is abhorrent for the **angles** <note>The four most powerful points in a chart: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses.</note> to be falling <note>original: "cadentes"; planets in these houses are considered weak and unable to act effectively.</note>; for example, when the sign of the 10th house from the ascendant comes by calculation into the 11th through the equalization of the houses <note>A technical error in house division where a powerful house "slips" into a weaker one.</note>. These he calls **retrograde**; however, if they are far off and moving forward, it is good and complete—just as when the 10th house comes into the 11th by calculation, it is called an **advancement**. ¶ And take care that the Lord of the Ascendant, or the planet to which the Moon joins, is not **occidental** <note>Setting in the west after the Sun; planets in this position are traditionally seen as losing their strength.</note>, for such a planet is like one who is half-exhausted. ¶ **Hermes** <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary founder of astrology and alchemy.</note> says in the *Book of Lengths* that the ascendant and the **Midheaven** <note>The highest point in the sky; the 10th house.</note>, and those who are in them, are like youths; the 7th house is like a preceding old man, and the 4th house is like an old man. And he says there that the planet gives, and it holds by the hand that which grows in that gift. ¶ The **Sun** in the ascendant is to be abhorred unless it is in **Leo** or **Aries**; and in the ascendant with **Saturn**, it ruins matters and does not permit them to be completed except with great pain and labor; and in journeys by sea, they are certainly to be abhorred in the ascendant. ¶ **Saturn** with the **Moon** in the ascendant signifies anxieties, great infirmity, death, and damage coming from the king, the loss of substance, and the destruction of kinsfolk and society; and it signifies a journey that is not long. ¶ If **Jupiter** is in the ascendant with the **Sun**, it signifies sadness, anxieties, a little good, and changing from one place to another. ¶ And if it is in the ascendant with the **Moon**, it signifies many waters, and youths, concubines, marriage, and honor. ¶ If **Mars** is in the ascendant with the **Sun**, it signifies sadness, anxiety, and pains on the part of ene-

<column-break/>

<margin>2 ra</margin>

-mies; and little perfection on the part of friends; and loss and sudden death by iron or fire. ¶ And if it is in the ascendant with the **Moon**, it signifies the strife of kinsfolk, because it signifies victory and power through fraud and betrayal. ¶ When **Venus** is in the ascendant with the **Sun**, it signifies laziness, happiness, and seeking vain trusts, and accusations of friends and kinsfolk. ¶ And if **Venus** is in the ascendant with the **Moon**, it signifies health of the body, improvement, and utility from women, except that in this there will be shameful and suspicious deeds. ¶ If the **Moon** is in slow motion, similar to the motion of **Saturn**, it signifies pains. ¶ And if **Mercury** is in the ascendant with the **Sun**, it signifies sadness. ¶ And if it is in the ascendant with the **Moon**, it signifies many good works, except that it signifies discord between kinsfolk and friends. ¶ If the **Moon** is in the ascendant with the **Sun**, it signifies burdens, distrust, spending and destroying, and pain in the eyes. ¶ Beware of **moveable signs** <note>Aries, Cancer, Libra, and Capricorn; signs that mark the start of seasons and signify change.</note> in any matter which you wish to be firm and lasting. Similarly, beware of **fixed signs** <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, and Aquarius; signs that signify stability and endurance.</note> in matters which you wish to be light and which you wish to pass quickly. Likewise, beware of **signs of direct ascension** <note>Signs that take longer to rise over the horizon (Cancer through Sagittarius in the northern hemisphere), associated with slow-moving but stable events.</note> in matters which you do not wish to be lasting and which should pass quickly. Likewise, beware of **tortuous signs** <note>Signs of short ascension (Capricorn through Gemini), which rise quickly and can signify difficulty or sudden change.</note> in matters which you wish to arrive directly and equally, for these signs are hard in all deeds and all actions.

Afterward, when you wish to begin any work, improve the Ascendant, its Lord, the Moon, and the Lord of its house, guarding yourself from the bad states of the Moon, as **Dorotheus** <note>Dorotheus of Sidon, a 1st-century astrologer whose work was foundational for medieval practice.</note> and other wise men said in all beginnings

however, when she is after the Sun, it is of less evil. ¶ The second is when she is in the degree of her **fall** <note>The sign where a planet's influence is at its weakest; for the Moon, this is Scorpio.</note>. ¶ The third is when she is in opposition to the Sun <note>The Full Moon.</note>. ¶ The fourth is when she is joined to the **ill-fortunes** <note>The "malefic" planets, Mars and Saturn.</note> bodily, or by a square or opposition aspect. ¶ The fifth is when she is within 12 degrees of the **Head or Tail** <note>The North and South Nodes of the Moon, the points where eclipses occur.</note>, which is the limit of an eclipse. ¶ The sixth is when she is in the final degrees of the signs, which are the **terms** <note>A specific subdivision of a zodiac sign ruled by a particular planet.</note> of the ill-fortunes. ¶ The seventh is when she is **falling from the angles** <note>Located in the "cadent" houses (3, 6, 9, or 12), where a planet's power is diminished.</note>, or when she is in the **Burned Way** <note>original: *via combusta*; a traditionally unlucky section of the zodiac stretching from the end of Libra to the start of Scorpio.</note>, and this is worse than all the ill-fortunes of the Moon, especially in marriages and all causes of women, and in buying and selling, and in journeys. ¶ The eighth is when the **duodenaria** <note>A twelfth-part division of a sign, used for more specific detail.</note> of the Moon is with the ill-fortunes, or when she is contrary to her own house, or when she does not behold her house with any aspect. ¶ The ninth is when she is of slow motion, which the wise call the "**motion of Saturn**," and it is when she moves 12 degrees or less in one day and night. ¶ The tenth is what **Masha'allah** <note>A famous 8th-century Persian Jewish astrologer and astronomer.</note> and others after him said: when she is **void of course** <term>A period when the Moon makes no further major aspects before leaving its current zodiac sign, signaling a time when plans may come to nothing.</term>. ¶ Afterward, take care as much as you can to improve the Moon, and never place her in the Ascendant, because she is bad there and signifies pains and afflictions in the body; unless the Moon be greatly fortunated by a well-placed fortune and far from the ill-fortunes, then she is not bad in the Ascendant for buying and selling. And place the Moon and the Lord of the Ascendant beholding the Ascendant, because when a planet does not behold its own house, it is like a man in a place where he can do no good, nor remove harm from himself. And when a planet beholds its house, it is like a man being in his own house and guarding it; those inside fear him, and those outside similarly have fear of entering it. ¶ And if the Lord of the Ascendant should be an ill-fortune, place it beholding the Ascendant from a trine or sextile. And beware not to place the Lord of the Ascendant, nor the Lord of the Moon's house, when they are ill-fortunes, beholding the Moon from an angle; nor place them similarly in any of the angles even if they do not behold her. Nor place the **Part of Fortune** <note>A mathematical point in a chart representing prosperity.</note> falling in any beginning or deed, nor unremoved from the aspects or conjunction of the Moon; and do not care about the Lord of the Part, nor about its aspects to the Moon. ¶ And strive to place the Lord of the Ascendant with the Part, because it is a great improvement in affairs and multiplies its utility. And never place the Moon openly in the second, sixth, or twelfth house, because that constellation is to be abhorred. And always, in every beginning, place the Ascendant in a sign of **direct ascension**, because signs of direct ascension signify safety in matters when in the Ascendant; and the fourth house from the Ascendant and its Lord signify the end of that begun matter. ¶ Afterward, consider the fortunes and ill-fortunes, and how they stand in power and weakness. ¶ Dorotheus says: when you see the Moon afflicted and you have a hurried matter that you cannot delay, do not give the Moon any part in the Ascendant, but make her fall from it and its angles; and place a fortune in the Ascendant, and strengthen the Ascendant and its dominion as much as you can. And do not forget the **Lord of the Hour** in any election, because in elections it has manifest power and significance.

### ¶ Chapter four: On the first house and its elections.

The elections <note>In astrology, an "election" is the process of choosing the most auspicious time to begin an activity.</note> which I have placed in this house concern entering the bath, cutting hair, undergoing bloodletting, applying cupping glasses, and trimming the nails.

### ¶ Chapter five: On entering the bath.

The majority of wise astrologers say that the best choice for this is when one of the houses of **Mars** <note>Aries or Scorpio.</note> is rising, provided it is not applying to **Saturn** or **Venus**. If it is not in the houses of Mars, let it be in the houses of **Jupiter** <note>Sagittarius or Pisces.</note>, or in the house of the **Sun** <note>Leo.</note>, or in its own house; let it not be in any house of Venus or **Mercury**. However, I say that the best election that can be made for entering a bath is when the **Moon** is in the watery signs <note>Cancer, Scorpio, or Pisces.</note>. If it is in **Cancer**, let it apply to Jupiter; if in **Scorpio**, let it apply to Venus. He who wishes to stay a long time in the bath should place the Moon in Cancer applying to Jupiter by a trine <note>original: "de .3.", an aspect of 120 degrees.</note> or a sextile <note>original: "fertili," likely a transcription for "sextili," an aspect of 60 degrees.</note>, or to Venus; for an application to Venus signifies beauty for the one who enters the bath, and a clarity or increase of good appearance. For him who wishes to exit quickly, place the Moon in movable signs <note>Aries, Cancer, Libra, or Capricorn.</note>. Do not wish to enter the bath while the Moon is in hot and dry signs <note>The fire signs: Aries, Leo, and Sagittarius.</note> unless you are doing this to heal from excess moisture or paralysis; in that case, it is expedient that the Moon applies to the Sun or Mars by a trine or sextile. If you desire the bath to soften the body, choose signs and planets contrary to these. Furthermore, when you wish to scent your body with fragrant things, it is a good election for the Moon to be under the rays <note>Close to the Sun but not yet "combust" or overwhelmed by its light.</note>, separating from the Sun and applying to some "fortune" <term>A "fortune" or benefic planet, usually Jupiter or Venus, believed to bring positive results.</term>. If it is in any house of Jupiter, Mars, or the Sun, or in its own house, it will be good.

### ¶ Chapter six: On cutting the hair.

The best election for this is for the Moon to be in **Libra**, **Sagittarius**, **Aquarius**, or **Pisces**, applying to Jupiter or Venus. Venus is better in this matter because it signifies a greater perfection of the hair's composition, and it will grow back more slowly. If the Moon applies to Mars or Saturn, it is not good. Beware that no iron <note>Scissors or a razor.</note> touches your head when Mars is in the **Ascendant** <term>The zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon.</term> and the Moon is likewise there; nor when it applies to Saturn or Mars, especially from the "angles" <note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses of a chart.</note>. For an application to Saturn signifies that until that hair grows back, the person will have worrisome thoughts and sadness; an application to Mars signifies some accident with the iron or an error by the one cutting the hair.

### ¶ Chapter seven: On bloodletting and cupping.

The best that can be for this is that the Ascendant and the Moon are in air or fire signs, both being fortunate and "received" <note>A technical term where one planet is in a sign ruled by the planet it is aspecting.</note>, being in their own lights; and their lords similarly. And take care that you do not

<column-break/>

place or touch a limb with iron while the Moon is in the sign representing that limb <note>In medical astrology, each zodiac sign rules a body part (e.g., Aries rules the head, Taurus the throat).</note>, nor when the Lord of the Ascendant is in such a sign. If the "complexion" <note>The balance of bodily humors.</note> of the one you wish to bleed inclines toward the **Sanguine**, the air signs will be better for them; if they are **Choleric**, the water signs will be better; if they are **Phlegmatic**, the fire signs; and if **Melancholic**, the air signs. ¶ And beware that the Lord of the 8th house <note>The house associated with death and shared resources.</note> does not join with the Moon or the Lord of the Ascendant, nor with any of their lords, and that it is not in any of the angles. Ensure that the Lord of the Midheaven <note>The 10th house, representing the highest point in the sky.</note> is a "fortune" or that it aspects the Moon or the Lord of the Ascendant. Take care that neither the Moon nor the Lord of the Ascendant is in the 4th house. ¶ The difference between cupping <note>Drawing blood to the surface using suction cups.</note> and bloodletting from a vein is this: when you wish to extract blood with a cupping glass, it is good to do so after the opposition <note>The Full Moon.</note> in the last part of the month. If you extract from a vein, it is better in the first half of the month, looking in both cases for the good constellations and fortunes we have mentioned. ¶ I also say that they should not be bled when the Moon is in "common" signs <note>Mutable signs: Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, and Pisces.</note>, because it signifies that the bloodletter will strike him more than once, or that it will be necessary to bleed him again a short time later. Similarly, bloodletting is not good when the Moon is moving toward Mars by opposition or square; the opposition is worse, for it perhaps signifies that the vein will be severed or more blood will exit than should, such that they cannot hold it back. However, applications by trine or sextile are not bad. ¶ The application of the Moon to Saturn by body or by square or opposition is likewise to be dreaded, for it signifies that perhaps the blood will not flow, or it will perhaps congeal, or the vein will contract; or the phlebotomist <note>The person performing the bloodletting.</note> will have melancholy and bad thoughts. ¶ When the Moon is in **Aries** or **Libra** applying to Venus or Jupiter (or both), it signifies that the one being bled will have no fear or worry about the procedure; they will feel light because of it, it will be profitable, and the body will restore what was taken of the blood for a long time to come. It will not cause harm if they delay after the bleeding; the bad blood will exit the body and they will recover good blood. Similarly, if the Moon applies to Mars or the Lord of the Ascendant, it signifies that after the bleeding, "choler" <note>The yellow bile humor, associated with anger and heat.</note> will be stirred. If it applies to Saturn, "melancholy" will be stirred. If the Moon is "void of course" <note>Moving through a sign without making any further aspects to planets.</note>, "phlegm" will be stirred. Take care in venesection that the Moon is not in the Ascendant when the Ascendant is **Gemini**; and in cupping, that it is not in the Ascendant when the Ascendant is **Taurus**.

## Chapter 9: On the Second House and its Elections.

The elections <note>The practice of choosing an auspicious time to act.</note> which are in this house are: depositing wealth; seeking wealth and debts; buying and selling; selling produce; giving capital; receiving capital; moving from one house to another; and working in alchemy or concerning alchemy. I say to you that it is necessary to know that in all cases of wealth generally, and in everything that is within its power regarding merchandise and buying and selling, one must prepare the **second house** <note>The astrological "house of possessions."</note> and its Lord, as well as **Jupiter**, and the **Part of Fortune** <note>An Arabic Part or mathematical point in a chart representing prosperity.</note>. For in this, there is a great and fortified significance. However, in that which a man wishes to keep for himself, it is necessary that the **Ascendant** <note>The sign rising on the eastern horizon.</note> and the other angles be in **fixed signs** <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, and Aquarius; signs associated with stability.</note>, and that they are not in "remote angles" as we said before; rather, let the figure be upright, whichever house is its sign. And in things that a man wants for buying, selling, and for trade, look for the opposite of all this, while improving the "roots" <note>The base conditions of the election.</note> of the elections and making them fortunate with **Jupiter**, according to what we have said.

## Chapter 10: On Managing Possessions, Seeking Them, and Receiving Debts.

It is appropriate in this, as we said before, that you make fortunate the second house and its Lord, the **Moon** and its Lord, **Jupiter**, the **Part of Fortune**, and the **Part of Substance**. Remove **Mars** from all of these, placing him in locations that are "falling" <note>Cadent houses, where a planet's influence is weakened.</note> from those significators of wealth we mentioned; for the damage of **Mars** in matters of wealth is very great, and similarly the damage of the **Tail** <note>The "Dragon's Tail" or South Node of the Moon, considered a point of decrease.</note>. However, the damage of **Saturn** regarding wealth is less. Place the significator in signs that "receive and give," for they are good in this house. ¶ If you wish to manage edible things, place the Moon in the Ascendant in "signs of much eating," which are **Aries**, **Taurus**, **Leo**, the last half of **Sagittarius**, **Capricorn**, and **Pisces**. Let neither the Moon nor the Ascendant be in the places of **Saturn**.

## Chapter 11: On Buying and Selling.

Know that the Ascendant, its Lord, and the planet to which the **Moon** applies <note>Moves toward an aspect with.</note> are the significators of the **buyer**. The **seventh house**, its Lord, and the planet from which the Moon separates are the significators of the **seller**. The **tenth house** and its Lord are significators of the **price**. The **fourth house** and its Lord are significators of the **object** being sold. The Moon is also a significator of the price. Therefore, whichever of these you improve, that part of the buying and selling will be improved; and whichever you damage, that part will be damaged. ¶ When you wish to buy any thing: prepare the **Part of Fortune** and place it in the house of **Jupiter**, and let it apply to the "fortunes" <note>The benefic planets, Jupiter and Venus.</note>; for this will be better for the buyer than for the seller. ¶ And if the Moon is in "signs of direct ascension" <note>Signs that take longer to rise: Cancer through Sagittarius.</note> and increasing in light and number <note>The speed of its daily motion.</note> while applying to the fortunes: in the thing which is bought at that hour, its master will lose out, and it will be better for the seller than the buyer. ¶ And it is necessary that **Mars** be "falling" from **Mercury** and from the place of the Moon, because

<column-break/>

**Mars** in buying, selling, and in debts signifies that there will be fear, anger, and lawsuits; and similarly the **Tail**. Whence it is necessary that you remove it from the Moon; though specifically, the Tail brings less evil than Mars in this matter. ¶ If you wish to sell: place the Moon in her "exaltation" or "triplicity" <note>Dignities or locations where a planet has more power.</note>, separating from the "fortunes" and looking toward the "infortunes" <note>The malefic planets, Saturn and Mars.</note>, but not applying to them. ¶ **Musil** <note>original: "Musil"; likely referring to an Arabic astrological authority such as Masha'allah.</note> said: when you wish to buy anything, place the **Part of Fortune** in one of the houses of **Jupiter** while applying; for the buyer will have good in this. ¶ When you wish to sell: place the Moon in her exaltation or triplicity, "falling" from the infortunes and not looking at them, and far from the fortunes; for with this, the sale will be completed according to your will. ¶ And when you wish to buy any thing for a **good price** <note>original: "bono foro"; a bargain.</note>: buy it when the Moon is in her second quadrature <note>The last quarter phase.</note> with the **Sun**, and in a "diminished sign," and she herself is diminished in light and number, and joined with **Mercury**; and both of them safe from the infortunes. <margin>Truly</margin> And if she is not joined with **Mercury**, let **Mercury** be safe from the infortunes. ¶ When the Moon is in her first quadrature with the Sun, things that are bought at that time will be bought for their just price, what they are worth; and every act begun then will have truth and justice in it. If **Jupiter** looks upon the Moon while she is in this place, he will have good fortune and righteousness in the things that are sold. When she has passed this quarter and is going toward the opposition <note>The Full Moon.</note>, then it is better for the seller and for him who seeks a lawsuit or a case, with him beginning the petition. When she separates from the opposition and goes toward the second quadrature <note>Moving from Full toward the last quarter.</note> of the Sun, then it is better for the buyer. When she separates from this quarter and goes toward the "conjunction" <note>The New Moon.</note>, then it is good for him who wants to buy something in secret, or a hidden thing which he does not want anyone to know about; and especially if she is seen by a "fortune" <note>Jupiter or Venus.</note>. When she is in the two western quarters—which are from the tenth house to the seventh, and from the fourth house to the Ascendant—and the Lord of the Ascendant is diminished in his motion, and the Lord of the Midheaven <note>The tenth house, or the highest point of the chart.</note> is safe from the infortunes: this is the best that can be for buying a thing at a good price. ¶ If you wish to invest capital <note>original: "mittere thesaurum"; literally "to send treasure."</note> to make a profit from it: prepare the **Moon** and **Mercury**, or the Lord of the house of wealth, and the degree of the "house of trust" <note>Likely the 11th house, which governs friends and hopes.</note>; and see in what place the Lord of one of them is. Give **Mercury** a part in it, and fortify him, and give the Moon some "mixture" <note>An aspect or connection.</note> with any fortune. As much as you can, remove **Mars** from them. Let **Mercury** be "direct" <note>Not retrograde.</note> and in his own house, exaltation, or joy, escaping from under the Sun's rays, and having no mixture with **Mars** nor **Saturn**. Nor should he be in his "fall" or in the "terms" of the infortunes, which are the ends of the signs. ¶ If you have haste to send for profit or wealth and **Mercury** is "retrograde" <note>Appearing to move backward, usually an ill omen for business.</note> and you cannot wait until he turns direct: specifically keep him safe from **Mars**, and join him bodily with **Jupiter** or **Venus**, and let him apply to them. And prepare the Moon, for you cannot excuse her <note>You cannot ignore her role.</note> while Mercury is retrograde; and make it so that the Lord of the "term" of the degree of the house of trust, or the Lord of the house of trust itself, is a "fortune" looking at **Mercury**, and let them not be falling from him, nor let the fortunes be falling from him. ¶ **Vuellius** and **Cadoros** <note>Names of astrological authorities.</note> said: when you wish to send money for profit, direct and prepare **Mercury**, the degree of the **Part of Fortune**, and the degree of the **house of trust**, and beware that **Mars** has no mixture with any of them.

## Chapter 12: On Selling Produce.
