You shall do this on the 4th or 2nd day of the month; and let the Moon be waxing in its motion, and in signs that are increasing let them be "twisted" <note>original: "tortuosa"; refers to signs of short ascension like Capricorn or Pisces</note>; and let it be in a figure in any of the two ascending quarters which are masculine; and let the **Lord of the Ascendant** <note>The planet ruling the sign rising on the eastern horizon</note> be in any of those good places; and let the **Midheaven** <note>The highest point in the sky; the 10th house</note> and its Lord be safe; and the Moon with **Mercury** safe; and in swift motion.

### ¶ Chapter 13: On giving capital.

Know that the **Ascendant** and its Lord are the significators of the master who gives the capital <note>The lender or investor</note>; and the **7th House** and its Lord are the significators of the one receiving it; and the **Moon** and **Mercury** are the significators of the capital itself. And when there is harmony between the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the 7th; and the Moon and Mercury are in the Ascendant or with its Lord, and fortunate: that matter will be completed easily and well. But if the Moon is under the rays of the Sun, it is a cause of loss: because the Sun "burns" the Moon, which is the significatrix of the capital. And when the Moon is in the **Burned Path** <note>original: "via combusta"; a specific unlucky area of the zodiac, usually 15° Libra to 15° Scorpio</note>, or is in latitude toward the southern part; or is in the first degrees of **Leo**, or **Gemini**, or **Sagittarius**; or the Ascendant is in those degrees: in all these things it is not good for the giver, though it is good for the receiver. ¶ A certain part of the wise say that it is not good to give capital in the hour of **Saturn** nor the **Sun**. And know that the Sun is the significator of the one giving capital, and the Moon of the one receiving: because the Moon always receives from the Sun.

### ¶ Chapter 14: On receiving capital.

Know that this is the opposite of those things we said before: because he who wants to receive capital should look for the Moon to be in **Leo**, **Virgo**, **Scorpio**, **Sagittarius**, or **Aquarius**; and that it should be diminishing in light, while aspecting **Venus** or **Jupiter** or **Mercury**; and let the Ascendant be one of the signs we mentioned before; and let the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the 7th be safe from misfortunes; and let them have harmony, that is, one with the other. ¶ And a certain part of the wise abhor the hour of **Mars** for this, and similarly the hour of the **Sun**.

### ¶ Chapter 15: On moving oneself from one house to another.

That which is necessary to observe for moving oneself from one house to another, that same thing is necessary for a traveler to observe at the entry of cities: and it is especially necessary in a move to place **Taurus** or **Leo** in the **4th House** <note>The house of home and foundations</note>; because this signifies the cleanliness of the house and the goodness of the place; and that it will be free from reptiles. However, if **Scorpio** is there, it signifies that many reptiles will be there, including venomous ones; and especially if **Saturn** or **Mars** aspects it there. And you should beware not to place a misfortune <note>A "malefic" planet like Mars or Saturn</note> in the 4th, nor let one aspect it with a hostile look. And in this, it is better for **Venus** to be in the 4th: however, the "root" of the election for moving from one house to another, and from one dwelling to another, is in placing the Ascendant and the 7th House safe from misfortunes; and the Moon similarly, and let the Moon be applying to a fortune <note>A "benefic" planet like Jupiter or Venus</note>, and let that fortune be ascending, in the north, and increasing; and the Moon increasing in light and in number; and let the Lord of the 8th House and the Lord of the 2nd be safe from misfortunes; and let the Lord of the 2nd be in the Ascendant, or the 4th, or in the **House of Trust** <note>likely referring to the 11th house of hopes/friends</note>: because this is the best that can be in this matter, with the help of God.

<column-break/>

### ¶ Chapter 16: On the work of alchemy.

When you wish to undertake the work of **alchemy**, or any other thing that is worked with fire, or a deed that you wish to be reiterated many times: look in this for the Moon to be in **common signs** <note>Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, or Pisces; signs of transition and change</note>, safe from misfortunes; and the Ascendant similarly. And the best thing in this, if the work is on **gold**, is to capture the **Sun** as much as you can; and similarly the planets of the other metals.

### ¶ Chapter 17: On the 3rd House and its elections.

The elections of this house are: establishing friendship with brothers and blood-relatives; and to know how to teach the law. It is suitable for brothers to prepare the **third house** and its Lord, looking first at the "roots" of the elections; and let the Lord of this house be applying to the Lord of the Ascendant from the 3rd: or in a sextile aspect with **reception** <note>A condition where two planets are in each other's signs, aiding cooperation</note>; and let it aspect the Ascendant with a good aspect. And it is good in this for the Lord of the Ascendant to be in the 10th or 11th house, and for the Moon to aspect them. ¶ And if the matter is with **elder brothers**, it is good to prepare **Saturn**, and let him aspect it with a good aspect and with reception. And if it is with **middle brothers**, look to **Mars** instead of Saturn. And if it is with **younger brothers**, **Mercury** instead of Saturn. And if it is with **sisters**, prepare **Venus** according to this manner we have set out. And according to this, look to the election in the friendships of fathers by doing with the **4th house** what we said for the 3rd; and similarly for children by doing with the **11th house** what we do for the third.

### ¶ Chapter 18: On beginning to teach legal knowledge.

It is suitable in this to prepare the third house and its Lord, **Jupiter**, and the luminaries <note>The Sun and Moon</note>; and if they are in any of the houses of Jupiter, it will be better. And if you wish to learn subtleties and decrees: prepare **Mercury** similarly, and place the significators which we have mentioned so that one aspects the other with a good aspect. Similarly, let one aspect the house of the other with good aspects; and look to as many of these as you can.

### ¶ Chapter 19: On the 4th house and its elections.

The elections of this house are: beginning the foundations of cities, fortresses, and houses; and in reclaiming fields; and in the course of streams; and in digging the earth; and in buying inheritances; and in populating them; in making mills; and in sowing and planting trees; and in taking lands for rent; and in taking covered houses for rent; and in **expelling and casting out the devil from a house**.

### ¶ Chapter 20: On making the foundations of towns and houses.

Know that cities and great houses are not built except by kings and high men: wherefore when you wish to make a good election for such a thing, look at what place they wish to build it; and see in what **climate** it is; and what planet is the Lord of that climate; and in what partition of the sign that place falls; and who is the Lord of that sign; and if it is a fortune or in...

### ¶ Chapter 22. On buying estates.

<margin>let it not be in [a place of] fortune</margin>
**I**n all these matters, it is necessary that the house of estates, which is the **4th** from the Ascendant, be arranged, setting it before the things we mentioned earlier. And remove Mars from her aspects: and let the 4th house be a **fixed sign**: and let the Lords of the angles be oriental, increasing in their motion, and ascending toward the north. And in buying every kind of estate, make sure that the fortunes have dignities in the angles, and especially in the Ascendant and the 4th: and that the **luminaries** <note>the Sun and Moon</note> look upon the Ascendant and the 4th house with a good aspect; and let there be no **retrograde** <note>appearing to move backward</note> planet in the angles, nor let their Lords be retrograde. ¶ **Al-Kindi** <note>9th-century Arab "Philosopher of the Arabs" and astrologer</note> said: <insert>let them not be</insert> in the 9th, nor in the 5th, nor in the 11th; nor let the 4th house be a **fire sign**, nor a fiery planet be in it: and especially if the malefic planets are supported in that house. And let Saturn not look upon the 4th house if it is a **water sign**; and if the Midheaven is unfortunate, it will be bad. ¶ And know that the Ascendant and its Lord signify the thing itself, and likewise the buyer and the profit that will be in it, and the dwellings; and the Midheaven and its Lord signify the things that are rooted there upon its surface, such as trees and the like. And the 4th and its Lord signify the estates, the inhabitants, and those who serve the lord of the estate. And it is said that they signify the herbs and its vegetation; and the **7th** and its Lord signify the good of the land and the plantings that will be there. Therefore, whichever of these indicators is harmed signifies loss in that matter; and whichever of them is improved signifies improvement in its own significance. ¶ **Arabari** <note>An uncertain name, likely a corruption of an Arabic authority like Al-Biruni or Al-Battani</note> said: Jupiter and the planet from which the Moon separates are the indicators of the one who buys the estate: and the planet to which the Moon applies is the indicator of the end, and what will become of that estate and the purchase.

### ¶ Chapter 23. On populating estates.

**I**t is fitting in this that the Moon be **received** <note>a planet being in a sign ruled by another planet that looks at it</note> by a fortune, and that fortune should be in an angle or a **succedent** house <note>the 2nd, 5th, 8th, or 11th houses</note>; and that the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the Moon’s house be in good states. And procure that some fortune is in the **house of substance** <note>the 2nd house of wealth</note>; and let it be safe from infortunes; or let the Lord of the **Part of Fortune** be there. ¶ **Al-Kindi** said: let the Lord of the house of substance be there; and make sure the place of conjunction or prevention <note>the previous New or Full Moon</note> is in an angle: and that the Moon, when she separates herself from the conjunction or prevention, is applying...

## ¶ Chapter 24. On the making of mills.

Observe in this that the **Ascendant** <note>The zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon</note> and the Moon are in **Aries**, **Libra**, or at the end of **Virgo**; and beware that the Moon is not in **Cancer** or **Capricorn**, because these are signs in which the days and nights vary. And when the Moon and the Lord of the Ascendant are in the aforementioned signs, and safe from the aspects of the **infortunes** <note>malefic planets, usually Mars or Saturn</note>, it will be a good election.
And if the election is for another kind of mill engine, you shall follow this same election.

## ¶ Chapter 25. On sowing and planting trees.

If your election is for sowing things that are meant to bear fruit that year, such as garden vegetables, wheat, and the like, each in its proper season: see that the Moon is in **movable signs** <note>Also called "cardinal" signs: Aries, Cancer, Libra, and Capricorn</note>. And if it is in **Capricorn**, **Cancer**, or **Virgo**, it will be good; let the Moon be increasing in its number <note>referring to its daily speed or numerical degree</note>; and likewise, it is good in **Pisces**. Then, if your election is for planting trees, see that the Moon is in **fixed signs** <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, or Aquarius</note> and especially in **Taurus** or **Aquarius**; because when Saturn is in a good state, either in a "succeedent" house or in any of its **dignities** <note>positions where a planet has more power</note>, and it has some testimony in the Ascendant; and let the Ascendant be any of the signs we mentioned; and let Jupiter be looking upon Saturn with a good aspect and from a place where it has some dignity. And with all this, guard yourself against **Mars**. And the **Lord of Exaltation** has greater power in planting trees than the **Lord of the House**. ¶ And **Al-Khayyat** <note>original: "Alhayath"; Abu 'Ali al-Khayyat, a 9th-century Persian astrologer</note> said: let the Lord of the Moon's house look upon the Moon in a **water sign**. And if the Ascendant is not a fixed sign, let it be a common sign; and let its Lord be in the East, rising in its latitude.

## ¶ Chapter 26. On the leasing of lands.

It is fitting in this that you make the Ascendant and its Lord fortunate; and let the Lord of the Ascendant be going toward an angle in an **earth sign**; and the Moon likewise; or let it be in an "angle of the earth" <note>likely the 4th house, the lowest point of the chart</note>; and let the planet from which the Moon is separating be a fortune free from the infortunes; because it is the "significator" <note>the planet representing the person or thing in question</note> of the lord to whom the land belongs. And let the Lord of the 7th house be a fortune, and let it have as much agreement as possible with the Lord of the Ascendant. And likewise, let the planet to which the Moon applies have some agreement with the planet from which it separates. And you shall use this same election for leasing rivers and for petitioning for lands. ¶ And know that the Ascendant and its Lord, and the planet from which the Moon separates, are the significators of the lord who owns the land; and the 4th house and its Lord are the significators of the land itself; and the 7th house and its Lord, and the planet toward which the Moon moves, are the significators of the one who takes the land for a **pension** <note>original: "pensionē"; a regular rental payment</note>. Therefore, take care to arrange whichever of these places you most wish to improve.

## ¶ Chapter 27. On leasing houses and renting out revenues.

Know that the Ascendant is the significator of the lord of the houses; and the 7th house is the significator of the one who dwells in it; and the **Midheaven** <note>original: "mediū celi"; the highest point of the chart</note> is the significator of the place itself; and the 4th house is the end of the matter. Therefore, choose the one whose significance you wish to improve. For if the Ascendant is unfortunate, it signifies that the lord of the house will cause ruin. And if the 7th house is unfortunate, it signifies that the one who holds it for

<column-break/>

rent will cause ruin. And the planet to which the Moon applies is the significator of the lord's **tenant** <note>original: "inquilini"</note>. And the planet from which it separates is the significator of the one who receives the tenant. And the Lord of that time is the significator of the end of the matter. ¶ **Al-Tabari** <note>original: "atabari"; a 9th-century astrologer</note> said it is fitting in this to arrange Jupiter and Saturn so that one looks upon the other with a good aspect.

## ¶ Chapter 28. On removing phantasms from a house.

When there is in any house or place any thing from which men are terrified, or any sign that scares those in the house, such that it is tedious for those dwelling in it; and you wish to remove and put to flight that thing from the house by incantation or any other way, or by any **mastery** <note>original: "magisteriuz"; likely a ritual or technical procedure</note> that you wish to perform there: beware that the Moon is not in the Ascendant, nor let the Ascendant be **Leo**, **Cancer**, **Scorpio**, or **Aquarius**; nor should the Moon be in any of these signs. Let it, however, be in other signs, separating itself from an infortune and applying to a fortune.

## ¶ Chapter 29. On the 3rd house and its elections.

The elections that are in this house are: lying with women to have a son; giving an infant to a nurse; removing him from her; baptizing; circumcising; and clothing him with new garments; on going out; in sending couriers; in writing letters and sending them; in eating and drinking; in fragrant things; in sending pigeons so that they may attract others; and in extracting a dead creature <note>a fetus</note> from the mother's womb.

## ¶ Chapter 30. On lying with a woman so that she may have a son.

The election that is fitting for this is that you place the Ascendant in a **masculine sign** of **direct ascension**; and let the angles be fixed signs; and the Lord of the Ascendant in the Ascendant or in the Midheaven or in the 11th house. And let the first planet that crosses through the degree of the Ascendant on the horizon be a fortune; and arrange the **luminaries** <note>The Sun and Moon</note> as much as you can in this election. And let Mars <note>unclear: possibly "mirate" or a contraction for "moderate"</note> the luminary of the time; nor should there be an infortune in any of the angles, but rather a fortune there, safe and strong. ¶ And it is fitting in this to look to the Lord of the Ascendant and to guard it so that it is not infortune in the **9th month** from the time of conception, because that will be the time of birth. And if you can guard it from being infortune in the 7th month or in the 10th after conception, it will be better, because birth can happen in those aforementioned times. Therefore, it is necessary that it be fortunate and powerful in those times, and the luminaries likewise. ¶ And guard yourself against the Lord of the 7th or 8th house; when they are unfortunate, they should not have any mixture with the aforementioned significators; and also guard yourself against the infortunes and the **Tail** <note>The South Node of the Moon</note>. And Al-Khayyat said the best that can be in this is that the Moon be in the Ascendant in the 3rd [degree] of the Sun. And he said: guard yourself against the **Combust Way** <note>original: "via cōbusta"; a segment of the zodiac considered highly unlucky</note> and arrange **Venus**; because if Venus were harmed, there would be harm to the mother. And if the Moon were harmed, there would be harm to the body of the creature. ¶ And arrange the 5th house and its Lord; and it is fitting that this be done in the **odd hours** of the day and night, such as the 1st, 3rd, 5th, and the like. ¶ And if it happens that the Ascendant is **Libra**, it being safe and its Lord likewise free, it will be good because it is a "rational sign"; and the Midheaven will be **Cancer**, which is a sign of many children, and the significators are in masculine signs; for this signifies that the conception will be of males. And it is necessary that you assist yourself in this matter with natural deeds which are...

### ¶ Chapter 31. On giving a child to a nurse.
**O**bserve in this matter that the Moon should be conjoined to **Venus** by body <note>occupying the same degree of the zodiac</note> and that both should be "healthy" <note>free from the negative influence of malefic planets</note>. ### ¶ Chapter 32. On weaning a child from the breast.
**O**bserve in this that the Moon should be far from the Sun, applying to the lord of its own house; and that the **Ascendant** <note>the sign rising on the eastern horizon</note> should be a house of fortune. ¶ And one group of the wise men abhors the 12 houses of Venus. ¶ And other wise men say that when a child is taken from the breast and the Moon is in the **mansion** <note>a division of the lunar zodiac</note> which is called **Azarsa** <note>original: "azarsa"; likely the seventh Arabic lunar mansion, al-Dhira'</note>, the child will not suffer pain because of the breast, nor will they seek it. ¶ Others say that when the lord of the Ascendant and the Moon are in signs signifying "vegetables that are not born" <note>referring to barren signs like Gemini, Leo, or Virgo</note>, the child will strive toward things that are born and will not care for the breast.

### ¶ Chapter 33. On circumcising and baptizing.
**A**nother point in this is that the Moon should be elevated above Venus, and Venus applying to **Jupiter**. And you must guard the Ascendant, its lord, Venus, and the Moon from all aspects of **Saturn**; and especially the Moon and the Ascendant, for if Saturn interferes, it may be necessary for the cutting to happen a second time, or much "poison" <note>meaning infection or poor healing</note> will occur there. And see that the lord of the Ascendant is increasing in latitude, and the Moon and its lord are in northern signs and in **succedent** <note>the houses following the "angles," which are the 2nd, 5th, 8th, and 11th</note> houses. And beware that **Mars** is not in an angle nor in the Ascendant, nor the Moon in **Scorpio**.

### ¶ Chapter 34. On cutting and wearing new clothes.
**T**he best thing in this is that the Moon be in **movable signs** <note>Aries, Cancer, Libra, or Capricorn</note> and be fortunate; and if she is in **common signs** <note>Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, or Pisces</note>, it is not bad. ¶ Take care that the Moon is not in **conjunction** with the Sun nor in **opposition** to it; nor should the Sun be in the Ascendant nor opposite to it. And likewise, beware of **fixed signs** <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, or Aquarius</note> at the beginning of the cutting, unless it is a military garment, because in that case, fixed signs are not bad. And place the Sun in the **Midheaven** <note>the highest point of the chart</note> and let the Moon be increasing in light; take [the lord of] the house and its lord at the hour of buying the cloth and cutting it, and also when wearing it. And let it be in a movable sign when you put it on; and among all signs, **Leo** is the worst for this.

### ¶ Chapter 35. On sending gifts.
**I**t is appropriate in this that you look to the **fifth house** and its lord at the hour you wish to send gifts; and you shall do the same in receiving them. ### ¶ Chapter 36. On sending couriers.
**O**bserve in this that the Moon should be applying to the planet which is the significator of the person to whom you are sending the messenger: thus, if it is a King, the Sun; if a judge or a merchant, Jupiter. And follow this way for others. And let neither the Moon nor that planet be falling from the angles; and let them be free from the **infortunes**.

### ¶ Chapter 37. On writing documents.
**W**hen you wish to write a document, see that the Moon is applying to **Mercury**, and is safe from the infortunes; and that Mercury is powerful, not unfortunate, nor **retrograde** <note>appearing to move backward</note>, nor "damaged." And let the Ascendant and its lord be safe from the infortunes and their rays.

### ¶ Chapter 39. On drinks. <gloss>specifically, on making wine</gloss>

## Chapter 40. On involving oneself with fragrant things.

**O**bserve in this matter that the Moon should be in **Aries**, **Leo**, or **Sagittarius**; or that one of these signs should be the **Ascendant** <note>the sign rising on the eastern horizon</note>. However, ensure that **Venus** is in the Ascendant and the Moon is in the **tenth house** <note>the house of success and public standing</note>, applying to Venus. This signifies that the preparation <note>original: "confectio"</note> will have a good scent, and that he who makes it will find joy in it. Nevertheless, if one wishes to make **suffumigations** <note>incense or medicinal vapors</note> separately, it is good for the Moon to be received by **Mars** or by the **Sun**, because this is a matter performed by fire. And when you make any fragrant preparation and the Moon is in **Gemini** applying to **Mercury**, it signifies that the work will be well completed.

## Chapter 41. On sending out pigeons to lead others.

**W**hen you wish to send out pigeons to attract others, provided that they return to their own nests, observe that the Moon applies to a planet that does not **combust** <note>a planet is "combust" when it is too close to the Sun, losing its power</note> quickly; for this signifies that they will return quickly and safely. And beware lest the Moon apply to **Mercury**, for he is the cause of many misfortunes; he often undergoes combustions and **retrogradations** <note>appearing to move backward in the sky</note>, and if any of this happens to him, the pigeons would neither be safe nor secure from capture. And when you send out birds, it is good for the Moon to be in a **water sign** <note>original: "figura aque"</note> and applying to **Venus**, and for Venus to be in a sign of **direct ascension** <note>signs that take longer to rise, associated with stability</note>; for this signifies that they will not wander from the path, nor will they lack water on the way. And if you send them while the Moon is applying to **Mars**, they will flee and depart, especially if the sign is an **airy sign**. And if the Moon applies to **Saturn**, they will wander from the path and be scattered on account of thirst, or by that which resembles him. And certain wise men have said that they have experienced this: that birds return to their nests on that day when the Moon returns to that sign, or on that day when it applies to that planet a second time.

## Chapter 42. On extracting a child from the mother's womb.

**W**hen you wish to do this, observe that the Moon is diminished in light, and descending southward in **latitude** <note>the distance north or south of the celestial equator</note> and **declination**, or in her own path; provided that the Moon is in the Ascendant, and the Lord of the Ascendant is in aspect with **Jupiter** and **Venus**. And the best signs for this matter are the **feminine** signs and those of **direct ascension**.

## Chapter 43. On the 6th house and its elections.

**I**n this house <note>the 6th house traditionally governs health, sickness, and servants</note> are these elections: healing infirmities; working with an **enema** <note>original: "clisterio"</note>; healing the eyes; taking **laxative** medicine; taking **restrictive** medicines; preparing gargles; inducing vomiting; buying captives and servants; giving statutes or laws to servants and captives; taming horses; and buying beasts, both great and small.

## Chapter 44. On treating the sick.

**W**hen you wish to heal a long-standing infirmity, place the Moon in **Taurus** or its **triplicity** <note>the group of earth signs: Taurus, Virgo, Capricorn</note>; however, Taurus is better, as it signifies internal infirmities. And let the Moon be safe from **malefics** <note>original: "infortunis," usually Saturn or Mars</note>, and in one of the **angles** <note>the four primary houses: 1st, 4th, 7th, 10th</note> of the Ascendant; for then the Moon will be more powerful for this purpose, and there will be greater security that the infirmity will not suffer a relapse after the sick person has been healed. And beware of the Moon's applications to **Saturn**, for he always signifies long durations in things and slowness. And **Mashallah** <note>original: "messahala," a famous 8th-century Jewish-Persian astrologer</note> said: observe in which part of the body that infirmity is. If it is in the parts of the head or the throat down to the chest, you shall begin to work when the Moon is in **Aries**, **Taurus**, or **Gemini**, for these are of the upper part of the body. And if the infirmity is in the parts from the belly down to the feet, begin to work when the Moon is in **Cancer**, **Leo**, **Virgo**, **Capricorn**, **Aquarius**, or **Pisces**; for these 

<column-break/>

are of the middle part of the body. And if the infirmity is in the lower part of the body, work on it when the Moon is in **Libra**, **Scorpio**, or **Sagittarius**; and in all these places, let her be applying to **benefics** <note>original: "fortūis," like Jupiter or Venus</note> and increased in light and number <note>referring to her speed in her orbit</note>. And he said: also every infirmity and pain that is from the head to the foot will be healed when the Moon is in an angle, ascending from the third house up to the angle of the **10th house** through the midheaven, and by descending to the angle of the third; and this part is called the **depressed part**. And if you wish to heal, I will perform well and for improvement. And if you wish to heal one who is foolish or **bewitched** <note>original: "maleficiatū," one under a magic spell</note>, act so that **Mercury** is in his own **term** <note>a specific subdivision of a zodiac sign where a planet has more power</note>. And do the same if you wish to heal a **demoniac** <note>one possessed by a demon</note>.

## Chapter 45. On treating with an enema.

**I**f you wish to work with an **enema**, place the Moon in **Libra** or **Scorpio**, and it will be better; and let the Lord of the Ascendant have no aspect with the Lord of the **6th house**; and let the Moon be applying to **Venus**. This constellation signifies that this will be useful and will have a good end.

## Chapter 46. On healing the eyes.

**Q**uando <note>The letter Q is an ornate initial.</note> **W**hen you wish to heal the eye from the infirmities that happen to the eyes—such as diminished sight, or a **cataract** <note>original: "albedo," literally "whiteness"</note> in the eye, or superfluous flesh that requires an incision with iron <note>surgery</note>, or another infirmity—observe that the Moon is increasing in light and number, free from **malefics**, and especially from **Mars**; for he is malignant and of great damage in infirmities of the eyes, especially when the Moon is waxing. However, if he <note>Mars</note> aspects her while she is increased in light and number at the beginning of the month, he will not do her damage. And when she is separated from the **opposition** <note>180 degrees from the Sun</note> and Mars aspects her from the **third house** while she is applying to **benefics**, then Mars will not do her great damage in infirmities; for all the wise men are agreed that Mars is a great damager of all members of the head. And **Thabit** <note>original: "siri," likely referring to Thabit ibn Qurra</note> says that every work of iron <note>surgical tool</note> that is necessary for the improvement of the body must be inspected according to the sign representing that member; and do not touch that member with iron, nor place the Ascendant in it. And similarly, beware of touching any place of the body with iron while the Moon is in a **common** <note>Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces</note> or **movable** <note>Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn</note> sign.

## Chapter 47. On taking laxative medicine.

**I**n the taking of **laxative** medicine, the wise men are in disagreement. However, **Ptolemy** says that this is a good election when the Moon is in the **wet triplicity**, which is **Cancer**, **Scorpio**, and **Pisces**. And **Hermes** says the same, as he was before him. But **Vettius Valens** <note>original: "vuelli[us] fertimus"</note> and the modern Arabs agree with them, saying that **Taurus**, **Virgo**, **Scorpio**, and **Pisces** are good for this. And in this opinion, **Mashallah**, **Al-Khayyat** <note>original: "alhazat"</note>, **Masha'allah** <note>original: "minegeth"?</note>, and many others of the modern astrologers agree. However, **Al-Kindi** <note>original: "alkind[us]"</note> holds an opinion which I affirm: although all the others we have named speak well for the sake of guarding the body and purging it of superfluous **humors** <note>the four bodily fluids: blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile</note> without pain or infirmity. And those who move away from these signs say this to remove infirmity and impediments from the body and by lifting that superfluous humor separately. However, the opinion of Al-Kindi, with which I agree, is that the Moon should be in the middle of the latter part of **Libra**, or in the middle of the former part of **Scorpio**; and that the Lord of the House be powerful, fortunate, **oriental** <note>rising before the sun</note>, and in an angle; and the planet bestowing fortune upon him should similarly be in an angle and oriental; and that the Lord of the Ascendant be of such a kind. And remove the malefics similarly from the Moon first...

And beware as much as you can lest the significators be **cadent** <note>weakly placed in the 3rd, 6th, 9th, or 12th houses</note> or afflicted by **infortunes** <note>malefic planets, Saturn and Mars</note>, and let no infortune be prominently placed, for this signifies great evil. And beware likewise as much as you can lest the Lord of the **House of Death** <note>the 8th house</note> be in any angle, nor should it have any connection with any significator, nor have great power there; and when you observe all this, you will achieve what you desire from the medicine.

### Chapter 48. On giving restrictive medicine.

In this matter, it is good for the Moon to be in the degrees of her **exaltation** <note>Taurus, where the Moon's influence is strongest</note>, joined to Jupiter by body or applying to him. It is also good for the Moon and the planet she applies to be of slow motion without retrogradation. ¶ And if the Moon and the planet she applies to, and the Lord of the Ascendant, are ascending toward the north, this is better and more advantageous. And in this matter, beware of Mars and Venus.

### Chapter 49. On administering medicines through the nostrils, and for vomiting and gargling.

The best choice in this is for the Ascendant, the Moon, and the significators to be in ruminating signs, while observing the constellations and choices we mentioned for drinking medicines. ¶ And **Al-Tabari** <note>an influential 9th-century Persian physician and astrologer</note> said that it is good for the Moon to be diminishing in light and in Taurus, and descending in latitude. ¶ And **Al-Khayyat** <note>Abu 'Ali al-Khayyat, a student of Mashallah</note> said it is good for the Moon and the Lord of the Ascendant to be in Cancer, Leo, or Virgo; and that the Moon should be applying to the fortunes and not to a "damned" <note>afflicted or malefic</note> planet. ¶ And others have said that it is

### Chapter 50. On buying servants.

<margin>her</margin>
If you wish to buy any servant who is to be a minister <note>a domestic worker or official</note>, you shall look at the **face** <note>the outward appearance or a specific 10-degree division of a sign</note> that is appropriate for his service; provide it with fortunes and place it in the Ascendant or in the place of the Moon, with both being fortunate. ¶ And if it is a laborer, place them in **vile signs** <note>low-status signs</note> at the end of Sagittarius or in Gemini, provided they are fortunate; and **Aquarius** is similarly good, except that it signifies he will perhaps be a deceiver and wise in his ways. ¶ And if the servant is male, place the locations of the significators and the signs in masculine places. And if it is a female, place them in feminine signs. ¶ And if you desire a servant for the purpose of lying with her or for having a child by her, place **Virgo** specifically for this; and remove the infortunes and their light from them, and strengthen them with the fortunes and their lights. ¶ And if you wish to improve any specific limb in her, place the Moon in the sign of that limb, made fortunate by the lights of the fortunes. ¶ And others have said: it is fitting when buying servants that the Ascendant and the Moon be in **fixed signs** <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius</note> and signs of **direct ascension**, and in domestic figures; and likewise for the Lord of the Ascendant. Arrange the **fourth house** and its Lord so that it applies to the Lord of the Ascendant with a good aspect and **reception** <note>a condition where one planet is in a sign ruled by the other</note>. Arrange the Moon and her Lord similarly, as well as the Lord of the **House of Servants** <note>the 6th house</note>. Beware lest the Ascendant or the Moon be the Lord of the 6th house in Leo; the best of these is Taurus and the end of Sagittarius. ¶ And others say let the Moon and the Lord of the Ascendant be in **human signs** <note>Gemini, Virgo, Libra, and Aquarius</note> and in other signs made fortunate, except for Aries, Scorpio, and Capricorn. Let the 6th house and its Lord be harmonious with the Ascendant and its Lord. ¶ And others say that the servant will be according to the nature of the sign and animal from which it is named: just as **Pisces** signifies power, and in this manner for the others; and this is a good conclusion. ¶ And they say that if the infortunes are "under the earth" <note>in the houses below the horizon</note>, the servant will be false; and Sagittarius specifically signifies that the servant will be good and law-abiding.

### Chapter 51. On giving laws to servants and captives, and on taming horses.

A good choice in this is to arrange the Ascendant and its Lord, because the Ascendant is the significator of the master; and the 7th house signifies the one to whom the statute or law is given; and the **Midheaven** <note>the 10th house</note> signifies the occasion for which the statute or law is given; and the 4th house signifies the end of that ordinance and what kind of status he will have in it. Hence, if the Moon and the 7th house are unfortunate, it signifies that he will perhaps be returned to servitude just as he was before. ¶ **Sahl ibn Bishr** <note>original: "Zahel benbziç," a famous 9th-century Jewish astrologer and physician</note> said: it is fitting in this that the Moon be clear of all harm, increasing in light and in number <note>moving faster than its average daily speed</note>, and applying to the fortunes. Let that fortune be **oriental** <note>rising before the Sun</note> and similarly increasing; for if the fortune is increasing but **occidental** <note>setting after the Sun</note>, it signifies he will have good things, yet pains and infirmities will happen to him that will never leave him until he dies. The increase of the Moon's light signifies health of the body, and the increase of its number signifies that he will gain wealth. ¶ And it is good in this that the Sun and the sign of the Midheaven be safe from infortunes. If these are unfortunate, it signifies that some trouble <note>original: "inbzigamentu," likely a corruption of "impedimentum"</note> will happen to the master according to the nature of that sign. ¶ And it is good that at the hour of giving a statute or law to a servant, the **luminaries** <note>the Sun and Moon</note> should be beholding each other from a **trine** or **sextile** <note>harmonious aspects of 120 or 60 degrees</note>, because this signifies there will be love between the servant and his master; and

### ¶ Chapter 52. On buying large and small beasts.

<margin>animals.</margin>
**W**hen you wish to buy animals, both large and small, place the Moon **applying** <note>moving toward an aspect</note> to the **fortunes** <note>the benefic planets, Jupiter and Venus</note>; let that fortune be **direct** <note>moving forward, not retrograde</note>, **oriental** <note>rising before the Sun</note>, and increasing in **latitude** <note>the planet's distance north or south of the ecliptic</note>. And beware of applications to the **infortunes** <note>the malefic planets, Mars and Saturn</note>, because they signify the death or loss of the animal. ¶ And if the beast you wish to buy is already broken or trained for riding, buy it when the **Ascendant** <note>the sign rising on the eastern horizon</note> is in a **common sign** <note>Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, or Pisces</note> and the Moon is in a fixed sign, except for Aquarius and Scorpio. And if the planet to which the Moon applies is direct and increasing in latitude, it signifies that although the animal has some blemish on its body, you will nonetheless make a profit from it. And if it is direct and descending in latitude, it signifies that its body is complete and healthy, yet you will not get the price for it that you expect. ¶ And if the beast you wish to buy is young and has never been ridden, ensure the Ascendant is a **movable sign** <note>Aries, Cancer, Libra, or Capricorn</note> while applying a fortune to it, and observe the "roots of elections" <note>the fundamental rules of astrological timing</note> which we spoke of in the first chapter. ¶ And others have said: it is appropriate for this that the Ascendant and the Moon be in a fixed sign for the specific animal you wish to buy, whether it be an animal for riding, or a cow, or a sheep, or a pig, or whatever else you desire; or let it be in the sign that is closest to the nature of that thing, and let it be made fortunate by the **Lord of that sign** <note>the planet that rules that specific zodiac sign</note> or by another if the Lord is not **received** <note>a state where one planet is in a sign ruled by another</note>; and if the Lord of that sign is not a "fortune," it does no harm if it watches over the sign with an aspect of friendship and reception. ¶ And if the beast is male, place the **significators** <note>the planets representing the animal</note> in masculine signs and degrees. And if it is female, in feminine signs. ¶ And arrange the **sixth house** <note>the astrological house governing small animals and livestock</note> and its Lord. And it is good for the Ascendant and the significators to be in Leo or at the end of Sagittarius. And if it is a cow, you should improve Taurus. And if sheep, Aries. And if goats, Capricorn; and so with the other animals of the Zodiac. And for each house, arrange its likeness and fortune with the benefic planets, and remove the infortunes. ¶ And know that when the Moon separates from a fortune and applies to an infortune, and that infortune is in a sign of fortune, that beast will be bad and will bite and strike. And if the infortune is in a **human sign** <note>Gemini, Virgo, Libra, or the first half of Sagittarius</note>, the beast will be easily terrified or will not allow itself to be bridled. And if the Moon applies to the infortunes, these things will happen to the animal after the purchase according to that influence.

### ¶ Chapter 53. On the 7th house and its elections.

**I**n this house, the elections concern marriages, lawsuits, confronting one person with another, making peace with enemies, destroying fortresses and villas, creating legal instruments for litigation, partnerships, and every matter conducted between two people; recovering a fugitive, making a thief confess the truth, hunting by land and sea, buying weapons and engines for fighting, and playing at chess, tables <note>backgammon-style games</note>, and the like.

### ¶ Chapter 54. On marriages.

**K**now that the Ascendant and its Lord and the Sun are the significators of the man; and the **7th house** and its Lord and **Venus** are the significators of the woman; and the **Midheaven** <note>the 10th house, representing the height of the sky</note> and its Lord are the

And the Moon itself, by its good state or its afflictions, signifies the good or evil that each of them will have. And **Mercury** signifies the child they will have together; therefore, when Mercury is with the fortunes, it signifies they will quickly have a son. And when the Moon and Venus are in movable signs, they signify that their joy will not be lasting. And if the woman is a widow, it signifies she committed some fraud against the other husband she had.

### Chapter 55. On elections for litigation.

**I**t is fitting in this that you place the ascendant in some house of the three higher planets <note>Saturn, Jupiter, and Mars</note>: and most powerful in this are the houses of Mars, and let Mars be in sextile <note>a 60-degree aspect</note> to the ascendant or in its trine <note>a 120-degree aspect</note>, and let the lord of the ascendant be in the ascendant or in the 11th or 10th house. And never go to a lawsuit unless Mars has dominion in the suit: and that he be the lord of the ascendant: and that he be powerful in a good place, not damned, nor suspect, nor combust, and that he be in a sign of direct ascension <note>signs that take longer to rise, associated with easier outcomes</note>. And it is necessary in causes of wars that you arrange the planets of war which are Mars, Mercury, and the Moon, and the lord of the house in which the Moon is: from which you should consider and arrange these: and do not forget any of them, for they are the roots of wars. ¶ And know that whichever of the two armies moves or arises in that constellation or election which we have described, and they confront each other to fight, that one will conquer who was born by night or who had Mars in a better place in his birth chart: for Mars is the significator and lord of wars: and perhaps they will agree together and have peace between them: and that [is] because of the good constellation which both had in

### ¶ Chapter 57. On engaging in wars and making peace.

<image-desc>Ornamental initial D featuring interlace and foliate patterns within a square frame.</image-desc>The directions <note>astrological timings</note> that come in the engagements of lawsuits or wars on account of one who has become a rebel: and for him who is against him who is his lord. ¶ Alkindus said: it is fitting for a king, or for him against whom someone has become a rebel, that he does not litigate with that same rebel until the Moon is fortunate: because the Moon and the lord of the ascendant are always for the one who has become a rebel; and it is always fitting for a rebel to beware of litigating when the Moon is un-

And afterward, the combust hours begin in the first hour of the night that follows Wednesday, and up until the morning of the following Friday. And similarly you shall begin from Monday night, and you shall do as you did before, and you shall go on doing so until the whole month is completed and another conjunction begins. And you shall begin from the hour of the conjunction in whatever hour it may be, and you shall extract the combust hours according to this manner and number which we have predicted. And if any suit is begun in these hours, it signifies that the beginner of the suit will be destroyed, or an impediment will happen to his body: ruin among his helpers and his company and his things, such that if he begins in the first four of the 12 hours, he will be destroyed; and if in the second four, he will have an impediment in his body. And if he begins in the last four, there will be loss in his company and among his helpers.

# Chapter 58: On destroying castles and towns of enemies

Begin the election for destroying the castles of enemies through the specific inception of buildings which we described, neither more nor less. And place the ascendant in an airy or fiery sign, and let the Moon and the lord of the ascendant be in such signs. And the Arabs said—

<column-break/>

—that the ascendant should be a sign of direct ascension, and the lord of the ascendant should be occidental <note>setting in the west</note>; and let the first planet that has the ascendant after the ascending sign be diminished in motion and applying to a planet while moving toward its fall <note>a sign where a planet’s influence is weakest</note>, and let it be remote from an angle <note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</note>, yet not retrograde. And it is good that the Moon be oriental in motion and diminished in light and remote from an angle, and applying to a planet that is similarly remote and also going toward its fall or toward the fall of the Moon.
¶ And if the Moon is above the earth, make it apply to a planet that is below the earth; nor should the lord of the ascendant be retrograde.
¶ And it is good that this be done in the 4th quarter of the month <note>the waning moon phase</note>; and let the Moon not aspect the lord of its own house nor the Sun. And this is the election for an enemy’s castle; and with such an election, you will prevail over the castle and destroy it.
¶ If there be another destruction or a lighter election of another manner, it can be done by looking at and improving the root of the elections, as we have said before in all things.

# Chapter 59: On making arms and engines to defeat enemies, namely galleys and other vessels of the sea.

It is appropriate in this that the ascending sign be fixed <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, or Aquarius</note>; and if all four angles are fixed signs and of direct ascension, it will be better.
¶ And it is good that the Moon and the lord of the ascendant be in the angles; and that in the midheaven there be a powerful fortune <note>Jupiter or Venus</note>, oriental and in its dignities and of swift motion; and that the Moon be in its greatest motion. And prepare Mars as best you can; and similarly prepare the lord of the conjunction or prevention <note>the New or Full Moon immediately preceding</note> that occurred before that act; and let the first application which the Moon makes after its separation from said conjunction or prevention be to a fortune.
¶ And if the lord of the ascendant is entering an angle, it will be good. And it is good that it aspects the 4th house, because the 4th house is the place of the ship and is likened to it; afterward, it is good to improve the 4th house and place a fixed sign there.
¶ And other wise men say that it is good in this for the Moon to be in Taurus or Gemini, because the figure and form of a river is in those signs.
¶ And you should beware in this of the aspects of Mars. And it is good for the Moon to be above the earth. And when you wish to put these vessels into the water, look for another such election as this one is.

# Chapter 60: On partnership and every matter that is between two parties.

The general rule in every matter that is between two parties is that the ascendant is the significator of the one beginning the matter; and the 7th house is the significator of the other; and the 10th house is for the one who mediates between the two. And if there is a dispute, it will similarly be the significator of victory; and the 4th house is the end of the matter. Similarly, the Moon is the significator of the one who mediates between them; and the planet from which the Moon separates is the significator of the one who begins; and the planet to which the Moon applies is the significator of the other; and the lord of the 4th house is the significator of the end. And look to which house—namely the house of the ascendant or the 7th house—the lord of the midheaven looks more and with a better aspect, and in which of those two houses it has greater dignities; and judge that he will be more successful in the matter.
¶ Yet in partnership or society, it is good for the ascendant to be a common sign <note>Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, or Pisces</note> and the Moon in a common sign. And Leo is good in this matter, because the Sun and its house are good in society.

### Chapter 61. On searching for a fugitive.

The election for searching for a fugitive must be looked at for the most part just as one looks at the election for enemies. Thus, if he is of the sort who has become a rebel, you should take the election, as we have said, from the 7th house and its lord, and by weakening the Moon and making them "falling" <note>original: *cadētes*; planets in houses that do not support action</note> according to the constellations we have mentioned before. However, if the fugitive is among other enemies, you should take the election for this from the 12th house and its lord. And if the fugitive is not of these two types, look at him as we have said before. ¶ Al-Khayyat <note>original: *alfayat*; a famous 9th-century Persian astrologer</note> said that when the Moon is applying to the "infortunes" <note>harmful planets, usually Mars or Saturn</note>, you should not place her, nor the planet to which she applies, in the 4th house. ¶ Mashallah <note>original: *messahala*; an influential 8th-century Jewish-Egyptian astrologer</note> said it is fitting that the lord of the ascendant and the lord of the 7th house be applying to one another; and he said that if the Moon is applying to any planet in the 12th or 6th house, it signifies that the fugitive will be destroyed and lost.

### Chapter 62. On making a thief reveal themselves.

Abu Ma'shar <note>original: *Albumazar*; a leading Persian astrologer of the Middle Ages</note> said that it is good in this matter for the Moon and the planet to which the Moon applies to be in "rational" signs and those of human forms <note>signs like Gemini, Virgo, Libra, or Aquarius, associated with human intellect</note>; and in this, he spoke well and held a good opinion. ¶ And I say that it is likewise good for these and the ascendant to be in signs of "direct ascension" <note>signs that take longer to rise, associated with honesty and straightforwardness</note> so that they may confess the truth and nothing else.

### Chapter 63. On hunting by land and by water.

When you wish to have an election for this: place the Moon in Taurus or its triplicity <note>the group of earth signs: Taurus, Virgo, and Capricorn</note>. ¶ And the wise men said that for one who wishes to hunt upon the land, it is fitting that he place the Moon in Aries, Leo, or Sagittarius, applying to Mars by a trine or sextile <note>harmonious angles of 120 or 60 degrees</note> with reception <note>when a planet is in a sign ruled by the planet it is "visiting"</note>; for this signifies that he will have whatever he wishes from the hunt; and the dogs and other beasts with which he hunts will be strengthened, whatever kind of hunting it may be. ¶ And when you wish to hunt, it is fitting that you apply the Moon to the "fortunes" <note>beneficial planets, usually Jupiter or Venus</note>; and place a fortune in the ascendant, and an infortune in the 7th house; and let that infortune be Mars, because he signifies blood. Nevertheless, if that infortune is Saturn, it signifies that they will see the prey but will not catch it. ¶ But in hunting by water, ensure that the Moon is in the Midheaven <note>original: *medio celi*; the highest point of the sky</note> applying to Venus in the 7th house; because this signifies they will catch whatever they wish. ¶ However, if you wish to hunt beasts having claws/nails <note>original: *vngulas*</note> such as foxes, hares, and the like: see to it that the Moon is received by Mars and one of them is in the Midheaven. ¶ But if your intention is to catch small beasts <note>likely meaning "fierce" or "vermin" in this context</note> such as wolves, wild boars, and the like: beware as much as you can that Mars is not in any of the "angles" <note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</note>, because if he is there, the hunter will not be safe from those beasts doing him harm. ¶ And it is likewise very bad in this matter for the ascendant to be of the quadruped signs, which are Aries, Leo, and Sagittarius; because this signifies that the beasts will kill the hunter's mount <note>original: *egtaturā*, likely *equitaturam*</note>. ¶ And if the Moon is made

### ¶ Chapter 64. On playing at tables, chess, dice, and similar games.

<margin>fixed</margin>
When you wish at the start of a game for it to be concluded quickly, set the ascendant as a moveable sign and the Moon likewise in a moveable sign. And if you wish for that game to last a long time, set the ascendant as a fixed sign <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, or Aquarius</note> and the Moon likewise in a fixed sign. ¶ And when the Moon applies to the "fortunes" <note>benefic planets, Jupiter or Venus</note>, he who played first will win; and if she applies to a fortune and afterward to an "infortune" <note>malefic planets, Mars or Saturn</note>, it signifies that he who played first will win at the start and lose afterward. And if she applies to the infortunes and afterward to the fortunes: he will lose in the beginning and win afterward. ¶ And in playing chess specifically, it is good for the Moon to apply to Mercury and then to Mars: because in chess there are diverse forms <note>referring to the different types of pieces</note>; and let both receive the Moon. ¶ And if the ascendant is a common sign <note>Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, or Pisces</note>, it signifies that neither he nor the other shall win. ¶ And in playing at dice, it is good for the Moon to apply to Venus or Mercury. ¶ And when a fortune is in the ascendant, the one beginning the play will win. And if with this there is an infortune in the 7th house, the other will lose much. And if the lord of the ascendant is in the midheaven, he who begins will win. ¶ And if the lord of the ascendant aspects the lord of the 7th house by opposition, it signifies that one will steal from the other. ¶ And if the Moon separates from Mercury and applies to the lord of the ascendant, it will happen to the one beginning the game that the win is shown to him. ¶ And when the Moon separates from Mercury and applies to the lord of the 7th house, it will happen to the other that it is shown to him. ¶ And when the lord of the ascendant is retrograde <note>appearing to move backward in the sky</note>, it signifies that the one beginning will play with fraud. ¶ And when Mercury is in the ascendant and the Moon is in the midheaven, it signifies they will leave the game as equals. ¶ And when Mars is in the ascendant, it signifies they will have many words and arguments over the game. ¶ And when Mercury is in the ascendant, it signifies they will tell many lies in that game. And when Saturn is in the ascendant, neither will win from the other, and they will part from the game out of boredom. ¶ And when Jupiter is in the ascendant, they will part with anger. ¶ And when Venus is in the ascendant, they will part cheerful and with good will. ¶ And when the Moon is in the ascendant, it signi-

<column-break/>

fies that he who was meant to win will win quickly. ¶ And when you play with the Moon in the ascendant: be careful not to start the game, for they would quickly win from you. ¶ And when the ascendant is a common sign and the lord of the ascendant is in a common sign, it signifies that others will play at that same game after them. ¶ And Messahala <note>an 8th-century Jewish-Persian astrologer</note> said: when you wish to play, look at which part the Moon is in—whether in the east or west, or in the south or north—and set yourself to sit so that your face is toward the Moon, and you shall win. ¶ And know that the east helps the north, and the west helps the south. ¶ And likewise, when you see two people playing and you wish to know which of them will win: look at which of them keeps his face toward the Moon, for that one shall win; however, in games of shingles <note>likely a game involving marking or pricking tablets</note> or anything that is pricked, see to it that the Moon is in moveable signs, and beware of Taurus or common signs. ¶ And it is good for the Moon to apply to the fortunes. ### ¶ Chapter 65. On lying with women.

When you wish to lie with women: look for those signs that have delight in that business, which are Aries, Capricorn, Leo, and Libra: for these signify great power in this and that they will not cease. ¶ And if the Moon with this applies to Venus and Mars, it will be better, because Venus signifies the joy they will have with one another and delightful conversation, and Mars signifies much sperm. ¶ And beware that the Moon does not apply to Saturn: for it signifies coldness, boredom, and a loathing of that act. ¶ And if the Moon applies to the Sun with reception <note>a mutual relationship between two planets</note>: it signifies great delight and agreement between both in that business. ¶ And beware that the Moon is not in Pisces, for it signifies that illnesses will occur there. And if the Moon is in Gemini, Libra, or Aquarius, which are human signs, it is good in this, for it signifies delight and joy. ¶ And if the Moon applies to Jupiter, it signifies that the woman will defend herself from that business by reason of the law. ¶ And if you wish to lie with a woman so that she does not conceive: place the Moon in Gemini, Leo, or Virgo, and let her apply to Venus and have no aspect to Jupiter. ¶ And be careful when you wish to lie with a woman so that she does not conceive that the Moon is not in Cancer, Scorpio, or Pisces, for these are signs of many children. ¶ And if the Moon aspects Mars, generation <note>conception</note> shall be prevented. ¶ And when Venus is in the ascendant in Libra or Pisces, he shall have much joy and delight. <margin>it will disturb him</margin> ¶ And when Saturn is in the 7th house, it will happen that he will cause discord between them.

### ¶ Chapter 66. On the 8th house and its elections.

The elections that are in this house are trials of death and looking into the causes of inheritances.

### Chapter 67. On the testament of death.

<image-desc>Decorative woodcut initial 'C' featuring floral and foliage motifs inside a square frame.</image-desc>

It is fitting for he who wishes to make his will <note>original: *testamentū*; a last will and testament</note> not to do so when the ascendant <note>the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon</note> and the Moon are in movable signs <note>Aries, Cancer, Libra, or Capricorn</note>: because this signifies that the will will not be upheld. It is, however, good in this matter if the Moon is decreasing in speed <note>original: *deficiens numero*; moving slower than its average daily motion</note> and increasing in light: and when it is not moving toward a planet existing under the rays <note>original: *sub radijs*; a planet so close to the Sun that its influence is hidden or weakened</note>: because that signifies he will die quickly, especially if the Moon is conjoined with Mars: nor should the Moon be in a square or opposition aspect to it: nor should Mars be in the ascendant or look upon it with a harmful aspect: because this signifies that the man will not change that will: and that he will die of that illness: nor will the will be observed, or it will be lost or stolen. However, if Saturn has the same positions with the ascendant and the Moon that we mentioned for Mars, it signifies that the man will still live: and that the will shall be guarded and observed during his life and even after his death. ¶ And if Jupiter or Venus is with the Moon and with the lord of the ascendant in such positions, it signifies that the one who makes the will should still live: and that he will yet make another will. And it is good for making a will firm that the ascendant, its lord, and the Moon be in firm, fixed signs <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, or Aquarius</note> because this signifies the firmness of the testament.

### Chapter 68. On matters of the incomes of the deceased.

<image-desc>Decorative woodcut initial 'C' featuring floral and foliage motifs inside a square frame.</image-desc>

It is fitting in this matter that you place in the 8th house <note>the house of death and inheritance</note> one of the houses of Venus or Jupiter <note>Taurus, Libra, Sagittarius, or Pisces</note>: and that the house itself and its lord be safe from misfortunes <note>afflictions from malefic planets like Mars or Saturn</note>: and that the same lord of the 8th house be in a succeeding house <note>the 2nd, 5th, 8th, or 11th houses</note>. And if it is in the 2nd house, it will be better for the one who remains:
<margin>The 8th house and its lord being safe, as we said before.</margin>
and it will be good if the degree of the 8th house is the term <note>a specific subdivision of a zodiac sign</note> of Jupiter or Venus if you can manage it: and that it looks upon the lord of the 8th house with a good aspect.

The elections that are in this house concern the choice of journeys and the transport of goods. On journeys from which a man wishes to return quickly. On journeys by water. On teaching songs and types of entertainment: on entering a city for one who has come from a journey.

### ¶ Chapter 71. On journeys for the sake of leisure.

<image-desc>A historiated decorative initial 'V' showing a traveler with a staff and cloak walking through a landscape of hills and a tree.</image-desc>
For one wishing to make a journey for the sake of **leisure** <note>original: *spaciandi*; walking or traveling for pleasure</note>: it is fitting that you place the Moon separating from a benefic and applying to a benefic: for this is good, and it signifies that he will be happy with those he meets, nor will he have sadness for those he leaves behind him. And if it happens that the Moon is in the Midheaven: he will be honored in his leisure and cheerful, and will rejoice in the places into which he enters, and in the places through which he passes. And if at the hour in which he moves to go for leisure the Moon is **void of course** <note>original: *cursu vacua*; when the Moon makes no further aspects before leaving its current sign</note>: and after its exit from that sign and entry into another it applies to Venus by aspect or conjunction: it signifies that he sets out for leisure or solace, yet he does not have great delight in that leisure or solace; but after he has entered into it and had companions and jesters, he will be cheered in that solace of his. And if, at the exit to a special and known place, the Moon and the ascendant are in signs of the body <note>possibly referring to human-shaped signs like Gemini or Virgo</note>, and the Moon applies to a benefic, and a benefic is in the ascendant: it signifies that he will rejoice in the place to which he goes, and that he will move from that place to another in which he will be glad and enjoy leisure more than in the first. ¶ And he who moves to go for leisure while the Moon is in an **earthy sign** and applying to Venus, and the ascendant is likewise an earthy sign, and both the Moon and Venus aspect the ascendant: he will have many comforts, many places, and good sights. ¶ And if the ascendant is a **fixed sign**: he will take leisure in beautiful works and labors and palaces, and his solace will have a good end. ¶ And he who goes out for leisure with the Moon conjoined with Mars by body or applying to it by a bad aspect: he will stop on the journey or fall, and will go through heights and valleys. ¶ And in this, the worst that can be in movements for leisure is that the Moon aspects Saturn in any manner: for it signifies that he will be solitary and sad. And in this it is also bad that the Moon be separated from a benefic and applying to a malefic: for this signifies that he will have poor solace in the place from which he departed and in the place to which he goes. ¶ Yet for him who wishes to **leisure by water**, it is fitting that you place the ascendant in a watery sign at the entry into the water, and that Venus be in the ascendant or in the Midheaven. ¶ And if you wish to stay long upon the water and go upon it for a long time: place the ascendant in a fixed sign, and the Moon in the Midheaven: for this signifies that you will last long on the water and will have a good journey and good winds. ¶ And if Venus is applied with the Moon from a common sign, the men who join themselves with them in that journey will rejoice with them. ¶ And if you wish that the journey not be prolonged, nor last long upon the water: place the ascendant in a **movable sign** <note>Aries, Cancer, Libra, or Capricorn</note> and some fortune in it, and beware that no malefic is in it; for if a fortune is there, it signifies that they will come out from there healthy and glad. ¶ And if a malefic is there: they will perhaps come out from there fleeing in fear. ¶ And if Mars is in the ascendant: it signifies that anger will happen, and they will not have pure wills toward one another. ¶ And for him who wishes to go for leisure by **land**, place the ascendant in an earthy sign, and let a fortune be in it. And if you wish that the journey last, place the ascendant in a movable sign: because it is better for moving forward; yet if you wish to stay and rest there...

### ¶ Chapter 72. For him who wishes to return quickly from his journey.

<image-desc>Decorative drop cap 'Q' with floral patterns.</image-desc>

**W**hen you wish for this: place Jupiter in **quadrature** <note>original: *qđratura*; a "square" aspect of 90 degrees, often considered tense but active</note> to the Sun, and Venus in its **sextile** <note>an aspect of 60 degrees, considered harmonious</note>: or joined with it: and place the Moon between the two **fortunes** <note>the "benefic" or helpful planets, Jupiter and Venus</note> separating from one and applying to the other: and let the Moon be increasing in light and in its number <note>referring to its daily speed</note>: because this signifies that he may return quickly, safe, and with profit.

### ¶ Chapter 73. Concerning journeys that a man wishes to make in secret.

<image-desc>Decorative drop cap 'D' with floral patterns.</image-desc>

**Ptolemy** said: in a matter such as this, you should place the Moon **under the rays of the Sun** <note>original: *sub radijs solis*; when a planet is so close to the Sun that it becomes invisible to the eye</note>, separated from the Sun and applying to a **fortune** and free from **malefics** <note>original: *infortunis*; harmful planets like Mars or Saturn</note>: and especially let them not be in its **angles** <note>the four most powerful houses: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th</note>: because they damage it greatly. ¶ And the ***Almagest*** <note>Ptolemy’s famous work on astronomy; here the author cites it for astrological advice</note> said: when you wish to do any of your business privately, and wish that it never be discovered or appear, you should begin it when the Moon is in **Scorpio** and **under the earth** <note>in the houses below the horizon, where things are hidden</note>. ¶ And others have said it is good in this case for the Moon to be under the rays of the Sun: then it happens exactly as Ptolemy said, applying to fortunes and free from malefics. ¶ And **Alhaçen son of Zahel** <note>likely referring to the astronomer/astrologer Ibn al-Haytham or, more probably in this context, the scholar Sahl ibn Bishr</note> said when you wish to do any thing in secret and hidden: you should place the Moon or the **Lord of the Ascendant** <note>the planet that rules the sign currently rising</note> under the rays of the Sun, but not **combust** <note>extreme proximity to the sun (within 8.5 degrees) was thought to "burn" or weaken a planet, while being "under the rays" (up to 15 degrees) provided a cloak of invisibility</note>; rather, let them be remote from the body of the Sun: and fortunate and safe from malefics: and let neither the Moon nor the Sun look upon the ascendant: nor let one look upon the other by any **aspect**. ¶ And if you wish for safety in that matter: make the Lord of the Ascendant and the Moon fortunate while they are

<column-break/>

under the rays: and let one of them be looked upon by

fortunes. ¶ And if you wish for that business to be done for the sake of causing harm, you should make them unfortunate. And always when the Moon and the **significator** <note>the planet representing the specific goal</note> of the matter are in the "angle of the earth" <note>the 4th house, at the very bottom of the chart</note>: or under the earth: they signify hidden things.

### ¶ Chapter 74. Concerning journeys by water.

<image-desc>Decorative drop cap 'S' with floral patterns and a bird (possibly an eagle or swan) inside the letter body.</image-desc>

**K**now that in the entering of water and journeys by water: and in the care of ships, it is necessary to have much consideration and to follow the **roots** <note>original: *radices*; the foundational principles or starting moments</note> of elections: and to consider the beginnings of this matter: because it is a thing that cannot be hidden from the wise of this science: for the greatest "root" in journeys by sea is the **ascendant** in which that ship was begun: because it signifies how long that ship is to last: and what kind of safety that ship will have, and those who go in it. And I have heard from men whom I believed, and I have seen ships that went by sea for 10 years and more, and never did an accident or any danger happen to those going in them. And I have seen other ships to which accidents always happened by the property of the winds, or by encountering enemies: or by another manner of accidents that happen at sea. And other ships that are destroyed and lost, both they and all who go in them: wherefore that which we said concerning the beginning of building the ship is one "root." And the second root is the hour that the ship is sent out. The third root is the hour in which it is placed in the water: and this is a strong root. The fourth root is the hour that a man enters the ship. And the fifth root is the hour that the ship moves: and this is a very much stronger root. And all these roots are to be observed. And I have seen men who entered a ship while the Moon was as fortunate as could be, joined to Jupiter by body in **Pisces** which is a watery sign: and Venus was looking upon them with a good aspect: and the malefics were falling away from them: yet it did not happen that the ship moved: because they had no wind: yet after some days they had wind: and they moved on the **day of Mercury** <note>Wednesday</note> at the third hour of the day: the Moon being in Scorpio, and the ascendant and the locations of the planets were according to what you will see in the following figure.
