¶ And I saw in the second part of the book of natures <note>A common title for medieval encyclopedias or astrological manuals</note> which speaks of the judgments of the hours: that he who goes by sea in the **hour of Saturn** <note>In planetary hours, Saturn’s hour is often considered unlucky for travel</note> will die or be lost: either the sea will cast him onto land or into distant islands and he will be lost. It happened to that ship just as that book related: for which reason it is appropriate for every astrologer wishing to make an **election** <term>election: the practice of choosing the most favorable astrological moment to start a project</term> for going by sea: that he first look at the election for making the ship: and afterwards when it was bought: and afterwards when they placed it in the water: and afterwards when they entered into it: and afterwards when it moves. And if he cannot have these elections, let him not involve himself in making an election for that ship: because great errors could happen there: for when I saw that ship in the hour of Saturn as we said: I said to one of my companions who understood something of this science: "these men are lost": and after a short time had passed, they all lost themselves.

### ¶ Chapter 75. On buying a ship, entering it, and moving it

Now we have already told in chapter 59 the election for making a ship: now we wish to show the elections for buying a ship and entering it as well as moving it: and all these are similar: and joined one to another. ¶ **Dorotheus** <note>Dorotheus of Sidon, a 1st-century astrological poet highly influential in the medieval period</note> said when you wish to buy a ship or make it, begin this with **Jupiter** and **Venus** being in the **angle of the earth** <note>The "Imum Coeli" or 4th house, representing the bottom of the sky and the foundations of a matter</term> in a **watery sign** <note>Cancer, Scorpio, or Pisces</note> or in a sign of the nature of Jupiter or Venus. ¶ And good signs for the **Moon** in this matter are **Taurus** or **Gemini** or the beginning of **Cancer** or **Virgo** or **Sagittarius** or the last degrees of **Capricorn**: because the beginning of Capricorn is earthy: and its end is watery. ¶ And when the Moon or the **ascendant** <note>The zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon</note> is in **Pisces**, it is best: yet in this, better than all signs is Taurus, and afterwards Pisces: and afterwards Gemini: and afterwards <margin>for a long time</margin> the last degrees of Capricorn. ¶ And afterwards it is fitting that the **Sun** be in a **trine** <note>A favorable 120-degree angle</note> of the **fortunes** <note>the "benefic" planets, Jupiter and Venus</note>: and the Moon increased in number, motion, light, and latitude, and in aspect from any of the fortunes. ¶ And beware that **Mars** is not looking at <note>original: *aspiciens*; making an astrological aspect to</note> the ascendant nor the Moon: because when Mars has harmed one of these: it signifies that the ship will have a bad end by occasion of fire or robbery: and things similar to these. ¶ And if a ship is begun and the Moon is in **Aquarius** and Mars and the Sun are joined with her by body <note>a physical conjunction</note> or looking at her from a **quartile** <note>a 90-degree angle of tension</note> or **opposition** <note>a 180-degree angle</note>: it signifies that that ship will cast its cargo into the water to free the men from death, or there will be great fear. ¶ Yet if the Moon is not in Aquarius, it will either be burned in the day: or a great loss will happen to it down to the bottom of the earth. ¶ And if the Moon is not in a watery sign: and is in the aspects of the Sun and Mars which we said before: it signifies that that ship will perish: and all who have entered into it: and they will be submerged: and will go to the bottom of the earth. ¶ And if the Moon is not in a watery sign: and is in a **dry sign** <note>Aries, Leo, Sagittarius, Taurus, Virgo, or Capricorn</note>: and in the aspects of the Sun and Mars which we said before: it signifies that the ship will be broken in the sea by striking against some rocky reef: or that which is similar to it, and it will be wrecked in the sea: and the greater part of the things that were in it will be lost. ¶ And if the Moon is not in a dry sign: and is in a **human sign** <note>Signs depicted as humans: Gemini, Virgo, Libra, and the first part of Sagittarius and Aquarius</note> and in the aforementioned aspects of Mars and the Sun: it signifies that that ship will encounter robbers

<column-break/>

and enemies who will kill those who are in the ship: so that they will be lost and that ship will be submerged by that occasion.

### ¶ Chapter 76. On putting a ship into the water.

If at the hour in which the ship is put into the water the Moon is in **Aries** or the beginning of Aries: and the fortunes have beheld this and not the **infortunes** <note>the "malefic" planets, Saturn and Mars</note>: it signifies that it will go well and without labor. ¶ And if the Moon is <margin>aspects except from a fortune [are] misfortunes</margin> in Taurus in the manner we said before: it signifies that they will have many waves in the sea: and if an infortune has beheld it: it signifies it will perish. ¶ And if the Moon is in Gemini, having passed eight degrees: it will be good: because it signifies utility and a good journey: except that it signifies they will make a long journey: and return late. ¶ And if the Moon is in Cancer, it signifies they will have few waves: and that they will go well and profit and gain in that journey. ¶ And when it is in **Leo**: it signifies that damage will happen to them in the sea. And if the infortunes have beheld it there: it signifies losses in diverse ways. ¶ And if it is in Virgo: it signifies they will return late. ¶ And if it is in **Libra**, having passed 10 degrees: it signifies that it is not good: because it has a bad significance in journeys of sea and land. ¶ And if it is in **Scorpio**: it signifies they will have a good journey, yet some fear will happen to them. ¶ And if it is in **Sagittarius**: it signifies they will have damage through waves. ¶ And if it is in Capricorn, having passed 9 degrees of it, it will be good: and it signifies good: they will however have some labor. ¶ And when it is in Aquarius: it signifies they will be delayed and will have labor in the journey: yet the end will be good. ¶ And if the Moon is in Pisces: it signifies losses and anxieties. ¶ And these aforementioned significations are when the Moon is in the signs without having any aspect of a fortune or infortune. ¶ And when the Moon is **below the earth** <note>Below the horizon, in the 1st through 6th houses</note> with infortunes or fortunes: it is bad: because when it is below the earth and **Saturn**, who is heavy, is with her: it signifies that great losses and labors will happen to the men who are in that ship: and they will have bad winds and strong waves: and water will enter the ship: and they will die because of it and be lost. ¶ And when the Moon is below the earth: and Saturn is **stationary** <note>appearing to stand still in the sky before changing direction; a state of great intensity</note> looking at her from a **third** <note>a sextile aspect, 60 degrees</note>: it signifies that the greater part of the things which they carry in the ship they will cast into the sea for the sake of saving their persons: and after many pains and labors they will be freed. ¶ And if the Moon is below the earth and Saturn has beheld her from a third as we said before: and is not stationary: it similarly signifies that they will escape after many labors: anxieties and dangers: it will however be less than the other: because when Saturn is stationary: his aspect is worse: yet if the **constellation** <note>the planetary arrangement</note> is as we said and **Mercury** is with Saturn: that loss is diminished and weakened. ¶ Similarly if the fortunes have looked at Saturn: his evil and loss is diminished: and especially if the fortunes are in good places and supported and looking at Saturn. ¶ And know that when a ship is put in the water, if Saturn is not in the aforementioned constellations harming the Moon as we said before: it nevertheless happens that he is in the sign in which he was at the **nativity** <note>birth chart</note> of that man or in the fourth or opposite or **triplicity** <note>signs of the same element</note>...

### ¶ Chapter 77. On learning sciences and instructions.

It is suitable in this that the **Ascendant** be a **human sign** <note>Signs represented by humans: Gemini, Virgo, Libra, and the first half of Sagittarius</note>: and the **Moon** in a **human sign** and the **Lord of the Ascendant** in the **Midheaven** <note>The highest point in the sky at the time</note> as though entering the Midheaven: and that the **Lord of the Midheaven** and the **Midheaven** have an agreement with the **Lord of the Ascendant**: and that the **Moon** be conjoined with **Mercury** or applying to him with a good aspect: and that **Mercury** be in a good state, fortunate and strong. ¶ And it is good in this that **Mercury** aspects the **Lord of the Ascendant**: and that the **Moon** is not diminished in light <note>Waning</note> nor descending in latitude. And prepare the **ninth house** <note>The house governing higher learning, philosophy, and religion</note> as much as you can: yet for learning to write, it must be inspected as we said before and more: because the **tenth [house]** is to be prepared since it signifies the matter of masteries: and in writing there is science and a work of mastery: and therefore it ought not to be postponed in sciences and masteries.

### ¶ Chapter 78. On learning songs and other forms of entertainment.

It is suitable in this to prepare the **Moon**, **Venus**, and **Mercury**: because these are the roots of this matter: and when **Venus** is in any of her **dignities** <note>A place in the zodiac where she has specific power</note>: and **Mercury** similarly is applying to her: and the **Moon** similarly is in any of her dignities: either in their [aspects]: or separating herself from **Mercury**: and applying to **Venus**: and that the **Ascendant** be a sign suitable to this matter: and **Venus** have dignity in it. ¶ And if **Venus** and **Mercury** both have dignity in the degree of the **Ascendant**, as if it were the **house** of one and the **term** of the other: it will be best: nor should **Venus**, nor the **Moon**, nor **Mercury** be removed from the **angles**: unless the **Moon** were in the <margin>house</margin> **ninth house**: because she is the Lord of science: and if she were fortunate and strong there: it signifies no evil: nor loss in this matter: rather it signifies the completion of the matter, with other significators being fortunate and well-placed as we said before. ¶ And similarly if the **Lord of the Ascendant** is in the ninth, fortunate and strong: it will be best. ¶ And some wise men say that for learning that which is similar to it, it is good for the **Moon** to be in **Capricorn**. ¶ And for learning the **drum** and its kind: it is good for the **Moon** to be at the end of **Leo**. ¶ And for learning the **trumpet** and every other instrument that is touched with the mouth: it is good that she be in **signs having no voice**: or which are **mute** <note>Water signs (Cancer, Scorpio, Pisces) were considered "mute" because the creatures they represent make no sound</note>. ¶ And for learning **noted songs** or reading: it is good: that she be in **signs having a voice** and especially in **Gemini**...

### Chapter 79. On the entry into a city by one who comes from a journey.

Know that the way of following this matter is in arranging the second house and its lord in this manner: place a **benefic** <term>benefic: a "lucky" planet, usually Jupiter or Venus</term> and its lord in it upon the earth: and the **Moon** in the earth or the fifth or eleventh [house] applying to a planet receiving her, whether it be a **benefic** or a **malefic**. ¶ And it is very much to be feared if the **Moon** is in an "angle of the earth" <note>The IC or 4th house cusp, the lowest point in the sky</note> or in the 8th or 6th or 12th [houses]. ¶ And if you have placed the **Moon** in the second [house] in this, received and fortunate, it is not an evil thing. ¶ And if he who enters wishes to stay in that place for a long time: place the lord of the second and the **Moon** in the angles. ¶ And if the **Moon** should have reception with **Saturn** from a good aspect: it is good in this. ¶ And if the one entering wishes to leave the city quickly: place the **Moon** in the third <margin>Delay</margin> or fourth, received: because this signifies that he will leave there quickly with what he desires. ¶ And if you place the lord of the second in the **Ascendant**, it is good there. And the lord of the **Ascendant** in the second is similarly good. ¶ And if the one entering wishes to obtain something from the king, it is appropriate that you arrange the "mid-heaven" <note>The 10th house, representing authority</note>. And if he wishes to procure or obtain [something] through lawful trade: arrange the lords of the 11th and 2nd. ¶ Generally, I say of all those entering, of whatever sort they may be: that you ought to look to the second house and its lord: so that they are safe from unfortunate rays and falls. ¶ And if the lord of the second is "combust" <term>combust: a planet weakened by being too close to the Sun</term>: it signifies that the one entering that city will die during that entry. ¶ And similarly it is worst if the lord of the second is in the seventh: and even more so if it is a **malefic**: because it signifies damage to the body and property of the one entering: and that he will have many anxieties and many who will move causes and quarrels against him, and an evil state regarding his property and his company. ¶ And if the **Moon** is in the "angle of the earth" <note>the 4th house</note>: it signifies that the one entering will die in that city before he departs from it. ¶ And the best choice that may be found for an entry is that **Jupiter** be the lord of the second: and that he be in the eleventh or second, having an application with the **Moon**: because this is the best choice that can be made for an entry. ¶ And do not forget the "Part of Fortune" but place it in the angles: or in the eleventh or fifth: because it is the best indication for the health of the body and for the sake of substance, and for the one entering so that he may have his petitions easily granted. ¶ And similarly it is good that this Part [of Fortune] applies to the lord of the house of the **Moon**: and this is a good indication for the end [of the matter] as well.

### Chapter 80. On the tenth house and its elections.

These are the choices of this house: entering into a dignity <note>A position of high rank or office</note> and leaving it: receiving an *alcaydia* <note>original: "alcaydiam"; the office of a governor or judge</note>: in the making of *alcaydos* <note>original: "alcaydos"; governors or magistrates</note> or judges: in receiving rents or in making an *almuterif* <note>original: "almuterif"; a market inspector or financial official</note>: in going with the king: in entering before the king: in showing

### Chapter 81. For entering a dignity.

**Alfayat** <note>Abu 'Ali al-Khayyat, a 9th-century Persian astrologer</note> said: Guard yourself in this from the "luminaries" <note>The Sun and Moon</note> and clear them from misfortunes, and place them received in their places, and place the **benefics** in the **Ascendant** and in their angles, they themselves being direct <note>Moving forward, not retrograde</note>: and the best of them is **Jupiter**: and let the **Sun** be in his own house free from misfortunes. ¶ And when the **malefics** are more powerful than the **benefics** and are safe from retrogradation: and the **benefics** are damaged, work by the **malefics**: because there will be no evil in this. And do not perform any [election for] dignity which is of the nature and manner of arms unless you make **Mars** a participant: and let him be supported and in a good state: or let him be the lord of the **Ascendant** not damaged. ¶ And beware lest the help of **Mars** be in any place other than the **Ascendant**: or his part in another place. ¶ And **Alhasen**, son of Zahel <note>Sahl ibn Bishr, a famous Jewish astrologer and mathematician of the 9th century</note> said: when <margin>† to accept</margin> you wish to arrange a dignity, arrange the **Moon** and the lord of her house: and place her in a good place from the **Ascendant**: and the lord of the **Ascendant** in a good place in the figure <note>The horoscope chart</note>: and in one of the houses of **Mars** or **Jupiter**: and let **Jupiter** aspect the **Ascendant** from the third or fifth [house]: because it will be better: and place a "fixed sign" in the **Ascendant**: and let the lord of the seventh be safe from retrogradation and combustion and from misfortunes: because such a choice signifies that he who receives the dignity will be powerful: lawful and truthful in his deeds and things. ¶ **Alfadal**, son of Zahel <note>Likely the brother or son of Sahl ibn Bishr</note> said: good choices for receiving crowns and kingdoms and great lordships are that the **Moon** be clear: safe: and not in the signs of the houses of the **malefics**: because if she is there: it signifies that he will be harsh: and will perform injustices and evil deeds: and similarly let her not be in **Cancer**: because it also signifies damages and injustices: and worse than these is if the lord of the **Ascendant** is in **Cancer**: or in any house of the **malefics**. ¶ And when the **Ascendant** is a fixed sign and the **Moon** is in a good place in the figure in an angle or succedent [house] and is fortunate: it signifies that that kingdom or lordship will endure for a long time. And for **Mars**, if it is in **Leo**: or in his triplicity. <margin>† or expanded</margin> ¶ And if there is a **benefic** in the **Ascendant**: it signifies the goodness of that king: and good morals and good deeds. ¶ And if there is a **malefic** there, judge evil: because **Mars** signifies depravity and the retention of long anger and deceptions: and **Saturn** signifies there baseness and very small things and slowness in deeds. ¶ And when the **Sun** is in the **Ascendant**: it signifies many military forces: and many helpers: and high and great fame, and he shall be named far and wide: and great lordship: and a high kingdom. ¶ And if **Jupiter** is in the **Ascendant**: it signifies that he will be upright and of upright morals: and of upright journeys and judgments: and a lover of good and of the law and victorious: and he shall have many friends. ¶ And if **Mercury** is there: it signifies that he will stand apart because he would not want [common] solace: and he will be wise and of good morals: and he will know how to perform his deeds through morals and the masteries of good thoughts: and in himself of great price. ¶ And if **Venus** is there: it signifies that he will have much pride...

### Chapter 82. On the election for a dignity of the land, or for rents or law.

**P**one <margin>+ better</margin> <note>The woodcut 'P' depicts a landscape with trees and a building, perhaps symbolizing the "land" mentioned in the chapter title.</note> Place the **Moon** in this case in some house of **Saturn** <note>Capricorn or Aquarius</note> applying to **Saturn** from a trine or sextile: and let it be at the beginning of the month: and let the benefics look upon it: because this signifies the good fortune of that matter, and that it will last a long time. ¶ And you shall know its durability from the **terms** <term>terms: specific sub-divisions of zodiac signs ruled by different planets</term> in which these planets are located: for if both are in the terms of the benefics and both planets are well-fortuned: it signifies their minor years in number of years. ¶ And if the sign of the Midheaven at this hour is a **fixed sign**: it signifies that the dignity which he holds, or that office, will be good as long as it lasts. ¶ And if that sign is **common** <term>common: also known as mutable signs (Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces), associated with change</term> and well-fortuned, and the benefics look upon it as we have said: it signifies that he will have two offices, or will change himself from one office to another. ¶ And if the sign is **mobile** <term>mobile: also known as cardinal signs (Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn)</term>: fears and labors will happen to him many times: yet they will not hinder him, nor cause loss, provided the Midheaven is strengthened and fortunate by the presence of benefics in it, or by their aspect as we have said.

### Chapter 87. On placing a king in the house of his dominion.

### ¶ Chapter 91. On learning to bear arms.

It is fitting in this that the ascendant and the Moon are in the <term>triplicity</term> of <term>Aries</term> <note>the fire signs: Aries, Leo, and Sagittarius</note>, and let Mars be fit in a good place and state; and let the Moon be in her <term>fall</term> <note>original: "casu" — a position of weakness</note>, especially for learning to bear arms while riding <note>original: "equitando"</note>. ¶ And if the Moon in this is in her <term>exaltation</term> <note>a position of great strength</note>, it will be much better. ¶ And it is best that the Lord of the Ascendant be in his exaltation. And if you cannot have him there, place him in the <term>Midheaven</term> <note>original: "medio celi" — the highest point of the chart</note> or entering into it. ¶ And some wise men say that in learning to wrestle, it is especially good for the Moon to be in the separation of <term>Gemini</term>.

### ¶ Chapter 92. On learning to swim through waters.

It is good in this for the Moon to be in <term>watery signs</term>, and that the Lord of the Ascendant be in the Midheaven or entering into it and <term>fortunate</term> <note>unafflicted by "bad" planets</note>; and let the Moon be ascending in the North, and in some of her dignities; and the best sign for this is <term>Cancer</term>.

### ¶ Chapter 93. On the 11th House and its elections.

The elections of this house are: beginning things which a man does to have a good name and good fame; in making any petition; in fulfilling promises; and in seeking love and friendship.

### ¶ Chapter 94. On things done for acquiring a good name and fame.

It is fitting that you arrange the beginning of the 11th house and its Lord; and place the ascendant in one of the signs of <term>Jupiter</term> <note>Sagittarius or Pisces</note>. And it will be better if you can place Jupiter in the 11th house or in the ascendant, or aspecting them with a good aspect. ¶ And it is also fitting that Jupiter be well-placed and safe from <term>infortunes</term> <note>the planets Saturn and Mars</note>. ¶ And if the Lord of the 11th is in the ascendant, or the Lord of the Ascendant is in the 11th, it is good. ¶ And it is good that the Sun be safe from infortunes and in the <term>10th house</term>, and the Moon applying to it by a trine or sextile. And if the Moon with this is separating herself from the Lord of the 11th or from Jupiter, it will be better, because it signifies that the matter will be of a famous, manifest, and complete name. ¶ And also, it is fitting that all 

<column-break/>

significators aspect one another with good aspects, and especially the <term>luminaries</term> <note>the Sun and Moon</note> and the ascendant and the tenth, and that they are <term>received</term>. ¶ And if you cannot arrange all of them, arrange whichever of them you can, always observing the "roots" <note>the foundations</note> of the elections.

### ¶ Chapter 95. On fulfilling promises and making petitions.

It is fitting in this that you arrange the eleventh house and its Lord, and the <term>Part of Fortune</term> <note>original: "partem fortune" — a calculated point in a chart representing prosperity</note> and its Lord; and let both or one of them aspect the ascendant. And let the Lord of the Ascendant and the Moon be received by the Lord of the 11th and by the planet signifying the thing sought. For the ascendant and its Lord are the significators of the petitioner, and the <term>7th house</term> and its Lord are of the person from whom it is sought. Therefore, it is fitting that the 7th house be safe, otherwise the petition is denied; and the Moon is the significatrix of the thing sought. ¶ Afterward, if the petition is to old men or any of those who are of the nature of <term>Saturn</term>, place the degree of the 11th house in a dignity of Saturn. And if the petition is to a scribe or from the significations of <term>Mercury</term>, place the eleventh house in a dignity of Mercury—namely, the exaltation, house, or <term>term</term>. And arrange the planet that is the significator of him from whom it is sought; thus, if he is an old man, arrange Saturn; and by this reasoning, you shall do for all planets. ¶ <term>Al-Tabari</term> <note>original: "atabari" — a famous 9th-century Persian astrologer and physician</note> said: it is fitting in this that Mercury be applying to Jupiter and <term>Venus</term>, and that the Lord of the Midheaven be compatible with the Lord of the Ascendant. ¶ And if the question is concerning wealth <note>original: "suba" for "substantia"</note>, arrange the <term>2nd house</term> and the Lord of the Ascendant, so that between the Lord of the 2nd house and the Lord of the Ascendant there is an amicable application, and no infortune cuts between them; and that the Lord of the 11th and the Lord of the Part of Fortune aspect him with good aspects. ¶ And when it is for the sake of a woman or marriage, do with the 7th house and its Lord what we said regarding the 2nd house and its Lord. And in this way, you may do for the other houses.

### ¶ Chapter 96. On seeking love and friendship.

For seeking love and friendship, it is fitting that the Moon be well-placed, and similarly the 11th house and its Lord, and that both be received by Venus by a trine aspect. And if the reception is by house or exaltation, it will be better. ¶ And if it is not such, let there be a trine aspect and let the Moon be received by Jupiter or by the Lord of her own house. And if the Moon is not such, nor in any of the dignities of Venus, let her be safe. ¶ And if the friendship is for the sake of profiting from wealth, let the Part of Fortune be in the ascendant; if for an inheritance, in the <term>4th house</term>; and according to this, you shall do for all other houses.

### ¶ Chapter 97. On the 12th House and its elections.

The elections of this house are: running horses so that one might defeat another. Also the hour in which a king or another might capture his enemy who is less powerful than him.

### ¶ Chapter 98. On the racing of horses.

A certain wise man said that he who wishes to win in racing horses, when he begins to go from his house, let him place the <term>Lord of the Hour</term> <note>the planet ruling the specific hour of the day</note> in the ascendant. ¶ <term>Al-Kindi</term> <note>original: "alkindus" — a 9th-century Arab philosopher and "Father of Arab Philosophy"</note> said that with this he will always win, observing the roots of the elections. ¶ And if the Lord of the Hour is in the 10th house, he will run in the middle, between the first and the last. And if he is in the 7th house, he will run with those at the back. And if he is in the <term>angle of the earth</term> <note>the 4th house</note>, he will be further back and remain behind. And beware lest the Lord of the Hour be in his fall, because it signifies that the beast will fall.

### Chapter 99: On the hour in which a king may capture his enemy who is less powerful than he.

**When** you wish to choose a time for a king to capture his enemy: see that the 12th house <note>the house of hidden enemies and imprisonment</note> is unfortunate, and its ruler likewise unfortunate and weak. And if its misfortune comes from the ruler of the **Ascendant** <note>the sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of the action</note>, it will be better. And if this is not possible: at the beginning of the journey, see that the **Moon** is in an unfortunate position relative to the **Sun**, and that the **Sun** is in a good place. And if she [the Moon] is made unfortunate by some other planet and not the **Sun**, it will be even better. Al-Tabari <note>original: "atabari"; a Persian astrologer and astronomer</note> said that when a king or another person wishes to capture an enemy of lesser value than himself: let the **Moon** be in **conjunction** <note>occupying the same degree</note> or **opposition** <note>180 degrees apart</note> or in the **Burning Path** <note>original: "via combusta"; a specific section of the zodiac, usually late Libra and early Scorpio, considered unlucky</note>; or with the **Head** or with the **Tail** <note>the North and South Nodes of the Moon</note>; or let her be in the **Ascendant**; and this is because the **Ascendant** is an enemy to him by its opposition; or let her be in an **aspect** <note>a specific geometric angle</note> of the **malefics** <note>unlucky planets like Saturn or Mars</note>, or three days before her **eclipse**; and let the **Sun** be safe and clear from misfortunes; and let the **benefics** <note>lucky planets like Jupiter or Venus</note> be in the **Midheaven** <note>original: "medio celi"; the highest point in the sky</note>. And the more unfortunate the **Moon** is, the worse and greater the harm will be for that enemy; because the **Moon** is the **significator** <note>the planet representing the person or group</note> of the common people and the lower classes. Here end the elections received according to the twelve houses; and let God be greatly praised and thanked for it.

<margin>harm</margin>

### Chapter 100: On the meanings of the hours.

**These** are the meanings received from the book of Abu Ali al-Khayyat <note>original: "abaleç filij çaed"; an 8th-century astrologer</note> and from the book of Abu Ma'shar <note>original: "albumasar"</note> which is called the *Book of Natures*; and I have placed them here so that this book of ours may not be seen to be lacking in any of the sayings of the wise men. And after the hours, I have likewise spoken of the elections of the **Moon** according to the **Mansions** <note>28 specific segments of the zodiac based on the Moon's daily travel</note>; because a great part of the Arabs use them and work by them; and their roots are taken from the Indians and were received from their books—that is, from the books of Dorotheus <note>Dorotheus of Sidon, a 1st-century astrologer</note>. However, these elections of the hours and mansions do not have as much power as the elections we spoke of before, which are taken from the positions of the planets and their conditions; nevertheless, we can help ourselves with them.

### Concerning the hour of the Sun.

**The hour** of the **Sun** is unfortunate in every matter except for going before a king; however, do not go to him when the **Sun** has set; nor should you put on new clothing in this hour; nor should you be bled; nor should you give your property to anyone for the purpose of trade or for doing any business; nor should you begin to perform any acts of wisdom, governance, or instruction; and do not lie with a woman; however, you may buy weapons, and ride a horse, and go out from your land for hunting; but if you are already outside, do not enter your house. And this hour is good for receiving a high office, and for having favor with a king or a lord, and for receiving a guarantee of safety so that you are never petitioned [sued], and for profiting.

<column-break/>

<margin>or</margin>

And if you give capital [money] in this same hour, the one who receives it will die and the capital will be lost. And he who falls sick in this hour will suffer a strong fever and will many times die; in a way that will cause him harm.

### Concerning the hour of Venus.

**It is good** in this hour to ride a horse, but do not enter any ship; seek governance in it, and involve yourself in jokes and comforts; play at chess in it, and go with women for amusement, and depart from your land. However, if you are outside, do not enter your house. And perform marriage with a woman, and drink medicines and spices. Let no blood be taken from your vein nor by cupping; do not plant trees nor sow any seed; do not strike your male or female servant; cut your clothes; and do not sleep when you are able to stay awake. He who begins a journey in this hour will have good and profit from women, or something similar. It is good in this hour to do whatever pertains to women and all painted and beautiful cloths, and to lie with women and be bold and whatever else. And he who receives capital [money] will scatter it on women, vices, and delights. And if anyone falls sick, he has that sickness by reason of anxieties or some error that happened to him, or some sorcery that a woman did to him or something similar.

### Concerning the hour of Mercury.

**Ride** in this hour every beast: mule and she-ass; and write a document, and send messengers, and give your property for trade; and lend whatever you wish to lend, and receive what is owed to you; and drink medicines, and plant trees, and go before the king. Yet do not perform marriage with a woman, nor buy an inheritance or land; nor enter your house when you are outside; nor buy servants; nor move yourself from one house to another; nor release anyone from prison. But begin every building; dig wells and ditches; ask no one for anything. It will be good for one beginning a journey, and he will have good and profit from it. Place a boy in every discipline, such as for writing letters and for [the education of] daughters. It will be good to do trade, to send messengers, to litigate, and to give and receive. He who receives capital will pay it back well and in a good manner; and he who gives it will be satisfied with it, and the one with the other.

### Concerning the hour of the Moon.

<margin>+ the book of natures</margin>
**Do not** begin any building in it; nor buy any medicine for healing; do not cut cloths; nor buy cattle or pigs or their offspring. Cut trees; buy fruit; dig ditches and wells; ride horses; honor women; give your son to learn letters and writing; pursue your enemy in this hour; depart from your land but do not enter into it. And it is said that he who makes a journey in the hour of the **Moon** will have good in it by reason of the death of some man or a partnership; however, if the **Moon** is in an earthy sign <note>Taurus, Virgo, or Capricorn</note>, this judgment is condemned. He who gives capital will have great labor to recover it, until he despairs of its recovery; afterward he will recover it, but not all of it.

**Do** not drink medicine during this hour: neither cut fabric nor put on new clothes: nor shave your head: nor trim your hair: nor board any ship: nor even leave your home if you wish to return that day. And seek out your enemy and the fugitive: buy weapons, but do not buy male or female servants: enter into your partnership: and write documents: ride every kind of donkey or mule: do not throw stones or arrows at anyone: do not seek to commit homicide: nor have a legal dispute <term>placitū</term><note>original: "placitū"; a formal legal assembly or plea</note> with anyone: nor let blood from a vein or by cupping: buy all provisions and all food: receive a gift <term>erēniū</term><note>original: "erēniū" (strenium); a traditional gift, often for the New Year or a formal occasion</note>: he who goes out to make a journey will have much danger of imprisonment or many anxieties, or delay on the road. ### Concerning the hour of Jupiter.

**During** this hour, make a king join in marriage with women: do not strike your male or female servant: cut clothes in this hour: ride on horseback: do not drink "bad species" <note>likely referring to harsh medicinal concoctions or purgatives</note>: depart from your land: do not buy weapons: beware of fire and its flames: do not dig ditches: sow every seed and plant every tree: begin every building: place yourself to sit with kings: do not buy beasts but buy birds: do not enter a ship: nor throw a stone or anything else at anyone: speak with the king: nor let blood from a vein or by cupping: he who goes out to make a journey will have good profit in substance and in his business: utility from a side which he does not expect, and joys: it is good to go before a king, governors <term>alcaidos</term><note>original: "alcaidos"; from the Arabic "al-qadi", referring to judges or local governors</note>, and judges: he who gives capital will have good from it and profit and love with his participating partner: he who falls ill will quickly be healed.

### Concerning the hour of Mars.

The hour of Mars is to be dreaded in every matter and in every beginning and deed.

### Chapter 101. On elections according to the motion of the moon through the mansions.

**Alnath** <note>The first Lunar Mansion, from the Arabic "al-Nath" (the Butting Horns of Aries)</note> from the beginning of **Aries** up to 12 degrees, 11 minutes and 26 seconds is the first mansion. ¶ The Indians say that when the **Moon** is in this mansion: it is good to drink medicines: to put beasts to pasture: to make a journey on that day except in the second hour of the day. ¶ Dorotheus <note>original: "dozothius"; Dorotheus of Sidon, a 1st-century Hellenistic astrologer</note> says it is not good to enter into marriage when the **Moon** is in this mansion: nor even in all of **Aries**: nor to buy servants in it, because they will be evil and disobedient or will flee: however, it is good to buy beasts that are tamed

From 8 degrees, 34 minutes, 18 seconds of **Taurus** up to the 21st degree, 44 minutes of the same. ¶ The Indians say that when the **Moon** is in this mansion: it is good to sow: to wear new clothes: and to receive women and their ornaments: to begin every building of a villa or other: to make a journey except in the third part of that day.

## Chapter 102. Regarding the times in which there is confidence that petitions may be fulfilled.

<image-desc>Decorative initial letter 'A' containing foliage patterns and a bird figure.</image-desc>
<margin>form</margin>
<margin>form</margin>
In determining the timing of things, there are differences based on the different outcomes arising from the <term>judgments</term> <note>The astrologer's "judgment" or interpretation of a chart.</note>. Thus, there are some matters and fortunes that cannot last beyond the following day; there are other matters and fortunes that can last for days and no more; and others that can last for months. The greatest classification made in this regard is for things that last for years. ¶ In knowing and determining these times, it is necessary to have great intellect and precision along with astrological diligence. This is because the astrologer must know the natures and fortunes of the planets, the arrangements of <term>interrogations</term> <note>Horary astrology, where a chart is cast for the moment a question is asked.</note> and their natures. He must be able to divide and adapt these natures and judge according to his insight and precision. ¶ And I shall speak on this according to what my own intellect and senses have been able to reach.

¶ **Dorotheus** says times are understood in seven ways:
¶ First, by the distance between one <term>significator</term> <note>A planet representing a person or topic in the chart.</note> and another.
¶ Second, from the aspects <note>original: "convenientiis", the geometric relationships between planets.</note> that exist between two significators.
¶ Third, from the <term>projection of rays</term> <note>original: "athazir", a method of progressing a planet to a new location to time an event.</note> from one of them to the place of the other.
¶ Fourth, from the distance between a significator and the place of the thing being sought.
¶ Fifth, from the things that preserve the "gift" of a planet and those that add to or subtract from it.
¶ Sixth, from the agreement of the significator with the place of the thing being sought.
¶ Seventh, from the projection of rays of a planet to the place naturally suited to the matter.

¶ However, others—excepting **Ptolemy**—say these things are determined in five ways. ¶ And there are others who say in four ways; and this is according to the differences of their intellects, senses, and opinions. ¶ I wish to state here the opinions that seem best to me according to my own understanding, and may God guide me in this. ¶ I say that the time in which a matter should appear, and the indications that the planets signify in a <term>nativity</term> <note>A birth chart.</note> concerning good or evil, is when that same planet has dominion in a "division" <note>likely referring to "bounds" or planetary periods like Firdaria</note>; or by carrying it through a certain number of its years (be they minor, middle, or major); or through the ascensions of the sign in which it resides, giving to each degree one year according to the ascensions that it has in that place where it was in the sky. ¶ Afterward, if it happens that the planet which signified good or evil in the <term>root</term> <note>original: "radice", referring to the original birth chart.</note> becomes the lord of the "perfection" of the year, and in that year it reaches one of the three arrangements of its years, or the number of the ascensions of the sign, then the indication which it had signified in the root will appear and be strengthened.

Similarly, the signs are of four natures: fiery, airy, earthy, and watery. Of these, the "lightest" <note>Referring to the speed with which events manifest.</note> are fiery, followed by airy, then watery, and finally earthy. And of these, the "lightest" are the **movable** signs <note>Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn; also called Cardinal.</note>; after those, the **common** <note>Mutable signs.</note>, and finally the **fixed**. ¶ Similarly, the "lightest" in their ways are the masculine signs, and the "heavy" ones are the feminine. ¶ And what is between the Ascendant and the Midheaven is light by the nature of hours; and from the Midheaven to the West: more heavy by the nature of days; and from the West to the Angle of the Earth <note>The 4th house or IC.</note>: heavier by the nature of months; and from the Angle of the Earth to the Ascendant: much heavier by the nature of years. ¶ And the Moon, because she is light and swift, is of the nature of hours; Mercury and Venus are of the nature of days; the Sun and Mars are of the nature of months; Jupiter and Saturn are of the nature of years. ¶ And the greatest speed that the Moon and other planets have is when they are **oriental** <note>Rising before the Sun.</note>. And the greatest slowness and heaviness is when they are **occidental** <note>Setting after the Sun.</note>. ¶ And all times in every judgment are of five modes. One is by looking at the degrees that are between the planet that is **applying** <note>Moving toward an aspect with another planet.</note> and the other to which it applies, whether the application is by ray or by body, setting them as years, months, days, or hours according to the places in which they were in the figure and according to the signs in which they were, by the order we have mentioned concerning lightness and heaviness. ¶ The second mode is by looking at when a planet will be in such a degree and minute as the planet to which it applies currently is. ¶ The third is by looking at how much distance is between the two planets by equal degrees, not by ascen-

-sions, and setting that number as days. ¶ The fourth mode is by observing when the applying planet separates from the planet to which it was applying by degree and minute. ¶ The fifth mode is by observing the number of the minor years of the planet that is the ruler in the figure <note>The birth chart or horary chart.</note> and has the greatest signification in it: setting them as days, months, or years according to the order we have mentioned regarding lightness and heaviness. And you shall judge that the indication will happen and appear according to what you find regarding the lightness and heaviness of the planets, the lightness and heaviness of the signs, and the heaviness and lightness of the places in the figure; you shall mix one with the other, and according to what you find, you shall determine the hours, days, months, or years, and you will be made certain with God's help. ¶ And when the planet giving and the planet receiving <note>A technical relationship where one planet is in the sign ruled by another.</note> are both in the quarter of the sky that is from the Ascendant to the Midheaven, and both are oriental and there is **reception** between them: you shall give one hour or one day to each degree between them. For if you wish to determine time by reason of kings or lords, or revolutions of the world, or for the changes of the weather, you shall determine this from the Sun: because he is the indicator of kings, and through him the times are changed, as well as the status of the planets in those times. ¶ And the Moon is the indicator of journeys, embassies, changes, and every thing that is transformed and moved because of her speed, lightness, and the change of her own status. ¶ Similarly, the other planets signify things agreeable to their natures and properties, and each of them draws itself to its own part with its own indications. ## ¶ Here begins the eighth part of his Complete Book on the Judgments of the Stars concerning the revolutions of the years of the world; and first, the preface.

<image-desc>Decorative drop cap initial D with foliate patterns and a central vertical element.</image-desc>Haly, son of Abenragel <note>original: "hali filius aberagel", the Latinized name of the Arab astrologer Abū l-Ḥasan 'Alī ibn Abī l-Rijāl</note>, said: Praised be God, who is the Lord of subtleties, nobilities, rewards, and pieties; the creator of all creatures; the knower of hidden things; the understander of reasons and purities; the compensator for losses and occasions; the governor of the whole world and all things through His grace and power; the giver of rains through His mercy; the defender of those who have faith in Him; and the guardian of those who give themselves to Him. The King whom all kings obey, as well as His powers and glory; He is powerful to those who humble themselves before Him, and the powerful are humbled by Him. There is no opposition to His judgments, nor is there anyone who may contradict His deeds; complete in all goodness and piety; and may He be praised as is fitting.

<image-desc>Decorative drop cap initial I with foliate scrollwork.</image-desc>In this book I have joined together those sayings of the wise concerning the revolutions of years which pleased me and which seemed to me to adhere more to the truth than the sayings of others, and which I have tested and found to be truthful in their significations. ### ¶ Chapter one on the rules necessary for this matter, which cannot be omitted.

<column-break/>

<image-desc>Decorative drop cap initial S with foliate scrollwork and a small animal or bird head at the top.</image-desc>Know that the revolutions of the years of the world <note>original: "reuolutiōes annoz mundi", the practice of casting a chart for the moment the Sun enters Aries to predict the year's events</note> are taken in many ways and by many paths. For there are some of the wise who take them from the conjunctions of planets, and from the **ascendant of that law** <note>referring to the astrological chart for the founding of a religion or a nation's legal system</note>, and from the places of their applications, and from the application of the sign of conjunction, and from the application of the **degree of division**, and from the state it holds from the ascendant in the year the ascendant of the proposed conjunction of any planet arises, and from the sign in which that conjunction occurs. ¶ These are the roots upon which the wise agree and by which they judge. The community of astrologers in this matter judge the state of that year from the revolution; they take it similarly from the place of the conjunction <note>New Moon</note> or opposition <note>Full Moon</note> of the Sun and Moon preceding the entry of the Sun into the head of Aries <note>the Spring Equinox</note>, and from the ascendant of that conjunction or prevention, and from the planet that has the greatest dominion <note>the Almuten</note> in the aforesaid ascendant, and from the one who has the greatest dominion similarly in the place of the aforesaid conjunction or prevention. And he who judges by these roots must look into these aforementioned things, because he cannot omit these sayings if he wishes to distinguish and determine future accidents. ¶ Accidents are divided into four types: One is in visible accidents that happen in this world and are common to all, such as epidemics, the abundance of things or their lack, the changeability of the air, rains, and similar things. ¶ The second is similarly visible in this world, and this can be general or special, such as earthquakes, floods, sounds <note>perhaps thunder or celestial noises</note>, and the like. ¶ The third type is in matters that are specific to one nation, such as battles and similar things. ¶ The fourth is in matters that happen in the air, such as fires that appear, rays, tailed comets, and similar things. ¶ And there are some of the early wise men who take all these significations from the eclipses that occur in the years of the planetary conjunctions, mixing them with the revolutions of the years. Ptolemy <note>the 2nd-century authority on astronomy and astrology</note> is of this opinion, because his greatest confidence is in all these judgments. ### Chapter 5. On the conjunctions of the planets according to the opinion of **Hermes**. <note>original: "Laplum .5." is an abbreviation/misprint for "Capitulum 5." Hermes refers to Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary founder of Western astrology.</note>

## Aries.

¶ When **Jupiter**, **Venus**, **Mercury**, and the **Moon** are joined, it signifies a good state for men, and everywhere many profits, perfect rains, and honor for women and the king’s scribes. ¶ And if the **Moon** and **Jupiter** alone are joined there, it signifies justice and legality among men.

## Taurus.

¶ When **Venus** and **Mars** are joined in **Taurus**, it signifies that women will quarrel with men; and there will be many epidemics, and mortalities among men, and slaughter among beasts; and strong and evil winds; and harm to trees and fruits. ¶ And when **Jupiter**, **Venus**, **Mars**, and the **Moon** are joined in **Taurus**, there will be many lies between one person and another, betrayals, earthquakes, much water, the destruction of kings and nobles, and that base men and warriors will rise from the mountains who will make war against the king. ¶ And when **Saturn**, **Jupiter**, and **Mars** are joined in this sign, it signifies mortality of beasts, and that kings will go out from their kingdoms to others; and many illnesses will happen to men from <term>choler</term> <note>original: "colera"; one of the four humors of the body, associated with a hot and dry temperament and irritability</note>; and there will be great mortality among men and beasts.

## Gemini.

¶ When the **Sun**, **Venus**, and **Mercury** are joined in **Gemini**, there will be harm in the <margin>ib.</margin> status of scribes, and those who involve themselves with numbers and computation, and those who keep books of accounts; and it signifies that soldiers will join the king; and there will be a good market for bread; and harm will happen on journeys because of robbers.

## Cancer.

¶ When **Saturn**, **Jupiter**, **Mars**, the **Sun**, the **Moon**, and **Venus** are joined in **Cancer**, it signifies a great deficiency in every thing; and fear will happen to men; and the king will commit crimes against men, and one man against another; and earthquakes and harm at sea and in the water.

### ¶ Leo

When **Saturn**, **Jupiter**, **Mars**, and the **Moon** are joined in **Leo**: kings will quarrel and kill one another; great terrors and losses will happen to men.

### ¶ Virgo

When **Saturn**, **Mars**, and **Mercury** join in **Virgo**: it signifies harm to women, and kings are deceived. ¶ And if the **Sun** undergoes an eclipse in this sign by the **Tail** <note>original: "per caudam"; refers to the South Node of the Moon, often seen as a point of depletion or misfortune</note>, and **Mars** is joined to the Sun: there will be killings and great strife between noblemen and commoners. ¶ And when **Saturn** and **Venus** join in this sign: it signifies an increase in the waters <note>flooding or heavy rainfall</note>.

### ¶ Libra

When **Mars** and **Jupiter** are joined in **Libra**: it signifies a poor state for nobles and their allies; and signs will appear in the air that year as before. ¶ And when **Jupiter**, the **Sun**, and the **Moon** join there: deaths will happen among women and righteous men; and there will be much rain, clouds, and ruin in the air.

### ¶ Scorpio

When **Saturn**, **Mars**, and **Venus** join in **Scorpio**: it signifies that some beast—or an animal of which the king is afraid—will bite the king; and that kings will leave their own lands for others; and that one king will disagree with another, and they will break and disregard the causes and truces they held between them. ¶ And if the **Moon** is joined with them there: it signifies much rain and an increase of waters. ¶ And if **Scorpio** is the <term>ascendant</term> <note>the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the start of the astrological year</note> of the year, and **Saturn** is there with **Mars** joined to it (or even far from it, yet still in the same division of the ascendant), and **Venus** is <term>combust</term> <note>rendered powerless by being too close to the Sun</note> and **Jupiter** is <term>retrograde</term> <note>appearing to move backward in the sky</note>: judge all things to be evil: wars and strife, the depopulation of villages and earthquakes, terrors, killings, mortality, and many wicked illnesses. This is because **Scorpio** is the **misfortune of the signs**, just as its lord <note>Mars</note> is the **misfortune of the planets**. Judge similarly in this: that kings will quarrel with one another, wealthy men will die, and sorrows and anxieties will happen in the world. And when both **fortunes** <note>the benefic planets, Jupiter and Venus</note> are joined together in this sign: it signifies that men—or an enemy—will be revealed who will invite people to be disobedient to God.

### ¶ Sagittarius

When **Saturn**, **Jupiter**, **Mercury**, and the **Moon** are joined in **Sagittarius**: it signifies that there will be much water flowing underground; and that kings will value themselves highly, and the wealthy, scribes, astrologers, <term>necromancers</term> <note>those who communicate with the dead or practice dark magic</note>, and divine augurs will be elevated; and they will issue decrees and be held in high esteem.

### ¶ Capricorn

When the **Sun**, **Mars**, and **Mercury** join in **Capricorn**: it signifies destruction among kings by reason of **hot illnesses** <note>original: "infirmitatū calidarum"; in medieval medicine, diseases like fevers associated with the humor of yellow bile</note>; and it signifies many fires and burnings in the air, many winds, a lessening of all growing plants, and there will be many thieves and robbers.

<column-break/>

### ¶ Aquarius

When **Mars**, **Saturn**, and the **Moon** join in **Aquarius**: it signifies a decrease in rainfall but an increase in the waters of springs; harm during travel; and there will be many vipers and snakes.

### ¶ Pisces

When **Saturn**, **Jupiter**, and **Mars** are joined in **Pisces**: it signifies death and much loss for high-ranking and noble men. ¶ And if the **Sun**, **Mars**, and **Saturn** join there: it signifies that a king will be killed, and there will be little rain, and many fish will be taken from the sea. ¶ And know that when the **Head** <note>original: "caput"; the North Node of the Moon, associated with increase and intensity</note> and **Saturn** join in one sign: it signifies harm and evil according to the nature of that sign in which the conjunction occurs. For if they join in any **fiery sign** <note>Aries, Leo, or Sagittarius</note>: there will be harm to beasts and every hairy animal. ¶ And if they join in an **earthy sign** <note>Taurus, Virgo, or Capricorn</note>: there will be harm to trees, fruits, and herbs; yet rains and the profits that come from them will be found. ¶ And if they join in **airy signs** <note>Gemini, Libra, or Aquarius</note>: illnesses, fears, and crimes will happen among men. ¶ And if in **watery signs** <note>Cancer, Scorpio, or Pisces</note>: it signifies harm in the waters, death among aquatic animals, many locusts and reptiles, as well as pains and <term>phlegm</term> <note>one of the four humors, associated with coldness and moisture</note>. ¶ **Albumasar** <note>Abu Ma'shar, a famous 9th-century Persian astrologer</note> said: we must always look to the state of the king’s <term>seneschal</term> <note>the chief steward or highest administrative official of the royal household</note> by observing **Jupiter**. See if he is in an **angle** <note>the powerful 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses of a chart</note> or in a good or bad state; from these states you can know the condition of the seneschal. For if in the <term>revolution</term> <note>the chart for the start of the year</note> Jupiter is **combust** or **retrograde** (moving toward opposition), or afflicted by **Saturn**: it signifies that in that year the king will punish his seneschal, or perhaps kill him, or take away his office. ¶ And if Jupiter is **oriental** <note>rising before the Sun</note> and powerful in his <term>triplicity</term> <note>a group of three signs of the same element where a planet has extra strength</note>: the seneschal will be in a good state and will increase in his work. ¶ **Mars** is the significator of the one who commands the king’s military. Therefore, if in the revolution he is in **opposition** to **Saturn**: it signifies that the king will be angry with him that year and despise him, and hardships will happen to the soldiers. ¶ And if Mars is in **square** <note>a 90-degree aspect of tension</note> to Saturn, or in square to Jupiter, or in square to both: the soldiers will have strife in that year with their enemies and with one another; for this reason, some of them will perish, and they will move from one place to another, and others among them will go to help the king’s enemies. ¶ And if, along with what we have said, Mars is the **Lord of the Tenth House** <note>the house of kingship and authority</note>: the king himself will go out from his land. ¶ And if Mars is **retrograde** in that same year or quarter: it signifies that the soldiers will be defeated and flee. And if with this Mars is in a **human sign** <note>signs like Gemini, Virgo, or Aquarius</note> and is unfortunate: killings will appear among the soldiers. ¶ And if with this the sign of the **Tenth House** is clear of misfortunes and harms: he will have this <note>The text cuts off here, likely continuing with a positive outcome for the king</note>.

### ¶ The significations of the Sun through the houses.

When the Sun is the <term>lord of the year</term> <note>The planet that rules the sign on the ascendant at the moment of the New Year or "revolution"</note> and is in the <term>ascendant</term> <note>the first house, representing the self and the physical body</note>, and is fortunate and <term>received</term> <note>original: "receptus"; a technical term where the planet is in a sign or position that another planet welcomes</note> there: it will be a good year for lords, kings, nobles, and high-ranking men, and they will always have prosperity. ¶ And if he should be unfortunate in that same place: it signifies evil and loss among high-ranking men and nobles, and damage will apply to the persons of kings and lords, and many will fall from their dignities and high positions. ¶ And when he is in the second [house]: the wealth of the common people will be lost and kings will take it; and kings will be eager to seize and manage wealth, gold, and silver; and the wealth of the people will be diminished, and they will live a life of poverty and need. ¶ And if he should be in the third: men will love the laws and good deeds, and they will praise prayers and religions. ¶ And if he should be in the fourth: settlements will be depopulated; and plants will be ruined if he is in signs signifying plants; and high-ranking men will fall from their nobility. If he is in a <term>watery sign</term> <note>Cancer, Scorpio, or Pisces</note>: the waters will diminish and the herbs of the earth will dry up. ¶ And if he should be in the fifth: creatures in pregnant women will be harmed and diminished; and hardly ever will any pregnant woman escape without harm. ¶ And if the Sun should be in the sixth: infirmities and many pains will occur, especially in the eyes; and beasts will die if the sign is of <term>quadrupeds</term> <note>four-footed animals</note>. ¶ And if he should be in the seventh: it signifies that the king will hide himself away from men. ¶ And if he should be in the eighth: it signifies mortality <note>death</note> if the lord of the eighth house <term>aspects</term> <note>forms a geometric relationship with</note> him. ¶ And if he should be in the ninth: he has great and weighty significations there: fortunes; and his fortunes and significations in law and religion will be all the stronger; and men will love the law, goodness, and chastity; and the law and those who involve themselves with it will be honored. ¶ And if he should be in the tenth: kings will be honored and will rise, and especially the king of that specific <term>clime</term> <note>original: "climatis"; a geographical region of the world</note> because his power and nobility, and that of his people, will increase; and his neighbors will honor him regarding his kingdom, and they will humble themselves before him and obey his commands. ¶ And if he should be in the eleventh: it signifies good and much joy for the people of that clime, and one will find utility with another; and their kings will love them; lords and superiors will protect them, and do good to them and give them rewards. ¶ And if he should be in the twelfth: it signifies that the people of that clime will hate the king; and kings and superiors will do evil and burdens to the people.

### Chapter 8: On knowing the location on Earth where an event will occur.

<margin>Note well</margin>
When **Ptolemy** <note>Claudius Ptolemy, the 2nd-century scholar whose "Tetrabiblos" was the foundation of medieval astrology</note> wished to know the longitude of the habitable earth, he began from the islands which are named **Haly-dat** <note>The Fortunate Isles, likely the Canaries, used as the prime meridian in antiquity</note>; and they are in the **Roman Sea** <note>The Mediterranean</note>; and from those islands forward it is not known what is there, except that the sun sets there. And he took from this place as far as the town which is at the end of the land of **Zyn** <note>China</note>; and from this town forward he does not know what is in that part, except that similarly the sun rises there. And he found the motion of the sun from one place to the other to be **12 hours**; whence he placed the total longitude of the habitable earth at **180 degrees**: and each of those degrees falls directly at the **zenith** <note>The point in the sky directly above a specific location</note> of a town, which is its longitude according to the number of that degree up to 180 degrees. ¶ Whence, when you wish to determine the town which would be in line with the degree in which a **fortune** or **infortune** <note>Benefic planets like Jupiter/Venus or malefic planets like Saturn/Mars</note> may be: direct the **Ascendant of the year of the world** <note>The sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment the Sun enters Aries</note> to the location of the midpoint of the earth; and it is a place named **Catha** <note>Likely "Arim" or a central meridian point in medieval geography, sometimes confused with Cathay/China</note>; and it is distant from the east by 90 degrees, and by the same amount from the west; nor does it have any latitude; and the hours of this place are less than the hours of **Baldach** <note>Baghdad</note> by one hour and a third, because the longitude from the east as far as Baghdad is 110 degrees. ¶ And afterwards, take from that degree of the Ascendant up to the body or the rays of the planet whose significance you wish to know by equal degrees, going through the **midheaven** <note>The highest point of the zodiac at a given time</note>; and know how many <margin>The ways they have proportion</margin> there are; and its proportion which they have out of 360 degrees, and take that proportion out of 180, and it will be double that. He also said: take those same degrees which you found from the Ascendant to the planet, <margin>Setting this</margin> not taking the proportion, and take half of them; and divide it by the longitudes of the towns; and whichever town whose longitude from the east you find matching with those degrees, will be at the zenith of that degree; and in that place there will be good or evil in that significance. For example: let us <margin>Example.</margin> suppose that the Ascendant was **3 degrees of Aries**: and the planet where the ray is which signified good or evil is in the **10th degree of Capricorn**: whence we take 3 degrees of Aries, Pisces, and Aquarius as 60 <note>This calculation involves counting the distance between signs</note>, and 20 of Capricorn; and they all amount to 83 degrees; we take half <margin>180</margin> of them according to the proportion of 183 to 60, and they amount to 41 degrees and 30 minutes; whence we say that every town whose longitude from the east was 41 and a half degrees will be at the zenith of that degree; and in that place, the significance of good or evil will happen. And look if that degree is in an eastern sign or

<column-break/>

western, or southern or northern; or if it is at the very point of that part, or if it is on its right or on its left; and judge that the event will be in that part. And look similarly at which towns belong to the division of the sign, and in which of the four parts they fall; and mix it with the division of the longitudes which we have spoken of. And for discerning these towns, you will determine the location of the thing itself in which the Ascendant falls, or very close to it. ¶ Afterward, consider of which **term** <note>A specific sub-division of a zodiac sign ruled by a particular planet</note> that degree is, and in what place the lord of that term falls, and what **aspect** <note>The geometric angle between two planets</note> he has with that planet. And if both planets are **fortunate**: they are confirmed and strengthened <note>original: "appodeantur"</note> in all significations. And if both are **unfortunate**: the opposite. And if one is a fortune and the other an infortune: mix the significations between them, and give the greater significance to the one more strengthened among them, and to him who is the **significator**. ¶ However, **Hermes** <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary sage to whom many astrological works were attributed</note> used to do it in this way: he took the terms of the planets from the beginning of **Aries**, which is the **eastern triplicity** <note>The group of fire signs: Aries, Leo, and Sagittarius</note>; and he joined the terms one to another; and he gave to each degree one town which was in its line, as far as the degree in which the planet—fortune or infortune—was, about which he wished to know the event and its significance; and he said that the significance and that event would happen to that town. And this method is followed in **eclipses** and other events which Hermes named. ¶ And other wise men following him in their books, when they say "look at the term in which the infortune was," [they ask] which of the towns it is from the towns of that sign in which that term was; and because all events come and go from the signs and planets, they divided the lands and their quarters by signs and planets. Similarly, they divided the **human body** in the same way by signs and planets; whence when you find a significance of sickness in the lineage of a man: determine the limb in which the sickness will be through the limbs over which that sign has dominion in the human body; and judge the decrease and increase of that sickness, and the time in which he will be healed according to the strengthening of the fortunes and infortunes in that place. ¶ And if the years and months in which the fortunes and infortunes end are according to the years given to the planets according to the **fridarias** <note>A Persian system of time-periods where different planets rule different stages of life</note>; and the planets similarly have a division in the limbs as has been said in the appropriate places. ¶ And when the **Sun** is in **square** <note>A harsh 90-degree angle</note> to **Saturn**, and **Mars** is joined with Saturn, or in square to the Sun from another side: this is the greatest damage and misfortune for the Sun; and especially if such a constellation should happen to it at the **entrance of its exaltation** <note>The specific degree where a planet is most powerful; for the Sun, 19 degrees of Aries</note>. ¶ And similarly, every planet which has these aspects of infortunes at the entrance of its exaltation—and the **Part of Fortune** <note>An Arabic Part/Lot calculated from the Sun, Moon, and Ascendant</note> and its lord were distant from their aspects—it is similarly a very strong misfortune and a bad significance. For it signifies that the people of the towns in which that planet has dominion will suffer great hardships <note>original: "gravitates"</note> and occasions; and that their kings will do great evils to them, and robberies; and damages and many **shipwrecks** <note>original: "trire" likely referring to triremes or vessels</note> will happen to them. ### Chapter 9. On the significations of the planets when they are the lords of the quarters of the year.

<margin><unclear>for always (?)</unclear></margin>
<image-desc>Decorative initial Q inside a square frame featuring foliage and geometric patterns.</image-desc>
**W**hen Saturn is the lord of any quarter of the year, and you find him in any of the angles of Mars <note>Specific geometric relationships, like squares or oppositions, with the planet Mars</note>: it signifies great killings and massive disputes. Those who live in the land assigned to Saturn's partition will be victorious, as will those in the lands and villages within the partition of the sign in which Saturn resides, because Saturn is the lord of that very year.

### Concerning Jupiter.

<margin>partition</margin>
**W**hen Jupiter is the lord of the time: it signifies salvation and security for that climate <note>In ancient geography, a "climate" refers to a latitudinal zone of the earth</note>. No killings shall happen there, nor any hardship. Saturn assists Jupiter in those places that share a partition with the lord.

### Concerning Mars.

**W**hen Mars is the lord of the time, and he has the aspects we mentioned before with Saturn, and he is far from the aspects of Jupiter but joined to Saturn: damage, fear, many brawls, foul words, and sadness will happen in that time. All of this will occur in the climate and the lands where the sign in which Mars resides holds dominion. However, if it happens that Jupiter is in one of the angles of Mars during this time, these significations are diminished; if any of these troubles do occur, there would be no further disturbance once Jupiter has cast his gaze <note>aspect</note> there.

### Concerning the Sun.

<margin>Arim (?)</margin>
<note>The marginal note "Aremonzhuz" likely refers to "Arim," a mythical city or center of the world used in medieval geography</note>
**W**hen the Sun is the lord of the time, and he possesses dignity <note>Astrological strength or status</note> in the sign where he resides: it signifies adaptation, quiet, peace, alliances, and much good in that time. However, if he is made unfortunate there by Mars: it signifies that many hardships and damages will fall upon noble lords, high-ranking men, and wise people, along with labors and sadness by reason of litigation and illnesses. Yet, if Jupiter is in a position to block the damage of Mars, these [good] significations are renewed.

### Concerning Venus.

**W**hen Venus is the lady of the time and Mars is far from her aspects: it signifies joys, cheerfulness, and only minor brawls in that quarter; no evil shall be done, if God wills.

### Concerning Mercury.

**W**hen Mercury is the lord of the time: it signifies that men will have news, documents, embassies, words, and arguments; and the King will have

<column-break/>

news in the land appropriate to Mercury, or a King will come from another land.

### Concerning the Moon

**W**hen the Moon is the lady of the quarter, and you find her dignified and fortunate: judge that there will be no killings nor any evil in that quarter. However, if she is damaged and unfortunate because of Mars: judge that killings and labors will occur. Evils will happen according to the nature and significations of the sign; this will be even stronger among the youth, and it will be according to the power and virtue that Mars holds over the Moon. Furthermore, when at the Sun's entry into Aries <note>The Spring Equinox, the start of the astrological year</note> you find no planet fit to be the lord of the quarter, always give the portion and lordship to Mars at the Sun’s entry into Aries, and judge the quarter according to his place and power, if you cannot have another lord. Do the same for the Moon at the Sun’s entry into Cancer <note>Summer Solstice</note>. Do the same for Venus at the Sun’s entry into Libra <note>Autumn Equinox</note>. And do the same for Saturn at the Sun’s entry into Capricorn <note>Winter Solstice</note>. You shall do this whenever you do not have a planet fit to be the lord of the quarter.

### Chapter 10. On knowing the locations of things that occur.

<image-desc>Decorative initial U inside a square frame containing geometric patterns and foliage.</image-desc>
**W**hen you wish to know the locations in which events occur: look at which planet is the lord of the ascending sign. And if Saturn is the lord of the year or the quarter: judge that the Romans <note>referring to the Byzantine or Holy Roman Empire</note> will have good fortune; they will be more powerful than their enemies and will conquer them. However, their king will die, and mortality will occur among some of them. Those of the land of Dailam <note>original: "deylęc", a region in Persia</note>, those of the land of Babylon <note>original: "debaylen"</note>, and those of Cabreictem will have good fortune, because Saturn holds dominion there. ¶ And if you find Jupiter or Venus in this, mixed with Saturn: the evil we mentioned for the Romans is diminished; and regarding what we said about their king dying, he will come close to death but escape. Saturn can be at his worst and most fraudulent at the entry of the Sun into Aries when he is opposite the Sun and retrograde, or when the Sun joins him in a foreign sign: for then it signifies brawls and killings between those of the East and the West, and disputes in various places. ¶ And when you find Jupiter as the lord of the year or the quarter: men will have fertility and fulfillment. Anxieties will occur in the land of the Persians, but men will have much wheat and good things will multiply among them. ¶ And if Mars has a mixture with Jupiter in this, and Mars is dignified: bread will become more expensive at the end of the quarter or at the end of that year, and all his significations will be in the land of the partition of the sign in which Mars resides. ¶ And when you find Mars as the lord of the year or the lord of the quarter: look at the sign in which he resides, and judge that in the lands of that sign there will be much rain. The peoples of lands that are not in the partition of Mars will have good fortune, but enemies will do evil in the land of Iraq <note>original: "layrach"</note>, and mortalities will occur among men, especially among the youth and those who are not old. ¶ And when Mars is stationary and moves with the motion of Saturn: it signifies destruction and the cutting off of lineage.
