### Chapter 14. On the states of kings and how long they shall last.

<column-break/>

<image-desc>A large decorative woodcut initial 'A' containing floral and leaf patterns within a square frame.</image-desc>
**A**spice <note>Look</note> at the durability of a king from two parts: from the revolution of the year of the world <note>The chart cast for the Sun's entry into Aries</note> and from the hour of his enthronement: for both ought to agree and come to one limit: and if they disagree, there will be an error there. ¶ And when you wish to look from the revolution of the year, it is that you look from the first part unto the second. And if you find the second part in a high house <note>An "angular" or strong position in the chart</note> having an aspect or not, give to every 30 degrees one year. And if it be in an inferior house and has an aspect: give similarly to every 30 degrees one year. And if it does not look [at it]: diminish the degrees by half and give to the remaining half—namely to every 30 degrees—one year: and you shall begin the number from the part that is weaker in its place, tending toward the more empowered one. And if both be equal in power and place: look which of them is in its *hayz* <term>Hayz: A condition where a planet is in a sign and hemisphere that matches its masculine/feminine or day/night nature</term>: and begin from the other, coming toward it. ¶ And when the division is complete in which you have fear lest the king be lost: consider the sign of the application of the year: and if you find it afflicted in the revolution of the year and the Sun be in the square <note>original: "quarta"; an aspect of 90 degrees, considered stressful</note> of Mars or Saturn: judge for him destruction in that year. And if not: make for him another revolution. And look when the revolution applies to the square of the ill-fortunes: judge then for perdition. And do not judge destruction for him except through the affliction of the sign to which the year applies and the greater *hayzir* <note>Likely a variant of "atazir" or a specific planetary period</note>: and through the affliction of the Sun so that both be afflicted: for if one of them be afflicted and the other is improved: do not judge death for him: but judge for him loss through sickness and that which is likened to it; and there is misfortune through the square of Mars or Saturn in the revolution of the year: or when the application comes to its squares <margin>+ in their months retaining the difference you make</margin> of the root of the law or of the greater conjunction: or when it applies to the square of that greater conjunction: and when the first part is in its own houses: make for them revolutions of their place just as you do for other principles.

### Chapter 15. On knowing the durability of him who reigns.

<image-desc>A large decorative woodcut initial 'Q' with floral patterns, similar in style to the initial 'A'.</image-desc>
**Q**uando <note>When</note> you wish to know the durability of the one reigning: take from the lord of the exaltation of the Part of Fortune unto the same Part; and whatever [distance] is between them, give to each sign one month, day, or year. ¶ However, when you wish for the durability of the one reigning from the hour of his enthronement: set the Ascendant and the Midheaven: and extract the *hylech* <term>Hylech: The "life-giver," a specific planet or point in a chart used to determine longevity</term> and *alchocoden* <term>Alchocoden: The "giver of years," a planet that determines the specific span of life based on its strength</term> just as you do in births, equally, neither more nor less. ¶ Afterward, make the *ataçir* <term>Atazir: A method of "directing" or moving a point through the zodiac to predict timing of events</term> to the degree of the Ascendant that you may know the state of his body: and make the *ataçir* to the degree of the Midheaven that you may know the state of his kingdom: and carry both of these through the revolutions until they find themselves with the ill-fortunes: and then judge destruction. # Chapter 18. On kings and their lives.

<image-desc>Ornamental initial 'D' with decorative geometric and floral borders.</image-desc>
<margin>† or necks, for from</margin>
Omar the son of Al-Farrukhan <note>original: "Haomar filius Alpharha"; an 8th-century Persian astrologer and architect who was a primary source for medieval European astrology</note> said: whoever wishes to know the life of a king from the revolution of the world years: give the ascendant of the revolution to the people; and the Sun to the king; and the seventh house to the enemies of the people; and the fourth house to the end of the people's affairs. Give the ninth from the ascendant of the revolution of the year to the enemies of the king, because it is the house of the king's enemies <note>In the "derived house" system, the 12th house from any house represents its secret enemies; the 9th house is the 12th house relative to the 10th (the king)</note>. Place the house of the people's substance <note>Wealth or resources</note> as the second from the ascendant, and do the same for the other houses. Place the house of the king's substance as the eleventh from the ascendant, because it is the second from the Midheaven <note>The 10th house, or Medium Coeli, represents the king; the house following it, the 11th, represents his assets</note>. Its lord, the Sun, and the lord of the Sun’s sign are the significators of the king. ¶ Afterward, inspect the lord of the eighth house from the Midheaven <note>The 5th house, representing the king's death</note>, which is the place of the king's death. Look at what aspect <note>Geometric angle</note> and what application <note>Approaching movement</note> it has with the lord of the Midheaven and with the Sun. If there is no aspect between them nor any application, see if any planet joins their lights, or if there is a "translation of light" <note>When a faster planet moves from an aspect with one planet to an aspect with another, "carrying" the influence</note>. If you find a translation of light between them or a "collection of light," and you find that the planet making the translation aspects the sign of the Midheaven: it signifies death in that year. If it does not aspect there: it does not signify death. ¶ And help yourself in this case with the applications of the Moon to the "fortunes" <note>Benefic planets, Jupiter and Venus</note> and "misfortunes" <note>Malefic planets, Saturn and Mars</note>. If she applies to the fortunes: it signifies salvation. If to the misfortunes: death and destruction, unless other significations liberate him; in that case, he will suffer hindrance and toil, but he will escape. This signification of the Moon applies when she has some dignity in the sign of the Midheaven by house, exaltation, triplicity, or face <note>Technical categories of planetary strength/ownership</note>.

# Chapter 19. On knowing the time of a king's death through the revolution of the world year.

<image-desc>Decorative initial 'H' with architectural and leaf motifs.</image-desc>
You will determine this time through the conjunction of the king's significator with the lord of the eighth house from the Midheaven or with the Sun; or by whether it aspects them from a square <note>90 degrees</note> or opposition <note>180 degrees</note>. Also by whether the lord of the eighth is in this conjunction, square, or opposition in a sign

<column-break/>

in which he has some dignity and is powerful, and is not retrograde, nor "combust" <note>Too close to the Sun, thus blinded by its light</note>, nor "occidental" from the Sun <note>Setting after the sun</note>, nor in the "fall" of his exaltation. When this constellation is arranged in this way, then it will be the time of the king's death.

# Chapter 20. On knowing how long a king will live by the year of his enthronement.

<image-desc>Ornamental initial 'A' containing stylized foliage and scrollwork.</image-desc>
Look to when the Sun enters the first minute of the entry of Aries <note>The Vernal Equinox</note>, and see if any king will be enthroned in that year. Observe Saturn at the hour of the Sun’s entry into Aries; if you find him in his own house or in any of the houses of the superior planets <note>Mars or Jupiter</note>: it signifies that the ruler will endure for one complete conjunction <note>Likely the 20-year cycle of Jupiter and Saturn</note>. This is even more certain if Saturn is in the tenth from the Sun or in its eleventh. If he is so placed, there is no doubt he would last a full conjunction. If he is not so placed, you shall subtract from his durability according to how much the planet is diminished in its power. ¶ And know that Saturn is the "first part" and Jupiter is the "second." Whence, if the first aspects the second, it adds to the king's life. For if it is in its highest point <note>original: "appode ato," likely apogee</note> it adds the number of its "minor years" <note>A standard astrological time-unit; 30 years for Saturn</note> as months. It will do the same if it is in any of its dignities. If it is in a "succedent" house <note>The 2nd, 5th, 8th, or 11th</note>: it adds as much as half of its minor years. ¶ And if you find the "first part" in the world revolution of the year in which the king was enthroned to be in any house of the inferior planets <note>Moon, Mercury, or Venus</note>, especially if it does not aspect the Sun, and even more so if it is in Virgo: then it signifies that he will endure for as long as remains for this first part to travel out of its sign, giving one year to each degree. Such will be the life of the enthroned one. ¶ If this limit passes, you shall "direct" the *athazir* <note>original: "athaҫir"; a method of calculating time by moving planetary positions forward</note> from the place of the first part to the place of the first "misfortune" <note>malefic planet</note> it encounters. When the revolution reaches that sign in which he was enthroned, then he will die; and in this calculation, you shall give one year to each sign. ¶ You may do this in another way: calculate from the lord of the house of the "part" <note>An Arabic Part or Lot</note> unto that same part and see how many signs are between them. Give one year to each sign, and judge that the enthroned one will endure for that long.

## Chapter 23. On knowing the judgments of the planets when Venus is elevated above another.

This is taken from the *Book of Accidents*, which says thus: when planets are elevated one above another, it signifies various things in this manner.

### Concerning Venus

When Venus is elevated above Mercury, it will happen that one will triumph over the other. And when she is elevated above the Moon, men will have cheerfulness and

<column-break/>

joy. And when she is elevated above Mars, women will become pregnant; and damage will happen to men in their stomachs through an excess of eating. And when she is elevated above the Sun, men will spend much. And when she is elevated above the <term>Tail</term><note>The South Node of the Moon, often associated with loss or decrease</note>, it signifies nothing good. And when she is elevated above Saturn, pains and illnesses will happen to men.

### Concerning Jupiter.

When Jupiter is elevated above the Moon, noble men will be increased and will grow in goodness and honor. And when he is elevated above Mercury, the king's officials will be increased and will have honor, utility, profit, and praise. And when he is elevated above Venus, the business of women and girls will improve and they will have good. And when he is <margin>high</margin> elevated above Mars, troubles and pains will happen to men. And when he is elevated above Saturn, it signifies sadness, pains, and lamentations. And when he is elevated above the <term>Head</term><note>The North Node of the Moon, usually considered a point of increase or "good" fortune</note>, it signifies every good and improvement. And when he is elevated above the Tail, it signifies depopulations and the destruction of <note>original: "edificiozū"</note> buildings. And when he is elevated above a <term>tailed star</term><note>original: "stellam caudatam"; a comet</note>, it signifies that noble and valued men will be killed.

### Concerning Mars.

When Mars is elevated above Mercury, it signifies killings, disputes, and strong quarrels. And when he is elevated above the Moon, it signifies strong earthquakes. And when he is elevated above Jupiter, it signifies that noble men will involve themselves in taking up arms, and one will kill another. And when he is elevated above Saturn, it does not signify much evil. And when he is elevated above the Head, it signifies that noble men will have great fame. And when he is elevated above the Tail, it signifies that great burnings will happen to men in their plants and in every vegetable. And when he is elevated above a tailed star, many killings will happen among men, and they will unsheathe weapons and strongly involve themselves with them.

### Concerning the Sun.

When the Sun is elevated above the planets, in all things it signifies much evil and loss, except when <term>supported</term><note>original: "appodeato"; likely meaning Mercury is in a strong or supportive position to the Sun</note> in Mercury.

### Concerning the Moon.

When the Moon is elevated above Mercury, it signifies that men will be sensible, and they will choose good counsels, and they will act with good sense. And when she is elevated above Venus, it signifies that noble and wealthy women will rise in value and honor. And when she is elevated above...

### Chapter 24. On the conjunctions of the planets.

<image-desc>Ornamental woodcut initial 'Q' containing floral and scrolling vine patterns.</image-desc>
When Venus joins with Mars in the <term>revolution of the year</term><note>The chart cast for the moment the Sun returns to the first point of Aries, used to predict the year's events.</note>, a great <term>slaughter</term><note>original: "occasio"; in medieval contexts, this often refers to a violent downfall or massacre.</note> will happen among the Romans. When Mercury joins with Venus, poverty will occur. When Venus is joined with Jupiter: it signifies a great scarcity of bread and all victuals. When Mercury is joined with Saturn: it signifies a lack of examples or precedents. When Mars joins with Jupiter: it signifies the death of a king by epidemic, and it signifies many locusts. When Mercury joins with Mars, it does no harm to Mars. When [Mars] joins with Saturn: it signifies the death of a high and powerful king and many locusts. When Mercury is joined with Jupiter: it signifies epidemics and mortalities among men, and there will be many locusts.

### ¶ Chapter 31. On epidemics, health, drought, and abundance.

Know that the world is divided into seven parts which are called **climates** <note>Latitudinal zones used in ancient and medieval geography.</note>: and this division is according to the number of the seven planets. ### ¶ Chapter 36. On knowing what the planets possess regarding the climates and the partition of the earth.

**S**aturn possesses the first **climate** <term>Climate: a geographical zone based on latitude, used by ancient geographers to divide the known world into seven horizontal bands.</term> and India, the land of the blacks <note>original: "azyn nigros"; likely a reference to the Zanj or East Africans</note>, and the coastal summits.
¶ **Jupiter**, according to the sayings of the Romans, possesses the fourth climate, which is Babylonia, the land of Faris <note>original: "feriz"; Persia</note>, Khorasan <note>original: "cozasen"</note>, and Al-Iraq <note>original: "alefrach"</note>. And according to the sayings of the Persians, it possesses Azuen, the climate of Ethiopia, and Nubia. ¶ **Mars**, according to the sayings of the Romans, possesses the seventh climate: the land of Turkey, the Promised Land, and Romania <note>original: "romania"; usually referring to the Byzantine Empire or eastern Roman territories</note>. And according to the sayings of the Indians, it possesses the land of Alexandria and the Promised Land. ¶ The **Sun**, according to the sayings of the Romans, possesses the climate of Romania and the second climate: the East, the land of China <note>original: "zyn"</note> with its borders, and Khorasan. And according to the sayings of the Persians, it possesses Babylonia. ¶ **Venus**, according to these two opinions, possesses the fifth climate and Al-Hijaz <note>original: "alhyget"</note>, the land of the West, and Tirmidh <note>original: "tremez"</note>. ¶ **Mercury**, according to the opinion of the Romans, possesses Alexandria, the land of the Greeks, and the Promised Land. And according to the opinion of the Persians, it possesses the sixth and third climates. ¶ The **Moon**, according to the opinion of the Romans, possesses the sixth climate: the land of the West, France, Spain and what belongs with them, and Armenia as far as the Turks and the mountains. And according to the opinion of the Persians, it possesses the seventh climate. ¶ We have named among the cities of the signs some cities belonging to certain signs, and those same cities belonging to other signs; and we did this same thing with the planets, and we did this because we find it this way in the sayings of the ancient wise men, such as in the *Book of Climates and Cities*, and in the *Book of Ptolemy*, and in the *Book of Abitamas*, and in the *Book of Al-Bakayme*, and in other books. ¶ And Zesar <note>original: "zesar"; likely referring to an Arabic authority like Qustā ibn Lūqā or a similar astrological source</note> says that the lordship and kingdoms of the middle climates are changed from one people to another; nevertheless, the lordships and kingdoms of the "heads" <note>original: "capitū"; the extreme northern and southern regions</note> are fixed, because no one ever leads or rules them except the natives of that land. ¶ And they agreed with him and said that Mars leads the hot part of these two heads, and Saturn leads the cold part of the other head; and Jupiter leads the temperate middle. Therefore, the people living in the middle ought to be secure because of the nature of Jupiter, and in the heads, wars ought to be stirred up because of the nature of Saturn and Mars. ¶ Abaaon says that he heard from his father saying: that Cayton thought on this reasoning of Zesar's and found that the fixed stars go about circling two parts in the north and south; and because of this, the kingdoms and lordships in the heads were firm; and the moving planets go arching over the middle; and because of this, the kingdoms and lordships there are made changeable according to the movement of the planets. ¶ Ptolemy says in his book, where he named cities, islands, and seas, and how they are divided through all the signs and planets, and he placed the root of the number and the distance of Alexandria, saying that this city belongs to Leo and Mars, because its hours [of daylight] are 14, and the longitude from the Beginning of the Islands <note>The Fortunate Isles, the traditional prime meridian</note> is 60 degrees

<column-break/>

and 30 minutes, which makes 4 equal hours and thirteen hours; and upon this root all the longitudes of cities are named which we wish to name in this book, lest the reasoning be distanced from that which is useful; for whoever wishes to see them should look for them in that book. ¶ Ptolemy says that Metba and the Gate of Elen belong to Libra and Saturn; and Almedma and Comza to Scorpio and Venus; and Rauda, Haluen, Emel, and Karaj <note>original: "carazen"</note> to Taurus and the Moon; and Bahrain <note>original: "albaharen"</note> and Tiberias <note>original: "tabaria"</note> to Pisces and Mars; and Egypt <note>original: "mizre"</note> of Fra Dirigen and Jerusalem to Cancer and Mars; ...Saturn. And in the decorative degrees <note>original: "decoralo"; likely referring to the adjusted or "face" degrees of a planet</note>. Likewise, afterward subtract that which is decorative from the degrees of Saturn from that which is decorative from the degrees of Jupiter. If the degrees of Saturn are more than the degrees of Jupiter by one full revolution (360 degrees), subtract those degrees from the total of Saturn, and name the remainder from the decorative degree "purity" <note>original: "puritatem"; a technical term for a refined or adjusted value</note>. Afterward, look from the beginning of Aries up to the place of the "Great Conjunction" <term>Great Conjunction: the meeting of Jupiter and Saturn, which medieval astrologers believed signaled the birth of new religions or empires</term> in which the law began. For the law of Muhammad <note>original: "mahometi"</note>, this was at 4 degrees and 12 minutes of Scorpio. In equal degrees according to the ascensions, this becomes 214 degrees and 12 minutes. Add these to the degrees you named "purity," and subtract the result from the beginning of Aries. Wherever the number falls, there is the location of the **First Part**. If the number increases to more than 360 degrees, subtract them from it, and subtract the remainder from the beginning of Aries as we said before; where the number falls will be the first part, which is the **Part of the Law**.

¶ After this, look at the conjunction in which it occurred, and how far it is from the beginning of Aries in equal degrees. Add this to the degrees you named "purity." If the result is more than one revolution, subtract that from it, and subtract the remainder from the beginning of Aries; where the number falls is the location of the **Second Part**. ¶ They are also extracted in another way: find the Ascendant of the year of the world's revolution in which this king was enthroned. Look at the locations of the planets in that revolution: which planet was oriental from Jupiter or Saturn, and how far it is from it to the degree of the Sun. Add this to the number of the "minor years" <note>In astrology, planets have "minor," "mean," and "greater" years</note> of the lord of that law; for the law of the Moors <note>original: "maurozum"; referring to Muslims</note>, these are 8 years. Subtract the resulting number from the Ascendant, and where it falls, there is the location of the **First Part**. Take the **Second Part** from the degree of the Sun to the degree of whichever of the two aforementioned planets was occidental. Subtract what comes out from the degree of the first part before the number of the years of the lord of the law was added to it. Subtract the remainder from the Ascendant, and where the number falls, there is the location of the **Second Part**.

of the terms
</margin>

### Chapter 39: On knowing the sign of application of the Ascendant of the shift <note>original: "pmutationis"; likely the shift of a conjunction into a new zodiacal triplicity</note> of the conjunction which signified the law of the Moors.

<image-desc>Ornamental square woodcut initial 'Q' with foliate scrolls.</image-desc>
When you wish to know this: take the completed years of Yazdegerd <note>original: "iesdagert"; the last Sassanid King of Persia, whose era began in 632 AD</note> and add to them the 61st year mentioned before, along with 12 months, 12 days, and 16 hours. Starting from Libra, give one sign to each year. The sign where the count ends is the "application of the Ascendant" of the law of the Moors. ¶ And if you wish to know the application of the sign from the application of the conjunction of the law, begin from Scorpio. ¶ And if you wish for the sign of the application of the revolution: begin from Gemini, because it is said that the Ascendant of the year in which the conjunction occurred that signified that law was Gemini, according to the tables of Ptolemy. But according to the tables of *Daemdilud* <note>possibly a corruption of a specific astronomer's name</note>, the Ascendant of the law was 6 degrees of Aries. According to the *Verified Tables* <note>original: "dalmontahan"; referring to the Zij al-Mumtahan, or Verified Tables, from the era of Caliph al-Ma'mun</note>, it is Cancer, and this is the truth. ¶ And if you wish to know the degree of the partition <note>original: "ptitionis"</note>, begin from the 20th degree of Pisces, giving one year to each degree; where it falls, there will be the degree of partition. When you are certain of the degree of partition at the start of the year, add to them for every degree which the sun travels in the circle of the signs 10 seconds, which becomes 5 minutes in each sign.

<column-break/>

<margin>
365 and 1/4 days
</margin>
¶ And Al-Kindi <note>original: "Alkindus"; a famous 9th-century Arab philosopher and astrologer</note> said that from the year of the conjunction which signified the law of the Moors until the year in which Muhammad was enthroned, there were 52 solar years. He said that the Ascendant of that conjunction which signified the law was Gemini, and the application of the year in which Muhammad set out <note>original: "motus est"; likely referring to the Hijra or the beginning of his mission</note> was in Virgo. From the year of his promotion until Yazdegerd, there are 3,624 days. Therefore, when you wish to know this, reduce all the years of Yazdegerd to days, and divide the result by 365 and a quarter days. What comes from the division will be solar years, and what remains will be the months and days of the incomplete year. Those solar years will be those that passed from the promotion of Muhammad until the year in which you are working. Give one sign to each year, starting from Virgo; where the number of signs falls, that sign will be the application of the year of the world for the Ascendant of the law. ¶ And know that the sign of the application of the Ascendant of the law is the significator of that which will happen to the people of that law. The sign of the application of the 10th house <note>The 10th house or Midheaven (MC) represents authority and government</note> of the law will be the significator of what happens in the kingdom of that law. The sign of the application of the location of the conjunction of the law will be the significator of what happens regarding the law itself—whether it will be well observed or not. The lord of this sign will be the significator of what happens to the defenders of that law, and the place of partition will be the significator of the status of all the wise men. The application of the Ascendant of the "conjunction of the shift" signifies what will happen to the nation and the people of that same law. And the application of its 10th house signifies what will happen to the king of that shift. And the application of the conjunction of the shift signifies what will happen to the king who shall reign during that shift, regarding his increase or decrease. The lord of that application signifies what will happen to the defenders and the great counselors of that same king who shall reign during that shift.

### Chapter 40: On knowing these applications and partitions in the law of Muhammad.

<image-desc>Ornamental square woodcut initial 'Q' containing a circular scene with buildings.</image-desc>
When you wish to know this: take the years of Yazdegerd and add to them the 61st year, 2 months, 12 days, and 16 hours. Reduce them to solar years, giving one sign to each year starting from Libra. Where the count ends, that will be the application of the Ascendant of the law of the Moors, because the Ascendant of the conjunction of the law was 18 degrees of Libra. ¶ And if you wish to know the application of the location of the conjunction of the law of the Moors, begin from Scorpio; where it falls, that will be the application of the conjunction. ¶ And if you wish for the partition, begin from the 20th degree of Pisces; where the number falls, there will be the application. ¶ And if you wish for the application of the shift from Sagittarius, subtract the years of Yazdegerd joined with those 61 years, reduced to solar years, plus 31 years and 14 days. From what remains, give one sign to each year, beginning from Leo; where it falls, there will be the application of the Ascendant of the shift. ¶ And if you wish for the application of the Ascendant of this dominion of this nature <note>original: "nā"; likely "natura"</note>: take the years of Yazdegerd joined with the said 61 years, and with the whole amount reduced to solar years, subtract from it 177 years, ten months, and 27 days reduced into solar years. From what remains, give one sign to each year, starting from Virgo.

### Chapter 41. On the vision of comets.

In my book, I did not place this chapter until after I had experienced it to be true in the death of the son of Abenboceyn <note>likely Al-Husayn</note> and in the death of Zaet, the son of Abenhazron; nevertheless, before I experienced it, I did not hold nor believe that it had any significance or efficacy. ¶ I say, therefore, that when any star falls <note>referring to comets or meteors</note> from **Aries** in such a way that it seems to cut through the sky and leaves its mark, it signifies that the King of the Christians will die, and that killings and wars will occur in the land of Babylon <note>often used in this period to refer to Old Cairo or the Middle East generally</note>. ¶ And if that fall should be from **Taurus**, it signifies that many cities will be depopulated in the lands of the Christians and mortality shall happen in the land of Babylon. ¶ And if that fall should be from **Gemini**, it signifies that strife will occur in the lands of the Christians, and the King of Egypt will die; a handsome and fit man will reign in his place, and mortality and infirmity will occur in the land of Persia. ¶ And if that fall should be from **Cancer**, it signifies that strife and killings will occur in the land, and the son of the king will die in a dispute, and in a short time the king himself will die. ¶ And if that fall should be from **Leo**, it signifies that the king will die and his enemies will rejoice; and there shall go out from the climate of Babylon one who will oppose the king and cause harm. ¶ And if that fall should be in **Virgo**, it signifies that the King of Egypt will kill his enemies, and many wars will happen to him. ¶ And if that fall should be from **Libra**, it signifies that the people will do evil to the king and commit hidden betrayals. ¶ And if that fall should be from **Scorpio**, it signifies that there will be many burnings of the air <note>likely atmospheric heat or lightning</note> in the land, and the waters of the rivers will be diminished. ¶ And if that fall should be from **Sagittarius**, it signifies that epidemics and mortalities will occur in the land of Babylon and in the land of Baghdad <note>original: "baldach"</note>, and that the king will die there. ¶ And if that fall should be from **Capricorn**, it signifies that much evil will occur in the land of the Medes <note>original: "methe"</note> and in the land of Lahore <note>original: "alahor"</note> through disputes and that which resembles them. ¶ And if that fall should be from **Aquarius**, it signifies that a mocked man will rise up and take power in the kingdom, but he will last in it only a little while. Afterward, many anxieties will occur; it also signifies deliverances and much water, and God knows best what is to come.

The "Complete Book on the Judgments of the Stars" ends happily, which was composed by Albohazen Hali, son of Abenragel <note>The 11th-century Arab astrologer Abu l-Hasan 'Ali ibn Abi r-Rijal</note>; well-revised and corrected with faithful study by Master Bartholomew de Alten of Neuss, a German and most excellent doctor of arts and medicine. Printed by the skill and at the expense of Erhard Ratdolt of Augsburg <note>A famous pioneer of printing known for astronomical works</note>: during the reign of Giovanni Mocenigo, Doge of Venice, in the year of the incarnation of our Lord 1485, on the fourth of the Nones of July, at Venice.
